  • The parts of your blog that’ll be imported into HubSpot are: title, post body (including inline images), URL, publish date, author, tags/categories, status, meta description, featured images.
  • PDF files linked in your posts and images in gallery tags won’t be included in an XML import.
  • Before you import your blog, review all internal links and images to confirm they include the absolute URL instead of a relative URL. This will prevent links and images from breaking in your imported posts.

Export blog posts

To import blog posts into HubSpot, first export them as an XML file from WordPress or Squarespace.

Export blog posts from WordPress

If your blog is hosted on WordPress, export your blog posts as an XML file from the WordPress admin tools.

  • Sign in to your WordPress website as a WordPress Admin and navigate to Tools > Export to select your blog posts for export.
  • If you’re using WordPress.com, you can follow the steps in this WordPress documentation about how to export your posts from WordPress.com.
  • If you’re using a custom WordPress website, you can follow this WordPress documentation about how to export your posts from your custom WordPress website.
Export blog posts from Squarespace

If your blog is hosted on Squarespace, export your blog posts as an XML file from the Import & export content panel.

  • Sign in to Squarespace and access the Import & export content panel to select your blog posts for export.
  • Follow the steps in this Squarespace documentation to export your blog posts.

Import XML files into HubSpot

After exporting your blog posts, upload the XML file to HubSpot and import the posts into a HubSpot blog.

Upload XML file

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.

  • Click the Current view dropdown menu and select Import blog.

  • Click the Start new import dropdown menu and select Blog posts.

  • Select the XML file upload option, then click Next.

  • In the top right, click Import new blog.

  • In the dialog box, click Upload and select an XML file. By default, the Remove shortcodes from imported posts is selected, which will delete shortcodes from WordPress or Squarespace blog posts. To include raw code in your posts, clear the checkbox.

  • Click Upload.

Import blog posts

After the XML file is uploaded, review the blog posts in the file and select which posts to import into your HubSpot blog.

  • To import blog posts in the file, hover over the file, then click Import posts or the File name. You’ll be directed to view all the blog posts in the file.

  • Select or clear the checkboxes next to each post you want to include or exclude from the import.

  • Click Import posts.

  • In the dialog box, click the blog dropdown menu and select the blog to import the posts to.

  • Click the Publishing status dropdown menu and select one of the options:

    • Keep existing status - This option will maintain the publish status from your WordPress blog and keep any draft posts as drafts, and any published posts as published.
    • Change all to draft - This option will change the publish status from your WordPress blog and save any imported posts as draft blog posts.

  • To import your blog tags into HubSpot, select the Import blog tags checkbox.

  • To replace any posts in your current blog that have the same URL, select the Overwrite any existing blog posts with imported posts checkbox.

  • When finished, click Import. You’ll receive an email notification and a message in your blog importer dashboard once your import is complete.

Export redirects for WordPress or Squarespace posts

After importing your blog posts, export redirects to ensure visitors and search engines are routed to the correct URLs. The way you set up your blog redirects depends on how much of your website is now hosted on HubSpot:

  • If your entire website, including the domain for your former WordPress blog, is now hosted on HubSpot, you can set up redirects in your website settings.
  • If the domain of your old WordPress blog is still hosted on WordPress, you’ll set up your redirects in WordPress. The Redirection plugin may be useful in implementing bulk redirects in WordPress.

To export your redirects:

  • Navigate back to your blog importer dashboard, then click on the File name of your recent import. Here you’ll see details about any errors or a notification that your posts have been imported.

  • Click Export your redirects.

  • In the dialog box, click the Format dropdown menu and select a format option (e.g., CSV, XLSX, XLS).

  • Enter an Email where you’d like the file to be delivered, then click Export. You’ll receive an email shortly with your file.

Troubleshoot common errors

If you encounter any issues during the blog import process, review how to troubleshoot the following errors.

Content missing from an import

If something you were expecting to import didn’t show up in your blog, confirm the desired imported content is in the expected XML tags. If the content you were expecting to import isn’t in the XML file, review the WordPress support documentation to confirm that all content was selected and exported correctly.

The file for this import is invalidly formatted

This error means the XML file you tried to import was malformed or has syntax errors which are preventing our blog importer from reading the XML file. We’ll provide as much detail on the error as possible, and it’s possible after correcting the mentioned error, more will arise. This is because the XML parser will stop running after finding an error.

You’ll see these same errors if you open the XML file in another XML parser, such as Google Chrome. For help resolving the XML errors, refer to the provider of the XML file (WordPress or Squarespace).

Retrieval of asset at URL failed

This means your XML file referenced an asset (usually an image) that didn’t lead to an asset. For example, if you see an error like the following:

Retrieval of asset at URL https://www.image.com/image.jpg failed. This asset was not uploaded to the file manager.

If you click on the mentioned URL and also confirm that it doesn’t lead to an image, you’ll need to correct this image URL in the XML file, and re-import the posts that were affected. You can also upload the image file to your file manager, and add the images to your post in HubSpot.

Manage blog authors

Blog authors represent the users credited on blog posts. Each author has a profile containing information, such as their display name, bio, and avatar. HubSpot automatically generates an author page for each blog that includes all posts attributed to the author. These pages have a title of [Blog name] | [Author name] and a meta description of the author’s bio.

Before you get started

Before you manage blog authors, review the requirements and considerations.

Permissions required Marketing Access with Edit and Publish permission are required to manage blog authors.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • If you’re creating blog content in multiple languages, learn more about creating language variations for blog authors.
  • Each blog post can have up to five blog authors.

Create a blog author

Create a new blog author by entering required information, including the name, internal name, and author slug. Additional optional details can be added to complete the author’s profile.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and select Authors in the top right.
  • On the Blog authors page, click Add new author on the top right.
  • In the right panel, enter the required author information:
    • Public Name: the author name that appears on live blog posts.
    • Internal Name: the author name that appears in the Authors dashboard in the blog tool.
    • Author Slug: the unique string of the author URL. The rest of the URL pulls from the blogs where the author appears.
  • Enter optional author information:
    • Language: the primary language of the author’s content. Only authors writing multi-language blog content need a value for this field.
    • Email address: the author’s email address.
    • Author avatar: an image of the author. You can use the author’s HubSpot profile avatar or add a custom avatar image from the files tool.
    • Author bio: a description of the author.
    • Website: the author’s personal website.
    • Facebook/X/LinkedIn: the author’s social media profiles.
  • When you’ve finished adding the author details, click Create author.

Edit a blog author’s profile

Edit existing blog author profiles, including changes to names, avatar images, bio, language, or other optional profile information.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and select Authors on the top right.
  • To filter by blog, click the All blogs dropdown menu and select a blog.
  • To filter by author, click the All authors dropdown menu and select Active or Inactive.
  • Hover over an author and click Edit full profile.
  • In the right panel, update the author’s profile information. Then click Update blog author to take the changes live.

Add blog authors to a post

Blog authors are assigned to a blog post from the post’s settings. Selecting authors determine whose names appear on the published post and which author pages the post is listed on.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.

  • Click the name of the blog post.

  • In the content editor, click Settings on the top right.

  • In the Settings dialog box, click the Author dropdown menu and select the existing authors. To create a new author, click Create a new author.

  • Click X to hide the dialog box.

  • When finished, click Publish or Update in the top right to take your changes live.

Delete a blog author

When a blog author is deleted, their posts must be reassigned to another author. Deleting an author removes their profile and updates author attribution on all affected blog posts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and select Authors on the top right.
  • On the Blog author page, hover over the author, and click the More dropdown menu. Then select Delete.
  • In the dialog box, click the Reassign blog posts to dropdown menu and select an author to reassign the blog posts. If the deleted author has no live posts, this option won’t appear.
  • Enter delete to confirm you want to delete this author.
  • Click Delete author.

Manage blog settings

Manage blog settings, including the template your blog is using, the root URL, subscription email settings, date format, and more. If you’re creating blog content in more than one language, learn how to create a multi-language blog.

Subscription required Some features require additional subscriptions:

  • Marketing Hub Enterprise is required to change a blog root URL.
  • Content Hub Professional or Enterprise is required to limit blog access to access groups.

Permissions required Website settings permission is required to edit blog settings.

Manage blogs

Select an existing blog to manage the blog settings. You can also create a new blog, import external blog content, or delete a blog in your blog settings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • Click the Current view dropdown menu:
    • To select an existing blog, click the name of the blog you want to manage settings for.
    • To create a new blog, click Create new blog. Learn more about creating a new blog
    • To import a blog, click Import blog. Learn more about different blog import methods.
  • To select a multi-language version of the blog, click the second dropdown menu and select a language. Learn more about working with multi-language blogs.
  • Continue editing the general blog settings.
Delete a blog

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.

  • Click the Current view dropdown menu and select the blog you want to delete.

  • Click the Options dropdown menu and select Delete blog in the top right.

  • In the dialog box, enter the name of the blog in the text field.

  • By default, the blog’s subscription form, subscriber notification emails, subscription email lists, subscription contact property, and subscription type will also be deleted. To maintain any of these, clear the checkbox next to it.

  • When finished, click Yes, delete to finish deleting the blog.

Edit general blog settings

Edit identifiers (e.g., blog name, header, title, etc.), access controls, metadata, and URL configuration to define how the blog is presented and accessed.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • On the General tab, enter text to edit the following blog details:
    • Blog name: the internal name of your blog. This name won’t be visible to visitors.
    • Blog header: the external blog name that’ll display if your templates use the group.public_title HubL variable.
    • Page title: the text that appears in the browser tab and in search engine results. It is recommended to keep the title to less than 70 characters.
    • Meta description: the summary that’ll appear in search engine results, generally.
  • In the Blog root URL section, select the Use language slug in URL checkbox to use a language slug in the blog’s root URL. This is recommended if your blog language doesn’t match your domain’s primary language.
  • In the Domain section, click the Domain dropdown menu and select a domain to change the blog root URL.

Please note: if you change a blog’s root URL, redirects will automatically be created to redirect any published blog content to their new URLs. If there’s no published blog content, redirects will not be created automatically.

  • To add a slug to the end of the blog root URL (e.g., mywebsite.com/blog), enter the slug in the Blog slug field.
  • To limit access to the blog, select an option in the Access control section:
    • Public: the blog can be accessed by anyone. To give visitors access to the entire blog, but only members access to full blog posts, select the checkbox.
    • Access group membership required: specific contacts can access the blog. Learn more about limiting blog access to access groups.
    • Single sign-on (SSO) required: SSO authentication is required to access the blog. Learn more about setting up SSO for private content.
  • To turn on BlogPosting schema for the blog, toggle the Structured Data switch on.
    • Blogs created after Aug. 4, 2022 have this setting turned on by default.
    • This will turn on the BlogPosting schema type to support article-rich results in search engines.
  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Please note: avoid enabling structured data if custom schema already exists. Duplicate schema may cause issues in search engines.

Manage blog templates

Edit or change the templates applied to your blog posts and blog listing page on the Templates tab. You can also customize your listing page setup and add custom HTML to your templates’ header and footer.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.

  • Click the Templates tab.

  • In the Blog Post Template section, click the Actions dropdown menu and select an option:

    • Change template: choose a different template. On the template selection screen, select your new template, then click Done. In the bottom left of your template settings, click Save.
    • Edit: to edit your template in the design manager. Learn more about editing a blog post or listing template.
    • Preview: view what a blog post looks like.
    • Edit theme settings: to edit the blog’s theme settings. Learn more about editing your theme settings.

  • In the Blog listing page section, click the Actions dropdown menu and select an option:

    • Preview: view what the blog listing page looks like.
    • Details: view the blog listing page details and performance data.
    • Change template: use a different template for the blog listing page. Learn more about using a different template.

  • Click Edit page to open the blog listing page in the content editor.

  • Enter the number of posts you want to appear on your listing page in the Number of posts per listing page field.

  • To display the content of blog posts up to the Read More separator on your listing page, select the Show summaries on listing page checkbox.

  • To display the featured images of your blog posts on your listing page, select the Use featured image in listing summaries checkbox.

  • In the Header HTML and Footer HTML sections, enter any custom HTML you want to apply to your blog post and listing templates. To apply different custom HTML to your blog post template, click Use custom header/footer HTML for blog posts.

  • In the CSS and stylesheets section, click + Add style sheet to add a style sheet to your blog listing and blog post templates.

  • In the dialog box, click the Choose a style sheet dropdown menu and select a style sheet. Then click Add.

  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Manage blog subscriptions

Turn the frequency of email subscription notifications on or off. You can also create, edit, and delete blog notification emails for each frequency and customize RSS feed settings. Learn more about setting up blog subscription emails.

Configure blog date formats

Configure the blog’s language and format for dates on blog posts and the blog listing page. This is separate from setting the language for a multi-language blog.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • Click the Date Formats tab.
  • To set a language for the blog’s dates, click the Language for dates dropdown menu and select a language. Selecting a language or location will pre-populate localized date formats for that language or the location it tends to prefer.
  • To set the date format for publish dates, click the Publish date format dropdown menu and select a date format.
  • To set the month format for posts, click the Posts by month format dropdown menu and select a date format.
  • To create a custom date format, click What’s this? to review guidelines for using Locale Data Markup Language.
    • Click Customize format next to Publish date format or Posts by month format.
    • In the dialog box, enter the custom date format and then click Create date format.
  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Please note: if your blog dates always show the same year (e.g.,, 2026), check the Publish date format and Post by month format for a hardcoded year (e.g., MMMM dd, 2026) and replace it with the dynamic year token (e.g.,, MMMM dd, YYYY).

Manage blog comment settings

Turn blog comments on or off. Manage blog comment notifications, moderator settings, and more. Learn more about setting up and moderating blog comments.

Configure social sharing settings

Configure which social accounts appear in a blog’s social sharing module. A counter for each social media sharing icon will display the number of times the blog post was shared on that network.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • Click the Social Sharing tab.
  • To set an X handle for blog posts shared via X Cards, click the Default X account dropdown menu and select an X account. Learn more about connecting an X account to HubSpot.
  • To include social sharing icons on the blog post, select the social network checkbox next to each associated social network in the Social sharing buttons section.
  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Please note: social sharing buttons are supported in default blog templates or templates with specific HubL variables. Learn more in the developer documentation.

Manage Google AMP

Turn Google Accelerated Mobile Pages on or off. Accelerated Mobile Pages (AMP) loads your content instantly. Learn more about using AMP on your blog.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • Click the Google AMP tab.
  • To turn on Google AMP, toggle the Turn on Google AMP formatted pages switch on.
  • Customize the appearance of your logo, header, and body text. Learn more about Google’s recommendations for AMP formatting.
  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Manage blog subscribers

Blog subscriber segments are created automatically for each active blog notification frequency (e.g., Daily). These segments determine the recipients for blog notification emails. Edit these segments or update individual contact preferences to manage your subscriber list.

To set up or edit blog subscription emails, learn more about setting up blog subscription emails.

Please note: for each blog, a contact can only be subscribed to a single notification frequency. For example, a contact could be subscribed to weekly notifications for two separate blogs, but not weekly and monthly notifications for the same blog.

Edit a blog subscription segment

Once you create a notification email for a specific frequency, a corresponding segment of subscribers will also be created. This segment will filter for all contacts with a [Your Blog] Email Subscription value of that frequency. Its default name will be [Subscription] Subscribers - [Your Blog].

Permissions required Edit permission is required to edit blog subscription segments.

To add additional filter criteria to your [Subscription] Subscriber - [Your Blog] segment:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • Enter subscribers in the search bar to view all blog subscription segments.
  • Click the name of the segment.
  • Adjust your filters and criteria, then click Save changes.

Edit a contact’s blog subscription

Edit a contact’s notification frequency from their contact record by editing the [Your Blog] Email Subscription property. To edit the notification frequency for multiple contacts, you can change the [Your Blog] Email Subscription property with a bulk edit or import.

Permissions required Edit permission is required to edit a contact’s blog subscription property.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of the contact.
  • In the About this contact section of the contact record, click the Actions dropdown menu and select View all properties.
  • In the right panel, enter email subscription in the search bar.
  • Click the [Your Blog} Email Subscription dropdown menu and select a subscription frequency. Select the blank value to remove a contact’s blog subscription.

Set a blog post’s publish date and time

Set and change the publish date of an unpublished or published blog post in the Publishing Options dropdown menu of the content editor.

Before you get started

Before you set a blog post’s publish date and time, review these requirements and considerations.

Permissions required Edit and Publish permission is required to set a blog post’s publish date and time.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • Changing a post’s publish date may cause external RSS emails to include the post because the blog’s RSS feed will be changed.
  • Changing a blog post’s publish date to a date in the past won’t trigger a duplicate blog subscription email or automated social post.
  • New blog posts with a publish date in the past won’t trigger blog subscription emails or automated social posts.
  • New blog posts with a publish date in the future won’t appear live or trigger blog notification emails until that date.

Set the publish date for an unpublished post

Publish a new blog post with a publish date in the past, or schedule it to be published on a future date.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the name of a blog post.
  • In the content editor, click the dropdown menu next to Publish in the top right and select Scheduling options.
  • In dialog box, click Schedule publish.
  • Click the date and time fields and select the date and time when your post will be published.
  • When finished, click Schedule.

Set the publish date for a published post

Set the publish date of an existing live post to a date in the past. I f blog subscription emails weren’t turned on in your blog settings when the post was originally published, then the post may be included in relevant weekly or monthly blog notification emails for the new publish date.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the name of a blog post.
  • In the content editor, click the dropdown menu next to Update in the top right and select Scheduling options.
  • In the dialog box, click Schedule update.
  • Click the date and time fields and select the date and time when your post will be published.
  • When finished, click Schedule.

Set up and moderate blog comments

Blog comments are responses from visitors that display on blog posts. You can turn on comments for your blog, adjust their display settings, and decide if comments are published instantly or require approval.

Customize the default comment form and manage the comments that come in. Depending on your moderation preferences, you can approve, reject, reply to, delete, or flag comments as spam.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Website settings permission is required to set up comments in blog settings.
  • Forms permission is required to edit blog comment forms.
  • Marketing Access with View and Edit permission is required to moderate blog comments.

Set up blog comments

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • Click the Comments tab.
  • To allow visitors to leave comments on your blog, toggle the Turn on commenting switch on.
  • To add visitors who comment on your blog to your contacts database, select the Allow comments to create contacts checkbox.
  • To require approval by your team before comments are published, select the Moderate comments checkbox.

Please note: if Allow comments and Moderate comments to create contacts are both selected, contacts won’t be created until their comments are approved.

  • To close comments automatically, select the Automatically close comments checkbox.
  • To send a specific user notifications of new comments on the blog, click the Who should receive notifications of new comments on this blog? dropdown menu and select the user.
  • To customize how many levels of comments can be threaded, click the Number of levels comments can thread dropdown menu and select the number of levels. The more levels added here, the more layers of replies visitors can leave on existing comments.
  • To show visitors a message after they leave a comment, enter a message in the Confirmation message after comments are submitted text field.
  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Edit blog comment forms

A blog comment form is automatically created for each blog in your account. If your blog has language variations, create separate comment forms for each variation. Add additional fields or customize required fields in the forms tool.

Please note: blog comment forms must include the Comment field. If you remove the Email field, contacts might not be created, depending on your settings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • In the Search field, enter comment form. By default, a blog comment form is named [Blog Title] Comment Form.
  • Hover over the form and click Edit.
  • Edit your form, then click Update in the top right.

Moderate comments

Blog comments can be replied to, deleted, or marked as spam. With the Moderate comments setting turned on, a user must approve comments before they appear on live blog posts.

Please note: any comments submitted before the Moderate comments setting is turned on cannot be rejected later.

Approve comments
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and then select Comments in the top right.
  • To filter comments by blog, click the All blogs dropdown menu and select a blog.
  • To filter comments by post author, click the All authors dropdown menu and select an author.
  • To view comments awaiting approval, click the All states dropdown menu and select Pending.
  • Select the checkbox next to each blog comment to approve. Then click Approve at the top of the table.
Reject comments
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and then select Comments in the top right.
  • To reject a blog comment, hover over a blog comment and click the More dropdown menu. Then select Reject.
Reply to comments
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and then select Comments in the top right.
  • Hover over the comment and click Reply.
  • In the dialog box, enter the name that’ll be displayed in the reply.
  • Enter the email address that’ll be displayed in the reply.
  • Enter the reply in the Comment field.
  • When finished, click Reply.
Remove comments
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and then select Comments in the top right.
  • To remove an individual blog comment, hover over the comment and click the More dropdown menu. Then select Delete.
  • To remove multiple blog comments, select the checkbox next to each blog comment. Then click Delete at the top of the table.
Mark comments as spam
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the Configure dropdown menu and then select Comments in the top right.
  • To mark an individual blog comment as spam, hover over the comment and click Mark as spam.
  • To mark multiple blog comments as spam, select the checkbox next to each blog comment. Then click Mark as spam at the top of the table.

Please note: HubSpot automatically filters for spam comments and hides them from your posts. To reduce the number of spam comments you’re seeing, turn on CAPTCHA in your form settings.

Set up blog subscription emails

Set up automated notification emails to send to contacts when new blog posts are published. Blog subscription emails can be sent instantly, daily, weekly, or monthly. This helps keep subscribers engaged with new blog content.

Before you get started

Before you set up blog subscription emails, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Website settings permission is required to edit blog settings.
  • Marketing access is required with Edit and Publish permission to edit and publish blog subscription emails.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Blog subscription emails count toward your email send limit.
  • A subscription type for notification emails is created automatically for each new blog.
  • Contacts can fill out a blog subscription form to be notified of blog posts at their chosen frequency.
  • A subscription form won’t appear on a published post unless at least one subscription email for that blog is published.
  • Each contact may only be subscribed to one notification frequency for each blog. For example, a contact can receive weekly updates from two different blogs, but can’t receive both weekly and monthly updates from the same blog.
  • Instant notification emails send 30 minutes after a blog post is published.
  • Daily, weekly, and monthly notifications emails send based on the schedule configured in each email.

Customize blog subscription settings

Customize the blog subscription settings to choose which subscription frequencies are available to visitors. You can also customize how summaries appear in RSS feeds or subscription emails.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.

  • In the Current View section, click the first dropdown menu and select a blog. In accounts with the Brands add-on, this will be the second dropdown menu.

  • Click the Subscriptions tab.

  • In the Blog subscriber notifications email section, click Create to create a new blog subscription email. Learn more about creating blog subscription emails.

  • To edit an existing blog subscription email, click Edit. Learn more about editing blog subscription emails.

  • To delete an existing blog subscription email, click Delete.

  • To turn a blog subscription email on or off, toggle the Send on or off.

  • In the RSS Feed section, customize the RSS feed options:

    • Number of posts in RSS feed: enter the number of posts that’ll appear in your RSS feed. Each RSS email will only include new posts since the previous send of the email, up to the selected number.
    • Show summaries in RSS: select the checkbox to show a preview of your blog post content in your RSS feed.
    • Show summaries in emails: select the checkbox to show a preview of your blog post content in your RSS emails.

  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Create a blog subscription email

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • In the Current View section, click the first dropdown menu and select a blog. In accounts with the Brands add-on, this will be the second dropdown menu.
  • Click the Subscriptions tab.
  • In the Blog subscriber notification emails section, click Create for any of the following email frequencies:
    • Instant notifications: subscribers receive an email of the latest post. The email is sent 30 minutes after you publish it. If you don’t want the email to send, backdate your blog post to a time before the thirty-minute delay.
    • Daily notifications: subscribers receive a daily email of the blog posts.
    • Weekly notifications: subscribers receive a weekly email of the blog posts.
    • Monthly notifications: subscribers receive a monthly email of the blog posts. The email is sent within 31 days of the date you choose in the Select or schedule tab when you set up the monthly email template.
  • Select a template for the blog subscription email notification.
  • Continue to edit your blog subscription email.

Please note: when instant blog subscription emails are turned on, an email will be sent out for any blog posts published within the past 12 hours. Turning on daily, weekly, or monthly blog subscription emails will send an email with any existing blog posts published within that time frame.

Edit and publish blog subscription emails

Edit the main body content, inbox content, and scheduled time of blog subscription notification emails.

Edit main body content
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • In the Current View section, click the first dropdown menu and select a blog. In accounts with the Brands add-on, this will be the second dropdown menu.
  • Click the Subscriptions tab.
  • In the Email Link column, click Edit.
  • In the email editor, click the main body of your email to edit its content.
  • In the sidebar editor, enter the text of your blog post descriptions in the Display field.
    • To rearrange the order of blog post information, click an RSS token and drag it to a new position. The following RSS tokens are available:
    • To add a new RSS token, click the RSS token icon.RSS Click the Token dropdown menu and select an RSS token.
  • Select a Post length option:
    • Summary: the email will only include the blog post’s title and a short snippet. This snippet will include content up to the Read More separator you’ve added for your blog post.
    • Full post: the email will include the entire blog post.
  • Enter the max number of articles to display.
  • Click Advanced settings to set the width of your featured images and your blog content’s padding.
Edit inbox content

Edit the email’s subject line and preview text. You can also specify the name, and address the email will display as the sender, as well as the address that’ll receive any replies.

  • In the email editor, click the inbox content module at the top of the page.

  • In the sidebar editor, enter a subject line for the email in the Subject line field. To add personalization tokens, click Personalize. Learn more about personalizing email subject lines.

  • In the Preview text field, enter a summary of the email that’ll display in some email clients.

  • Click the From name dropdown menu and select a sender.

  • Click the From address dropdown menu and select an email address that’ll display as the sender’s email.

  • By default, email replies will go to the email set as the from address. To send replies to a different email address, clear the Use as reply-to address checkbox and then select a new reply-to address.

Schedule and publish
  • In the email editor, click the Schedule icon in the left sidebar.
  • The available scheduling options will depend on the frequency of the blog subscription email.
    • Instant emails will send thirty minutes after a post is published.
    • For daily emails, click the Time dropdown menu and select a time when your email will be sent. This email will send to your subscribers at the selected time each day a new blog post is published.
    • For weekly emails, click the Time dropdown menu and select a time when your email will be sent. Click the Day of the week dropdown menu and select a day when your email will send. This email will send to your subscribers every week on this day and time, as long as new blog content has been published.
    • For monthly emails, click the Time dropdown menu and select a time when your email will be sent. Click the Day of the month dropdown menu and select a day when your email will send. This email will send to your subscribers every month on this day and time, as long as new blog content has been published.
  • When you’ve finished editing your email, click Review and publish in the top right. Confirm the email’s details are correct, then click Publish. In the dialog box, click Publish email.

Please note: blog subscription emails count towards your email send limit.

Edit your blog subscription form

HubSpot blog subscription forms are created automatically after you publish a blog subscription email. If you want your subscribers to opt in to your blog subscription emails through another HubSpot form, add a blog subscription field to your form. The field options you select should match the frequencies in your blog subscription settings.

Please note: a blog subscription form will only appear on your live website if it is associated with a published blog subscription email.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • By default, each blog subscription form will be named Subscribe to [Blog name] Notifications. Hover over your blog subscription form and click Edit.
  • In the form editor, click the Notification Frequency field on the right.
  • In the left sidebar menu, in the Field options section, click Add options to add subscription options to the form field.
  • In the dialog box, select your live email frequencies and click Add. To delete an existing option, hover over it and click Remove.
  • If there’s only one option, you can hide this field, and pre-select that option. This will prevent visitors from having to select a value for this field.
  • In the top right, click Publish to update the form.

Set up self-registration for private blog content

With self-registration turned on, blog visitors can register to view private blog posts. The first time visitors view your blog, they will only be able to read private blog posts up to the read more separator. Learn more about customizing registration page templates.

Before you get started

Before you set up self-registration for private blog content, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Website settings permission is required to set up self-registration in Private content and Blog settings.
  • Edit, Publish, and Manage private content permission is required to edit and publish blog posts.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Emails sent to visitors after they have self-registered aren’t customizable.
  • Turning on Give anyone access to the entire blog but only members access to full posts setting gives you the choice of setting blog posts to use self-registration. You’ll still need to set blog posts to use self-registration.

Set up self-registration

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Private Content.

  • Click the Choose a domain to edit dropdown menu and select the domain your private content is hosted on.

  • In the Sign-in Options section, select the Enable self-registration checkbox.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.

  • In the Current View section, click the first dropdown menu and select a blog. In accounts with the Brands add-on, this will be the second dropdown menu.

  • In the Access Control section, select Public, then select the Give anyone access to the entire blog but only members access to full posts checkbox.

  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Set up self-registration for blog posts

After you’ve set up self-registration, set whether each blog post will require visitors to register to view it. Self-registration can be set individually or in bulk.

Individual blog posts

Self-registration can be turned on for individual blog posts in the content editor.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.

  • Click the name of a post.

  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.

  • In the dialog box, select Access control on the left menu.

  • In the Access Control section, select Self-registration required.

  • To allow search engines to crawl the private content, select the SEO crawling checkbox. If SEO crawling isn’t selected, search engines will only be able to crawl the content before the read more separator.

  • Click X to close the Settings dialog box.

  • To preview how the post will appear to visitors who aren’t signed in:

    • Click Preview in the top right.
    • Click the Preview as dropdown menu and select Visitor (not signed in).
    • When finished previewing, click Back to go back to the content editor.

  • When finished, click Publish or Update in the top right.

Multiple blog posts

Self-registration can be turned on for multiple blog posts at once from the blog post index page.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Select the checkbox next to each blog post.
  • At the top of the table, click the More dropdown menu and select Control audience access.
  • In the right panel, select Self-registration required, then click Save.

Find contacts who have self-registered

Find contacts who have self-registered by filtering for a known Registered at contact property and an unknown Time registration email was sent contact property.

To learn more about finding contacts who have self-registered:

  • Contact properties associated with private content
  • View and filter records

Use a featured image on a page or blog post

Featured images appear as thumbnails when pages or blog posts are shared on social media. A featured image may be set on individual pages or posts and displayed on the blog listing page.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Edit and Publish permission is required to edit and publish blog posts and pages.
  • Website settings permission is required to edit blog settings.

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to generate a featured image with HubSpot’s AI. Learn more about generating images with AI.

Add a featured image

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the name of your content.
  • In the content editor, click Settings on the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select Featured image in the left menu.
  • Toggle the Enabled featured image switch on. If an image appears in your blog post before the read more separator, HubSpot will automatically assign that image as the featured image.
  • To select a different image, click an option:
    • Browse images: select an image from the files tool,
    • Upload: use an image from your computer.
    • Generate with AI: generate an image using Breeze.
    • If your image is shown as an option, but doesn’t have the Featured label, click the image to select it as the featured image.
  • In the Image alt text field, enter a description of the image for search engines and screen readers to use.
  • In the dialog box, click X to go back to the content editor.
  • When finished, click Publish or Update in the top right.

Display featured images on a blog listing page

A blog’s featured images may be displayed on the blog listing page. When configured in the blog settings, the image appears with each post in the blog listing listing template.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.
  • In the Content View section, click the first dropdown menu and select a blog.
  • Click the Templates tab.
  • In the Blog Listing Page section, select the Use featured image in listing summaries checkbox.
  • In the bottom left, click Save.

Use Accelerated Mobile Pages (AMP) in a blog

AMP, or Accelerated Mobile Pages, is a mobile-specific page format that loads almost instantly on mobile devices. To load the content quickly, the AMP version of your blog posts won’t load any JavaScript files, stylesheets, HubSpot forms, head HTML, or footer HTML.

Before you get started

Before you use AMP for your blog, review these requirements and considerations.

Permissions required The following permissions are required depending on where you apply AMP to your blog.

  • Website settings permission is required to apply AMP across all posts on a blog.
  • Edit and Publish permission is required to apply AMP to individual blog posts.

Understand limitations & considerations

  • AMP isn’t available for HubSpot landing pages or website pages.
  • Featured images on blog posts with AMP turned on should be at least 1200 pixels wide.
  • Views of content with AMP turned on will not be tracked on a contact’s timeline because AMP blocks the JavaScript included in the HubSpot tracking code.
  • You can turn on AMP for all posts on a blog or only for specific posts.

Apply AMP across all posts on a blog

Use this option to turn on AMP for all existing and future blog posts. This approach is best if you want AMP applied consistently across your blog without managing it post by post.

Please note: if you want to turn on AMP for multiple HubSpot-hosted blogs, you will need to repeat these steps for each blog.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Blog.

  • If you have multiple blogs, click the Current view dropdown menu and select a blog.

  • Click the Google AMP tab.

  • Toggle the Turn on Google AMP formatted pages switch on.

  • Customize the logo, font, and font color of your Google AMP pages. Learn more about Google’s recommendations for this content.

  • When finished, click Save.

HubSpot will validate each blog post for your blog template. The next time Google crawls the blog post, they will cache the AMP version. If there are errors with the AMP version, Google will send you an email directly to let you know.

Apply AMP to an individual blog post

Use this option if you only want AMP turned on for individual blog posts. This is helpful if you’re testing AMP or only need it for specific content.

Please note: this option is only available if AMP is not turned on in your blog settings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click on the name of your post.
  • In the content editor, click Publish in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select the Enable Google AMP just for this blog post checkbox, then click Publish.

HubSpot will now validate this specific blog post. The next time Google crawls the blog post, they will cache the AMP version. If there are errors with the AMP version, Google will send you an email directly to let you know.

Troubleshoot AMP issues

If Google Search Console reports issues with your AMP pages, HubSpot recommends checking the AMP validator. This tool gives descriptive error messages and will find the error’s location.

  • In your browser, open the AMP validator, then open a new tab to access HubSpot.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.

  • Click on the name of your post.

  • Click the File menu and select Blog settings.

  • In the Post URL section, click Copy link.

  • In the AMP validator, paste the URL of the blog post in the URL field.

  • At the end of the URL, enter ?hs_amp=true, then click Validate.

  • Once you’ve validated your URL, any AMP errors will appear below the HTML. AMP errors may include:

    • The attribute ‘style’ doesn’t appear in <div> tag: this is frequently caused by a Wistia embed code, which is not yet supported in AMP pages.
    • The <script> tag is disallowed except in specific forms: this is frequently caused by a Wistia embed code, which is not yet supported in AMP pages.
    • The ‘style’ attribute doesn’t appear in the <span> tag: this is frequently caused by a Wistia embed code, which is not yet supported in AMP pages.
    • Malformed URL ‘…’ for attribute ‘href’ in <a> tag: a link URL in the post body is formatted incorrectly.
    • Invalid URL protocol ‘…’ for attribute ‘href’ in <a> tag: a link URL in the post body is formatted incorrectly.
    • Images should be at least 1200 pixels wide for AMP: your blog post doesn’t have a featured image that is at least 1200 pixels wide.

Content: Design Manager

Add an RSS feed to a page or post template

Add a feed of your HubSpot-hosted or external blog posts to your website with the RSS Listing module. Use this module on a page or post template in the layout editor within the design manager.

Before you get started

Before you add an RSS feed to a page or post template, review the following requirements and considerations.

Permissions required Design tools permission is required to add the RSS Listing module to a page or post template in the design manager.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • The RSS Listing module can be added to pages or posts that are using a drag and drop template in the design manager.
  • If you’re using a template that includes editable drag and drop areas, the RSS Listing module may be available in the content editor. Learn more about adding modules in the content editor.
  • External RSS feeds don’t display featured images in the RSS Listing module.
  • Changes made to a template affect all pages or posts using that template.

Add an RSS Listing module to a template

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • In the finder, click the name of the template.

  • In the inspector, click + Add on the top right.

  • In the Search field, enter the text ‘rss listing’. Drag the RSS Listing module to your template in the layout editor, then drop it into position.

  • In the layout editor, click the module to open it in the inspector and then navigate to the Default Content section on the right.

  • In the RSS module header field, enter the text that’ll appear above the RSS feed.

  • In the Add an RSS Feed section, select an option:

    • Use an external RSS feed: enter the feed URL in the RSS URL field.
    • Use a HubSpot-hosted blog: click the Blog dropdown menu and select a blog. To only show posts using a specific blog tag, click the Filter by tag dropdown menu and select a tag.

  • To change the number of posts displayed, click the Maximum number of posts to display field and enter a number. By default, the RSS Listing module will display five posts.

  • To configure the feeds author name, summary, and publish date options, select the relevant checkboxes (e.g., Show author name). Clear the checkboxes to hide the options from the RSS feed.

  • Click Publish changes to take your changes live.

Example: RSS Listing module

The following example is an RSS feed displaying a post’s title and publish date.

Add default content to template modules

Add default content to template modules to create a starting point for pages, posts, emails or other assets that use the template. Default content appears automatically when a module is first added in the content editor.

Default content can also be locked at the template level to prevent edits in the content editor.

Permissions required Design tools permission is required to add default content to template modules.

Understand limitations & considerations

  • Once a module’s content is edited in the content editor, updates to default content in the design manager don’t replace the edited version of that module.

Add default content to a module

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Email: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click on the name of your content.

  • For blog posts and pages:

    • In the content editor, click the Settings menu, then select Template.

    • In the dialog box, click Edit this template.

  • For marketing emails using the classic editor:

    • In the left sidebar, click the Template design icon.
    • Click the Actions dropdown menu and select Edit this template.

  • In the design manager, click the module in the layout editor.

  • In the inspector, locate the Default content section. Available fields vary depending on the module type.

  • To prevent the module’s default content from being edited in the content editor, scroll down to the Editor options section in the inspector and click to toggle the Prevent editing in content editors switch on.

  • To preview your default content within the template, click the Preview dropdown menu and select Live preview with display options in the top right.

  • When finished, click Publish changes in the top right to take your changes live.

Add media from Media Bridge apps to HubSpot content

Add external, provider-specific media to your HubSpot content by creating a custom module that uses the data from a Media Bridge app. Media Bridge apps supply the media data, while the custom module controls how that media is rendered on your pages.

After adding media to your pages, analyze how visitors interact with it using timeline events and custom reports.

Before you get started

Before adding media from Media Bridge apps and a custom module, review the following requirements and setup steps.

Understand requirements
  • A Media Bridge app must be installed or built in your HubSpot account.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Design tools permission is required to create a custom module and customize page or post templates in the design manager.
  • App marketplace access permission is required to install pre-built Media Bridge apps.
  • Edit and publish permission is required to edit and publish content in the content editor.
Set up a Media Bridge app

Choose one of the following options to connect a Media Bridge app:

  • If you’re a developer or have developer resources, use the Media Bridge API to build a Media Bridge app.
  • Install pre-built Media Bridge apps on the HubSpot App Marketplace. Learn more about connecting apps in HubSpot.

Please note: installing or building a Media Bridge app is required, but does not add media to your content. To display Media Bridge content, you must create a custom module that uses the app’s data.

Create a custom module for Media Bridge content

After the Media Bridge app has been installed, create a custom module to display the Media Bridge content on a page or template.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • Create a new module.

  • In the inspector, click the Add field dropdown menu in the Fields section, then select the Embed field.

  • In the Supported source types section, select the Media integration checkbox.

  • In the Embed Type section, select Media integration.

  • Click the Select a provider dropdown menu and select your connected app. If you only have one pre-built Media Bridge app installed, you may see that specific provider (e.g., Select from Wistia).

  • Click the module icon in the top left.

  • In the inspector, hover over the field, click the Actions dropdown menu, and select Copy snippet. Paste the contents in the module.html section.

  • Click Publish changes.

Add the module to content

To add the module, choose one of the following options:

  • Add the module to templates using the layout editor in the design manager.
  • Add the module to pages or posts using the drag and drop area in the content editor. If you choose this option, in the content editor, enter the URL in the Media URL field to add your media to the page.

Analyze media events

After you publish your pages or posts that include the Media Bridge content, analyze how visitors interact with your media.

Media events track interactions such as playing embedded media and appear as timeline events. You can also use custom reports to analyze engagement across pages.

To learn more about analyzing engagement, review how to analyze video views on your pages.

Build a custom coded template

Developers can build blog, website page, landing page, and email templates from scratch using HTML + HubL. You can also clone a drag and drop template layout to HTML, then customize it as a coded template.

Learn more about designing custom assets in our developer documentation.

Permissions required Design tools permission is required for creating and editing templates in the design manager.

Permissions required Global content and theme settings and Website Settings permission is required to edit global website assets and blog or website settings.

Create a new HTML + HubL file

Subscription required Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to build custom email templates. Accounts with Content Hub can create emails using the drag and drop email editor.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • At the top of the finder, click the File dropdown menu and select New file.

  • In the dialog box, click the What would you like to build today? dropdown menu and select HTML + HubL.

  • In the What are you building? field, select an option:

    • Template: defines the layout and the structure of the content that will be displayed on the website pages, landing pages, blog posts, or email.
    • Template Partial: is reusable code or a snippet of code that can be included in multiple other templates.

  • Click the Template type dropdown menu and select a type for the custom coded template (page, blog post/listing, email, or system page). Learn more about template types.

  • Enter a file name in the File name field.

  • To update the file’s location, click Change in the File location section and select a folder.

  • When finished, click Create.

Add HTML + HubL to your template

After you have configured your new file, you’ll be directed to the code editor to add your custom code and preview how it’ll appear on a live page.

Add HTML + HubL
  • Enter the HTML for the template. Learn more about adding CSS and JavaScript files to custom coded templates.
  • To display how the HTML + HubL will render, toggle the Show output switch on on the top left. A panel will open on the right with the rendered preview.
Add required HTML + HubL

Custom coded templates require specific HTML or HubL variables to function. If any of these required variables are missing, an error message may appear when you try to publish the template.

  • Page and blog templates require the following variables:

` <!– Enter above the closing </header> tag

{{ standard_header_includes }}

<!– Enter above the closing </body> tag

{{ standard_footer_includes }}`

  • Email templates require the following variables to be CAN-SPAM compliant:

` <!– Enter variables above the closing </body> tag

{{ site_settings.company_name }}

{{ site_settings.company_street_address_1 }}

{{ site_settings.company_city }}

{{ site_settings.company_state }}

{{ site_settings.company_zip }}

{{ site_settings.company_country }}

<!– Choose one unsubscribe variable

{{ unsubscribe_link }}

{{ unsubscribe_link_all }}`

  • Email templates require the following code to display preview text in certain email clients:

`<!– Preview text (text which appears right after subject in certain email clients)

<div id=“preview_text” style=“display:none!important”>{% text “preview_text” label=“Preview Text <span class=help-text>This will be used as the preview text that displays in some email clients</span>”, value=““, no_wrapper=True %}

</div>`

Clone a template to HTML

In addition to creating templates from scratch, you can also clone drag and drop templates for blogs, website pages, and landing pages to HTML.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.
  • In the finder, click the name of template you want to clone.
  • Click the Actions dropdown menu and select Clone to HTML. The HTML file will be created in the same folder as the original file.

Preview and publish your template

Once you’ve created your template, you can preview how it’ll appear on a live page, then publish it.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • In the finder, click the name of template you want to preview or publish.

  • In the top right, click the Preview dropdown menu and select an option:

    • If you select Live preview with display options, you can preview your template as it appears on other devices by selecting the Viewport preset.
    • If you select Preview without display options, you can only preview how your template will appear on browsers.

  • When finished, click Publish changes.

  • If there are any code errors, an error message will appear. Review more information about these errors in the error console below the code editor:

    • In the error message at the top of the page, click error console to open the console below the code editor.
    • Alternatively, navigate to the bottom left of the code editor and click Show details.

Copy design manager assets to another HubSpot account

If you have access to multiple HubSpot accounts, you can copy templates, coded files, folders, and themes from one account to another from within the design manager.

Free templates, themes, and modules can be freely copied to multiple accounts. Themes and modules purchased from the HubSpot Marketplace can only be present in a single account at a time.

Before you get started

Before you begin copying assets, review these requirements and considerations.

Understand requirements
  • Your user account must use the same email address in both HubSpot accounts to copy assets between them.
  • When copying assets with external dependencies such as linked stylesheets and global groups, it’s recommended to move all assets into one folder, then copy the folder.
  • It’s recommended that a Super Admin or the person who made the original purchase contact support to transfer a purchased template or module to another account.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Any assets outside of the folder being copied won’t be copied across accounts. This includes any attached CSS/JS files, global groups, custom modules, etc.
  • Image files won’t be moved to the destination account— they will only be linked to in order to maintain the same file URL, which originates from the source account.
  • Copying a template doesn’t copy content created with that template.
  • Theme folders in the @hubspot or @marketplace directories can’t be copied between accounts.
  • You can’t copy individual assets within a theme folder across accounts. You’ll either need to copy the entire theme folder, or clone the asset and move it out of the theme folder before copying.
  • A module can only be copied to an account once. If you need to copy a module multiple times, it’s recommended to clone the module first.
  • Purchased assets can only be transferred to a new account, not copied. Transferred assets won’t stay in the original account.

Copy a free template, theme, or module

Copy templates, themes, or modules that weren’t purchased from the HubSpot Marketplace to additional HubSpot accounts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • In the finder, click the asset, then click the File dropdown menu, and select Copy to different account. You can also right-click the asset and select Copy to different account.

  • In the dialog box, click the Destination account dropdown menu and select an account, then click Copy assets.

  • The copy will begin processing, and you’ll see a confirmation once that process has completed.

If you encounter an external dependency error, ensure that all linked files, global groups, and custom modules are included in the folder.

Transfer a purchased theme or module

With the help of HubSpot Support, you can transfer a module or theme purchased from the HubSpot Marketplace to another account. Transferred assets won’t stay in the original account.

The transfer grants access to the purchased theme; it doesn’t move or recreate pages or page content that used the theme.

  • Verify that the asset isn’t used in any draft or live content in your account.
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketplace Downloads.
  • Click the Modules tab or stay on the Themes tab.
  • To the right of the theme or module, click the Actions dropdown menu and select Uninstall.
  • In the dialog box, select Uninstall.
  • Contact HubSpot Support and request that the theme or module be transferred to an account.

Create and add a JavaScript file to HubSpot

Create and add JavaScript files in the Design Manager to customize the functionality of your HubSpot-hosted content. Create a JavaScript file, attach it to a template, or add it across an entire domain or on individual pages.

For example, use a JavaScript file to add interactive elements, integrate third-party scripts, or customize page behavior beyond standard modules.

Before you get started

Before working with JavaScript files, review the following requirements and considerations.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Design tools permission is required to create and edit JavaScript files in the Design Manager.
  • Website settings permission is required to add JavaScript files to a domain.
  • Edit and publish permission is required to add JavaScript files to an individual page.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Publishing changes makes updates live immediately on associated templates or pages.
  • Adding JavaScript at the domain level applies the script to all HubSpot-hosted pages on that domain.

Create a JavaScript file

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • In the finder, click the File dropdown menu and select New file.

  • In the dialog box, click the What would you like to build today? dropdown menu and select JavaScript. Then click Next.

  • In the File name field, enter a name for your JavaScript file.

  • To update the file’s location, in the File location section, click Change and select the folder to add the file to.

  • Click Create.

  • Enter your JavaScript into the code editor.

  • If you’ve enabled ESLint, view any JavaScript warnings or errors by toggling the Show output switch on.

  • When finished, click Publish changes in the top right.

Attach a JavaScript file to a drag and drop template

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.
  • In the finder, click the template you want to update.
  • In the inspector on the right, click the Edit tab.
  • In the Linked JavaScript files section, click the Add dropdown menu and select your JavaScript file.
  • When finished, click Publish changes in the top right.

Attach a JavaScript file to a coded template

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.
  • In the finder, click the template you want to update.
  • In the code editor, enter the require_js HubL function. Learn more about using the require_js HubL function.

Add a JavaScript file to HubSpot pages

Add a JavaScript file on all pages of a HubSpot-hosted domain, or on individual pages by using the public URL.

Access a JavaScript file’s public URL
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.
  • In the finder, click the name of the JavaScript file. Then click the Actions dropdown menu and select Copy public URL.
Add a JavaScript file to all pages on a domain
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Pages.
  • Click the Choose a domain to edit its settings dropdown menu and select the domain to add the JavaScript file to. To apply the JavaScript file to all connected domains, select Default settings for all domains.
  • In the Site footer HTML section, paste the public URL as the value for the script tag’s source:

&lt;!-- start example.js Do Not Remove

&lt;script src='insert your file's public URL here'>&lt;/script>

&lt;!---End example.js

  • When finished, click Save on the bottom left.
Add a JavaScript file to an individual page

Please note: advanced settings are not available in starter templates.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click the Settings menu and select Advanced.
  • In the Footer HTML section of the dialog box, paste the public URL as the value for the script tag’s source:

&lt;!-- start example.js Do Not Remove

&lt;script src='insert your file's public URL here'>&lt;/script>

&lt;!---End example.js

  • When finished, click Publish or Update in the top right.

Create and edit modules in the design manager

Create custom modules in the design manager to add advanced features to your blog, pages, or emails. Custom modules offer a wide range of functionalities so that content can be fully customized within the page, email, or blog editor.

Before you get started

Before you begin creating or editing custom modules in the design manager, review the requirements and considerations.

Permissions required Design tools permission is required to create and edit modules in the design manager.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • if you’re unfamiliar with HTML, HubL, and CSS, it is recommended to work with a developer to create modules in the design manager.

Create a module

Subscription required Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to create a module for emails.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • At the top of the finder, click the File dropdown menu and select New file.

  • In the dialog box, click the What would you like to build today? dropdown menu and select Module.

  • Click Next.

  • In the Where would you like to use this module field, select the checkbox next to each type of content where your module will be used (e.g., Blog posts, Emails, or Landing pages).

  • In the Module content scope field, select an option (e.g., Local module or Global module). If you create a global module, editing this module’s content will update every location where the module is used.

  • Enter a file name for the module.

  • To change the module’s file location, click Change in the File location section. In the pop-up box, select a new location and then click Select.

  • When finished, click Create.

  • Continue editing the module.

Please note: modules used in emails don’t include CSS or JavaScript.

Edit a module

After creating a module in the design manager, you can customize its functionality and appearance. Label the module for clarity, add and configure fields, and adjust field editor options such as default content. Set display conditions and repeater options, and group the related fields for better organization. You can also copy and paste field snippets, write custom module syntax, add helpful instructional text, and edit which template types your module can be used with.

Add a label to a module

In the design manager, add or update a label for a module to help users find it in the content editor. If the label is blank, the module’s name will be shown by default.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.
  • In the finder, click to open a module you’d like to edit the label for.
  • In the inspector, enter a label.
Add fields to a module

Add fields to a module to set the module’s content or styling and make it editable in the content editor. Learn more about available field types.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • In the finder, click to open a module.

  • In the inspector, in the Fields section, click the Add field dropdown menu. Then select a field to add to the module.

  • To edit the name of the field click the edit edit icon and enter a new name. To edit the HubL variable name, enter a new name in the HubL variable name field.

Customize field default content

In the Content Options section, add default content that appears when the module is used in templates and content editors. The options for default content will differ depending on the field type.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.
  • In the finder, click to open a module.
  • In the inspector, in the Fields section, hover over a field and click Edit.
  • In the Content options section, add or edit default content options. The available default content options will depend on the field type selected.

For example, by adding a Date and time field type to a module, you can select a default date and time. You can also enter a default time interval.

Set field editor options
