Your topic’s pillar page and subtopic content can be HubSpot-hosted pages or blog posts, or URLs of pages hosted outside of HubSpot.

Add the first topic

When you’re ready to create your first topic, you can do so in the SEO tool. Learn more about choosing a relevant topic.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SEO directly.
  • Click the Topic Clusters tab.
  • Click Research Topics.
  • In the Enter a topic field, enter a topic.
  • In the bottom right, click Done.

Create a new topic

For topics created after your first one, you’ll be able to view the popularity of the topic phrase and how difficult it’ll be to rank for this phrase in Google search results before completing topic creation:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SEO directly.

  • Click the Topic Clusters tab.

  • In the top right, click Add a topic.

  • Enter a topic in the field, then click Add to analyze SEO metrics for the topic.

    • Review the topic’s Monthly Search Volume and Difficulty validation metrics, which you can compare with the metrics for Recommended Topics.
    • To view topic validation data for a different location, click the Country dropdown menu in the top left and select a country.

  • After researching data for your topic, select the Topic. Then in the bottom left, click Create Topic.

Attach topic content

Once your topic has been created, you can attach your pillar page, a comprehensive resource page that covers the topic in depth. This page links to high-quality content for supporting subtopic keywords.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SEO directly.

  • Click the Topic Clusters tab.

  • Click the name of a topic.

  • In the center of the topic, click Attach content URL.

  • In the right panel, enter text in the Search field for an existing page or post (e.g., URL or name). Then click the content in the results to attach it.

  • To link to external content, click Add external URL. Then enter the URL of your external page or blog post, and click Save. The SEO tool will validate the external link in about 20 seconds.

  • To create a new page or blog post for your topic’s pillar page, click Create a post.

    • In the dialog box, click the Content type dropdown menu to select the content type (e.g., Blog Post, Landing Page, or Site Page).
    • Enter a title for your new page or post, then click Create to attach the new drafted content.

  • To attach existing content that contains phrases related to your topic, click a piece of content in the Suggested Content section, and then click Save.

Add subtopic keywords and supporting content

After you’ve attached a pillar page to your topic, you’ll attach supporting content based on subtopic keywords. Subtopic content should include a link back to the topic’s pillar page to establish your website’s authority for your topic and subtopic keywords in search engine results.

Please note:

  • Each topic can have up to 100 subtopic keywords.

  • After adding 20 subtopic keywords, new subtopic keywords must be added in the Content Performance view.

  • Internal links from HubSpot-hosted content to your pillar page won’t validate immediately. You can check internal links in the SEO tool at a later time and in the optimize panel in the content editor.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SEO directly.

  • Click the Topic Clusters tab.

  • Click the name of a topic.

  • In the top right, click Add subtopic keyword.

  • In the right panel, enter a subtopic keyword, then click Research subtopic keywords. You’ll see metrics for the average monthly searches for the subtopic keyword, along with a listing of similar subtopic keywords.

  • Select your subtopic keyword, then click Save.

  • After the subtopic keyword is created, you’ll be directed to attach the subtopic content. Learn more about attaching content to a topic or subtopic.

Please note: you can only attach one piece of content to each topic or subtopic keyword. If you have two pages that cover to the same subtopic keywords, they’ll both rank lower in search results. For best results, combine similar content or define a unique subtopic keyword to write about for one of your duplicate pages.

Manage subtopic keyword content

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SEO directly.
  • Click the Topic Clusters tab.
  • Click the name of a topic.
  • To edit the attached subtopic content, click a subtopic keyword.
    • In the right panel, in the Subtopic content section, click Remove Attached Content.
    • Select a new piece of content to attach.
    • When finished, click the X icon to close the right panel.
  • To delete a subtopic keyword, click a subtopic keyword, then click Delete Topic in the right panel.

Language settings for the SEO tool

The SEO tool in HubSpot is available in multiple languages, where you can organize, analyze, and optimize content. Language support varies by feature and interface element, including the SEO tool overall, topics/subtopic keywords, topic validation data, and subtopic keyword suggestions.

SEO tool

The SEO tool—including navigation, labels, instructions, and help text—is available in all languages supported by HubSpot. To change the SEO tool language, learn more about managing your user profile or account defaults.

Topics and subtopic keywords

Topics and subtopic keywords are available in any supported language. If your content is in a language not available for HubSpot, you can still add topics and keywords in the desired language for organization and reporting. Learn more about adding topics and keywords.

Topic validation data

Topic validation and keyword performance data rely on search engine results, which can differ by location. For the most exact data on monthly search volume and domain authority, set the correct location for the topic cluster.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SEO directly.
  • Click the Topic Clusters tab.
  • On the Topics page, click the name of a topic.
  • In the top left, click the Country dropdown menu and select an option (e.g., United States).

You can see locations available for monthly search volume and subtopic keyword suggestions from SEMrush databases.

Subtopic suggestions

Currently, the machine learning models for subtopic keyword suggestions are based in English. Some other subtopic keyword suggestions are provided according to the locales available from SEMrush.

Manage AEO settings

After setting up AEO, update your brand details, domains, competitors, ICPs, products, prompt groups, and answer engines in your AEO settings. These settings determine which mentions AEO counts as your brand, which domains AEO identifies as owned, which companies your visibility is compared against, which audiences and products AEO analyzes, how prompts are organized, and which answer engines are tracked.

Review these settings as your business changes so your dashboard data reflects your current brand, competitors, and the answer engines your audience uses. To track a distinct brand, learn how to manage multiple brands and domains. To review visibility results after updating your settings, learn how to analyze the AEO dashboard.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Edit brand settings

Answer engines refer to brands in different ways, such as with abbreviations, spacing differences, or former names. AEO only counts a mention when it matches a brand name variation, and variations are case-sensitive. Add each variation of your brand name so those mentions are included in your brand visibility and share of voice reports.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Settings icon.
  • On the Brand settings tab, enter your brand name variations in the Brand name variation field. Separate each variation with a comma (e.g., AcmeCo, Acme Co). Brand name variations are case-sensitive, so enter each variation exactly as it appears.
  • Click Save.

Manage multiple brands and domains

Add additional root domains that belong to the same brand to a single AEO setup, or use separate AEO setups to track unique brands. AEO uses the domains you add to identify owned citations in answer engine responses and displays the results on the AEO dashboard.

For example, if your primary domain is mydomain.com, you can add mydomain.org or mydomain.edu as additional domains for the same brand. To track a distinct brand, set up a separate brand in your account.

Add root domains for the same brand

To add another root domain to an existing brand:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Settings icon.
  • On the Brand settings tab, enter the additional domains in the Add additional domains to your brand section.
  • When finished, click Save.
Track multiple brands

Each unique brand requires its own AEO setup. To organize and track multiple brands, use one of the following approaches:

  • Use the Brands add-on to set up separate brands within your account to track each brand independently.
  • Use a separate standalone HubSpot AEO subscription for each brand.

Prompt groups can help organize prompts within an AEO dashboard, but they don’t create separate dashboards or recommendations for each brand.

Manage competitors

Competitors set the benchmark for your brand visibility, share of voice, and citation reports. Add the companies you compete with and remove those you no longer compete with so these comparisons reflect your market.

Please note: changes to competitors only affect future data runs. To view data without a removed competitor, set the dashboard date range filter to start after the date the change was made.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Settings icon.
  • Click the Competitors tab, then complete the relevant action:
    • To edit a competitor, click the competitor’s name. In the right panel, update the competitor’s details, then click Save.
    • To add a competitor, click Add more competitors at the bottom of the page. In the right panel, enter the competitor details, then click Add competitor.
    • To delete competitors, select the checkboxes next to each competitor, then click Delete [#] selected.

Edit ICPs

Edit your Ideal Customer Profiles (ICPs) to ensure AEO tracks visibility for your current target audiences.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Settings icon.
  • Click the All ICPs tab, then complete the relevant action below.
    • To edit an ICP, click Edit next to the ICP name. Update the details in the right panel, then click Save.
    • To create an ICP, click Create new Ideal Customer Profile. In the right panel, enter the ICP details, then click Save.
    • To delete an ICP, click Delete. In the dialog box, click Delete.

Edit products and services

Keep your tracked products current to ensure AEO generates prompts that reflect your latest offerings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Settings icon.
  • Click the All products and services tab, then complete the relevant action below.
    • To edit a product, click Edit next to the product name. Update the product details in the right panel, then click Save.
    • To add a product, click Add new product or service. Enter the product details in the right panel, then click Save.
    • To delete a product, click Delete. In the dialog box, click Delete.

Manage prompt groups

Organize tracked prompts into groups to analyze visibility by topic, product, or audience segment.

Please note: groups organize prompts within a single AEO dashboard. They don’t create separate dashboards or recommendations for each group.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Settings icon.
  • Click the All groups tab.
  • To create a group, click Create a group. In the dialog box, enter a group name, then click Save.

Turn on premium engines

Turn on premium engines to run tracked prompts across six answer engines. In addition to ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini, premium engines include Claude, Google AI Mode, and Google AI Overviews.

Please note: If you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the AEO Multi-Engine beta.

After turning on premium engines, results from all six engines contribute to your overall brand visibility score. To review your prompt results and manage the prompts tracked for your brand, see Review and manage AEO prompts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • In the upper right, click the Settings icon.
  • Click the Answer engines settings tab.
  • Toggle the Premium pack switch on.

Please note: tracking prompts across six engines uses twice as many answers per prompt as tracking across three engines. Your account must have enough AEO answer capacity before prompts run on premium engines. To add capacity, purchase the AEO Answers Limit Increase Add-on. For pricing details, see the HubSpot Product and Services Catalog.

Understand Google AI Overview results

Google AI Overview behaves differently from the other five engines. Before reviewing your results, note the following:

  • It’s expected that not every tracked prompt returns a Google AI Overview. Google determines when to display an AI Overview, so your visibility is calculated only from prompts that return a result.
  • Each tracked prompt uses answer capacity, even if Google doesn’t return an AI Overview for that prompt.
  • AI Overview results can change quickly. Visibility may change from one day to the next, even when nothing about your brand has changed.
  • AI Overview data is available on the Dashboard tab and the Prompts tab. To exclude it from your results, click the AI Overviews switch off in the upper right.

Prevent content from appearing in search results

Prevent new content from appearing in results by adding the URL slug to a robots.txt file. Search engines use these files to understand how to index a website’s content. Content on HubSpot system domains containing hs-sites is always set as no-index in a robots.txt file.

If search engines have already indexed your content, you can add a “noindex” meta tag to the content’s head HTML. This will tell search engines to stop displaying it in search results.

Please note: only content hosted on a domain connected to HubSpot can be blocked in your robots.txt file. Learn more about customizing file URLs in the files tool.

Use robot.txt files

Add content that hasn’t yet been indexed by search engines to a robots.txt file to prevent it from being shown in search results.

To edit your robots.txt file in HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Pages.
  • Select the domain whose robots.txt file you want to edit:
    • To edit the robots.txt file for all connected domains, click the Choose a domain to edit its settings dropdown menu and select Default settings for all domains (selected by default).
    • To edit the robots.txt file for a specific domain, click the Choose a domain to edit its settings dropdown menu and select the domain. If necessary, click Override default settings. This will override any robots.txt default settings for this domain.
  • Click the SEO & Crawlers tab.
  • In the Robots.txt section, edit the content of the file. There are two parts of a robots.txt file:
    • User-agent: defines the search engine or web bot that a rule applies to. By default, this will be set to include all search engines, which is shown with an asterisk (*), but you can specify specific search engines here. If you’re using HubSpot’s site search module, you will need to include HubSpotContentSearchBot as a separate user-agent. This will allow the search feature to crawl your pages.
    • Disallow: tells a search engine not to crawl and index any files or pages using a specific URL slug. For each page you want to add to the robots.txt file, enter Disallow: /url-slug (e.g., www.hubspot.com/welcome would appear as Disallow: /welcome).
  • When finished, click Save on the bottom left.

Learn more about formatting a robots.txt file in Google’s developer documentation.

Use “noindex” meta tags

If content has already been indexed by search engines, you can add a “noindex” meta tag to instruct search engines to stop indexing it in the future.

Please note: this method should not be combined with the robots.txt method, as this will prevent search engines from seeing the “noindex” tag.

Add “noindex” meta tags to pages and posts

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.

  • Click the name of your content.

  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.

  • In the dialog box, click Advanced on the left sidebar menu.

  • In the Additional code snippets section, enter the following code to the Head HTML field: &lt;meta name="robots" content="noindex">.

  • Click X to close the settings dialog box.

  • To take your changes live, click Update or Publish in the top right.

Add “noindex” meta tags to knowledge base articles

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.

  • Click the name of your content.

  • In the article editor, click Settings in the top right.

  • In the dialog box, click Advanced Options in the left sidebar menu.

  • In the Additional code snippets section, enter the following code to the Head HTML field: &lt;meta name="robots" content="noindex">.

  • Click X to close the settings dialog box.

  • To take your changes live, click Update or Publish in the top right.

Content is still appearing in search results

After adding a noindex tag or updating your robots.txt file, search engines need time to recrawl and deindex your content. If your content continues to appear in search results, confirm the following:

  • Page accessibility: the page must be publicly accessible for search engines to crawl it. Private or password-protected pages won’t be crawled, which prevents the noindex tag from being read.
  • Head HTML: check the Head HTML field in the page settings and the live page source to confirm the noindex tag was saved and is rendering correctly on the page.
  • robots.txt conflicts: review your robots.txt file to confirm no Disallow rules are blocking search engines from accessing the page. If search engines are blocked from crawling the page, they won’t be able to read the noindex tag.

To accelerate deindexing for Google search results, use Google Search Console’s Removals Tool.

Review and manage AEO prompts

After setting up AEO, use prompts to track how your brand appears in answer engine responses for the queries your ideal customers are asking. Prompts represent the questions users ask in answer engines, such as ChatGPT or Perplexity. Monitoring them helps you gauge your brand’s AI visibility, analyze competitors, and identify which content is earning citations.

Prompts are generated using your HubSpot data, audience, and offerings. Update this information in your Brand settings. Add and remove prompts on the Prompts tab.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before working with AEO prompts, review the requirements and considerations.

Understand requirements
  • A Super Admin must toggle the following switches on in AI Settings:
    • Give users access to generative AI tools and features
    • CRM data
    • Customer conversion data
    • Files data
    • Give users access to Breeze Assistant
Understand limitations & considerations
  • To align SEO efforts with AI-driven visibility, review how to set up and analyze AEO and optimize content and improve brand visibility for AI.
  • Data collection begins after setting up AEO and tracking prompts.
  • AEO runs tracked prompts daily. Because responses change over time, review performance across multiple days or weeks before evaluating trends.
  • Prompt usage limits vary by subscription.

Understand the buyer journey phases

Each prompt is assigned to a single buyer journey phase based on its intent. Understanding these phases helps you interpret your visibility data. For example, lower brand mentions are expected at the Awareness stage, where users are exploring broad topics rather than evaluating specific solutions. Use these phases to evaluate where your brand has strong visibility and where gaps exist across the customer journey.

The four Buyer Journey phases are:

  • Awareness: broad, unbranded, problem-based queries where brand mentions are typically lower.
  • Consideration: unbranded queries where users compare available solutions.
  • Evaluation: branded comparisons that explicitly name your company or competitors.
  • Decision: high-intent queries focused on deciding whether a specific product or company meets defined needs or features.

A prompt can only be associated with one Buyer Journey stage. This ensures reporting and visibility metrics are interpreted consistently. Changing the stage isn’t recommended.

Review prompts

Review your tracked prompts to monitor how your brand visibility and competitor presence change over time. Each prompt includes metrics and detailed analysis reports, including competitor visibility, citation sources, and content type breakdowns.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Prompts tab.
  • To filter your prompts, click Filter and select your options (e.g., Engine).
  • At the top of the view, review your prompt metrics including Total prompts, Average visibility, Total responses, and Total citations. To hide metrics, click Hide metrics on the top right.
  • To view details for a specific prompt, click the prompt.
  • In the right panel, click the Prompts Analysis tab and review the following reports:
    • Competitor visibility: how your competitors’ brand visibility compares to yours over time.
    • Prompt visibility rate vs competitors: shows a list of competitors comparing how much of the conversation your brand owns versus competitors.
    • Citations by channel: displays the percentage of channels with the most citations for this tracked prompt.
    • Top citations overall: lists the specific pages most frequently referenced in answer engines for your prompt.
    • Citations by content type: displays the percentage of citations by content type, such as listicles, blogs, documentation, and more.
    • Owned domain citation rate vs competitors: displays the percentage of how often answer engines cite content from your website versus competitor domains for your prompt.
    • Citations with brand mention rate vs competitors: displays the percentage of how often your brand is referenced in citations, regardless of where the cited content originates.

Manage prompts

Manage your prompts to keep AEO tracking aligned with your current products, services, and target audiences. Add new prompts manually, organize them into groups for reporting, or remove prompts that are no longer relevant to your business.

When writing prompts, use the language your target ICP would use in answer engines based on their location. For example, if your ICP is travel agents in Spain, write prompts in Spanish.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Prompts tab.
  • To add a new prompt, click the Add prompts dropdown menu and select Manually add prompts on the top right. In the right panel, enter the prompt details and then click Add prompts.
  • To associate prompts with a group, select the checkbox next to each prompt you want to associate.
    • Click Add or edit group at the top of the table.
    • In the dialog box, click the Group dropdown menu and select a group. To create a new group, click Create new group.
    • When finished, click Save.
  • To export prompts, click Export on the top right. In the dialog box, select your filters and date range and then click Export [#] prompts.
  • To remove prompts, select the checkbox next to each prompt you want to remove and then click Delete. In the dialog box, click Confirm.

Please note: after deleting prompts it can take up to 72 hours for your changes to reflect.

Review and manage AEO recommendations

Use the Recommendations tab in AEO to identify and act on the content opportunities that may improve how often your brand is cited in answer engines.

Recommendations are generated from citation patterns across your tracked prompts, showing which content types and channels answer engines consistently reference for your topics.

After reviewing your recommendations, generate blog posts or social posts from identified gaps. Once completed, AEO tracks changes in brand mentions, visibility scores, and citation patterns over time so you can evaluate impact.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before working with AEO recommendations, review these requirements and considerations.

Understand requirements
  • A Super Admin must toggle the following switches on in AI Settings:
    • Give users access to generative AI tools and features
    • CRM data
    • Customer conversion data
    • Files data
    • Give users access to Breeze Assistant

HubSpot Credits required HubSpot Credits are required to generate content from recommendations. Learn more about how many HubSpot Credits content agent uses in the Product & Services Catalog.

Permissions required Edit and Publish permissions are required to create, edit, and publish blog posts.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • To align SEO efforts with AI-driven visibility, review how to set up an analyze AEO and optimize content and improve brand visibility for AI.
  • Answer engine responses change over time, so improvements may not appear immediately. Review results across multiple analysis cycles to evaluate impact.
  • Completed recommendations remain associated with the prompts they affect.

Understand how recommendations are generated

For each tracked prompt, AEO analyzes answer engine responses and extracts all cited sources. It then identifies patterns across those citations to determine the content and structural signals most commonly linked to a citation.

Pattern analysis includes:

  • Frequently cited domains
  • Common content formats (e.g., blog posts)
  • Recurring themes and keywords
  • Competitor presence

Recommendations are generated directly from these observed patterns and reflect what answer engines consistently reference for your tracked prompts. Each recommendation includes a content type, channel, and priority indicator.

Recommendations are also generated through the site audit, which scans your website directly for content and technical issues from citation pattern analysis.

The following content and channel types may appear in recommendations:

  • Top lists: listicle-style articles that rank or compile products and services.

  • Comparison: articles that evaluate two or more products side-by-side.

  • Product: pages that describe a specific product or service.

  • Blog: blog posts or news-style articles published by a brand or publication.

  • Documentation: technical documentation, help articles, or product guides.

  • Wiki: informational pages within a knowledge base or glossary.

  • News: articles published by journalists or editorial outlets.

  • PR: press releases issued by companies.

  • Research: research reports, studies, or data analysis.

  • User reviews: reviews published by users on third-party platforms (e.g., G2 or Trustpilot).

  • Social: posts published on social media platforms.

  • Owned: content published on your own website.

  • Competitor: content from competitor domains configured in your AEO settings.

  • Earned: coverage from third-party sites, such as news outlets or industry blogs.

  • Peer: content from companies in your industry that aren’t tracked as competitors (e.g., adjacent tools or services).

  • User-generated content (UGC): content created by individual users on platforms such as Reddit.

  • Affiliate: content published on sites that feature sponsored or paid placements.

  • Social: content published on social media platforms (e.g., LinkedIn).

Review and manage recommendations

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Recommendations tab.
  • Recommendations are organized in tabs at the top of the page. By default, all recommendations are displayed. To filter the recommendations, click the recommendation type:
    • All recommendations: view all available recommendations.
    • Site audit: scan your pages and review content and technical issues that may be affecting your brand’s visibility in answer engines. Learn more about running and reviewing site audit recommendations.
    • Owned content: create or update content on your own website.
    • Social amplification: engage with relevant Reddit threads and create LinkedIn or YouTube content based on citation trends.
    • Outreach: identify third-party publishers and sites where you can reach out to be included in their content.
  • To add more filters, click the filter dropdown menu (e.g., Priority) at the top of the table and select your options (e.g., Medium).
  • In the recommendation table, review the following columns:
    • Content type: the type of content recommended (e.g., Video or Listicle).
    • Channel type: where the recommended content is applicable (e.g., Blog or YouTube).
    • Recommendation type: the type of recommendation (e.g., Net new content or Update content).
    • Priority: the relative impact of the recommendation based on citation signal strength (e.g., High).
    • Status: the current progress of the recommendation (e.g., Not started or Done).
    • Citation lift: the projected increase in your citation rate if you act on the recommendation. Use this value to compare recommendations and prioritize the ones most likely to improve your AI visibility.
    • Assignee: the user responsible for completing the recommendation.
  • To view more details for a recommended action, click the title of the recommendation.
    • In the right panel, view the recommendation details:
      • Suggested content: the suggested content to create. This includes the title, summary, target audience, and suggested keywords to use.
      • What’s driving this recommendation: the analysis that was completed on your citations for tracked prompts. This includes associated prompts, content type distribution, and top citations identified.
    • To change the status of a recommendation, click the Change status dropdown menu and select a status (e.g., Mark as In Progress).
    • When finished, click X in the top right to close the recommendation details.
  • To change the status or assignee of multiple recommendations, select the checkbox next to each recommendation in the table. Then click the Change status or Change assignee dropdown menu and select a status (e.g., Dismiss) or assignee.

Run and review site audit recommendations

Run a site audit to analyze your pages and review the content and technical issues likely to reduce your brand’s visibility in answer engines. Results will display in recommendations on the Site audit tab.

Recommendations in site audits are organized into two types:

  • Content: scans your pages against tracked prompts to flag AEO best practice issues (e.g., missing titles). Then the results display a prioritized list of recommendations mapped to specific pages.
  • Technical: scans your pages for structural and metadata issues, including structured data markup, canonical tags, page speed signals, and crawlability. Then the results display a prioritized list of recommendations ranked by estimated impact on your brand’s visibility in answer engines.

To run and review site audit recommendations:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Recommendations tab.
  • At the top of the page, click the Site audit tab.
  • Click the domain dropdown menu and select a domain to audit.
    • To scan your pages for content issues, click Run content audit.
    • To scan your pages for technical issues, click Run technical audit.
  • Review the recommendations in the table. To view and individual recommendation, click the name in the Site audit column.
    • In the right panel, review the affected pages on the Recommendation tab.
    • Click the Impact tab to track how often the page is referenced by answer engines. To track the page, click Track URL. In the dialog box, enter the URL and Start date, then click Track.
  • To rescan your pages, click Rescan now on the upper right.

Generate blog posts from recommendations

After reviewing new content recommendations for your blog, generate blog posts to turn identified content gaps into drafted blog content aligned with your brand. Once generated, review and refine the post in the blog editor, or copy the generated content into your external blog.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Recommendations tab.
  • At the top of the page, click the Owned content tab.
  • In the Title column, Click Generate blog post for a recommendation.
  • If you haven’t set up your brand voice, in the dialog box, click Add writing samples. Then, upload a file or paste a writing sample that uses your brand voice. Learn how to set up brand voice.
  • Click the Blog dropdown menu and select the blog where the blog post should be created.
  • Click Generate blog post.
  • After the content is generated, click Open in editor to customize the blog post or click Open in Breeze Assistant. If your blog is hosted outside of HubSpot, click the copy icon to copy the generated content to your external blog.
Understand how blog posts are generated

After you click Generate blog post, HubSpot’s AI processes your request in several phases. Generation may take a few minutes, and you’ll receive an in-app notification and email when the draft is ready.

  • Research: HubSpot’s AI gathers the following inputs to generate the draft.
    • Brand voice, ideal customer profiles (ICPs), and product details from your brand identity data.
    • Existing blog post titles to prevent duplicate topics.
    • AEO recommendation history to build on previously accepted recommendations while excluding dismissed recommendations.
    • Keyword volume and difficulty data.
    • Web pages that reference your brand, identified through web search.
    • Competitor positioning and audience profiles, identified through web search.
    • The selected recommendation’s topic, format, audience, and goals.
  • Generate: HubSpot’s AI drafts the blog post.
    • Defines the article structure and format (e.g., listicle, comparison, how-to, or guide).
    • Generates the title, body content, and meta description.
    • Incorporates keywords, answer-first sections, FAQ coverage, and relevant brand references.
  • Refine: HubSpot’s AI improves the draft in two steps.
    • Aligns the content’s tone, vocabulary, and sentence structure with your brand voice.
    • Adds and verifies relevant internal and external links, excluding competitor domains.
  • Validate: HubSpot’s AI evaluates the draft before delivery.
    • Scores content using a quality rubric.
    • Confirms formatting and content requirements, such as title length, meta description length, link requirements, and formatting consistency.
    • Reviews audience targeting, brand integration, and use of verifiable sources.

If the blog post draft doesn’t meet the quality threshold, HubSpot’s AI may refine and validate the draft up to two times before delivery.

Refine a generated blog post in Breeze Assistant

After generating a blog post from a recommendation, use Breeze Assistant to refine the content conversationally.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Recommendations tab.
  • At the top of the page, click the Owned content tab.
  • Click the title of the recommendation that you generated the blog post for.
  • In the right panel, click the Content tab.
  • Click Open in Breeze Assistant.
  • In Breeze Assistant, enter your edits.
  • When finished, click Open in editor to continue publishing the post.

Generate LinkedIn articles and posts from recommendations

After reviewing social amplification recommendations, generate a LinkedIn article and optional social post based on the recommendation. Review and edit the generated content, then copy it to Linkedin to publish.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Recommendations tab.
  • At the top of the page, click the Social amplification tab.
  • Click a recommendation where the Channel column contains LinkedIn.
  • In the right panel, click Generate LinkedIn article.
  • After the article is generated, the article will display on the Content> tab in the right panel.
    • The title and body content have separate Copy icons.
    • An optional social post is also included so you can announce the article on your LinkedIn feed.
  • Click the Copy icons and paste the content into LinkedIn’s article editor. Review and edit the draft, then publish.

Review and manage AEO with the HubSpot connector

Before you get started

Before you begin reviewing and managing AEO with the HubSpot connector, review these requirements and limitations.

Permissions required A Super Admin must approve the HubSpot connector before users can connect it. During approval, Super Admins select which data permissions the connector can access and who in the account can install it. Learn more about managing access to apps.

Understand requirements

  • Set up AEO in your HubSpot account before using the HubSpot connector.

  • Set up the HubSpot connector for a supported assistant:

    • Set up and use the HubSpot connector for Claude
    • Set up and use the HubSpot connector for ChatGPT

Monitor AEO performance

Ask the connected AI assistant to retrieve and summarize AEO performance data, including brand visibility, tracked prompt performance, citations, and competitor share of voice.

For example, ask:

To learn more about AEO metrics and analysis, see Set up and analyze AEO.

Manage tracked prompts

Review tracked prompts or create and manage prompts through the connected AI assistant.

For example, ask:

  • “Create a tracked prompt for topic.”

When a request creates or changes a tracked prompt, the AI assistant may display a preview before completing the action. Review the proposed changes before approving them.

To learn more about prompt metrics, groups, buyer journey phases, and prompt management, see Review and manage AEO prompts.

Review and take action on recommendations

Review recommendations based on AEO performance and tracked prompt results. Take action on a recommendation from your connected AI assistant.

Subscription required Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise is required to generate content from AEO recommendations.

For example, ask:

To learn more about recommendation types, priorities, site audits, and content actions, see Review and manage AEO recommendations.

Set canonical URLs for duplicate content

If you’re hosting duplicate content on multiple pages of your website, setting a canonical URL will tell search engines which content contains the preferred version.

Manage canonical URL settings

By default, when you create a new page or blog post, its URL is set as canonical for that content. This is the recommended setting, as it helps search engines recognize that your content is authoritative. In contrast, blog listing pages don’t have canonical URLs set by default - this helps search engines find subsequent pages for the same blog listing page.

Change either of these default settings in your website settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Pages.

  • Click the SEO & Crawlers tab.

  • In the Pages and blog posts field, select an option. If you select Don’t add canonical URLs to any pages or blog posts, you’ll need to manually set canonical URLs.

  • In the Blog listing pages field, select an option. If you select Set each blog listing page’s canonical URL to the first page in its series, search engines may be unable to find subsequent pages for your blog listing page.

  • When finished, click Save in the bottom left.

Add or edit canonical URLs for individual posts and pages

Manually add or edit a canonical URL for a blog post or page. Canonical URLs configured on individual pages or posts will take priority over your canonical URL settings.

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.

  • Hover over an existing page or post, and click Edit.

  • In the content editor, click the Settings menu and select Advanced.

  • In the dialog box, enter a canonical URL in the Customize canonical URL field. This is the URL search engines will prioritize when displaying search results relevant to this content.

  • To take your changes live, click Publish or Update in the top right.

Set up and analyze AEO

Measure how your brand appears in answer engine responses using answer engine optimization (AEO).

Similar to how search engine optimization (SEO) measures visibility in search results, AEO tracks how often your brand is mentioned across prompts and analyzes the sources used to generate responses.

After confirming your brand details, prompts are tracked across supported answer engines. AEO aggregates these results into visibility metrics, helping you analyze brand mentions, prompt coverage, and citation patterns over time.

Learn more about this feature by joining a small group coaching session

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before working with AEO, review these requirements, available features, and usage limits.

Subscription required One of the following subscriptions is required to set up and analyze AEO:

  • Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription.

  • HubSpot AEO subscription or 28 day free trial.

  • Users with a View-Only seat can view AEO data, but can’t create or edit prompts.

  • Each unique brand requires its own AEO setup. Learn how to manage multiple brands and domains.

  • AEO includes the following default answer engines: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. To also track Claude, Google AI Mode, and Google AI Overviews, opt your account into the AEO Multi-Engine beta, then turn on premium engines.

  • To align SEO efforts with AI-driven visibility, review how to optimize content and improve brand visibility for AI.

  • Data collection begins after setting up AEO and tracking prompts.

  • AEO runs tracked prompts daily. Because responses change over time, review performance across multiple days or weeks before evaluating trends.

  • While both experiences track brand visibility across answer engines, available features and limits differ.

Set up AEO

Set up AEO for the first time by confirming your brand details, competitors, products, ICPs, and prompts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click Get started.
  • In the dialog box, enter your brand name in the Brand field (e.g., AcmeDemo).
  • Enter your domain in the Domain field (e.g., acme-demo.test). To add more root domains later, go to your AEO settings.
  • Enter your brand name variations.
    • You must separate each variation with a comma (e.g., AcmeDemo, Acme Demo).
    • Brand name variations are case-sensitive, so enter each variation exactly as it appears.
  • Click the Business type dropdown menu and select an option (e.g., B2B).
  • When finished, click Next.
Review competitors

Review competitors to compare your brand’s visibility against competitors in answer engine responses. Add or edit competitor names, domain, and brand name variations to improve accuracy. Update competitors later in your AEO settings.

  • To edit a competitor, hover over the competitor name and click Edit. In the right panel, enter the competitor details and then click Save.
  • To add more competitors, click Add more competitors. In the right panel, add the competitor details and then click Save.
  • To remove a competitor, hover over the competitor name and click Delete.
  • When finished, click Continue.
Review products and ICPs

Review products and your Ideal Customer Profiles (ICPs) to define the solutions and target audiences AEO tracks.

Prompts are generated based on your selected product and ICP. These selections decide how your brand’s visibility is analyzed. Update products and audiences in your AEO settings.

  • Select a product or click Add product. If you click Add product, enter the product details and then click Save in the right panel.
  • Select an ICP or click Add ICP. If you click Add ICP, enter the ICP details and then click Save in the right panel.
  • To add additional products or ICPs, click the Add more dropdown menu and select Add more products or Add more ICPs.
  • When finished, click Continue.
Review prompts

Prompts are questions that people might ask AI answer engines (such as ChatGPT) when searching for brands, products, or services related to your business. After confirming your brand details, competitors, products, and ICPs, HubSpot generates suggested prompts. Edit prompts in this step or later when you review and manage AEO prompts. For Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise accounts, prompts are generated using your business context.

Review prompts to ensure they reflect how your target audience would naturally search and align with your business, products, competitors, and ICPs:

  • To edit a prompt, hover over the prompt and click Edit. In the right panel, edit the prompt details and then click Save.
  • To generate more prompts, click the Add more prompts dropdown menu and select Generate with AI. An additional 8-15 more prompts will be added.
  • To add more prompts manually, click the Add more prompts dropdown menu and select Add prompts manually. In the right panel, enter the prompt details and then click Save.
  • When finished, click Add and track [#] prompts.

Analyze the AEO dashboard

Use the Dashboard tab to analyze your AEO performance, including brand visibility, prompts, domains, citations, and competitor benchmarks.

Each answer engine may generate different responses, cite different sources, or return different levels of detail for the same prompt. Use filters to compare results by engine. Manage competitors directly from your AEO settings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Dashboard tab.
  • To filter the dashboard, click Filters. In the right panel, select your filter options (e.g., Date).
  • When finished, click Apply.

Please note: removing or updating a competitor in your AEO settings only affects future data runs. Historical data remains in charts when the selected date range includes a period when the competitor was tracked. To view data without the removed competitor, set the dashboard date range to start after the date you made the change.

Brand metrics

Brand visibility is how often your brand is mentioned among the prompts you track. It also shows how answer engines interpret your brand based on public information on the web. Brand visibility is analyzed on:

  • Prompt coverage: the percentage of prompts where your brand appears at least once.
  • Frequency across answer engines: whether your brand shows up consistently across different answer engines.
  • Relative competitor presence: how often competitors appear in the same prompt results.

Use brand visibility trends to evaluate consistency over time. A lower score may indicate that your brand appears in fewer prompts, appears inconsistently across answer engines, or is mentioned less often than competitors.

Review the following reports on the Brand visibility tab:

  • Brand visibility: displays a percentage score on how often your brand appears in answer engine responses across tracked prompts.

  • Brand visibility over time: displays how your brand visibility score changes over time.

Review the following reports on the Sentiment analysis tab:

  • Sentiment score: displays a score of how positively or negatively your brand is described in answer engine responses.
  • Sentiment over time: displays how your brand’s sentiment changes over time.
Competitor landscape

In the Competitor landscape section, review the following reports:

  • Share of Voice: the proportion of total brand mentions that belong to your brand across tracked prompts.
    • A higher share of voice means your brand accounts for a larger portion of total mentions across responses.
    • This metric is calculated by dividing your brand’s mentions by the total number of brand mentions from all competitors for the tracked prompts.
  • Competitor Visibility: compares your brand identity to your competitors.
Citation analysis

In the Citation analysis section, review the following reports:

  • Top domains: displays websites that answer engines most often cite across your tracked prompts. If you click this report, you’ll be directed to the Citations tab.
  • Citations by channel: displays the channels of all citations for your tracked prompts.
  • Citations with brand mention rate vs competitors: displays the percentage of sources cited by answer engines that mention your brand.

Analyze citations

Analyze citations to understand which websites answer engines reference, how authoritative your content appears, and whether third-party sources influence your brand’s visibility. Use this information to decide whether to update existing content or create new content.

A citation is recorded when an answer engine includes or references:

  • A link to a webpage
  • A domain name embedded in its answer

To review your citations:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Citations tab.
  • To filter the dashboard, click Filter and select your options (e.g., Date).

Please note: citations are separate from brand mentions. A source can be cited without mentioning your brand name.

Owned domain citation rate vs. competitors

Use the Owned domain citation rate vs. competitors report to compare how often answer engines cite content from your website versus competitor domains across your tracked prompts.

A higher share of owned citations means answer engines rely more on content you control when generating responses. This gives you more influence over how your brand is represented in answer engines.

Review this report to:

  • Find trends in how often your owned content is cited over time.
  • Compare your citation share against competitors for the same prompt.
  • Find potential gaps where competitors are cited more often. This may show opportunities to improve the clarity, coverage, or relevance of your content.

If no data is shown, no citations were detected for the selected time range.

Citations with brand mention rate vs. competitors

Use the Citations with brand mention rate vs. competitors report to understand how often your brand is referenced in citations, regardless of where the cited content originates.

This report includes citations from third-party sources such as reviews, news articles, and industry publications. Even if answer engines don’t cite your website directly, they may still reference your brand through external sources.

Review this report to:

  • Evaluate overall brand visibility in answer engine responses.
  • Track changes in influence over time.
  • Find when competitors are becoming more prominent for the same topics.
Citations by content type

Use the Citations by content type report to understand which content formats answer engines most often reference for your tracked prompts.

Content types include:

Top lists and listicles

Blogs and news articles

Research and reports

Comparison articles

Documentation and technical docs

User reviews

Product pages

Wiki-style information pages

Social content

Review this report to:

  • Find out which content formats answer engines prefer for your topic area.
  • Find gaps where answer engines cite formats you don’t produce.
  • Prioritize creating or updating content formats that are more likely to earn citations.
Citations by channel

Use the Citations by channel report to view what types of websites answer engines reference when generating responses.

Source types include:

Owned domains

Peer companies

Social platforms

Competitor sites

User-generated content

Earned media

Affiliate sites

Review this report to:

  • Understand how much of your brand visibility comes from content you control versus external sources.
  • Find reliance on third-party validation such as earned or peer sources.
  • Track growth in user-generated or social sources, which may show increased awareness or discussion.
Review additional citation reports

In addition to the above citation charts, review the following reports for insight into how answer engines reference your content and external sources:

  • Top domains: lists the websites most commonly referenced by answer engines.
  • Top owned citations: lists the pages on your domain that answer engines reference most often. This helps you understand which content answer engines consider most authoritative for your brand.
  • Top citations overall: lists the websites that appear most often across all citations for your tracked prompts. This helps you understand which third-party sources most influence how answer engines describe your brand.

Analyze channel insights

Use the Insights tab to view how each of your channels drives citations and visibility compared to your competitors. The Insights tab includes three channel tabs: Social channel insights, Owned content insights, and Outreach insights.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > AEO. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > AEO directly.
  • Click the Insights tab and select a channel tab (e.g., Social channel insights).
  • Review each channel tab. The following reports are included:
    • Citation trend: displays your citation rate versus competitors across answer engines over time.
    • Visibility score: displays your visibility score versus competitors for your tracked prompts.
    • Top citations: lists the pages referenced most in answer engines for your tracked prompts.
    • Prompt performance: displays how each of your tracked prompts performs over time.

On the Social channel insights tab, reports are grouped by channel (e.g., LinkedIn, Reddit, or YouTube). Click a channel at the top of the page to review the individual reports for each channel.

On the Owned content insights tab, the Estimated impact report shows the estimated citation impact if you act on all recommendations for your owned content channel. To review the full list of recommendations, click View all recommendations. Learn more about reviewing and managing AEO recommendations.

Next steps

  • Manage AEO settings
  • Review and manage AEO prompts
  • Review and manage AEO recommendations

Topics, pillar pages, and subtopic keywords

With HubSpot’s SEO tools, you can organize your content into topics that matter to your customers. Each topic is composed of a pillar page and supporting content. Linking supporting content back to a pillar page on your main website helps search engines discover your content and surface it in search results.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential consequences of using it.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • Creating topic clusters in HubSpot doesn’t affect your website’s SEO directly.
  • A pillar page should sit on the top level of your website in a location that gets a lot of organic traffic. To ensure that everything on the page can be crawled by search engines, the pillar page shouldn’t have any content locked behind a form or a password.
  • There’s a limit of 100 subtopic keywords for each topic. Additionally, each piece of subtopic keyword content, such as a blog post or landing page, can only be attached to one topic.

Topic

A topic is a main goal, problem, or idea that your customers are interested in. You can research and compare which topics are worth writing about directly in the SEO tool. Learn more about creating a topic.

When you’re researching new topics, the tool calculates the following metrics:

  • Monthly Search Volume: the average monthly searches for this term in search engines. Longer or niche terms might have no or low monthly search volume, and broader terms might be highly popular but difficult to rank for.
  • Difficulty: an estimation of the difficulty you’ll face breaking into the front page of search results for this topic. This score is measured on a 100 point scale, meaning it’s easier to see success with topics that have lower score

Pillar page

A pillar page is a comprehensive resource page that covers a topic in depth. This page links to high-quality content for supporting subtopic keywords. A pillar page should apply on-page SEO best practices, referencing the topic in the page title, URL, and H1 tag. Content on a pillar page should also be adapted to convert visitors, since all your supporting content links back here. Learn more about attaching a topic to a pillar page.

Want to see how other users are building their pillar pages? Check out a few examples on the HubSpot Marketing blog.

Subtopic keywords

Subtopic keywords address a specific question about your pillar page topic. This piece of content should include a link back to your pillar page to drive traffic to your website. When you attach a blog post, landing page, or website page to a subtopic keyword, the SEO tool tracks how many inbound links you have referring back to your pillar page. Learn more about adding subtopic keywords.

You can attach the following types of content to your subtopic keywords in the SEO tool:

  • One of your HubSpot blog posts, landing pages, or website pages
  • The full URL of a webpage
  • A link to a high-quality external website or blog

When you add a new subtopic keyword, you’ll see analytics in the Subtopic Keyword panel for Monthly Search Volume.

Understand Google Search Console metrics in HubSpot

The Google Search Console integration adds search performance metrics to the SEO tool in HubSpot. These metrics show how content appears and performs in Google search results.

Please note: for detailed information on how Google calculates metrics, refer to Google’s Support documentation.

What do the Google Search Console metrics mean?

The following metrics are available in the SEO tool from the Google Search Console integration:

  • Total pages: the number of pages detected by Google Search Console.
  • Total impressions: the number of times a link to your website appears in Google search results. An impression is counted when a result loads on a page, even if it isn’t scrolled into view. For infinite scroll results, the result must be visible.
  • Total clicks: the number of times a visitor selects a link to your website from Google search results. Clicks from one part of the Google platform to another aren’t counted.
  • Average clickthrough: the number of clicks on your website relative to impressions. The average clickthrough rate is calculated by dividing the number of clicks by the number of impressions, then multiplying by 100.
  • Average position: the average ranking of the Google search result linking to your website.

How is the average position calculated?

The Average position metric shows the average position of the top search result linking to your website across all searches.

Several factors can affect position, including:

  • Device type
  • Location
  • Search history
  • Search filters

Search results may vary based on these factors, so results may differ from what appears in a personal search.

What counts as a position?

On a search results page:

  • Only elements that link to external websites are counted.
  • Ads and query refinement links aren’t counted.
  • Results are counted from top to bottom and left to right (based on language direction).

For example, when searching Google for pasta, most results link to external websites, such as Wikipedia. These results are counted as position placeholders.

You may also see query refinement links or images on the search results page. These often appear in a carousel.

Selecting one of these links opens another Google search, such as for spaghetti or pizza, instead of an external website. These query refinement links aren’t counted as position placeholders and are skipped when calculating position.

Please note: some carousel images or featured links do lead to external websites, so these would be counted as position placeholders.

In the examples below, the diagram on the left includes an image carousel that links to external pages, so it is counted as a position placeholder. The diagram on the right includes query refinement links, so it is not counted.

Please note: similar-looking search results pages may produce different position values depending on whether the links point to external websites or additional Google searches.

To determine whether a result is counted, hover over a link to preview the URL. Query refinement links begin with https://www.google.com/search?q and aren’t counted as position placeholders.

Why are the number of clicks, views, or sessions different in Google Search Console and HubSpot?

Metrics may differ between HubSpot and Google Search Console for the following reasons:

  • Hubspot may exclude internal traffic using IP filtering, which removes internal engagement.
  • Google Search Console may exclude traffic based on configured filters.
  • Google applies additional automated filtering based on its own data modesl.

Which URL is data associated with?

Google Search Console assigns data to a canonical URL that represents all variations of a page. This includes:

  • Desktop and mobile versions.
  • Alternate URLs that point to the same page.
  • Multi-language variations.

Clicks, impressions, and position data from all variations are grouped under the canonincal URL.

Understand SEO crawling errors

If an SEO crawler can’t index a page, it will return a crawling error. This can happen with the crawlers in HubSpot’s SEO and import tools, as well as external crawlers like Semrush. The steps for resolving a crawling error depend on the error and where the page is hosted.

HubSpot’s SEO tools crawling a HubSpot page

You can view SEO recommendations on the Optimization tab of a page or post’s performance details.

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.

  • Hover over your content and click Performance.

  • Click the Optimization tab.

  • By default, Recommendations will be selected in the left sidebar menu. To rescan the content, click Rescan now. If there are issues crawling the page, you may see one of the following error messages:

    • Status 301: Moved Permanently: a 301 redirect is preventing the crawler from accessing the content.
    • Status 302: Object moved: a 302 (temporary) redirect is preventing the crawler from accessing the content.
    • Status 403: Forbidden: the server can be reached, but access to content is denied.
    • Status 404: Not Found: the crawler is unable to find a live version of the content because it was deleted or moved.
    • Crawl of [site] blocked by robots.txt: a robots.txt file is blocking the content from being indexed.

HubSpot’s SEO tools crawling an external page

If you have attempted to crawl external pages using HubSpot’s SEO tools or are importing external content to HubSpot, you may encounter one of these errors:

  • Scan blocked by robots.txt file: if your external page is excluded from indexing by your robots.txt file, add the HubSpot crawler’s user agent “HubSpot Crawler” as an exemption. Learn more about working with a robots.txt file.
  • Robots.txt file couldn’t be retrieved: if HubSpot’s crawlers can’t access your site’s robots.txt file, verify that the robots.txt file is accessible and in the top-level directory of your site. Learn more about working with a robots.txt file.
  • The crawler isn’t able to scan this URL: if HubSpot’s crawlers can’t crawl a specific URL, try the following troubleshooting steps:
    • Verify that the URL has been entered correctly.
    • Verify that the page being crawled is currently live.
    • Verify that DNS can resolve the URL. Learn more about resolving DNS errors in Google’s documentation.
    • Reach out to your site administrator and request that they add our crawler’s user agent, “HubSpot Crawler,” to the allow list as an exemption.

An external SEO tool crawling a HubSpot page

If you have attempted to crawl your HubSpot pages using an external SEO tool such as Moz or Semrush, you may find that you are unable to crawl your pages successfully.

Common causes for this issue include:

  • The inclusion of your pages in the robots.txt file is preventing them from being indexed or crawled.
  • A “noindex” meta tag in the head HTML of your pages is preventing them from being indexed or crawled.
  • Auditing a root domain, rather than the subdomain connected to HubSpot, is causing a timeout error.
  • Links for RSS feeds and blog listing pages expire when new blog posts are published, which can generate blocked resources errors.
  • Non-essential resources, such as the scripts that load the HubSpot sprocket menu, may prompt blocked resources errors. This does not prevent the rest of the page from being crawled.

Understand SEO recommendations

SEO recommendations identify issues that can affect how your content is discovered and understood by search engines. This article explains what each SEO recommendation means, why it may affect your content’s search performance, and what actions you can take to resolve it. Learn more about accessing your SEO recommendations.

Before you get started

  • Recommendations are organized in the SEO tools according to:
    • Impact on your site’s SEO.
    • Technical difficulty of resolving them.
    • Suggested role of the person resolving them.
  • Recommendations with a Technical Difficulty of High may require the help of a developer to resolve.
  • Page titles and meta descriptions can be set for pages and blog posts. However, search engines decide what displays in search results and may show different titles or descriptions based on page content or user queries. To influence what appears, ensure your titles and descriptions accurately reflect the page content and are relevant to your target keywords.
  • To align SEO efforts with AI-driven visibility, review how to optimize content and improve brand visibility for AI.

SEO recommendations

The following recommendations are organized by category, then listed in order of their potential SEO impact. Straightforward recommendations and those requiring developer assistance will only appear in HubSpot’s SEO tools.

Accessibility

Add image alt text attribute

Images can make it difficult for search engines and visitors using screen readers to understand your content. To resolve this issue, add alt text to images that describes their appearance and content. This will improve the accessibility and SEO of your site. Learn more about website accessibility.

Verify image alt text should be blank

Adding alt text to a page’s images lets search engines and visitors using screen readers understand its content. Some images, like icons that separate parts of a page, don’t have any meaningful content. These images should have a blank alt text attribute instead. Review your images with blank alt text attributes to make sure they shouldn’t contain alt text.

Define a page’s language with the “lang” attribute

A page’s language is set by the “lang” attribute. Screen readers rely on this attribute to determine which language library to use. If the language isn’t set correctly, visitors’ screen reading software may not work correctly. Learn more about [using the “lang” attribute](https://www.w3.org/International/questions/qa-lang-why#:~:text=The%20lang%20(or%20sometimes%20the,the%20text%20on%20the%20page.).

The “lang” attribute is set inside the <html> tag at the start of your page’s source code. A correctly formatted “lang” attribute will look like this:

&lt;html lang="en">...&lt;/html>.

Compare the language code in your <html> tag with the list of accepted two-letter codes for languages, then replace the code. If your <html> tag doesn’t contain a “lang” attribute, add lang="[language code]" to your tag.

Remove the <meta http-equiv=“refresh”> tag

A page containing the &lt;meta http-equiv="refresh"> tag will refresh automatically after a specified amount of time. This can create a confusing user experience and interfere with screen-reading software. Use JavaScript instead for any pages that need to refresh automatically.

Crawling and Indexing

Confirm the correct pages are hidden from search results and blocked by a robots.txt file

If any pages hosted on your domain are blocked from search engines, you’ll see a recommendation to review a list of these pages. This is a way to confirm there aren’t any pages on your website that are blocked from search engines by mistake.

If all the pages listed are hidden from search results intentionally, no action is needed.

If you see a website page that’s hidden from search results that should be indexed for search results, work with your website administrator to update your robots.txt file or remove any tags on the page that might be blocking it from search results.

Confirm canonical links configuration

Search engines like Google use canonical links to find the primary version of a page to display in search results. Avoid duplicate content issues by adding a valid canonical link to each page. Learn more about how canonical URLs influence SEO.

Canonical links will be marked as invalid for any of the following reasons:

  • There is more than one canonical link.
  • The canonical link is not a valid URL.
  • The canonical link is a relative URL.
  • The canonical link points to a page for a different region or language.
  • The canonical link points to a different domain.
  • The canonical link points to the site’s root.

Learn more about how to edit a page’s canonical URL from the Settings tab in the content editor.

Please note: blog listing pages may trigger a false duplicate content alert.

Confirm search engines can process your page links

Search engines prefer links that are formatted as an <a> tag with an href attribute. A correctly formatted link looks like this:

&lt;a href="https://www.hubspot.com">Link text here&lt;/a>.

Make sure the links on your page follow this format to allow search engines to crawl them.

Fix broken pages

HubSpot’s crawler wasn’t able to scan these pages because of an error. This could be due to one of the following reasons:

  • Missing HTTP status code: HTTP status codes show whether a web page has successfully been reached. If the scan can’t return an HTTP status code, the scan will fail. Learn more about HTTP status codes.
  • HTTP status code returns an error: HTTP status codes show whether a web page has successfully been reached. Status codes in the 400s and 500s show client or server errors and will prevent a scan from being completed. Learn more about different HTTP status codes.
  • Page HTML is blank: if the source code of the page has no HTML, the scan won’t be able to process the page.

Work with your web developer to verify that the listed pages are set up and working correctly.

Confirm all hreflang links contain a valid language code

Using hreflang links in your multi-language website enables search engines to know a page’s language. Search engines can then give international users a search result for the page that matches their preferred language. Learn more about using hreflang links for your multi-language content.

If these links have an invalid language code, search engines won’t be able to correctly find the page’s language or include it with the results for that language to international users. Multi-language pages hosted on HubSpot will automatically use valid language codes.

Compare the language codes in your links with the lists of accepted two-letter codes for languages and regions. Then replace any invalid codes. Specifying a region in your hreflang link is optional— if used, you should format it as hreflang=”[language]-[region]”. For example, a page in Spanish targeted at users in Spain would be formatted as hreflang="es-es,"while one for all Spanish speakers worldwide would use hreflang=”es”.

Confirm all hreflang links use a full URL

Using hreflang links in your multi-language website enables search engines to know a page’s language. Search engines can then give international users a search result for the page that matches their preferred language. Learn more about using hreflang links for your multi-language content.

Some hreflang links use relative URLs, which contain only a URL path, rather than a full URL starting with http/https. While these links may work, they have an increased risk of breaking in the future if the original URL changes. Multi-language pages hosted on HubSpot will automatically use full URLs.

Edit your relative hreflang links in your page’s source code. Learn more about editing a page’s source code in the page editor and in the module editor.

For the page hubspot.com, a relative link might look like this:

link rel="alternate" href="/example-page/fr/" hreflang="fr-fr" />.

You can change this to a full link by editing the href to contain the full URL including the protocol (http/https):

link rel="alternate" href="https://www.hubspot.com/example-page/fr/" hreflang="fr-fr" />.

Write descriptive Edit link anchor text to be more descriptive

In a link, anchor text is the clickable word or phrase. This text should clearly communicate the link’s target. Replace generic anchor text like “click here” or “learn more” with specific link descriptions. Learn more about Google’s anchor text best practices or read a list of phrases that trigger this recommendation.

Mobile Experience

Confirm mobile users can click on each page element

If buttons and links are too small or close together, it can be hard to tap them on mobile devices. Interactive elements should be at least 48 pixels by 48 pixels in size. If an element needs to stay the same size, adding padding will also resolve this error.

Learn how to edit the size or padding of different types of elements in HubSpot:

  • Edit the size of a CTA
  • Edit content in a rich text module
  • Customize module styles in the content editor
  • Create, edit, and attach CSS files to style your site
Confirm each page has a viewport tag

A viewport tag controls the scale of your website content on different device types. If this tag is missing or set up incorrectly, your website appears less mobile-friendly to search engines. This can have a negative affect on your rankings in search results.
