  • Service Hub Enterprise is required for knowledge base articles.

Permissions required Super Admin permission is required to set up content approval. Users must have one of the following permissions to approve content, depending on the content type:

  • Marketing Access with Approve permission is required to approve marketing emails, blog posts, pages, or social posts.
  • Service Access with Knowledge base articles access and Approve permission is required to approve knowledge base articles.

Seats required An assigned Service Hub Enterprise seat is required to approve knowledge base articles.

Understand limitations and considerations
  • Super Admins can skip approvals.
  • Content that’s pending approval can only be published by assigned approvers.
  • Only one approval request can be submitted at a time.
  • An approval can have up to 10 stages and up to 10 approvers total. Each stage requires at least one approver.
  • Approval stages and request changes aren’t available for pages in the new content editor (BETA).
  • Approval settings for deals and quotes are managed within their respective tools and don’t appear on the Approvals settings page.
  • When requesting an approval for an RSS or blog subscription email, the email only needs to be approved once. Any subsequent updates to the email can be published immediately without the need to regain approval.
  • If you’ve opted into the Team approvers for content approvals (BETA), these considerations apply to team approvers:
    • A team counts as one approver toward the limit of 10 approvers.
    • Team members can approve on behalf of their team even if they don’t have the Approve permission. Being on a team doesn’t change their individual approval permissions, and users removed from a team can no longer approve on its behalf.
    • Only users on the team can approve the request, including users who have the team as an additional team. Members of child teams can’t approve for a parent team.
    • If a team has no members, or is no longer set up to approve, the approval sidebar shows a warning so the team can be removed as an approver or updated.
    • Team approvers aren’t available for knowledge base articles, social posts, or pages in the new content editor (BETA).

Set up content approval

Set up content approval requests in your Approval settings, then assign the proper permissions to users or teams who should review and approve content.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the Team approvers for content approvals (BETA).

Turn on content approval requests
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Approvals.
  • On the Approvals page, toggle the switches for the applicable content type on.
  • On the Choose who can skip approvals page, select an option for which users don’t need approval to publish or schedule content:
    • Only Super Admins can skip approvals: only Super Admins can publish content without requesting approval.
    • Everyone can skip approvals: all users can publish content without requesting approval.
    • Only users I choose can skip approvals: specific users can publish content without requesting approval. When selecting this option, select the checkbox next to each user who can skip approvals. Super Admins can’t be selected because they always have the ability to skip approvals.
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
  • On the Review approvers page, choose who users can request approval from:
    • Approving Teams (BETA): click the Select teams dropdown menu and select the teams that can approve this content type. Any member of a selected team can approve requests.
    • Individual users: Super Admins can always approve requests. To let other users approve, give Approval permission to users in your Users & teams settings.
  • Click Done.
Give approval permission to other users

After content approvals are turned on, Super Admins automatically have permission to approve content. Assign Approval permission to more users as needed.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar, click Users & teams.
  • Hover over a user, then click Edit permissions.
  • To give users approval permissions for marketing emails, blog posts, landing pages, website pages, and social posts:
    • In the left panel, click the Marketing tab.
    • Toggle the Marketing Access switch on.
    • In the Approvals section, toggle the Approve [content type] switch on for each type of content the user should approve.
  • To give users approval permission for knowledge base articles:
    • In the left panel, click the Service tab.
    • Toggle the Service Access switch on.
    • In the Knowledge base articles section, toggle the Approve switch on for knowledge base articles.
  • In the top right, click Save.

Request approval

Request approval from one or more groups of approvers. To use a single group of approvers, add approvers to Stage 1 only. To route content through multiple groups of approvers in a specific order, add additional stages.

Please note: if a Super Admin has opted your account into the Team approvers for content approvals (BETA), you can request approval from a team.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Knowledge base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Marketing emails: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • Social posts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • Click the name of your content.
  • In the top right of the content editor, click Request approval.
  • In the dialog box, in the This asset needs approval from section, select an option:
    • All approvers: every approver in each stage must approve before the stage is complete.
    • One approver per stage: only one approver in each stage needs to approve before the stage is complete. This selection applies to every stage.
  • In the Approval process section, click Add approver for Stage 1, then select the approvers for the first stage. If you’ve opted into the Team approvers for content approvals (BETA), you can select a team in the Teams section of the dropdown menu. Add teams and users to any stage.
  • To add another group of approvers, click the add icon below the last stage, then select at least one user or team for the new stage.
  • Enter a due date and time.
  • In the Request note field, enter an optional message for the approvers.
  • Click Request approval.

Please note: each stage must be completed before the next one begins. Only Stage 1 approvers are notified when an approval is first requested. When a stage is complete, approvers in the next stage are notified.

If your account is opted into the Team approvers for content approvals (BETA), everyone on the team receives the request notification.

Approve content or request changes

Review content and submit a decision from the approval sidebar.

Please note: if you’ve opted into the Team approvers for content approvals (BETA), members of an approving team can approve or request changes on behalf of their team.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Knowledge base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Marketing emails: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • Social posts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • In the top right of the content editor, click View approval.
  • In the approval sidebar, click Approve or Request changes below your name or your team’s name (BETA):
    • Approve: in the dialog box, enter an optional message, then click Approve. Approved content can be published by any user with Publish permission for the relevant content type.
    • Request changes: in the dialog box, enter a message describing what needs to change, then click Request changes. A message is required and is included in the requester’s notification. The approval status changes to Changes requested.

Please note: when a team is an approver, one member’s response completes the team’s step. The approval sidebar shows who responded on the team’s behalf, for example, Approved by [name]. While the team’s step is pending, click the member count next to the team’s name to see who’s on the team.

  • If you requested the approval, you can’t approve it on behalf of a team you’re on.
  • If you’re on more than one team in the same approval, approve for each team separately.

Make changes and ask for another review

When an approver requests changes, you’ll receive a notification with their note. After making your edits, ask the approver to review the content again.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Knowledge base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Marketing emails: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • Social posts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • In the top right of the content editor, click View approval.
  • In the approval sidebar, review the approver’s note below the approver’s name or teams name.
  • Make your edits to the content.
  • In the approval sidebar, click Ask to review again below the approver’s name or teams name.

Please note: once all approvers who requested changes have been asked to review again, the approval status returns to Pending. Approvals already given by other approvers stay in place.

Manage an approval in progress

Reassign approvers, add and remove stages that haven’t started, or cancel an approval from the More dropdown menu in the approval sidebar.

Reassign approvers
  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.

Add or remove stages
  • Navigate to your content:

    • Landing pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Knowledge base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Marketing emails: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • Social posts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • In the top right of the content editor, click View approval.
  • In the approval sidebar, click the More dropdown menu and select Reassign approval.
  • To remove a stage that has not started, click the delete icon.

Cancel approval
  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Knowledge base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Marketing emails: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • Social posts: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • In the top right of the content editor, click View approval.

View approval activity

The approval activity log is on the Activity tab at the top of the approval sidebar. Use it to review the full history of an approval, including stage completions, change requests, and approvals given.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.

Manage approvals on mobile devices

Requesting approvals on mobile is supported for marketing emails and social posts only. Users can cancel and approve content, including social posts, marketing emails, blog posts, landing pages, website pages, and knowledge base articles, using the HubSpot mobile app.

Please note: approval stages and request changes are available in the content editor on desktop. Mobile approval remains limited to the actions described below.

Request marketing email or social post approvals on mobile devices
  • Open the HubSpot mobile app on your device.
  • Navigate to your content:
    • Marketing email: In the top left, tap the Menu icon, then tap Marketing email.
    • Social posts: In the top left, tap the Menu icon, then tap Social Publish.
  • Tap the content that needs approval.
  • In the top right, tap the three vertical dots icon, then tap Request approval.
  • In the Request approval section, tap Approvers, then select the checkbox next to each user whose approval is requested.
  • Select an approval threshold:
    • All selected approvers: all selected approvers must approve the content before it can be published or scheduled.
    • One approver: only one selected approver must approve the content before it can be published or scheduled.
  • Tap Send.
Cancel approvals on mobile devices
  • Open the HubSpot mobile app on your device.
  • In the top left, tap the Menu icon, then tap Approvals.
  • Tap an approval.
  • At the bottom of the screen, tap Cancel approval.
  • In the field, enter the reason for the cancellation, then tap Cancel approval. A notification is sent to all of the approvers.
Approve content on mobile devices
  • Open the HubSpot mobile app on your device.
  • In the top left, tap the Menu icon, then tap Approvals.
  • Tap an approval.
  • To approve the content:
    • At the bottom of the screen, tap Approve.
    • In the field, enter any comments, then tap Approve.
  • To request changes to the content:
    • At the bottom of the screen, tap Request changes.
    • In the field, enter comments detailing the changes that need to be made, then tap the Send icon.

Archive your content

Archive content, such as a blog post, page, knowledge base article, or email, to hide it from your content dashboard without deleting it permanently. For example, archive a campaign landing page after the campaign ends, then unarchive it if you need it again. You can also archive files in the files tool.

Archive a page or blog post

Archive a website page, landing page, or blog post to remove it from your content dashboard. Pages and posts can be archived with or without being unpublished.

Permissions required Edit permission is required to archive a page or post.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Hover over your content, click the More dropdown menu, and select Archive.
  • In the dialog box, confirm your action:
    • If your content is unpublished, click Archive. This will move the page or post to the Archived section.
    • If your content is published, click Archive to move the published page or post to the Archived section. To return your content to Draft status, as well as move it to the Archived section, click Archive and unpublish.

Archive knowledge base articles

Archive a knowledge base article to remove it from your articles dashboard. All archived knowledge base articles are unpublished.

Subscription required A Service Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to archive knowledge base articles.

Seats required An assigned Service Hub seat is required to archive knowledge base articles.

Permissions required Knowledge base articles permission is required to archive knowledge base articles.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
  • Navigate to the Articles tab.
  • Hover over an article, then click the More dropdown menu and select Archive.
  • In the dialog box, confirm your action:
    • If the article is unpublished, click Archive. This will move the article to the Archived section of your articles.
    • If the article is published, click Archive and unpublish. This will return the article to Draft status and move it to the Archived section of your articles.

Archive emails

Archive an email to remove it from your email dashboard. Automated emails can be archived with or without being unpublished.

Permissions required Marketing email permission is required to archive emails.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Hover over an email, then click the Actions dropdown menu and select Archive.
  • In the dialog box, confirm your action:
    • If your email isn’t automated, click Archive. This will move the email to the Archived section of your emails.
    • If your email is automated and you want to keep using it in workflows, click Archive. This will move the email to the Archived section of your emails.
    • If your email is automated and you don’t want to keep using it in workflows, select the Archive and stop sending checkbox, then click Archive and stop sending. This will return the email to draft status and move it to the Archived section of your emails. Any workflows using this email won’t be able to send the email until it is published again.

Manage archived content

All archived pages and posts have a Publish status of Archived. Archived pages that are still published display an unfilled green circle, while archived pages that are unpublished display an unfilled grey circle. If you unarchive an email, the email returns to your email dashboard but stays unpublished.

To view or restore archived content:

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages:
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Email: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
    • Knowledge Base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
  • Click the Publish status dropdown menu, and select Archived. For marketing emails, click the Archived tab.
  • Hover over your content, then unarchive it:
    • Pages, posts, and articles: click the Actions dropdown menu and select Unarchive. In the dialog box, click Unarchive.
    • Emails: click the Actions dropdown menu and select Unarchive.

Attach a document to content

Add a link to a document, such as a PDF, spec sheet, or guide, in any rich text editor. When visitors or recipients click the linked text, the file opens or downloads from your HubSpot files tool. This helps you share supporting material directly in your emails, pages, blog posts, and knowledge base articles without visitors or recipients needing to request it separately.

For example, Sprocket Supply Co., an ecommerce company selling sustainable office supplies, publishes a landing page for its bulk ordering program. A marketer links the text “Download the 2025 product catalog” to a PDF stored in the files tool. Visitors can review pricing and product details on their own, which limits the number of catalog requests the sales team handles manually.

Attach a document to content

Permissions required The following permissions are required depending on the content type:

  • Edit and Publish permission are required to edit and publish pages or posts.

  • Marketing Access with Marketing email permission is required to edit and publish marketing emails.

  • Service Access with an assigned Service Hub seat and Knowledge base articles permission is required to edit and publish articles.

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Knowledge Base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Email: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of your content.

  • In the rich text editor, highlight the text you’d like to link to your document, then click the link icon.

  • In the pop-up box, click the Link to dropdown menu and select File.

  • Click Select a file.

  • In the right panel, locate your document in the files tool. If you need to upload a new file, click Upload files. Click the name of the file.

  • In the pop-up box, click Insert.

  • In the upper right, click Publish, Update, or Send when you’ve finished editing your content.

Automatically translate multi-language content

Translate pages and blog posts into multiple languages using HubSpot’s AI, powered by DeepL. Creating content in additional languages allows you to reach more customers who may not be fluent in your content’s original language.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand limitations & considerations

Generate content translations

Generate translated versions of existing pages or blog posts as a new language variation, then review and publish.

Bulk publish, update, or unpublish pages

Publish, update, or unpublish multiple website pages and landing pages from the content dashboard. Schedule these actions for a specific date and time to coordinate content releases or page removals.

Before you get started

Before you publish, update, or unpublish multiple pages, review these requirements and considerations.

  • Pages in multi-language groups can’t be managed in bulk.
  • If the selected pages include A/B tests or adaptive tests, all variations will be published or updated together.
  • Draft and published pages can be managed together.

Permissions required Edit and Publish permission is required to publish, update, or unpublish pages.

Publish or update multiple pages

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Select the checkbox next to each page you want to publish or update.
  • At the top of the table, click the More dropdown menu and select Publishing options.
  • In the dialog box, select one of the following:
    • Publish/Update: publish draft pages and update published pages immediately.
    • Schedule publish/update: publish draft pages and update published pages at a specific date and time. If you select this option, click the date picker and select a date, then click the time dropdown menu and select a time.
  • Review the publishing details, including:
    • The number of draft pages that will be published.
    • The number of published pages that will be updated.
    • The Access Control status for the selected pages.
    • The number of pages with A/B tests or adaptive tests.
  • When finished, click Publish/Update or Schedule publish/update.

Unpublish multiple pages

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Select the checkbox next to each page you want to unpublish.
  • At the top of the table, click the More dropdown menu and select Unpublishing options.
  • In the dialog box, select one of the following:
    • Unpublish: unpublish the selected pages immediately.
    • Schedule unpublish: unpublish the selected pages at a selected date and time. If you select this option, click the date picker and select a date, then click the time dropdown menu and select a time.
      • Click the dropdown menu, and select an existing page to redirect visitors.
      • To redirect visitors to an external URL, click the dropdown menu and select Enter an external URL. Then, enter the external URL.
  • Review the total number of pages that will be unpublished.
  • When finished, click Unpublish or Schedule unpublish.

Change content URLs

Change the URL of any published page, blog post, or knowledge base article. Once the content is published or updated, this will automatically create a redirect from the old URL to the new URL.

Before you get started

Before you begin editing the URL of any published content, review the requirements and considerations.

Permissions required The following permissions are required depending on the content type you are editing:

  • Edit permission and Publish permission are required to edit and publish changes to settings for website pages, landing pages, or blog posts in the content editor.
  • Knowledge base articles must be turned on with Edit permission and Publish permission to edit and publish changes to settings for knowledge base articles in the article editor.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Changes to the URL of a page, post, or article will reset its view data in your analytics and affect the page’s search rankings. Learn more about how URL changes can impact SEO.
  • Changes to a knowledge base root URL or domain in knowledge base settings don’t automatically create redirects for existing article URLs. Instead, configure redirects separately based on your domain configuration.
  • If the URL you’re trying to set is already in use by other content, you’ll need to change that content’s URL before making your edits.

Edit a page’s URL

In the content editor, edit a page’s domain or URL slug. You can also edit that page’s canonical URL in its advanced settings.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of a page.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select General on the left menu.
  • If the page has already been published, click the edit edit icon next to Page URL.
  • To change the domain of your page, click the Domain dropdown menu and select a domain. Only primary and secondary domains set up for publishing this type of page will be listed. Learn more about connecting a domain and the subscription limits for domains.
  • To change the rest of the URL, enter a new URL string in the Content slug field.
  • Click X to close the Settings dialog box.
  • To take your changes live, click Publish or Update in the top right.

Edit a blog post’s URL

In the content editor, edit a blog post’s URL slug or move the post to a different blog. You can change the domain and root URL of a specific blog in your blog settings. Learn more about connecting a domain and the subscription limits for domains.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
  • Click the name of a post.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select General on the left menu.
  • To change which blog the post is hosted on, click the Blog dropdown menu and select a new blog. The post’s URL will update automatically to include the URL of the new blog. The live post’s URL won’t change until the post is updated.
  • If the post has already been published, click the edit edit icon next to the Post URL.
  • In the Content slug field, enter a new URL string.
  • Click X to close the Settings dialog box.
  • To take your changes live, click Publish or Update in the top right.

Edit a knowledge base article’s URL

In the article editor, edit a knowledge base article’s URL slug. Navigate to your knowledge base settings to change your knowledge base’s root URL. Learn more about connecting a domain and the subscription limits for domains.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
  • Click the name of an article.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select General on the left menu.
  • To change the root URL of your entire knowledge base, click Edit the root URL in settings. In your knowledge base settings, click Edit root URL in the Domain section. In the dialog box, click Yes, save it.
  • To change the article’s URL, enter a new URL slug in the Article URL field.
  • Click X to close the Settings dialog box.
  • To take your changes live, click Publish or Update in the top right.

Bulk update domains in page URLs

Bulk update the domain where multiple pages are hosted from the content index page. The URLs previously used for these pages will be automatically redirected to the URLs using the new domain.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Select the checkbox next to each page you want to update.
  • At the top of the table, click the More dropdown menu and select Update domain.
  • In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select a domain, then click Update.

Clear cache in a browser

Clearing your browser’s cache can help resolve pages that don’t load correctly, display outdated content, or behave inconsistently in HubSpot. Use the troubleshooting steps below to determine whether your browser is causing the issue, then follow the instructions for your browser.

Troubleshoot page and loading issues

If a HubSpot-hosted page doesn’t reflect recent changes, open the page in an incognito or private browsing window.

  • If the page displays correctly, clear your browser’s cache.
  • Reload the page or restart your browser.
  • If the issue continues, try the following:
    • Update your browser to the latest version.
    • Log out of your HubSpot account, then log back in.
    • Open the page in a different browser.
    • Test the page on a different device and network.

For access or loading issues, identify the scope of the problem before troubleshooting further:

  • Does the issue affect one user, some users, or all users?
  • Does the issue occur on specific pages, features, or across browsers, devices, or networks?
  • Did the issue start recently, or has it been ongoing?

Clear cache in a browser

Clearing your browser’s cache may sign you out of HubSpot and other websites. When you log back in to HubSpot, it may recognize your browser as a new device and request email verification or two-factor authentication (2FA). Clearing cache and cookies doesn’t remove saved passwords unless you separately select an option to delete saved passwords.

The process for clearing cache varies by browser. Confirm your browser and follow the external instructions:

  • Google Chrome
  • Safari
  • Mozilla Firefox
  • Internet Explorer
  • Microsoft Edge

After clearing cache in a browser

  • Restart your browser.
  • Reload the affected HubSpot page.
  • If the issue continues, test the page in another browser, device, or network.
  • If you continue to experience the issue, contact HubSpot Support.

Clone HubSpot content

Clone a HubSpot blog post, email, or page to use an existing piece of content as a starting point for a new piece of content. In the design manager, you can also clone a template, theme, or module to make changes without affecting pages using the original file.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before you clone HubSpot content, review the requirements and considerations.

  • To use HubSpot’s AI to clone content, turn on Give users access to Breeze Assistant in your AI settings.

Permissions required Users may require additional permissions depending on the content they are cloning. For example, cloning a landing page requires Edit and Publish permission to edit and publish landing pages.

Clone blog posts, articles, and website pages

Changes made to a cloned page won’t affect the original page. If you change the cloned page’s template, those changes will affect all pages using that template.

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.

    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.

    • Knowledge Base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.

  • Hover over the content and click Clone.
  • In the dialog box, enter an internal name for your new blog post, article, or website page and then click Clone.
  • In the content editor, customize your cloned content.

Please note: legacy knowledge base articles can’t be cloned. Learn more about migrating your knowledge base.

Clone landing pages

Clone landing pages and customize the content manually, or use HubSpot’s AI, to generate new content.

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to generate new content for landing pages with HubSpot’s AI tools.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.

  • Hover over the content and click Clone.

  • In the dialog box, enter an internal name for the landing page.

  • To generate new content using AI, select the Generate new content with AI checkbox. Otherwise, skip the checkbox.

    • If you select the Generate new content with AI checkbox, you’ll be directed to the Generate content page to provide more details.
    • If you don’t select the Generate new content with AI checkbox, you’ll be directed to the content editor to continue customizing the landing page.

  • When finished, click Clone.

Clone emails

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Hover over your email and click Clone.
  • In the right side panel, enter the email name in the Email name field.
  • In the Email type section, select whether your new email will be Regular or Automated.
  • To include the original email’s simple workflows, select the Copy simple workflows checkbox. This option is only available for regular emails.
  • In the email editor, customize your cloned email. By default, your cloned email will have the same settings, options, and recipients lists as the original email.

Please note: HubSpot blog subscription emails can’t be cloned.

Clone emails on the HubSpot mobile app

You can also clone a marketing email using the HubSpot mobile app.

  • Open the HubSot mobile app on your mobile device.
  • Tap Menu, then tap Marketing emails in the left sidebar.
  • Tap a marketing email.
  • In the top right, tap the three horizontal dots, then tap Clone.

Clone templates, themes, and module

Accounts with access to the design manager can clone assets created there, such as templates, themes, and modules.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Design Manager. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Design Manager directly.

  • In the finder, click the name of a template, theme, or module.

  • Click the File dropdown menu and select Clone “[file name]”. A copy of the file will be created with the name [File name] copy. The copy will open automatically in the layout editor.

  • To create an HTML copy of a drag and drop template, click the Actions dropdown menu and select Clone to HTML. The cloned template will contain raw HTML, rather than drag and drop modules.

Create a click-to-call or mailto link

Click-to-call and mailto links help visitors contact your team directly from your content. Click-to-call links are useful for visitors who want to call with a single tap or click. Mailto links open a new email message in the visitor’s default email program.

Before you get started

Before you begin creating a click-to-call or mailto link, review the requirements and considerations.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Marketing Access with Edit and Publish permission is required to edit and publish pages or posts.
  • Marketing Access with Marketing email permission is required to edit and publish emails.
  • Service Access with Knowledge base articles permission is required to edit a rich text module for a knowledge base article.
  • Marketing Access with CTA permission is required to edit an publish CTAs.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Click-to-call and mailto links are supported in rich text modules and CTAs (legacy).
  • Click-to-call links can’t contain spaces or dashes.

Create a click-to-call link

Click-to-call links connect visitors to a phone number when clicked or tapped on your content. These links are commonly used on content where calling is the next step.

Add a click-to-call link to a rich text module
  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Knowledge Base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Email: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of your content.
  • In the content editor, highlight a section of text or image.
  • In the rich text toolbar, click the link InInInsert link icon.
  • In the pop-up box, click the Link to dropdown menu and select URL.
  • In the URL field, enter ‘tel:’ then the phone number (e.g., tel:+1239990000).
  • Click Insert.
  • When finished, click Publish or Update in the top right.
Add a click-to-call link to a CTA (legacy)

Add a click-to-call link to a CTA (legacy) and then add the CTA (legacy) to your content.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > CTAs. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > CTAs directly.
  • In the top left, click the dropdown menu and select CTAs (Legacy).
  • Hover over a CTA, click the Actions dropdown menu, and select Edit.
  • In the right panel, customize your CTA design, then click Next in the bottom right.
  • Click the URL redirect type dropdown menu and select Phone number.
  • Enter a phone number in the Enter phone number field.
  • When finished, click Save in the bottom right.

Create a mailto link

Mailto links open a new email message addressed to a specific recipient in the visitor’s default email program. These links are useful when a page needs to prompt email-based outreach, such as support requests or general inquiries.

Add a mailto link in a rich text module
  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • Blog: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Blog. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Blog directly.
    • Knowledge Base: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Service > Knowledge Base. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Service > Knowledge Base directly.
    • Email: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of your content.
  • In the content editor, highlight a section of text or image.
  • In the rich text toolbar, click the link Insert link icon.
  • In the pop-up box, click the Link to dropdown menu and select Email address.
  • Enter the email address in the mailto: field. Learn how to add a subject line and email body to a mailto link.
  • Click Insert.
  • When finished, click Publish or Update in the top right.
Add a mailto link to a CTA (legacy)

Add a mailto link to a CTA (legacy) and then add the CTA (legacy) to your content.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > CTAs. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > CTAs directly.
  • In the top left, click the dropdown menu and select CTAs (Legacy).
  • Hover over a CTA and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Edit.
  • Set your CTA design, then click Next in the bottom right.
  • Click the URL redirect type dropdown menu and select Email address.
  • Enter the email address in the Enter email address field. Learn how to add a subject line and email body to a mailto link.
  • When finished, click Save.
Format a mailto link manually

Manually formatting mailto links is required when a mailto link isn’t added through a rich text module or a CTA (legacy).

Basic mailto link
  • A basic mailto link opens a new email message addressed to a specific recipient. Use the following format:

mailto:recipient@mydemo.test

  • Replace recipient@mydemo.test with the intended email address.
Mailto link with a subject line and email body

Mailto links can include a predefined subject line and email body. This is useful for standardizing inbound requests, such as support or sales inquiries.

  • Use these formatting rules:
    • Use ?subject= to define the subject line.
    • Use &body= to define the email body.
    • Replace spaces with %20.
  • Use the this format:

mailto:recipient@mydemo.test?subject=[email subject]&body=[email body]

  • Replace the [email subject] and [email body] placeholder values with the desired subject and email body text.
  • This is an example of a manually formatted mailto link for a sales team, including recipient, subject, and email body:

mailto:sales@mydemo.test?subject=Sales%20Inquiry&body=Hello%2C%20I%20would%20like%20to%20learn%20more%20about%20your%20product%20and%20pricing.%20Thanks

To: sales@mydemo.test

Subject: Sales Inquiry

Hello, I would like to learn more about your product and pricing. Thanks

  • For longer subject lines or email body content, consider using a mailto link generator to avoid formatting errors.

Create and customize pages

Create website and landing pages for your site to build an online presence and drive your marketing efforts. Generate personalized pages using HubSpot’s AI by entering a prompt describing your page’s purpose, goal for visitors, and Ideal Customer Profiles (ICP).

Customize page content and settings, as well as optimize pages for search engines, ensuring your content reaches the right audience.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before you begin creating and customizing pages, review these requirements and considerations.

Permissions required Edit and Publish permission is required to edit and publish pages.

Understand requirements
  • To generate pages with HubSpot’s AI, a Super Admin must toggle the Give users access to generative AI tools and features switch on in AI Settings.
  • Removing HubSpot branding from published pages requires a Content Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription. If you see an upgrade banner, you must have an active Starter subscription first. After you upgrade, the branding is removed from your pages automatically.
Understand limitations & considerations
  • Content Hub Starter includes up to 30 landing pages. After reaching this limit, no additional landing pages can be created or cloned.
  • Confirm that your domain is connected to HubSpot for publishing. If you’re using HubSpot’s free tools, your account includes a HubSpot-branded domain that’s ready for publishing.
  • Understand the different types of page template available:
    • Theme templates support drag and drop editing features, unique theme modules, and customizable theme styling.
    • Custom templates are created in the design manager, either in the layout editor or using custom code. Drag and drop editing features are only available on custom templates with drag and drop areas.

Create pages manually

Create pages manually using templates from your active theme in the content editor. You can also change the theme for the page, edit the theme, or use other templates.

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.

  • To align your pages with your brand, click Set up Brand Kit at the top of the page.

    • In the dialog box, click Add next to of Logo, Favicon, and Colors.
    • Select Save to apply the changes for each option.
    • When finished, click X to close the dialog box. Learn more about customizing your company branding.

  • In the top right, click Create a [website/landing] page. If you don’t have existing pages, click Get Started or Start from Scratch.

    • If you have existing pages, you’ll be directed to the Select a template page.
    • If you’re creating pages for the first time, you’ll be directed to the Choose a theme page before selecting a template. To select a theme, hover over a theme and click Set as active theme.

  • On the Select a template page, you can do the following:

    • To change the theme, click the name of the theme below the Search field (e.g., Theme: Elevate) on the top left.
      • On the Themes page, click Set as active theme on the theme card.
      • You’ll be directed back to the Select a template page.
    • To preview the theme, click the name of the theme below the Search field (e.g., Theme: Elevate).
      • On the Themes page, click Preview on the theme card.
      • On the preview, click the Template dropdown menu and select a template to view the theme.
      • When finished previewing the theme, click Set as active theme in the top right or click Back in the top left.
    • To preview a template, click Preview on the template card.
    • To use a template from your active theme, click the template card. Then click Edit manually.
    • To use a template that isn’t part of a theme, click Other in the left side menu.

  • In the content editor, the editing options available depend on the page’s template type and modules used. Learn more about editing pages using theme templates, global content spanning multiple pages, drag and drop areas, and rich text or image modules.

Generate pages with AI

Generate pages tailored to your goals with Hubspot’s AI. Write a prompt for the purpose of your page and the agent will generate content suggestions, including copy, images, automated forms, and meeting links.

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to generate pages with HubSpot’s AI.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
  • Align your pages with your brand.
  • In the top right, click Create.
    • If you have existing pages, you’ll be directed to the Select a template page.
    • If you’re creating pages for the first time, you’ll be directed to the Choose a theme page before selecting a template. To select a theme, hover over a theme and click Set as active theme.
  • To use a template from your active theme, click the template card.
  • In the top right, click Generate with AI. You’ll be directed to the Generate content page.
  • In the Describe your page section, enter text to describe your landing page. Include the purpose, target audience, key content, tone, and messaging for the page. Learn more using this example.
    • For help with your prompt, click the Help me prompt dropdown menu and select an example prompt (e.g., Sign up for an event) to get started.
    • Enter your specific details in the placeholder text.
  • To configure images, click the Image options dropdown menu and select an option (e.g., Use placeholder images).
  • To add supporting files, click the Add files dropdown menu and select Add files for context.
    • In the right panel, select a content type (e.g., Documents).
    • Select a file from the files tool or click Upload to upload a file from your device. Add up to five files to improve the content of your pages.
  • To add a file for downloadable content, click the Add files dropdown menu and select Add a file for downloadable content. Then select a file from the files tool or click Upload to upload a file from your device.
  • When finished, click Generate with Breeze.
  • After the page is generated, you’ll be directed to the content editor to continue customizing the page.
Example: Generate a landing page with AI

To generate a landing page with HubSpot’s AI, use the following example details:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click Create a landing page.
  • On the Select a template page, click a template card. Then click Generate with AI in the top right.
  • On the Generate content page, enter the following text in the Describe your section:

Create a landing page for existing customers that persuades visitors to book a meeting with a sales rep. It should clearly communicate how a 1:1 meeting will help them optimize their current tools and unlock additional value from their subscription. Use a friendly, expert, and confidence-building tone for visitors coming from an email nurture campaign.

Include additional options:

Add a short customer value summary at the top of the page.

Add a scheduling CTA above the fold.

Include a section outlining the top three benefits of meeting with a rep.

Add a testimonial from an existing customer.

Add a brief FAQ about what to expect in the meeting.

  • Click the Image options dropdown menu and select an option (e.g., Use placeholder images).
  • When finished, click Generate with Breeze.
  • After the landing page is generated, you’ll be directed to the content editor to continue customizing the page.

Generate landing pages with Claude

Generate pages tailored to your goals with Claude. Write a prompt for the purpose of your page and Claude will generate a landing page which can be opened and edited in HubSpot.

  • Set up the HubSpot connector for Claude.
  • In Claude, enter text to describe the landing page. Include the purpose, target audience, key content, tone, and messaging for the page.
  • Once finished, click Open in HubSpot.
  • In the dialog box, click Open link.
  • In the content editor, the editing options available depend on the page’s template type and modules used. Learn more about editing pages using theme templates, global content spanning multiple pages, drag and drop areas, and rich text or image modules.
Example: Generate a landing page with Claude

To generate a landing page with Claude, use the following example details:

  • In Claude, enter the following text in the text field.

Create a landing page for existing customers that persuades visitors to book a meeting with a sales rep. It should clearly communicate how a 1:1 meeting will help them optimize their current tools and unlock additional value from their subscription. Use a friendly, expert, and confidence-building tone for visitors coming from an email nurture campaign.

Include additional options:

Add a short customer value summary at the top of the page.

Add a scheduling CTA above the fold.

Include a section outlining the top three benefits of meeting with a rep.

Add a testimonial from an existing customer.

Add a brief FAQ about what to expect in the meeting.

  • Once finished, click Open in HubSpot.

Customize page settings

Once you’ve edited your page content, you can customize page attributes like URL, meta description, and language.

Customize basic page settings

Customize page settings, including the internal page name, page title, page URL, and meta description. You can also associate a page with a campaign.

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to associate a page with a campaign.

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.

  • Click the name of your page.

  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.

  • In the dialog box, enter an internal name in the Internal page name field. This name won’t be visible to visitors.

  • In the Page title field, enter an external name for the page. This name will appear in the tab at the top of a visitor’s web browser when the page loads.

  • In the Page URL section, click the Domains dropdown menu and select the domain where your page will be hosted. Then enter a URL slug in the Content slug field. Learn more about editing a page’s URL.

  • In the Meta description field, enter a description of the page’s content that’ll be displayed in search results. To improve the description using AI, click the artificialIntelligenceIcon Breeze icon. Learn more about generating meta descriptions using Breeze.

  • To associate the page with a campaign:

    • To associate your page with an existing campaign, click the Campaign dropdown menu and select a campaign.
    • To associate your page with your first campaign or a new campaign, click the Campaign dropdown menu and click Create campaign. Then, continue setting up your campaign.
Set the featured image

To add a featured image to be included when the page is shared on social media:

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select Featured image on the left menu.
  • Toggle the Enabled featured image switch on.
  • Click Upload to select an image from your computer, or Browse images to select an image from the files tool.
  • To increase accessibility, enter a description of your image in the Image alt text field.
Change the page template
  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select Template on the left menu.
  • To select a different template, click Use different template. If you’re switching the template of a published page, make sure to click Update to take any unpublished changes live. Otherwise, these changes may be lost when you switch the template.
  • On the Choose a template page, select a template.
  • To change the theme, click the Theme dropdown menu and select Change theme.
    • On the Choose a theme page, select a new theme.
    • To use a theme from the HubSpot Marketplace, click View themes in the Marketplace. Learn more about installing themes from the HubSpot Marketplace.
  • To see how your page will look with the new template, click Preview. Then click Use template to finish switching the template or Back to select a different template.
Set the page’s language
  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select Language on the left menu.
  • Click the Page language dropdown menu and select a language. Learn more about managing multi-language pages.
Set the page’s visibility

You can set a page’s visibility in the Audience access menu within the page settings.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select Audience access on the left menu.
  • In the Access control section, select an audience access option:
    • Select Public to make the page’s content available to any visitor.
    • Select Password required to add a required password for visitors to access the page content.
    • In a Content Hub Enterprise account, you can also select Access group membership required to require visitors to register with your site to view this content.
    • In a Content Hub Enterprise account, you can select Single sign on (SSO) required to require visitors to sign in with an identity provider, such as Google or Okta.
Set advanced page options

You can set advanced page options, like making the page a dynamic page, adding header html, or footer html code snippets. You can also manage the different stylesheets for the page.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click Settings in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select Advanced on the left menu.
  • To make this page a dynamic page, click the Data source dropdown menu in the dialog box and select a HubDB table or property. Learn more about working with dynamic pages.
  • To add code snippets to the header or footer of the page, enter your code snippet in the Head HTML or Footer HTML field. To add code snippets to all pages on a domain, access your website settings.
  • To add a custom canonical URL, enter the URL in the Customize canonical URL field. Learn more about using canonical URLs.
  • To manage the different types of stylesheets attached to the page:
    • Domain Stylesheets: these stylesheets are attached to all pages on a single domain in your website settings. To turn off domain stylesheets for a particular page, click the dropdown menu and select Disabled. Learn more about working with domain stylesheets.
    • Template Stylesheets: these stylesheets are set by the page’s template. To turn off template stylesheets for a particular page, click the dropdown menu and select Disabled. This section won’t appear for pages using theme templates.
    • Page Stylesheets: these stylesheets will only apply to this page. To attach a page stylesheet, click the Attach a stylesheet dropdown menu and select a stylesheet. If domain and template stylesheets are also used, their styling will take precedence.

Optimize pages for search engines

In the Optimize section of the sidebar editor, you can view a page’s SEO recommendations or attach it to a topic.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click the gauge Optimize icon in the left sidebar.
  • To attach the content to a topic:
    • To add an existing topic, click the Core Topic dropdown menu and select a topic for your page.
    • To create a new topic, click the Core Topic dropdown menu and select Add core topic. In the dialog box, enter the topic, then click Save
  • To attach the page to a subtopic keyword:
    • Select the Is this supporting content? checkbox.
    • Click the Subtopic keyword dropdown menu and select a subtopic keyword
    • To create a new keyword, click the Subtopic keyword dropdown menu and click Add subtopic keyword. In the dialog box, enter the subtopic keyword, then click Save.
  • To view incomplete SEO recommendations, click a category with a red circle. Each completed recommendation will have a green checkmark. Each incomplete recommendation will have a gray checkmark. Learn more about working with SEO recommendations.

Preview pages

Before publishing a page, you can preview it on different device types and test smart content and personalization. Preview links are designed to be shared internally with other users in your account; sharing them with external visitors isn’t recommended.

  • Navigate to your content:

    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.

  • Click the name of your page.

  • In the content editor, click Preview in the top right.

  • To access a full-page preview, click Open in new tab in the top right. To share this preview page with users in your account, click Copy link on the preview page. If the page is hosted on a HubSpot system domain, users must be logged into HubSpot to view this preview.

  • To preview the page on a different device, click a mobile device icon in the upper right of the preview page.

  • To preview personalization or smart content, click the Preview as dropdown menu:

    • Select Contact to preview the page’s personalization. Then click the second dropdown menu and select a contact to preview how the page would appear for that contact.
    • Select Smart rule to preview the page’s smart content. Then click the second dropdown menu and select one or more smart rules to preview how the page would appear for a visitor matching those rules.
    • To return to the page’s default appearance, click Reset.

Publish pages

Once you’ve customized your page’s content and settings, you can publish your page or schedule it for future publication:

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • To publish the page immediately, click Publish in the top right.
  • To schedule a page for later publishing:

    • In the top right, click the dropdown menu next to the Publish button, then select Scheduling options.

    • In the dialog box, click Schedule publish.

    • Click the date field and select the date when your page will be published.

    • Click the time field and select the time when your page will be published.

    • Click Schedule, Any changes you make to the page will be included in the scheduled publish.

  • To set your page to be unpublished automatically in the future:

    • In the top right, click the dropdown menu next to the Publish button, then select Scheduling options.

    • In the dialog box, click the Schedule unpublish tab.

    • Click Schedule unpublish.

    • Click the date field and select the date when your page will be unpublished.

    • Click the time field and select the time when your page will be unpublished.

    • Click the When page is unpublished, redirect visitors to dropdown menu select a page. To use an external destination URL, click Enter an external URL and enter the URL, then click Save.

    • Click Schedule.

Create and customize pages in the new editor

Create and customize pages in the new content editor. Create content with HubSpot’s AI, edit elements directly on the page, and reposition content using drag-and-drop.

The new content editor reduces the need to switch between tools or update theme files when making changes. Make updates directly within the page layout, adjust styles in one place, and preview how content appears across devices during editing.

For example, create a landing page, update text in-line, and adjust your brand styles directly in the editor. Your theme settings apply automatically and can be updated at any time from the editor.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Please note: HubSpot Credits are not required to create and customize pages in the new editor. Usage may require credits in the future.

Before you get started

Before you begin creating and customizing pages in the new content editor, review the requirements and considerations.

Understand requirements
  • A Super Admin must opt your HubSpot account into the AI-powered landing page editor (BETA) or the AI-powered website editor (BETA).
  • A Super Admin must toggle the following switches on in AI Settings:
    • Give users access to generative AI tools and features
    • CRM data
    • Customer conversion data
    • Files data
    • Give users access to Breeze Assistant

Permissions required Edit and Publish permission is required to create and customize pages in the new content editor.

Permissions required Global content and theme settings permission is required to edit global content and themes.

Understand limitations & considerations
  • Only new pages can be created and customized in the new editor. Existing pages, including drafts, will need to be customized in the legacy content editor.
  • Custom templates aren’t supported in the new content editor. To use a custom template, create or customize the page in the legacy content editor.
  • In the mobile preview, you can only resize elements and sections. To edit text or add and remove content, use the desktop view.

Create pages with AI

  • Navigate to your content:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
  • Click the Create dropdown menu and select Create with AI.
  • In the content editor, Breeze Assistant opens on the left. Enter text to describe your page’s goal, audience, and key details in the chat box. For example, enter Create a landing page to promote a free ebook, with a professional tone, and a clear call-to-action download.
  • Click the Send icon.
  • Breeze Assistant will process your request and may ask clarifying questions. For example, how to handle images if there isn’t a good match in your file manager. Select an option or type a response in the chat box.
  • Continue to customize the page.

Create pages from scratch

  • Navigate to your content:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
  • Click the Create dropdown menu and select Create from scratch.
  • In the content editor, select a starting point:
    • Clone an existing page (landing pages only): use an existing page as your starting point. Click the dropdown menu and select a page.
    • Start with a blank page: start with an empty page.
    • Use a template: select a template from the available options.
  • Click Create.
  • Continue to customize the page.

Customize pages

After creating a page, use HubSpot’s AI or the content editor to update the text, elements, layout, and theme.

  • To use HubSpot’s AI to customize your pages, click the chat box and enter a description of your changes in the bottom left of the content editor. For example, enter Try a new layout or Add a background image.
  • To customize your page manually, review the following sections.
Edit theme styles

Edit theme styles to apply consistent brand settings across the page. Changes made here will update all pages using the theme.

  • At the top of the editor, click Theme.
  • In the pop-up box on the right, hover over the applied theme and click Edit theme. To create a branded theme, click + New theme.
  • In the dialog box, click the style (e.g., Fonts or Buttons) you want to edit.
    • Fonts: select the font family, size, and weight applied to headings and body text across the page.
    • Colors: select the section color styles and the primary, neutral, and accent colors used throughout the page.
    • Elements: select the styles for interactive elements on the page, such as buttons, forms, cards, and icons. You can create up to four different styles for elements.
  • When finished, click Save theme.
Edit page text
  • To edit the text on a page, click the text on the page. Enter new text or remove the text in-line.
  • To change font color, style, or formatting, select an option from the text toolbar.
Manage sections

  • To add a new section, hover over the preview and click Add section. Enter text to describe the section for HubSpot’s AI to create or select a layout in the Browse section layouts section.

  • To resize a section, click the section and then click the drag handles to extend the section from the top or bottom.

  • To move a section to a different position on the page, click the section. Then click the upIcon Move up icon or downIcon Move down icon in the left toolbar.

  • To remove a section, click the section. Then click the deleteIcon Remove icon in the left toolbar.

Manage elements
  • To add a new element to the page, click a section and then click Add element. In the pop-up box, drag the element into position on the page.
  • To edit an element, click the element. In the toolbar, click the editIcon Edit icon.
  • To remove an element from the page, click the element and then click the deleteIcon Remove icon in the toolbar.
Edit the mobile view

The content editor displays the desktop and mobile views side by side. Use the mobile view to resize elements and sections to fit the mobile layout independently from the desktop.

  • To resize an element on mobile, click the element in the mobile view, then drag the resize handles to adjust its size.
  • To resize a section on mobile, click the section in the mobile view, then drag the section border up or down.
Hide or display elements on desktop or mobile devices

In the Layers pop-up box within the content editor, review the structure of your page and show or hide individual elements for desktop and mobile devices. This gives you control over how your page appears across different screen sizes.

  • In the content editor, click the layersIcon Layers icon on the bottom right of the page.
  • In the pop-up box, click the desktopIcon desktop or mobileIcon mobile icon to show or hide the element.

Manage page settings
