  • These metrics are affected by the attribution model selected and because of this, may vary from other metrics (e.g., Revenue from deals metric compared to the Closed revenue by source report) because they have a different attribution model.
  • It’s recommended to match the time zone in your HubSpot account and your external ad platforms to avoid discrepancies between metrics such as ad spend.
  • Metrics pulled directly from the connected ad network will always display, while metrics calculated by HubSpot will only display if the ad campaign is tracked:
    • Any metrics that are pulled directly from the ad network, such as impressions or clicks, will appear regardless of whether or not an ad campaign is tracked.
    • Metrics that are calculated by HubSpot (e.g., total contacts or cost per contact) can only be reported if the campaign is tracked.
  • It’s not recommended to compare HubSpot-specific metrics to metrics in other ad platforms, as the platforms cannot calculate them without visibility into your HubSpot account. The following metrics include: Total contacts, Cost per contact, Customers, Leads, Marketing qualified leads, Sales qualified leads, Opportunities, Deals, and Revenue.
General metrics
  • Account Name: the name of the ad account that an ad campaign is from. The account name appears below the campaign name, next to the campaign’s status. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Amount Spent: the amount of money spent on an ad during the selected time frame. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Amount Spent (Currency Converted): the amount of money spent on an ad during the selected time frame displayed in your account’s company currency. If you have a Sales Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise account or a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise account, configure a company currency in HubSpot to report on multiple currencies. Currency from your different ad accounts will be converted to your company currency.
  • Campaign Type: the campaign objective or type that was selected during campaign creation. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Click-Through Rate (CTR): the percentage of people who saw your ad and clicked on it. Calculated by HubSpot by dividing the number of clicks by the number of impressions.
  • Clicks: the number of times your ad was clicked during the selected time frame. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Total Contacts: the number of HubSpot contacts attributed to each ad during the selected timeframe. Attribution is defined by the selected attribution report. Calculated by HubSpot.
  • Cost per Contact: the amount of money spent on the ad divided by the number of attributed contacts shown in the Total Contacts column. Calculated by HubSpot.
  • Cost per session: money spent on the ad divided by the number of people who visited your website after they clicked on the ad.
  • Deals: the number of Closed Won deals associated with the attributed contacts in the Total Contacts column. Since the Total Contacts amount will vary depending on the selected attribution report, this metric will also vary based on attribution report. The below must be true to be attributed to an ad:
    • The deal stage is Closed won.
    • The deal is associated with a contact.
    • The Close date property is populated. The Close date occurs on or after the starting date of the date range applied on the Manage tab.
    • The associated contact Lifecycle stage is the HubSpot default Customer stage. If you are using a custom lifecycle stage, the deal will not be included.
    • The associated contact is attributed to an ad on the Ads dashboard.
    • The correct date range is selected. The date range is based on the deal’s Closed Won date.
  • Engagements: the number of engagements on your ad during the selected timeframe. The actions that count as engagements vary by network, but some examples include comments, likes, reactions, and shares. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Impressions: the number of times your ad was viewed during the selected timeframe. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Likes: the number of likes your ad received during the selected timeframe, if applicable. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Network conversions: the number of times the ad achieved its goal, based on how you defined a conversion when you created the campaign. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Sessions: the number of times a person visited your website after clicking on an ad. In most cases, it is expected that clicks and sessions will not match as visitor clicks may not always result in a session. For example, if a visitor clicks on an ad, but closes the window before the page loads.
Additional metrics

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to apply additional metrics.

  • Lifecycle Stages: the number of Total Contacts broken down by current lifecycle stage. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Leads: the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle Stage of Lead. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Marketing Qualified Leads: the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle Stage of Marketing qualified lead. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Sales Qualified Leads: the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle Stage of Sales qualified lead. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Opportunities: the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle Stage of Opportunity. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Customers: the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle Stage of Customer. Calculated by HubSpot.
  • Cost per deal: the amount of money spent on the ad divided by the number of Closed Won deals associated with attributed contacts. Calculated by HubSpot.
  • Cost per Lifecycle Stage: the amount of money spent on the ad divided by the number of attributed contacts that entered a certain lifecycle stage:
    • Cost per MQL: the amount of money spent on the ad divided by the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle stage of Marketing qualified lead. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Cost per SQL: the amount of money spent on the ad divided by the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle stage of Sales qualified lead. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Cost per lead: the amount of money spent on the ad divided by the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle stage of Lead. Calculated by HubSpot.
    • Cost per opportunity: the amount of money spent on the ad divided by the number of attributed contacts that currently have a Lifecycle stage of Opportunity. Calculated by HubSpot.
  • Revenue from deals: the total Amount associated with all HubSpot deals that have been attributed to your ad. Calculated by HubSpot.
  • ROI: the return on investment calculated by HubSpot. The calculation used to determine your ROI is dependent on the option you’ve selected in your HubSpot Ads settings.
Google ad group and keyword metrics
  • 1st page CPC: the cost per click for ads on the first page of Google search results. Google Ads only. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Average Position: the ad’s average position on the Google search results page. Google Ads only. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Conversion Rate: how often, on average, an ad interaction leads to a conversion. Based on the conversion events set up in your Google Ads account. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Max CPC: the max cost per click set for a specific Google ad or ad group. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Top CPC: the highest cost per click set for a specific Google ad. This information comes from the ad network.
Google asset group metrics
  • Ad Strength: how well an ad creative follows Google’s best practices for optimal performance. Typically a higher ad strength leads to better performance.
  • Amount Spent: the amount of money spent on an ad during the selected time frame. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Amount Spent (Currency Converted): the amount of money spent on an ad during the selected time frame displayed in your account’s company currency. If you have a Sales Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise account or a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise account, configure a company currency in HubSpot to report on multiple currencies. Currency from your different ad accounts will be converted to your company currency.
  • Click-Through Rate (CTR): the percentage of people who saw your ad and clicked on it. Calculated by HubSpot by dividing the number of clicks by the number of impressions.
  • Clicks: the number of times your ad was clicked during the selected time frame. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Conversion Value: the monetary value of specific actions completed by users interacting with an ad, based on how you defined a conversion when you created the campaign. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Impressions: the number of times your ad was viewed during the selected timeframe. This information comes from the ad network.
  • Network Conversions: the number of times the ad achieved its goal, based on how you defined a conversion when you created the campaign. This information comes from the ad network.

Configure sync timeframe and property mappings for your lead ads

When you connect your ad accounts to HubSpot and you want to sync leads from your lead ads, you can choose whether to sync historical leads, configure custom field mappings between your lead generation forms and the associated HubSpot properties, and review form submissions for each of your lead ad campaigns.

To connect and configure your lead syncing settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • Click the Lead syncing tab.
  • In the upper right, click Connect.
    • In the dialog box, select an ad network.
    • Select the checkbox next to the page you want to connect to HubSpot.
    • Click the Sync timeframe dropdown menu and select a timeframe:
      • All leads: HubSpot will sync all leads from the last 90 days, as well as any new leads after you connect the page.
      • New leads: HubSpot will only sync new leads.
    • Toggle the Marketing Contacts switch on or off to set your leads as marketing or non-marketing.

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Starter, Professional, or Enterprise subscription is required to set your leads as marketing or non-marketing.

  • Click Save.

Please note: the Sync timeframe option cannot be changed once you connect the page. If you need to update your timeframe preference after you connected the page, you’ll need to disconnect and reconnect the page.

Configure custom field mappings and review form submissions

You can review the connected page’s forms and customize the mappings between any custom form field and the associated HubSpot property. From the Leads tab, you can edit field mappings across multiple forms at once.

  • In the Lead syncing tab, click the page name.
  • In the right panel, under Forms, locate and click a form.
  • To change a custom field mapping:
    • Hover over the custom field and click Edit mapping.
    • Click the HubSpot property dropdown menu, then select a new HubSpot property that you want to map your custom field to.
    • Click Save.

Please note:

  • Standard properties cannot be changed.

  • Any changes to custom field mappings will only be reflected on new leads that are synced with HubSpot. Previously synced contacts will still have the old field mappings.

  • To review form submissions, click View submissions. You’ll be redirected to the Forms tool, where you can analyze your submission data.

Fix lead syncing errors

If HubSpot detects issues with any of your connected pages or their associated forms, the ad account status at the top of the ads tool will show the number of issues. You can also review and resolve errors directly from the Leads tab. Otherwise, follow the steps below.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.

  • Click the ad account status in the upper right.

  • Click to expand the Sync errors section.

  • Review and click an error to open the Lead syncing tab in your account settings.

  • Locate the page that lists a form error, then click the page name.

  • In the right panel, under Forms, click the form name of the form that needs to be fixed.

  • Under the Status column of the Field mappings table, hover over the error to see details about the issue and how to resolve it.

  • If the error is due to an issue with a field mapping, click Edit mapping to update the custom field mapping and resolve the issue.

Configure the calculation of return on investment (ROI) for paid ad campaigns

Configure your return on investment (ROI) calculation to determine how exactly you want to measure the effectiveness of your paid ad campaigns within HubSpot.

To configure the calculation of ROI for your paid ad campaigns:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • In the upper right, click the settings settings icon.
  • Click the ROI tab.
  • Configure how you want ROI to be calculated:
    • Revenue from your deals: calculates ROI based on your deals in HubSpot. The revenue will be determined by the Default deal amount settings. This option is recommended if you are using deals in HubSpot. To be included on your ads dashboard, the deal must meet both conditions:
      • The deal must be marked as closed won.
      • The deal must be associated with a contact who was attributed to your ad campaign.
        • The contact must be in the HubSpot default lifecycle stage of Customer.
        • If you are using a custom lifecycle stage as the Customer stage, the deal will not be included.
    • Estimate revenue: HubSpot estimates the ROI based on your average sale price and average contact-to-customer rate.
      • In the Average Sale Price section, enter the numerical value of your average sale price. Enter your average Contact to customer Rate as a percentage.
      • The formula for ROI estimation is: (Contacts - Customers) * Contact-to-Customer rate * Average sale price + Customers * Average sale price
  • Select a currency setting:
    • Company currency: your ad spend, ROI, and all cost-associated metrics will be converted to your default HubSpot account currency. Learn more about how to configure your account currencies.
    • Ad account currency: your ad spend, ROI, and all cost-associated metrics will use the currency from your connected ad account.
  • After updating your setting, in the bottom left, click Save.

Please note: if you use your ad account currency for your ROI calculation, you won’t be able to report across ad accounts with different currencies.

Connect and manage your Reddit Ads account in HubSpot

Connect your Reddit Ads account to HubSpot to track your Reddit ad performance alongside your other ad channels. Once connected, you can view campaign reporting in one place, see which contacts and deals are attributed to your Reddit ad campaigns, and enroll contacts that interact with your ads into workflows for follow-up.

For example, if you run Reddit ad campaigns targeting niche interest communities, you can see which campaigns brought in new contacts and track those contacts through to closed deals within HubSpot.

After connecting your account, learn how to review ads attribution in HubSpot or use campaigns with workflows.

Permissions required Account Access permissions are required to connect your ad accounts. Ads publishing permissions are also required. If this permission is granted through a permission set, update that permission set to include Ads publishing.

Please note: if you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the Reddit Ads Integration beta.

Before you get started

  • If you’ve installed an ad blocker extension in your browser, turn it off when connecting your Reddit Ads account and when using the HubSpot ads tool.
  • You must have the Admin or Creator role on your Reddit Ads account. Users with the Analyst role can connect an account, but HubSpot will not be able to apply tracking to their ads. To check your role, go to your Reddit Ads account settings.

Connect your Reddit ad account

Connect your Reddit Ads account to HubSpot. If you’re connecting your ad account for the first time, learn more about setting up your ad accounts in the ads tool.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • In the Ad accounts tab, click Connect account.
  • In the dialog box, select Reddit Ads.
  • In the pop-up window, log in to your Reddit account. Then, review the displayed permissions. HubSpot requires all of these permissions in order to integrate with your ad account. After reviewing the permissions, click Continue.
  • If you have multiple Reddit ads accounts, a list of your accounts will appear in the dialog box. Select the checkboxes next to the Reddit ads accounts you want to connect to HubSpot.
  • If you want to track contacts that interact with your ads, leave the auto tracking switch toggled on. This will apply HubSpot tracking to the Reddit ads in the account you connect.
  • Click Connect.

Manage connected Reddit ad accounts

After connecting your Reddit Ads account, all accounts you’ve connected will appear in your ads accounts settings in HubSpot. Once your Reddit Ads account is connected, you can also connect additional users so they can manage and create ad campaigns for the account.

To manage your Reddit ad account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • Hover over an ad account and click the Actions dropdown menu to:
    • View details: review additional information for your connected ad account, such as auto-tracking settings and primary users.
    • Connect Reddit user account: connect a Reddit user for this ad account. This option will be greyed out if a user has already been connected.
    • Manage access: if you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can manage access to your ad accounts. Learn more about limiting access to your HubSpot assets.
    • Move to another brand: if you have the Brands add-on, you can assign the ad account to a specific brand.
    • Disconnect ad account: disconnect your Reddit ad account.

Necessary disclosure: your use of the Reddit Ads integration is subject to the Reddit Advertising Policy. HubSpot will be able to view and manage your account and will store your Reddit Ads account ID. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions for the connected ad accounts. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts you have permissions for. Reddit will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all campaigns, ad groups, and ads in the accounts you connected.

Connect and set up your ad accounts in HubSpot

Set up HubSpot’s ads tool by connecting your Meta, Google, LinkedIn, Microsoft, or TikTok ad accounts. After connecting an account, you can select the pages or accounts to sync leads from and install pixels to track contacts from the connected ad networks.

Permissions required Ads publishing permissions are required to connect your ad accounts. If this permission is granted through a permission set, update that permission set to include Ads publishing.

Before you get started

Before connecting your ad accounts, review the requirements below. These apply whether you’re connecting your first ad account or an additional one.

  • The user must have the required access in the ad network account (e.g., Account Manager access) and must accept all requested permissions during the connection flow.

  • For Meta or shared Facebook ad accounts, each teammate must connect using their own Meta login and have the required ad account, Facebook Page, and leads access if applicable.

  • Depending on your ad account, additional requirements may apply. See the requirements for your network:

    • Facebook
    • Google
    • LinkedIn
    • TikTok

Connect and set up your ad accounts

When setting up the ads tool for the first time, connect your ad accounts, configure lead syncing, and install pixels.

  • To navigate to your ad settings:
    • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
    • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • To navigate to your ads tool:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • Select an option:
    • Connect ad network: link an existing ad account network.
    • Create ad account: sign up for a new account with an ad network.
  • Select an ad network.
  • Authenticate with your ad network log in details, then in the bottom right, click Next.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the accounts you want to connect to HubSpot, then click Next.
    • Auto-tracking is turned on by default. This appends UTM parameters to your ad URLs so HubSpot can attribute contacts and deals to specific ad campaigns.
    • For networks that support lead form ads (Meta and LinkedIn), turn on the Lead syncing toggle to pull lead form submissions directly into HubSpot as contacts. Learn more about syncing leads.
  • If you want to install pixels, select the checkboxes next to the ones you want to install.
  • Click Done.
  • After connecting your ad account, click to expand the Connected ad accounts section to review your connected accounts.
  • To connect another account, select another ad network. Then, click Sign into [ad network]. Or, click Create a [ad network] ad account.
  • After connecting your ad accounts, in the bottom left, click Next: Sync Leads.
  • Any existing lead ad campaigns for the connected ad accounts will automatically appear. Select the checkbox next to the pages or accounts that you’d like to sync. Learn more about syncing leads.
  • In the bottom right, click Next: Add Pixels.
  • Click the Pixels from your connected ad accounts dropdown menu. Any pixels for the connected ad accounts will automatically appear. Select the checkbox next to the pixels that you’d like to sync.
  • In the bottom right, click Go to ads.

In the ads tool, you can also click Learn ads to review recommended ads features and access related setup instructions.

Necessary disclosure:

  • Your use of the LinkedIn Ads integration is subject to LinkedIn’s terms and conditions. HubSpot will be able to view and manage your account, as well as store your LinkedIn Ads account number. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions on the connected ad accounts and pages. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts and pages you have permissions for. LinkedIn will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all ad campaign groups, campaigns, and ads in the ad accounts you connected.
  • Your use of the Google Ads integration is subject to the Google Ads Terms and Conditions. HubSpot will be able to view and manage your account, and will store your Google Ads account number. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions on the connected ad accounts. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts you have permission for. Google will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all campaigns, ad groups, and ads in the ad accounts you connected.
  • If you share data from your HubSpot account with Facebook as part of the HubSpot Ads integration, Facebook’s Self-serve Ad Terms will apply. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions on the connected ad accounts and pages. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts and pages you have permission for. Facebook will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all ad campaigns, ad sets, and ads in the ad accounts you connected.

Connect your Facebook ad account to HubSpot

Connect your Facebook ad account to HubSpot to create and manage your Facebook ads in the HubSpot ads tool. Before you get started, review the requirements below to connect your account.

Once you connect your account, HubSpot will display and report on all existing ad campaigns in that account.

Facebook ad account connection requirements

  • If you’ve installed an ad blocker extension for your browser, ensure it is turned off when connecting your Facebook ads account and using the HubSpot Ads tool.
  • The Facebook ad account must be active. Disabled Facebook ad accounts cannot be connected to HubSpot. If a connected Facebook ad account is disabled, it will be disconnected from HubSpot. An error will show in HubSpot next to any disabled accounts. Learn more about disabled Facebook ad accounts and how to reenable them in Facebook’s documentation.
  • The HubSpot user connecting the Facebook ad account must have Publish access to the ads tool.
  • The HubSpot user connecting the Facebook ad account must be an admin of the ad account in Business Manager. To confirm that you’re an admin of your ad account:

    • Go to your Facebook business manager.

    • In the left sidebar menu, under Accounts, click Ad Accounts.

    • Select the ad account that you want to connect to HubSpot.

    • In the right pane, click the name of your Facebook user to see all your ad account permissions.

    • Confirm that the Manage Ad Account permission switch is toggled on.

Connect your Facebook ad account

You can connect Facebook ad accounts from your HubSpot Ads settings. If you encounter any errors during the process, check out our troubleshooting guide. If you’re connecting your ad account for the first time, learn how to set up your ad accounts in the ads tool.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • In the Ad Accounts tab, in the top right, click Connect account.
  • In the dialog box, select Facebook.
  • In the pop-up window, log in to your Facebook account. Then, review the displayed permissions. HubSpot requires all of these permissions in order to integrate with your ad account. After reviewing the permissions, click Continue.
  • If you have multiple Facebook ads accounts, a list of your accounts will appear in the dialog box. Select the checkboxes next to the Facebook ads accounts you want to connect to HubSpot.
  • If you want to track contacts that interact with your ads, leave the auto tracking switch toggled on. This will apply HubSpot tracking to the Facebook ads in the account you connect.
  • Click Connect.

Manage connected Facebook ad accounts

The connected Facebook ad accounts will appear in your Ad Accounts settings in HubSpot. You can then configure additional settings or start running ads:

  • Create lead ad campaigns from within HubSpot.
  • Connect additional users so that they can create and manage ad campaigns for the account.

To manage your Facebook ad account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • Hover over an ad account and click the Actions dropdown menu to:
    • View details: review additional information for your connected ad account, such as auto-tracking settings and primary users.
    • Connect Facebook user account: connect a Facebook user for this ad account. This option will be greyed out if a user has already been connected.
    • Manage access: if you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can manage access to your ad accounts. Learn more about limiting access to your HubSpot assets.
    • Move to another brand: if you have the Brands add-on, you can assign the ad account to a specific brand.
    • Disconnect ad account: disconnect your Facebook ad account. Learn more about what happens when disconnecting your Facebook ad account.

Please note:

  • If your ad account has any outstanding billing issues, or has otherwise been disabled by Facebook for a violation of their ad policies, HubSpot will mark the ad account as Inactive. To fix this issue, you’ll need to check your Facebook business settings and Facebook’s support resources.
  • If you want to disconnect your Facebook ad account from HubSpot, it’s recommended to do so from HubSpot and not from Facebook. Disconnecting your Facebook ad account in Facebook will remove all account connections that the logged-in Facebook user has access to, including all other Facebook ad accounts that were not connected to HubSpot.

Necessary disclosure: if you share data from your HubSpot account with Facebook as part of the HubSpot Ads integration, Facebook’s Self-serve Ad Terms will apply. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions on the connected ad accounts and pages. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts and pages you have permission for. Facebook will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all ad campaigns, ad sets, and ads in the ad accounts you connected.

Connect your Google Ads account to HubSpot

Connect your Google Ads account to HubSpot to manage, track, and report on all your Google Ads campaigns in one place. Once your Google Ads account is connected, your existing campaigns will automatically appear in HubSpot’s ads tool.

Google Ads connection requirements

  • Only individual Google Ads accounts can be connected to HubSpot, not manager accounts. If your account sits under a manager account, connect it individually.
  • Cancelled Google Ads accounts cannot be connected. If a connected account gets cancelled, HubSpot will disconnect it and display an error. You can reactivate cancelled accounts through Google’s documentation.
  • Turn off any ad blocker extensions before connecting your account and while using HubSpot’s ads tool.
  • The user should have the right permissions before starting:
    • In HubSpot, the user will need Publish access to the ads tools.
    • In your Google Ads account, the user will need Admin access for that individual account. You can check the access level by clicking the Tools dropdown menu and selecting Access.

Connect your Google Ads account

Connect your Google Ads account to HubSpot. If you encounter any errors during the connection process, learn how to troubleshoot these issues. If you’re connecting your ad account for the first time, learn how to set up your ad accounts in the ads tool by following the instructions below:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • On the Accounts tab, click Connect account.
  • In the dialog box, select Google Ads.
  • In the pop-up window, log in to your Google account using the email address associated with your Google Ads account, then click Allow.
  • If your Google account has existing Google Ads accounts, they’ll appear in the dialog box. Select the ones you want to connect, then click Connect.
  • If you don’t have an existing Google Ads account, you can create one from within HubSpot:
    • In the dialog box, click Create ad account.
    • Configure your account information:
      • Ad account name: enter a name for your ad account.
      • Email address: enter the email address you used to log in to your Google account.
      • Time zone: select a timezone for your Google Ads account.
      • Currency: select a currency for your Google Ads account. This currency will be set within your new Google Ads account and cannot be changed later.
  • Click the Go to your new Google ad account settings and add your billing information link to open a new browser tab and finish setting up your account from within Google Ads.
  • After you’ve added your billing information from your Google Ads account, navigate back to the original tab and click I’ve added billing information.

Manage connected Google ad accounts

Your connected accounts will appear under your Ads account settings. From there, you can also connect additional users so they can manage and create campaigns.

To access a Google Ads account connected by a team member:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • Hover over an ad account and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Connect a Google user for this ad account. This option will be grayed out if a user has already been connected.

To manage your Google Ads account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • Hover over an ad account and click the Actions dropdown menu to:
    • View details: review additional information for your connected ad account, such as auto-tracking settings and primary users.
    • Connect Google user account: connect a Google user for this ad account. This option will be greyed out if a user has already been connected.
    • Manage access: if you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can manage access to your ad accounts. Learn more about limiting access to your HubSpot assets.
    • Move to another brand: if you have the Brands add-on, you can assign the ad account to a specific brand.
    • Disconnect ad account: disconnect your Google ad account. Learn more about what happens when disconnecting your Google ad account.

Please note: if your ad account has billing issues, policy violations, or has been inactive for a long time, HubSpot will mark it as Inactive. To resolve this, check your Google Ads account settings or visit Google’s support resources.

Manage your Google Ads connection with HubSpot’s manager account

After you connect, you’ll get an email saying your Google Ads account has been linked to HubSpot Customer MCC, HubSpot’s manager account. This link lets HubSpot monitor and track ad performance across connected accounts.

Linking your Google Ads account to HubSpot’s manager account allows HubSpot to:

  • Escalate issues regarding your account to Google.
  • Enroll you in one of Google’s ad credit offers if you qualify (see Terms and Conditions).
  • Make you eligible for beta products and other benefits that Google makes available to HubSpot customers.

Please note:

  • Linking your Google Ads account to HubSpot’s manager account is not necessary for the core contact tracking and reporting functionality in HubSpot’s ads tool. Learn how to unlink HubSpot’s manager account (HubSpot Customer MCC) from your Google Ads account.
  • If the billing in your Google Ads account is configured to default to the manager account, you may see some changes from HubSpot Customer MCC in your account. To prevent changes from occurring, ensure that your Google Ads account’s billing is set up for the account and not defaulting to the manager account.

Necessary disclosure: your use of the Google Ads integration is subject to the Google Ads Terms and Conditions. HubSpot will be able to view and manage your account, and will store your Google Ads account number. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions on the connected ad accounts. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts you have permission for. Google will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all campaigns, ad groups, and ads in the ad accounts you connected.

Connect your LinkedIn Ads account to HubSpot

Connect your LinkedIn Ads account to HubSpot to manage and analyze your LinkedIn ads in HubSpot’s ads tool. Once connected, HubSpot will display and report on all existing ad campaigns in that account.

If you encounter any errors during the process, check out our LinkedIn Ads troubleshooting guide.

Please note: to comply with LinkedIn’s legal requirements, HubSpot only reports on the most recent year of your LinkedIn Ads account data.

LinkedIn Ads connection requirements

  • LinkedIn Ads accounts that are on hold cannot be connected to HubSpot. If a connected LinkedIn Ads account is put on hold, it will be disconnected from HubSpot. An error will show in HubSpot next to any LinkedIn Ads accounts on hold. Learn more about how to remove the hold status in LinkedIn’s documentation.

  • If you’ve installed an ad blocker extension for your browser, ensure it is turned off when connecting your LinkedIn Ads account and using the HubSpot Ads tool.

  • The HubSpot user who connects a LinkedIn Ads account must have Publish access to the ads tool in HubSpot.

  • The HubSpot user who connects a LinkedIn Ads account must be an Account Manager in that LinkedIn Ads account. To check user permissions in your LinkedIn Ads account:

    • Navigate to the Campaign Manager.
    • Select your LinkedIn Ads account.
    • In the left menu, click Account settings > Manage access.

Connect your LinkedIn Ads account

If you’re connecting your ad account for the first time, learn how to set up your ad accounts in the ads tool.

To connect your LinkedIn ads account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • In the top right, click Connect account.
  • In the dialog box, select LinkedIn.
  • In the pop-up window, log in to your LinkedIn account. Review the permissions, then click Allow.
  • In the dialog box, select the LinkedIn Ads accounts to connect to HubSpot. If you want to track contacts that interact with your ads, leave the auto tracking switch toggled on. This will apply HubSpot tracking to your LinkedIn ads.
  • Click Connect.
  • In the dialog box, select the LinkedIn Ads accounts to sync leads from. Learn more about managing LinkedIn Ads accounts syncing leads to HubSpot.
  • Click Save.

Please note: if LinkedIn app permissions for HubSpot are later removed or changed, the ads tool may stop working and you may need to reconnect the account.

Manage connected LinkedIn ad accounts

After the LinkedIn Ads account has been connected, The connected LinkedIn Ads account will appear in your Ads Accounts settings in HubSpot. You can then configure additional settings or start running ads:

  • Create lead ad campaigns from within HubSpot. If you encounter any account permission issues when connecting or syncing leads from your ad account, learn how to troubleshoot your LinkedIn lead sync.
  • Connect additional users so that they can create and manage ad campaigns for the account.

To manage your LinkedIn ad account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Ads.
  • Hover over an ad account and click the Actions dropdown menu to:
    • View details: review additional information for your connected ad account, such as auto-tracking settings and primary users.
    • Connect LinkedIn user account: connect a LinkedIn user for this ad account. This option will be greyed out if a user has already been connected.
    • Manage access: if you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can manage access to your ad accounts. Learn more about limiting access to your HubSpot assets.
    • Move to another brand: if you have the Brands add-on, you can assign the ad account to a specific brand.
    • Disconnect ad account: disconnect your LinkedIn ad account. Learn more about what happens when disconnecting your LinkedIn ad account.

Please note: if your LinkedIn ad account has any outstanding billing issues, or has otherwise been disabled by LinkedIn for a violation of their ad policies, HubSpot will mark the account as Inactive. To fix this issue, check your LinkedIn ad account settings and consult LinkedIn’s support resources.

Necessary disclosure: your use of the LinkedIn Ads integration is subject to LinkedIn’s terms and conditions. HubSpot will be able to view and manage your account, as well as store your LinkedIn Ads account number. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions on the connected ad accounts and pages. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts and pages you have permissions for. LinkedIn will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all ad campaign groups, campaigns, and ads in the ad accounts you connected.

Connect your TikTok ad account to HubSpot

Connect your TikTok account to HubSpot to manage your ads and customer data in one place. In HubSpot, you can track how your TikTok ads are performing, see exactly which ads are leading to new sales, and automatically send your HubSpot contact lists to TikTok to help target your ads more effectively.

After connecting your TikTok ad account, you can create TikTok Smart+ ad campaigns in HubSpot. Learn how to create TikTok Smart+ ad campaigns in HubSpot.

Use case: Closing the attribution loop

It’s hard to tell if someone who watched your TikTok video actually bought something later. You might see “likes” on TikTok and “new customers” in HubSpot, but no way to prove they are the same people.

By linking your TikTok ad account to HubSpot, you can follow the full path: a person clicks your TikTok ad, fills out a form on your site, and eventually becomes a customer. HubSpot tracks this journey automatically, showing you exactly which videos are making money and which ones aren’t, so you know where to spend your budget.

Before you get started

Please note the following:

  • You must have Account Access permissions in HubSpot.
  • You must have an active TikTok For Business account.

Connect your TikTok ads account

To get started, you’ll need to link your TikTok For Business account to HubSpot.

If you have never used the Ads tool before:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • Click Get started with ads.
  • Click the TikTok icon and follow the authentication flow.

If you already have other ad accounts in HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar, under Tools, click Marketing, then click Ads.
  • Click Connect account.
  • Click the TikTok icon and follow the authentication flow.
  • In the Choose TikTok ad accounts dialog box, click the checkboxes next to any existing HubSpot ad accounts you want to link to your TikTok account. If you’d like to create a new one, click Create ad account.
  • To track ads for reporting and attribution, toggle the Auto tracking switch on for each ad account.
  • Click Connect accounts.

Review reporting and attribution

Once connected, your TikTok campaigns will show up in the Manage and Analyze tabs. Campaign, ad group, and ad-level reporting are available in the same places as other social networks.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • Click the Manage tab to view details about your TikTok ad campaigns. To manage a specific campaign, hover over the campaign in the table, then select View details. In the right side panel, review campaign information. Click Edit at the bottom to update information.
  • Click the Analyze tab to view metrics about your ad campaigns. Use the filters to adjust which metrics are visible. To save metrics as a report, navigate to that metric and click Save report. In the right side panel, adjust your report settings, then click Next. Select the level of access you want to grant, then click Save.

If you turned on auto-tracking when you connected your TikTok account, HubSpot will append UTM parameters to the end of your ad URL and will be able to track which contacts have interacted with your ads. From that, HubSpot will be able to calculate how many deals were made from TikTok and how much ROI they’ve resulted in.

Create a contact segment audience or lookalike audience

TikTok supports creating a contact segment audience or a lookalike audience.

  • Contact segment audiences: allow you to create an audience from a contact segment in your CRM to re-engage with contacts wherever they are online.
  • Lookalike audiences: allow you to create an audience based on your ideal customer and expand your reach to people who are more likely to convert.

To create an audience:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • In the top right, click Create, then select Audience.
  • In the right side panel, click Contact segment or Lookalike.
    • Contact segment:
      • Click the Contact segment dropdown menu to select a segment. The number of contacts that will be sent to the ad network will appear. If any contacts are not set as marketing contacts, you can add them to the send out and register them by clicking the Set all contacts as marketing contacts checkbox.
      • Click the Ad account dropdown menu to select the ad account.
      • Type the audience name.
      • Click Save.
    • Lookalike:
      • Click the Source audience dropdown menu to select a source. The ad account will appear below.
      • Click the Target location dropdown menu to select a target location.
      • Move the dial to select whether you want the audience size to be narrow or broad.
      • Click the Include source checkbox to include the source.
      • Click Save.

Add pixels

Add a pixel on your website to start tracking conversions and re-engaging people who’ve visited your website by showing them relevant TikTok ads.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar, under Tools, click Marketing, then click Ads.
  • Click the Pixels tab. From there you can select all the pixels that exist in your TikTok account, which will add them to wherever the HubSpot tracking code exists.
  • If you want to create pixels, click Add pixel in the top right.
  • In the dialog box, select TikTok.
  • Click the Pixel dropdown menu, and click the checkboxes to select your ad accounts.
  • Click Add pixel.

Create ad campaigns in HubSpot

After connecting your ad accounts to HubSpot, you can create ad campaigns for Facebook, Google, LinkedIn, ChatGPT and TikTok directly in the ads tool. Managing campaigns from one place lets you track performance, automate contact follow-up, and associate ads with your HubSpot marketing campaigns.

Permissions required Ads publishing permissions are required to connect your ad accounts. If this permission is granted through a permission set, update that permission set to include Ads publishing.

Before you get started

Before creating an ad campaign, your ad account must be connected to HubSpot. Learn how to connect and set up your ad accounts.

Facebook

After connecting your Facebook ad account, you can create the following types of ad campaigns in HubSpot:

  • Engagement ad: create ads that get visitors to interact with your content.
  • Website visit ad: promote and direct visitors to your website. You can also create a website visit ad directly from a HubSpot landing page.
  • Lead generation ad: collect visitor information using a Facebook lead form. Requires Marketing contacts access permission.

Learn how to create Facebook ad campaigns.

Google

After connecting your Google Ads account, you can create the following types of ad campaigns in HubSpot:

  • Search ad: display ads near Google search results when users search for specific keywords related to your business.
  • Performance Max (PMax) campaign: serve ads across all Google channels using a single, asset-based campaign.

You can also use AI assistants to generate ad creative for your Google search ads.

Learn how to create Google search ad campaigns.

LinkedIn

After connecting your LinkedIn ad account, you can create the following types of ad campaigns in HubSpot:

  • Website visit ad: promote and direct visitors to your website. You can also create a website visit ad directly from a HubSpot landing page.
  • Lead generation ad: collect visitor information using a LinkedIn lead gen form.

Please note: when creating a LinkedIn ad campaign in HubSpot, you can create one ad per campaign.

Learn how to create LinkedIn ad campaigns.

ChatGPT

After connecting your ChatGPT ad account, you can create a ChatGPT Chat Card in HubSpot. This is a conversational ad that is shown to visitors on ChatGPT.

Learn how to create ChatGPT Ad campaigns in HubSpot.

TikTok

After connecting your TikTok ad account, you can create a TikTok Smart+ Campaign in HubSpot. Smart+ is a TikTok ad format that automatically generates, tests, and optimizes ad combinations from your assets.

Learn how to create TikTok Smart+ ad campaigns in HubSpot.

Create ads audiences in HubSpot

Use ads audiences to control who sees your Facebook, Google, Microsoft and LinkedIn ads. In HubSpot, you can create audiences based on website visitors, HubSpot contacts, or existing audiences, and they’ll automatically sync both ways with your ad networks.

Before you get started

  • Your Facebook Ads, Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, or LinkedIn Ads accounts must be connected to HubSpot.
  • To build website visitor audiences, install your ad network tracking pixels.
  • Facebook limits each ad account to 500 total audiences.
  • Minimum audience sizes by network:
    • Google Ads: 1,000 users (Search, YouTube) or 100 users (Display, Gmail) within 30 days.
    • Facebook Ads: at least 20 users.
    • LinkedIn Ads: at least 300 members.
    • Microsoft Ads: at least 300 users.

Website visitors audience

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • Click Create audience.
  • Select Website visitors.
  • Choose your source pixel: Facebook, Google, Microsoft, or LinkedIn. Add a new pixel if needed.
  • Optionally specify which pages or URLs to include (Marketing Hub Starter+ only).
  • Select a timeframe (the default is the last 60 days, but keep in mind Google can only filter for the last 540 days), enter a name, and click Create audience.

Contact segment audience (Marketing Hub Starter, Professional, and Enterprise)

Create a contact segment audience to target ads based on your contact segments. It is recommended to use segments that include Legal basis for processing. Google and Facebook have additional advertiser conditions (Customer Match Policy, EU consent, business manager requirement).

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.. Then, click Create audience.
  • Select Contact segment, then choose your source segment. Confirm data sharing, select your ad accounts, name the audience, and click Create audience.

LinkedIn company segment audience

Sync companies from your target accounts or a company profile tier to a matched audience on LinkedIn. To set this up:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly. Then, click Create audience.
  • Select Company segment. Then, choose Target accounts or a tier.
  • Select LinkedIn ad accounts, name it, then click Create audience.

Lookalike audience (Marketing Hub Starter, Professional, and Enterprise)

Target Facebook ads to users who resemble your existing audiences.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly. Then, click Create audience.
  • Select Lookalike. Then, choose a source audience, and select target locations.
  • Click Create audience.

View and manage your ads audiences

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly. Then, click the Audiences tab.
  • Click any column header to sort by name, type, source, matched size, or ad account.
  • To remove an audience, click its name and click Delete in the right panel.

Audience matching

The Size column shows matched size, which is the number of people the ad network matched to known users. This number will typically be much lower than your total visitors or contacts.

  • Website visitor audiences: The ad network analyzes visitor cookies and matches them to known users.
  • Contact segment audiences: Matches based on contact properties like name, phone, and email.
  • Company segment audiences: LinkedIn matches based on company name, domain, and industry.

Create and sync ad conversion events with your Google Ads account

Once your Google Ads account is connected, you can create ad conversion events that sync your CRM lifecycle stage changes from HubSpot using Google’s Enhanced Conversions. This helps Google optimize your ad targeting based on contacts attributed in HubSpot’s ads tool.

You can also create new enhanced events or enhance your existing Google events with HubSpot form submissions. This uses Google’s Enhanced Conversions for more accurate conversion measurement and better ad optimization.

You can also create and sync ad conversion events with your LinkedIn Ads account or Facebook Ads account.

Before you get started

Before you create your first ad conversion event, keep the following in mind:

  • When creating a lifecycle stage ad conversion event:

    • Only lifecycle stage changes that occur after creating the conversion event in HubSpot will be counted and used to optimize the delivery of your ads.

    • After creating a conversion event in HubSpot, lifecycle stage data from contacts who engage with your ads will sync with your Google Ads account. To sync, a contact needs at least one of the following:

      • A value populated for the Google Ad click id contact property, which represents their Google Click Identifier (GCLID).
      • Contact data such as email address, phone number, or address must be shared with Google.

    • If you’ve created events for multiple lifecycle stages and a contact moves through each one, an event will sync for each stage change. For example, if you have events for the Lead and Customer stages and a contact passes through both, each stage change will sync separately.

  • If you’re using a Google Ads Manager account or My Client Centre (MCC) for form submission and conversion events, you can’t sync using Google’s Enhanced Conversions. You can still create the event in HubSpot, but the form data won’t sync. Form submission events may appear as sent in HubSpot without registering as conversions in Google Ads. Connecting the individual ad account directly does not avoid this limitation if it is still managed under an MCC.

Create ad conversion events

The number of ad conversion events you can create depends on your HubSpot subscription. Review HubSpot’s Product & Services Catalog for the most up-to-date pricing and packaging information.

  • Marketing Hub Starter: up to five events.
  • Marketing Hub Professional: up to 50 events.
  • Marketing Hub Enterprise: up to 100 events.

To create an ad conversion event using Google’s Enhanced Conversion:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • In the upper right, click Create, then select Conversion event.
  • In the right panel, customize the details for your event:
    • Ad network: the ad network the event is for. Select Google to create an ad conversion event for your Google Ads account.
    • Ad account: the Google Ads account you want to sync the event with.
    • Event trigger: select the Lifecycle stage change radio button.
    • Lifecycle stage: the HubSpot lifecycle stage specified for the event. If you want to associate the HubSpot lifecycle stage with a different lifecycle stage in your ad account:
      • Click the dropdown menu below the HubSpot lifecycle stage.
      • Then, select the corresponding ad network lifecycle stage.
    • Value: specify a monetary value for your event.
      • Native Google Ads lifecycle stage conversion events use a fixed value. The Use the Deal amount option is no longer available. Choose a representative amount, such as your average deal size, rather than each deal’s actual revenue.
      • Enter a fixed value for the lifecycle event change.
      • To use actual deal amounts for Google bidding, a developer can build a custom setup using HubSpot workflows and Google’s Offline Conversions API.
    • Consent to share data (optional): Google recommends obtaining your contacts’ consent before sharing data with third parties. If you send consent data, Google will only use consented contacts for measuring and optimizing ad events.
      • To set up the consent to share data fields with an existing property, select a property used to store consent and a property value that indicates that a contact has consented to share data.
      • If you’re setting up consent for the first time, we recommend creating a custom contact property. You can use this property to:
        • Store your contact’s consent data.
        • Use it as a consent field in your forms. When using a custom consent field, it is recommended to use this in all forms where visitors can convert. For example, you can create a single checkbox property with the label I consent that this data may be shared with third parties such as Facebook, LinkedIn, and Google.
    • Data sharing: select the checkboxes next to the HubSpot contact data that you would like to share with Google. HubSpot will use a secure one-way hashing algorithm called SHA-256 to secure customer data before sending it to Google.
      • To use Enhanced Conversions, at least one option must be selected.
      • It is recommended to select at least the default Email property for a better identity match.
    • Choose contacts to share with the network: select which contacts to share with Google.
      • All contacts that move to the selected lifecycle stage(s): syncs all HubSpot contacts who reach the selected stage. We strongly recommend this option for the best ad optimization.
      • Only contacts that move to the selected lifecycle stage(s) and have interacted with your ads: sync only HubSpot contacts that have moved to the selected lifecycle stage and interacted with your Google Ads.
    • Set the event as a primary action in Google: select the checkbox to set the event as a primary event in your Google Ads account. Select this option to report on the event in the Conversions column of your Google reports and use the event for bidding.
    • Event name: enter a name for your event.
  • If it’s your first time creating a lifecycle stage change event with Enhanced Conversions, you’ll need to turn on this setting in your Google Ads account:
    • Click Sign into Google Ads to sign in to your Google Ads account.
    • In your Google Ads account settings, click to expand the Enhanced Conversions section.
    • Click the Turn on Enhanced Conversions checkbox.
    • Click the Choose a method for setting up and managing user-provided data dropdown menu, then select Google Ads API.
    • Click Save.
  • After updating your Google Ads account settings, return to your HubSpot account.
  • Click Create event.

Create form submission ad conversion events

To create a form submission ad conversion event:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • In the upper right, click Create, then select Conversion event.
  • In the right panel, customize the details for your event:
    • Ad network: the ad network the event is for. Select Google to create an ad conversion event for your Google Ads account.
    • Ad account: the Google Ads account you want to sync the event with.
    • Event trigger: select the Form submission radio button.
    • Pixel: if you’ve previously installed a Google pixel in your HubSpot account, the pixel will display. If there isn’t one, click Add pixel to install a new Google pixel.
    • HubSpot form: select a form to use as the event trigger. Each HubSpot form can only be used as an event trigger once.
    • Accept Google’s customer data terms: this is required the first time you create a form submission ad conversion event using Google’s Enhanced Conversions for web. Click the link to your Google settings to read and accept the terms.
    • Google conversion action: select whether to create a new event or map the form submission to enhance an existing Google conversion event.
      • Create a new conversion action for this HubSpot form: select a conversion action the event should be mapped to in your Google Ads account.
      • Map HubSpot form to an existing conversion action: search and select an action from a list of existing Google conversion actions in your Google Ads account. If you’ve selected this option, it is recommended to set a value for the form submission.
    • Consent to share data: Google recommends obtaining your contacts’ consent to share data. Select a property and property value used to store and indicate a contact’s consent to share data.
    • Data sharing: select the checkboxes next to the HubSpot contact data that you would like to share with Google. HubSpot will use a secure one-way hashing algorithm called SHA-256 to secure customer data before sending it to Google.
      • To use Enhanced Conversions, at least one option must be selected.
      • It is recommended to select the default Email property for a better identity match.
    • Event name: enter a name for your event.
  • After setting up your lifecycle stage or form submission conversion event, click Create event.

Manage events in HubSpot

To review and manage your conversion events:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • Click the Events tab. You can review all conversion events.
  • If any of your conversion events have stopped syncing, a Needs Attention section appears at the top of the tab. It shows which events have stopped syncing so you can navigate directly to the affected event and resolve the issue. Events with authentication errors are flagged in red; other issues appear in yellow.
  • To disable syncing data from your HubSpot account, toggle the switch off next to the name of the corresponding event.
  • To view more details on each event, click the name of the event. In the right panel, review additional details for your conversion event and view error messages with guidance on how to fix the issue.
  • To delete an event in your HubSpot account, click the name of the event. Then, in the right panel, click Delete.
    • Deleting an event in HubSpot will not automatically delete the corresponding event in Google Ads. The event must be deleted manually from your Google Ads account.
    • If an event is created with the same details as a previously deleted event, and the conversion action name in Google Ads was not edited, the new HubSpot event will send offline conversions to the same Google Ads conversion action as before.

Review ad conversion events in Google

In Google Ads, ad conversion events are called conversion actions. Each one has an All conversions column that shows the total count of conversions.

The All conversions column only displays the attributed conversions according to your conversion action settings in Google Ads.

Enhanced Conversion events synced from HubSpot will be included in the All conversions column only if that conversion can also be attributed to a Google Ads campaign.

Please note: the All conversions total in Google Ads may not match HubSpot’s data because Google calculates each metric differently. HubSpot Support can only pull event syncing logs when there’s an error, so Support won’t be able to investigate discrepancies unless an error is present. Learn more about All conversions and conversion actions in Google’s documentation.

View and use lifecycle stage change events in your Google Ads account

Google will use the CRM lifecycle data from your HubSpot account to optimize the delivery of your ads. You’ll also be able to report on the value of your CRM lifecycle event changes from within your Google Ads account.

The CRM lifecycle event changes will sync to your Google Ads account as conversion actions. Google will use this data to optimize the bidding strategy for your ads.

  • To view the events you created in HubSpot in your Google Ads account:
    • Sign in to your Google Ads account.
    • In the upper right, click Tools & Settings.
    • In the dropdown menu, under Measurement, click Conversions.
  • To use your events when creating a Google Ad campaign:
    • In the left sidebar, click Budget and bidding.
    • Click the What do you want to focus on? dropdown menu, then select Conversions.

How your form submission data will sync with Google

After creating a form submission conversion event in HubSpot, contact data from HubSpot form submissions on your site will sync to your Google Ads account. Data such as email addresses, phone numbers, first names, last names, and street addresses will be hashed using the SHA-256 algorithm before being uploaded.

The Turn on Enhanced Conversions option in your Google conversions settings will be automatically selected within 48 hours of the first event sync from HubSpot. You do not need to turn this on manually.

HubSpot adheres to the following process when sending data for Google’s Enhanced Conversions. This information will be configured by HubSpot, and you will not need to take any action. For reference, the process for sending data for Enhanced Conversions is similar to other Google conversion adjustments. Keep the following key differences in mind when populating the ConversionAdjustment:

  • order_id is required.
  • adjustment_type must be ENHANCEMENT.
  • conversion_action must be the resource_name of a ConversionAction with a type of WEBPAGE and Enhanced Conversions enabled.
  • user_identifiers must contain between one and five identifiers. Enhancements support the following identifiers:
    • hashed_emailers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/conversions/upload-adjustments
    • hashed_phone_number
    • address_info
  • user_identifier_source of each identifier is optional.
  • gclid_date_time_pair with conversion_date_time is optional but recommended. Set this to the date and time at which the conversion with the specified order_id occurred. Include the time zone offset and use the format yyyy-mm-dd HH:mm:ss+|-HH:mm. For example: 2022-01-01 19:32:45-05:00, ignoring daylight saving time. Setting the gclid of the gclid_date_time_pair is optional.
  • user_agent is optional but recommended. This should match the user agent of the request that sent the original conversion so the conversion and its enhancement are either both attributed as same-device or both attributed as cross-device.
  • restatement_value with adjusted_value and currency_code is optional but recommended.

In addition, you must upload the enhancement adjustment within 24 hours of the original conversion for the order_id. To avoid errors due to differences in clock times, upload the adjustment no later than several minutes before the end of the 24-hour period.

Please note: your use of our Google Ads integration is subject to the Google Ads Terms and Conditions and our Customer Terms of Service. By using our Google Enhanced Conversions feature, you authorize us to provide necessary data to Google in order to make this functionality available to you; you also agree to comply with Google’s Customer data policies and Customer Data Terms. Please review Google’s Customer data policies carefully as they contain examples of where you can collect customer data, requirements, restrictions on measurements in sensitive categories, ramifications for violations of these policies, and user choice and control. Please note that your legal team is the best resource to give you advice on how to comply with these policies.

HubSpot will be able to view and manage your account, and will store your Google Ads account number. When you authorize the integration, HubSpot receives a user token with permissions on the connected ad accounts. HubSpot can view but does not store all the ad accounts you have permission for. Google will share settings details (e.g., name, budget, bid strategy, creative) and performance metrics (impressions, clicks, etc.) for all campaigns, ad groups, and ads in the ad accounts you connected.

Create and sync ad conversion events with your LinkedIn Ads account

After connecting your LinkedIn Ads account to HubSpot, you can create new events and update existing events to use LinkedIn’s Conversions API. This will allow the ad network to optimize the delivery of your ads when a contact lifecycle stage is updated in HubSpot, as well as strengthen performance and privacy.

You can also create and sync ad conversion events with your Google Ads account or Facebook Ads account. In the Conversion Events tab, you can also view and manage your conversion events, including syncing status and error details.

Before you get started

Before getting started with ad conversion events, do note the following:

  • Only updates to records’ lifecycle stages that occur after creating the conversion event in HubSpot will be counted and used to optimize the delivery of your ads.
  • LinkedIn can ingest ad conversion events that happen within the last 90 days. Ad conversion events are then attributed to ads within the configurable attribution lookback window, which defaults to 90 days from an ad click or view event. For example, if your contact clicked a LinkedIn ad on January 1, 2022, but didn’t change to an SQL until June 1, 2022, that contact won’t be counted because it is outside the 90-day window.
  • LinkedIn also supports a longer 365-day attribution lookback window for certain conversion types, as documented in their help article, LinkedIn Conversions FAQ. This setting isn’t configurable within HubSpot, but after the conversion is created, you can adjust it directly in LinkedIn Campaign Manager.
  • When creating a LinkedIn conversion event, HubSpot will send the following data to LinkedIn:
    • Email address (hashed)
    • First name
    • Last name
    • Title
    • Company
    • Country
    • Click ID (hidden; enabled by default)
    • Lead ID (hidden; enabled by default)
    • If the contact has clicked on a LinkedIn ad, HubSpot will send Lifecycle stage data to LinkedIn.

Create ad conversion events

The number of ad conversion events you can create depends on your HubSpot subscription. Please review HubSpot’s Product & Services Catalog for the most up-to-date pricing and packaging information.

  • If you have a Marketing Hub Starter subscription, you can create up to 5 ad conversion events.
  • If you have a Marketing Hub Professional subscription, you can create up to 50 ad conversion events.
  • If you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can create up to 100 ad conversion events.

To create an ad conversion event using LinkedIn’s Conversion API:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.

  • In the upper right, click Create event.

  • In the dialog box, configure the details for your event:

    • Ad network: the ad network the event is for. Select LinkedIn to create an ad conversion event for your LinkedIn ads account.

    • Ad account: the LinkedIn Ads account you want to sync the event with.

    • Lifecycle stage: the HubSpot lifecycle stage specified for the event. The HubSpot lifecycle stage will be automatically associated with the matching conversion type in LinkedIn. To associate the HubSpot lifecycle stage with a different LinkedIn conversion type, edit the conversion rule in LinkedIn.

    • Value: specify a monetary value for your event (this is how much each event is worth to you).

  • In the bottom right, click Next: Data sharing settings.

  • In your Data sharing settings, configure the following:

    • Consent to share data: LinkedIn recommends obtaining your contacts’ consent to share data with third parties such as LinkedIn. If you choose to send consent data, only contacts with consent will be used by LinkedIn in the measurement and optimization of ad events. This field is optional.
      • To set up the consent to share data field with an existing property, select a property used to store consent and a property value that indicates that a contact has consented to share data.
      • If you’re setting up consent for the first time, it is recommended to create a custom contact property. You can use this property to:
        • Store your contact’s consent data.
        • Use it as a consent field in your forms. When using a custom consent field, it is recommended to use this in all forms where visitors can convert. For example, you can create a single checkbox property with the label I consent that this data may be shared with third parties such as Facebook, LinkedIn, and Google.
    • Data sharing: select the checkboxes next to the HubSpot contact data to share with LinkedIn. HubSpot will use a secure one-way hashing algorithm called SHA256 to secure contact email addresses before sending to LinkedIn.
      • To use LinkedIn’s conversion API, at least one option must be selected.
      • It is recommended to select all available user identifiers, including the default Email, First name, and Last name properties, for the optimal identity match.
    • Choose contacts to share with network: select which contacts to share with LinkedIn.
      • All contacts that move to the selected lifecycle stage(s): sync all HubSpot contacts that have moved to the selected lifecycle stage. It is strongly recommended to use this option to provide the best ad optimization.
      • Only contacts that move to the selected lifecycle stage(s) and have interacted with your ads: sync only HubSpot contacts that have moved to the selected lifecycle stage and interacted with your LinkedIn Ads.
    • Event name: the name of your event.

  • At the bottom, click Create event.

Please note: after the new conversion event has been created, the LinkedIn conversion status will be set to Unverified until data has synced from HubSpot to LinkedIn. After a conversion event has synced, the LinkedIn conversion status will appear as Active. Learn more about the different LinkedIn conversion statuses.

Update lifecycle stage change ad conversion events to use LinkedIn’s Conversions API

Replace your existing LinkedIn lifecycle stage events to use LinkedIn’s new Conversions API. When replacing your events, existing lifecycle stage events will automatically be deleted. You can also update your event details. This new event will use LinkedIn’s Conversions API.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.
  • Click the Events tab. You can review all conversion events.
  • To replace an existing LinkedIn event with one that uses LinkedIn’s Conversion API, click Replace event.
  • By default, the details from your existing event should automatically populate. In the right panel, continue setting up your new event.

Manage events in HubSpot

To review and manage your conversion events:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Ads. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Ads directly.

  • Click the Events tab. You can review all conversion events.

  • To disable syncing lifecycle data from your HubSpot account, click to toggle the switch off next to the name of the corresponding event.

  • To delete an event in your HubSpot account, click the name of the event. Then, in the right panel, click Delete.

  • To view more details on each event, click the name of the event. In the right panel, review additional details for your conversion event.

Please note: the total events in LinkedIn ads is not expected to match the data in HubSpot due to LinkedIn’s requirements for how each metric is calculated. In addition, HubSpot support cannot pull event syncing logs unless there is an error with the event. This means, unless there is an error, we will not be able to identify why discrepancies between HubSpot and LinkedIn events are occurring.

Create and sync ad conversion events with your Meta Ads accounts using Meta’s Conversion API

After connecting your Meta Ads account, you can create events using Meta’s Conversion API to sync your CRM lifecycle stage changes or form submissions from HubSpot.

You can also create and sync ad conversion events with your LinkedIn Ads account or Google Ads account. In the Conversion Events tab, you can also view and manage your conversion events, including syncing status and error details.

Before you get started

Before getting started with ad conversion events, do also note the following:

  • Only form submissions and lifecycle stage changes that occur after creating the conversion event in HubSpot will be counted and used to optimize the delivery of your ads.
  • You can only create ad conversion events using forms you created in HubSpot. Submissions from non-HubSpot forms cannot be synced with Meta.
  • You must have a Meta pixel installed in your HubSpot account.

    • Connecting your pixel turns on standard browser tracking through Meta’s Conversions API. As such, it is recommended to only install the Meta pixel via HubSpot. If you have previously added the pixel code in your website’s header or footer HTML, please remove the manually installed code. Otherwise, this can result in duplicate events and inconsistent data in your reporting.

    • HubSpot will send both server and browser events for the pixel to allow Meta to deduplicate these events. Learn more about server and browser events.

  • Clicking the Add pixel button will immediately add the pixel to all pages that include the tracking code.
    • It is not currently possible to limit which pages/domains the pixel is added to.
    • Data, such as page views, will start syncing to Meta immediately, even if no conversion events are created.
  • To create conversion events for Meta, your ad account must be part of a Business Manager Account. Learn how to add your ad account to Business Manager in Meta’s Help Center.
