To create a report of the top campaigns by total influenced contacts, create a report with the following configuration:

  • Data sources: Contacts as Primary data source and Campaigns as Secondary data source.
  • Chart type example: Horizontal bar
  • X-axis: Campaign - Campaign name. It’s recommended you click Edit field and sort by Descending.
  • Y-axis: Count of contacts
Asset type or channel mix by campaign

To break down the asset type or channel mix by campaign, use the following report configuration:

  • Data source: Campaigns as Primary data source.
  • Chart type example: Table
  • Columns:
    • Campaign - Campaign name
    • Campaign - Number of Ad Campaigns
    • Campaign - Number of Blog posts
    • Campaign - Number of CTAs
    • Campaign - Number of Emails
    • Campaign - Number of Forms
    • Campaign - Number of Landing pages
    • Campaign - Number of Lists
Companies influenced by campaign

To create a report to analyze a count of the companies influenced by each campaign, create a report with the following configuration:

  • Data sources: Campaigns as Primary data source and Companies as Secondary data source.
  • Chart type example: Pivot table
  • Rows:
    • Campaign - Campaign name
    • Campaign Influence - Asset type
  • Values: Count of companies

Review and manage campaign associations using CRM cards

Use the Campaigns card to manually associate a contact, deal, or ticket with a campaign directly from the record. Contacts associated with a campaign will be included in the campaign’s influenced contacts.

You can use this feature to manually associate a record if an engagement isn’t captured automatically. For example, during an event check-in or a conversation at a convention booth.

After manually associating records using CRM cards, you can review all manually associated records from the campaign’s performance page.

Add contacts to a campaign using the Campaigns CRM card

Permissions required Edit association permissions are required to create associations using the Campaigns CRM card.

  • Navigate to your record:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Tickets. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Tickets directly.
  • On the contact index page, locate the contact and click the contact name.
  • In the right panel, locate your Campaign card and click the + Add.

.

  • In the right panel, click the Marketing campaign dropdown menu and select the campaign that you’d like to associate with your contact.
  • If you’re associating a contact record to a campaign, you can also add an influence type. This option is not available when associating deals or tickets from CRM cards.
    • Click the Influence type dropdown menu and select an influence type. To create a new custom event:
      • From the dropdown menu, click Create new influence type. You can create up to 50 influence types.
      • Enter a name for your influence type.
      • At the bottom, click Save.
  • At the bottom, click Save. After adding your campaign, the campaign will appear on the campaign card. Only manually associated campaigns will appear on the campaign card.

Please note: once a contact is marked as influenced, that influence cannot be removed from the total influence count. Learn more about your campaign metrics.

Review a record’s associated campaigns

  • Navigate to your record:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Deals. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Deals directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Tickets. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Tickets directly.
  • On the re index page, locate the contact and click the record name. Then, in the right panel, locate your Campaign card.
  • To search for a specific campaign, click the search icon. Then enter your campaign name, For example, you may want to check if a specific campaign has been associated with the record.
  • To sort your campaign, click the Sort dropdown menu and select Campaign name, Object create date/time, or Association Label.
  • If you’re reviewing and managing contact associations, the following additional options will appear:

    • To filter the campaigns by influence type, click Filters. Then, click the Association label dropdown menu and select an influence type.

    • To change your contact’s influence type, click pencil icon next to the campaign name.

    • To review your contact record’s campaign influences:

      • Click View all campaigns.
      • In the right panel, you can review the campaigns, and count of campaign influences that influenced the contact.
      • To review the influences in detail, click the campaign name or number of influences. In the dialog box, you can review the timestamp, the asset type, and asset name that influenced the record.

Please note: the total count reflects campaigns that influenced this contact, either through engagement with campaign assets or manual association. Each entry includes the campaign name, the type of engagement, and when it occurred.

Review your campaigns card

By default, the campaigns card will appear in your contact records. However, if you’ve previously customized your contacts CRM view or you’re unable to find the card on your records, you can manually add the campaigns card to the record view. Learn more about customizing records.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Objects, then select the Contacts.

  • At the top, click the Record Customization tab.

  • To edit the default view, click Default view. Or, select a team view. In the right column, check for the Campaigns card.

  • If the campaign card is not appearing, to add a Campaigns card:

    • Hover over of the section that you’d like to add the card, then click the + Add icon.
    • In the right panel, click the Card library tab.
    • Search for the Campaigns card. Then, click + Add card.
    • In the top right, click the X icon to close the panel.

  • After setting up your Campaigns card, click Save and exit.

Review and manage your campaign calendar in Marketing Studio

Use the marketing calendar in Marketing Studio to keep track of marketing events such as campaigns and tasks. You can also create and edit tasks directly from the marketing calendar.

Permissions required Super Admin or Campaign permissions are required to review and manage the campaign calendar in Marketing Studio.

Review your campaign schedule in calendar view

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Marketing Studio.

  • At the top, click the Calendar tab.

  • To filter your calendar by different event types, at the top, click the All calendar events, My tasks, My campaigns, or Marketing email tab. You can also create your own custom views.

  • In the top left, select and apply your filters:

    • Statuses: filter your calendar events by the status of your event. For example, to review your upcoming campaigns, you may want to filter by scheduled events only.
    • Asset types: filter your calendar events by type of event. For example, you can filter to display blog posts or social posts only. The full list of available event types for the marketing calendar will also appear.
    • Campaigns: filter your calendar events by their associated campaign.
    • Owners: filter your calendar events by the user that owns the associated asset.

  • To change your calendar view, in the top right, select Month, Week, or Day. To view a chronological list of all calendar events in a month, click List.

  • To automatically navigate to today’s date, in the top left, click Today.

  • To navigate between different months, weeks, or days in the calendar, above the calendar, click the leftright arrow icons.

  • To create a new task in the marketing calendar:

    • In the top right, click the dropdown menu and select the Month view.
    • Hover over a date in the calendar, then click the add plus icon. The date selected will be automatically set as the Due date for the task.

  • To view the overall details of a calendar event, click the name of the event in the Marketing calendar. You can view and update details in the pop-up box.

    • To edit the calendar event in the tool’s editor, click Edit.
    • To view more details of the calendar event directly in the tool, click Details.

Please note: the events displayed in the marketing calendar are dependent on a user’s permissions. For example, a user without any social publishing permissions would not be able to view any social posts on the calendar

Review campaign activity history

From the Activity tab of your campaign’s details page, you can review the past events and activities that have occurred in a HubSpot campaign.

Permissions required Super Admin or Campaign permissions are required to use the campaigns tool.

Review your campaign activity history

Activities will be grouped by date, time, and the user who performed the activity. When changes are made by the HubSpot system, it will be logged as HubSpot updated this campaign.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Campaigns. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Campaigns directly.
  • Click on a campaign.
  • At the top, click the Activity tab.
  • To create an AI summary of all activities, click Summarize activity. A summary of activity history appear in the Breeze Assistant panel.
  • From the Activity tab, you can filter your campaign activity with the following:
    • All activities: filter by the type of activity performed, such as commenting, adding an asset, and more.
    • All users: filter by the HubSpot user that performed the activity. To filter by changes made by the HubSpot system, select HubSpot.
    • Date range: filter by the date that the activity occurred.
  • To see more details for each activity, click to expand x updates.

Please note: if you’ve you filtered your activity history by activity type, you will not be able to summarize your activity. The Summarize activity option will be greyed out.

Review campaign assets and content in Marketing Studio

From the Assets tab in Marketing Studio, review all assets and content in your HubSpot account. This includes assets that may or may not be associated with a campaign.

When reviewing your assets, you can filter for a specific subset of assets and content. For example, you may want to view all forms associated with a specific summer campaign, or all marketing emails in your account. Learn more about the asset types that can be associated with campaigns in HubSpot.

Review campaign assets and content in Marketing Studio

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Marketing Studio.

  • At the top, click the Assets tab.

    • All assets in your HubSpot account will appear in the table, including assets that may not be associated with a campaign.
    • In the table, you can review details such as the asset’s associated campaign, owner, current status, and when the asset was last updated.

  • At the top left, you can filter your assets by any of the following:

    • Brands: if you have the brands add-on, filter by assets associated to a specific brand.
    • Status: filter by the asset’s current status. You can filter by the following statuses: Draft, Scheduled, Published, Archived, or Unknown.
    • Asset types: filter by the asset type. For example, you may want to see all forms associated with campaigns in your account.
    • Campaigns: filter by assets associated to a specific campaign. For example, you can filter by assets for a conference event.
    • Owners: filter by the HubSpot user that owns a specific asset.

  • To clear all filters from your assets view, at the top, click Clear all.

  • To navigate to a specific asset, click the asset name. For example, if you’ve selected a workflow, you’ll be automatically redirected to the workflow’s performance page.

  • To take actions on assets in bulk, click the checkboxes next to the asset name. Or, click the checkbox in the top left of the table to select all assets on the page. Then, select from the following:

    • Clone: clone the selected assets.
    • Archive: archive the selected assets. The archived assets will still exist with an archived flag in the CRM for a limited time, but will no longer show up on the asset’s index page.
    • Add to campaign: add the selected assets to a specified campaign.

Review individual campaign performance in Marketing Studio

After creating your campaign in Marketing Studio, you can access and review your individual campaign performance from your campaign details page. You can also review the performance of individual campaign assets such as forms or marketing emails from directly within Marketing Studio.

Permissions required Super Admin or Campaign permissions are required to review and manage campaigns in Marketing Studio.

Review the performance of an individual campaign

After creating your campaign with Marketing Studio, to review your campaign performance:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Marketing Studio.
  • In the table, click the campaign that you’d like to analyze. You’ll be automatically redirected to the campaign details page.
    • When reviewing assets in your performance page, published assets will appear in the assets section of the performance page.
    • Campaign assets that have not been published yet, such as draft social posts, draft emails, etc, will not appear.
  • In the top right, click Analyze campaign. You’ll be automatically redirected to the Analyze tab filtered to the specific campaign.

Please note: to access your overall campaign analytics, use the global search bar to search for campaign analytics.

Review the performance of individual assets in Marketing Studio

After creating your campaign with Marketing Studio, to review your campaign performance:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Marketing Studio.
  • In the table, hover over the campaign and click theverticalMenuIconthree vertical dots icon next to the campaign. Then, click Edit in canvas.
  • Click the asset card of the asset that you’d like to review.
  • In the dialog box, click the Performance tab. Associated metrics for the asset will appear.
  • To review the metrics directly in the tool, click View performance. For example, if you’d like to review marketing email metrics from the marketing email’s performance page.

Troubleshoot individual campaign influenced contacts

When reviewing your individual campaign performance, if the expected number of influenced contacts does not correspond with the number of interactions in your asset list, it may be due to contact interaction occuring before the asset was associated with the campaign.

Influences contacts in a campaign will only appear if the interaction happens after the asset is associated with the campaign. Influences contacts will not be associated with the asset retroactively.

If you would like to include contacts that were influenced before the asset was associated with the campaign, create a segment and associate this segment with the campaign. This will attribute these contacts to the campaign from the list association.

Review the performance of multiple campaigns

From the campaigns tool or Marketing Studio, you can review the performance of multiple campaigns at once. You’ll be able to review reports for the performance of selected specific campaigns, or all campaigns in a specific folder.

For example, you may want to review the performance of campaigns by a specific user, or review how different types of campaigns have performed.

Please note: to access multi-campaign reporting from the campaigns tool, you’ll need to opt-in to the Multi-campaign reporting beta.

Select your campaigns for review

You can select your campaigns for review from the campaigns table in the Manage tab or from specific folders in the campaigns tool or Marketing Studio.

Review the performance of multiple campaigns
  • You can navigate to the Manage tab from both the campaigns tool or Marketing Studio:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Campaigns. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Campaigns directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Marketing Studio.
  • At the top, click the Manage tab.
  • In the table, select the checkboxes next to the campaigns you want to analyze.
  • At the top of the table, click Analyze campaigns. You’ll be automatically redirected to the Analyze tab to review your aggregated campaign reports.
Review the performance of a specific folder
  • You can navigate to your folders the campaigns tool or Marketing Studio:
    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Campaigns. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Campaigns directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Marketing Studio.
  • At the top, click the Manage tab.
  • In the top right, click Folders to navigate to your campaign folders.
  • In the left sidebar menu, select the folder that you want to analyze.
  • In the top right, click Analyze folder campaigns. You’ll be automatically redirected to the Analyze tab to review your aggregated campaign reports.

All campaigns in the folder will be automatically included in the multiple campaigns reports. If the folder includes any subfolders, campaigns in the subfolders will be included as well.

Filter your multiple campaign reports

After selecting your campaigns, you’ll be redirected to the Analyze tab in your campaigns tool. If you’ve selected a folder or specific campaigns from the campaigns table, the campaigns will be automatically selected. You can also select campaigns directly from the filters.

  • You can navigate to the Analyze tab from the campaigns tool or Marketing Studio:

    • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Campaigns. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Campaigns directly.
    • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > Marketing Studio.

  • At the top, click the Analyze tab.

  • At the top, you can filter the data for your reports:

    • Campaigns: select or edit the selected campaigns for your reports.
    • Date range: adjust the date range for your data. By default, this will be set to Date range (This year).
    • Attribution model: select the attribution model for your reports. By default, this will be set to Attribution model (Linear).

Understand your multiple campaign reports

You can review the following reports:

  • Campaign goals: review the campaign goal name, goal type, percentage progress, and status. Goal data is not aggregated and will be displayed seperately for each campaign.
  • Revenue attribution: review an aggregated overview of the campaign’s revenue attribution. This includes the campaign spend total, attributed revenue, ROI, deals, and contacts.
  • Contact lifecycle: review the aggregated count of contacts in each lifecycle stage for your selected campaigns.
  • Website traffic: review the total count of sessions, new contacts (first touch), and new contacts (last touch), for the selected campaigns.
  • Total influenced contacts: review the total number of unique marketing influences for your influenced contacts aggregated across the selected campaigns.
  • Influenced contacts over time: review the count of influenced contacts for each individual campaign, as well as the aggregated count of influenced contacts over time for the selected campaigns.
  • Specific asset reports: review the aggregated data for different asset types. The metrics in each report vary depending on the asset or content type associated with the campaign.

Understand Campaigns

Whether you’ve just started marketing with HubSpot or you’ve been using Hubspot for some time, the campaigns tool can help you organize and keep track of your efforts in one place. You can also create campaigns using Marketing Studio (BETA).

The term campaigns may be used with or in reference to other tools outside of HubSpot. Learn more about the differences between HubSpot campaigns and other campaigns.

Permissions required Super Admin or Campaign permissions are required to use the campaigns tool.

What is a campaign?

In HubSpot, a campaign is an organized, strategic effort to promote a specific goal. The HubSpot Campaigns tool helps you create, manage, and report on a single marketing campaign using multiple assets in one place. For example, you can create a campaign to use social posts and ad campaigns to raise awareness of a new product or an event.

After setting up your campaign, you can track the performance of these assets collectively or individually in the campaigns tool.

What are campaign assets?

Campaign assets refer to the added content used as part of the organized strategy to market a campaign. Review the full list of assets that can be added to a campaign in HubSpot.

In HubSpot’s Campaigns tool, you can organize and tag assets like blog posts, social posts, and more. These assets should all correspond to the campaign and work toward achieving the campaign goal. For example, you can have a series of marketing emails and social posts directed to the same landing page to encourage visitors to sign up for a webinar.

Strategizing your campaign

Before setting up your campaign, it is recommended to plan your overall campaign goals and how you want to measure the success of your campaign. Use specific and measurable metrics to keep track of your goal attainment. Learn more about campaign metrics.

Some common goals and result pairings include:

Goal

Strategy

Reviewing results

Increasing the number of leads for your sales team

You can use the following templates when setting up your campaign:

  • Lead generation
  • Email drip campaign

When reviewing the overall campaign, use metrics such as:

  • New contacts
  • Influenced contacts

You can set goals for specific intervals such as:

  • 15 influenced contacts a week
  • 5 new contacts a week

You can also set goals for the overall campaign:

  • 100 total influenced contacts during the campaign period

Increasing awareness of a product or brand

You can use the following templates when setting up your campaign:

  • Product launch
  • In-person event promotion
  • Online event promotion

When reviewing the overall campaign, use metrics such as:

  • Sessions
  • New contacts

When looking at the success of specific assets, use engagement metrics such as:

  • Page views
  • Social interactions
  • Opens and clicks on your marketing emails

You can set goals for specific intervals such as:

  • 1000 sessions a month
  • 15 new contacts a month

You can also set goals for the overall campaign:

  • 5000 sessions during the campaign period
  • 200 new contacts from the campaign

Campaign Templates

If you want to use HubSpot for marketing but don’t know where to start, or what kind of content you want to add to your campaign, you can use one of HubSpot’s campaign templates.

HubSpot currently provides 12 templates to achieve your campaign goals:

  • Abandoned cart: target customers that have abandoned their shopping carts and encourage them to complete their purchase with automated emails and ad campaigns.
  • Email drip campaigns: nurture relationships with your customers through automated emails.
  • In-person event promotion: attract attendees to your in-person event, such as a conference or trade show through various marketing efforts, such as automated emails, social posts, and ad campaigns.
  • Internal newsletter: inform your team and stakeholders through internal newsletters via automated emails promoting blog posts.
  • Lead generation: attract visitors and generate qualified leads across multiple channels such as emails, ad campaigns, and social posts.
  • Loyalty program: encourage customers to sign up for a loyalty program and nurture the relationship between your brand and customers. This campaign uses landing pages, emails, CTAs, social posts, and ad campaigns.
  • Nurture: build customer relationships, increase engagement, and guide prospects toward conversion using emails, ad campaigns, and social posts.
  • Onboarding & welcome: onboard new customers and welcome them to your brand with personalized messages through emails and dedicated website pages.
  • Online event promotion: attract attendees by promoting your online event, such as a webinar (through event integrations).
  • Product launch: introduce your new products or services using landing pages, emails, CTAs, social posts, and ad campaigns.
  • Product sales: generate sales, increase revenue, and promote your products or services using landing pages, emails, CTAs, social posts, and ad campaigns.
  • Re-engagement: connect and nurture cold leads to encourage renewed engagement and interaction using automated emails and social posts.

Campaign tasks

Stay organized and keep track of your campaign. If you have a team, keep track of the progress of your team members. You can also use the Tasks tab in the campaigns tool to keep track of what you need to do. Here are some examples:

  • If you’re using a campaign template, a number of tasks will have been created for you. Use the tasks view to check off each task, whether it’s creating a blog post or a new landing page.
  • If you’re managing a team, you can create and assign tasks from the task view. You can also keep track of the progress of the different tasks to keep agile, prevent duplicate work, and optimize your team.

Campaign calendar

Within the campaigns tool, you can review each week, month, or day of your campaign on the campaign calendar. After creating your campaign, it is recommended to use the marketing calendar to ensure that you have content consistently published.

During certain months like December, the campaign calendar is especially useful to run events such as an advent calendar giveaway.

In addition to keeping track of you and your team’s work, you can use the marketing calendar to share information on the campaign’s execution with other stakeholders.

Additional information

If you’re using the campaigns tool for the first time:

  • Use templates to get started on your first campaign. If you’re not sure which to use, it is recommended to start with the Lead generation template.
  • Use the marketing calendar to ensure that you’re posting content on a regular schedule.

If you want to speed up your campaign management processes:

  • Use the tasks views to keep track of the progress of work across different teams.
  • Use the calendar to take note of key holidays to plan your campaigns.
  • Create your own campaign templates for you and other members of your team to use.
  • Customize the campaigns form for the more important campaign properties.

Using the campaigns tool

  • Creating your campaign
  • Associating assets with a campaign
  • Track the performance of your campaigns
  • Campaign metrics

Understand Loop Marketing

Loop Marketing is a four stage framework that helps marketers grow in the AI era. Unlike traditional linear marketing approaches, Loop Marketing is designed for a world where buyers research with AI, get answers before clicking, and discover solutions across scattered channels like TikTok and podcasts.

With Loop Marketing, marketers can use AI to become more efficient and drive better results through human-driven strategy and creativity, and AI-driven execution and optimization. When using the Loop Marketing framework, use Breeze to:

  • Express your story: work with AI to create campaigns based on your objectives, informed by your brand style guide and ideal customer profile.
  • Tailor your approach: build audience segments, enrich your data, and make content personal.
  • Amplify your reach: build, optimize, and activate your content for humans and answer engines across channels like YouTube, social, ads, creator feeds, and more.
  • Evolve your strategy: monitor real-time performance, run experiments, and tweak campaigns to match your needs.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Understand prerequisites

Subscription required A Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use data enrichment.

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use brand identity, data agent, and buyer intent.

Subscription required A Data Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use Data Studio.

To effectively implement the Loop framework, complete the following foundational tasks.

  • Set up Breeze Assistant: throughout the framework, Breeze Assistant will be used to generate insights and content. Suggested prompts will also be provided.
    • Before getting started with Loop Marketing, you must set up Breeze Assistant and provide user permissions for the relevant tools. For example, to create campaigns in the express stage, users will need Campaign Edit permissions.
    • It is also strongly recommended to create a project for Loop Marketing and a knowledge vault to provide any additional context on your brand.
    • It is strongly recommended to review AI outputs throughout the process. Flagging any patterns of errors will help to refine your style guide and prompts.
  • Define your audience: use Breeze Assistant or the HubSpot Connectors for ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini (BETA) to summarize CRM data from your highest-value customers to create an audience profile. This will be used when setting up your brand identity and reviewing your data layer.
    • Suggested prompt: tell me about our most successful customers. What are the biggest pain points that leads have expressed in their intake forms? Give me the history of our best deals.
  • Craft a style guide and use it in HubSpot: define a brand style guide to capture your unique branding and how it applies to your target audience. This will be your brand identity context. Input this into the brand identity tool. Then, when creating content with AI, brand-specific context including voice, tone, ideal customer profile, products, and competitive insight will always be applied.
  • Set up your data layer: to effectively generate content and tailor your messaging, set up the following tools to ensure that your data is unified. It is also recommended to audit your CRM data with your defined audience using a Breeze Assistant prompt.
    • Tools to unify data: consolidate and complete your data with the following tools.
      • Data Studio (BETA): consolidate your data from different platforms into HubSpot. You can also use datasets with other tools such as lists, workflows, and reports. Learn how to set up Data Studio.
      • Data agent: fill gaps in your CRM with custom enrichment, such as researching company information, enriching contact properties, and turning unstructured data from calls and notes into structured fields. Learn how to set up and use data agent.
      • Buyer intent: set up buyer intent to identify leads based on active intent signals and target based on intent during the Tailor stage. Learn how to set up buyer intent.
    • Suggested prompt: are my contacts currently effectively organized based on the characteristics, tiering, and signals from this audience [audience description].

Express: define your campaign story

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use marketing studio.

During this stage, define a campaign story based on an objective, rooted in your foundational context. At the end of this stage, you should have:

  • A campaign objective: the purpose of your campaign. For example, you can set an objective of generating new leads for a specific product during this campaign.
  • A campaign story: the story you want to tell based on your objective. This includes the key idea and messaging for this campaign.
  • Core asset: the asset that you’re trying to drive traffic to, such as a playbook, a landing page, etc. In later stages, you can repurpose this to generate the campaign’s supporting content and assets.
  • Campaign plan: a structured campaign, including timelines and planned channel activation, as well as desired outcomes based on the campaign objective.

To execute the Express stage in Loop Marketing, you will need to generate a campaign story, a core asset, and a campaign plan:

Step

Description

Example prompt

Generate a campaign story

Use Breeze Assistant to generate campaign ideas based on your objective, guided by your Brand Identity context.

Create three campaign ideas with key messages for our target customers [in target industry, with target persona]. List 5 ideas for content about our product and services.”

Generate a core asset

Use Breeze Assistant to generate a core asset.

Create the core asset, or hero offer, for my campaign. My target audience is [persona/industry], my campaign objective is [goal], and my core message is [key theme or POV]. Generate the full asset including [format: guide, playbook, landing page copy, etc.].

Plan your campaign

  • Use Breeze Assistant to generate a messaging and channel strategy.
  • Upload the campaign brief and core asset to Marketing Studio (BETA). Begin creating and structuring your campaign by adding content ideas and asset placeholders to your campaign.

Tailor: personalize your message

Subscription required A Starter, Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use data enrichment.

Subscription required A Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use data agent, buyer intent, and customer agent.

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use AI-powered email.

Subscription required A Content or Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use the personalization tool and content variants.

During this stage, leverage behavioral signals, intent data, and contextual information to tailor messaging to your leads. At the end of the stage, you should have:

  • Audience segments with personalization logic
  • Dynamic content variations
  • Active agents on high-intent pages

When tailoring your content, it is strongly recommended to manually review your content for the following:

  • Brand voice and tone should be kept consistent across all variations.
  • Personalization feels natural and not overly familiar.
  • Personalization and facts used are accurate.
  • Value propositions align with actual customer needs and segment.
  • CTAs make sense for the customer or company’s lifecycle.

Step

Description

Example prompt

Target records by Intent

Use buyer intent to identify leads with active intent signals such as job postings, product launches. Then, use AI to generate filters and descriptions in segments. These segments can be used with content assets such as Marketing emails, ad audiences, and more.

Find contacts who have shown signs of buying intent in the past 30 days across our CRM, such as pricing page visits or email replies.

Enrich your customer data

Gather additional behavioral signals, intent data, and contextual information. Use data enrichment to automatically fill in data, such as company size, industry, job title, and more.

Use Data Agent to further enrich records. For example, you can prompt Data Agent for additional information, then populate these answers in CRM properties. This information can later be used for segments and personalization.

Research [example companies] and tell me: Are they actively hiring in [buying committee roles]? What’s their likely tech stack? Have they mentioned any pain points or competitors in past CRM notes?

Personalize your messaging

Use the personalization tool (BETA) to create and manage personalized content variants (BETA).

Use smart content to personalize your marketing assets such as CTAs and landing pages based on your audience.

You can also create marketing and automated emails using the AI email creation (BETA) to tailor outreach using CRM data and generate a personal email for each recipient.

Engage buyers on high intent pages

Set up customer agent on your highest intent pages such as pricing and comparison pages, to answer questions fast and increase likelihood of conversion.

Amplify: deploy across diversified channels

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use the video clip agent and content remix.

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use AEO.

During this stage, the goal is to be discoverable and consistent messaging across a range of different channels. A t the end of the stage, you should have:

  • AEO-optimized content
  • Published multi-channel campaign assets (social, ads, video, etc)
  • Creator collaboration content

Step

Description

Example prompt

Optimize your content for answer engines

Use the AEO tool to track your brand’s visibility across answer engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini.

Compare your performance against competitors, understand which sources are being cited, and act on prioritized recommendations with content briefs.

Collaborate with trusted creators

Partner with creators that your audience already follows and trusts.

Use the HubSpot Connectors for ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini (BETA) to identify high-intent, high-engagement partners within your industry that would be good fits with your brand.

Which distribution channels and creator types are best aligned to reach [target audience looking for your specific product or service]?

Scale content production with AI

Use the video clip agent to identify clips from your existing video library based on trending topics. You can also use the video editor to convert longer videos into short-form clips optimized for social platforms.

Use content remix to easily create campaign assets for all channels from one core asset. You can use content remix directly from Marketing Studio.

Launch advertising

In HubSpot’s ads tool, you can use AI when creating Google Performance Max Ad campaigns for smart distribution across search, social, and display.

Create a Google PMax campaign using [specific messaging]. Optimize for demo signups over 14 days.

Evolve: optimize in real time

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription is required to use email engagment optimization.

Subscription required A Marketing, Sales, or Service Hub Enterprise subscription is required to create a report with journey analytics.

During this stage, use AI to track performance and deliver real-time recommendations. Use AI to spot early trends, run experiments, and continuously refine your strategy. At the end of this stage, you should have:

  • Performance analysis and insights
  • Campaign optimization recommendations (or new ones to start)
  • Learnings documented for your next Loop cycle

Step

Description

Example prompt

Simulate Campaign Outcomes

Use AI to predict results before launching. In Hubspot, use email engagement optimization (BETA) to predict which recipients are most likely to engage. Use this tool to optimize your send lists for engagement.

Monitor in Real-Time

Create a report with journey analytics to analyze customer journey paths between key touchpoints. Identify where prospects drop off and which paths lead to conversions, then apply these insights to optimize your next iteration.

Which hook version resulted in the highest conversion rate for [target audience] in Segment A? Include analysis of form fills, time on page, and email click-throughs.

Refine strategy continuously

Use Breeze Assistant to analyze the performance of your last campaign and make recommendations on what to change moving forward. Complement this with custom reports to track performance across assets, segments, and channels. Apply these learnings to refine your strategy for the next Loop cycle.

Use Breeze-powered A/B testing (BETA) to generate suggested copy for your landing pages to discover what resonates most with your audience and create the most effective versions.

Use the marketing analytics suite to analyze reports pertaining to what channels are driving the most engagement, how your website is performing, and contact insights.

Analyze the performance of our last campaign using the data from [specific timeframe]. Compare their performance across key metrics and recommend which approach to continue or update for better results.

Frequently Asked Questions about Loop Marketing

Is Loop Marketing a product or feature in HubSpot?

No, it’s a framework that can be utilized with or without HubSpot. However, HubSpot provides a unified platform for executing the Loop Marketing framework.

When should customers use Breeze Assistant versus HubSpot’s Connectors for ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini (BETA) in Loop Marketing?

Through the Loop Marketing framework, you can use either Breeze Assistant or HubSpot’s connectors, or both, to execute tasks.

  • Breeze Assistant: use Breeze Assistant for full context and memory of tasks within HubSpot. It is recommended to use Breeze Assistant when analyzing your customer profile and creating a style guide.
  • HubSpot’s Connectors: use these HubSpot’s connectors when you want to use additional data from external sources. These allow you to take your HubSpot context into other AI tools.
Do I still need to focus on SEO when using Loop Marketing?

It is recommended to use both SEO and AEO in your content as part of a healthy and cohesive marketing strategy. Learn more about the differences between SEO and AEO.

What are the differences between SEO and AEO?

SEO

AEO

Goals

Be part of top 5 links

Be part of the presented answer

Strategies

Use keywords, backlinks, meta tags to rank

Use statistics, quotations, high authority sources

Rewards

Rewards domain reputation

Rewards repetition across trusted sources

Optimize

Optimize for website visits and volume

Optimize for AI visibility and conversion

Is Loop Marketing replacing Inbound Marketing?

No, it is a way to bring Inbound Marketing into the age of AI. It remains true to the principles that made Inbound work: educating customers, creating value, and building relationships. The difference is in the ways marketers need to deliver on these principles.

Does Loop Marketing replace the funnel?

Loop Marketing is a framework designed to drive momentum in the funnel. It brings your funnel into the AI era, but it is not a funnel itself.

Understand your campaign details page

From the campaign details page, you can get an overview of the campaign and associated assets. You can also review a campaign’s performance, any associated campaign tasks, and keep track of your campaign’s budget and spending.

Permissions required Super Admin or Campaign permissions are required to use the campaigns tool.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Campaigns. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Campaigns directly.
  • Click the campaign you want to review. In the left panel, review your campaign details and associated assets. This will include the automatically generated unique Campaign UTM.
  • To take action on your campaign, at the top, click Actions dropdown menu to:

    • Summarize: use AI to generate a campaign summary. Learn more about generating campaign insights using AI.

    • Edit campaign: edit your campaign details. Learn more about creating and editing campaigns.

    • Create tracking URL: create a tracking URL to track traffic from a campaign to a page with the HubSpot tracking code.

    • Create task: create a marketing task for the campaign.

    • Manage access: select which users and teams have access to this campaign. Learn more about managing access to your campaigns.

    • Export: export the selected campaign’s performance details. You can export the campaign performance data in a csv, xls, xlsx, or an image PDF format. Learn more about exporting your campaign’s performance details.

    • Delete: permanently delete the campaign. Learn more about deleting campaigns.

  • To edit the campaign, click Edit campaign. Learn more about editing your campaign details.
  • To clone the campaign, click Clone. Learn more about cloning campaigns.
  • From the Details tab, review your campaign properties. To edit a property, hover over the property and click the edit icon.
  • To review associated assets, click the Assets tab. Then, click on the asset type to review associated assets.
  • In the right panel, navigate to any of the following tabs:

    • Performance

    • Attribution

    • Assets

    • Tasks

    • Budget

    • Activity
