Create and edit video clips directly from the social tool

Create video clips from longer videos and edit them directly in the social tool. After generating clips, review, edit, and publish them to your social accounts without navigating to the video editor. For example, generate clips from a webinar recording, trim one during review, and publish it to LinkedIn or Instagram.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Create video clips

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.

  • In the upper right, click Create post.

  • In the Upload media section, click the Generate with AI dropdown menu and select Clip a video.

  • In the right panel, click Select video. The video must be at least 3 minutes long.

  • From your video file picker, select a video. To upload a new video, in the bottom, click Upload video.

    • To change the selected video, click Replace video.
    • To remove the video, click Remove.

  • After selecting your video, at the bottom, click Next.

  • Set up your video focus:

    • To use a template, at the top select a template option. This will automatically populate a prompt in the text field and replace any existing content.
    • To manually set up your clip focus, enter a prompt in the text field.

  • Set up you video options:

    • Network: select the checkboxes next to the social networks that the clips will be generated for.
    • Number of clips: you can choose to generate 3 or 5 video clips.
    • Duration: select the duration of your clips. You can generate clips up to 90 seconds.
    • Include captions: choose whether to include captions in your video clips. These will be automatically generated by AI. If you’ve chosen to include captions, you will also need to select a caption style.
    • Layout: select the layout for your video. You can choose between keeping the original layout, landscape, portrait, or a square layout.

  • After setting up your video focus and options, at the bottom, click Generate.

  • To use a video clip, hover over the clip and click Review.

  • In the dialog box, you can review the clip and recommended caption. To use the clip in your social post, at the bottom, click Select accounts and insert.

  • In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select the checkboxes next to the accounts that you’d like to publish to. Then, click Insert.

  • Continue setting up your social post.

Edit video clips

After inserting a clip into your social post, you can edit the video, thumbnail, or captions without leaving the social editor.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • In the left panel, click the Drafts tab and select an existing social draft. Or, create a new social post with a video clip.
  • In your social post editor, click the edit iconedit video icon to update your video content. You’ll be automatically directed to the video editor.
    • Continue editing your video. Learn more about editing and trimming videos using the transcript and timeline.
    • When finished, click Export in the upper right.
      • A progress bar in the left sidebar will show the rendering status.
      • Once rendering is complete, the updated video automatically replaces the original in the editor.
  • Within the uploaded video section: - To update your video thumbnail, click the insertImageicon edit thumbnail icon. Learn how to edit your video thumbnails. - To update your video captions, click the closedCaptionsicon captions icon. Learn how to edit your video captions. - To remove the video, click the delete icondelete icon.
  • Continue setting up your social post.

Edit videos in HubSpot

Edit your video clips directly in HubSpot using the video editor. Add audio, image, and text overlays, combine multiple clips, apply captions and branding, and use AI to remove filler words or background noise from your audio.

After editing, export the clip to save it to the files tool. For example, after recording a product demo, you can trim the footage, add a company logo as a watermark, and use AI to remove filler words before exporting the final version.

Edit clips from a video

If you have a Content Hub subscription, you can create and edit videos directly from the video tool. If you have a Marketing Hub subscription, you can access the video editor from the files tool.

If you have a Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • To edit an existing clip, hover over the video. Then, click the edit edit icon.The video editor will open.
  • From here, you can edit clips using the video timeline or using the video transcript.

If you have a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.​
  • Double-click the video file to open the Video Details page. Or, click the verticalMenuIcon three vertical dots icon, then click View Details.
  • At the bottom, click Edit. You’ll be automatically redirected to the video editor.

You can also create and edit video clips directly from the social tool.

Edit a video from the page or embed editor

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to edit videos from the pages and embed editors.

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to edit videos from the social tool.

Edit videos from the website page, landing page, or embed editor before publishing or sharing your content. After exporting your changes, the updated video automatically replaces the original version in the editor. For example, you can trim a video or adjust its aspect ratio while building a landing page, without leaving the landing page editor.

Add audio, images, or text to your video

Add audio, images, or text to your video for additional context or to match your brand. You can upload your own audio files or use trending TikTok audio, place image and text overlays over your footage, and add a static image as an intro or outro slide.

Add an audio track to your video

To add an audio track to your video:

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the + add icon. Alternatively, click Add in the timeline editor.
  • In the left panel, select Audio.
    • To use your own audio file, click Your uploads. Then, select an existing audio file or click Upload to add a new audio file. The audio clip will automatically appear in the timeline editor
    • To use a trending TikTok audio, click TikTok trending audio. Learn more about using TikTok audio in your videos.
  • To configure the volume for your audio overlay:
    • Click the audio overlay in the timeline editor, then click the edit pencil icon.
    • In the dialog box, use the volume slider to adjust.
Add an image overlay to your video

To add an image overlay to your video:

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the + add icon. Alternatively, click Add in the timeline editor.
  • In the left panel, select Image overlay.
  • In the right panel, select an existing image file or click Upload to add a new image file. A timeline clip for the image will automatically appear in the timeline editor.
  • To move your overlay, in the preview screen, click and drag the image overlay to the desired position. When moving your overlay, guide lines will automatically appear in the preview.
    • You can also use the arrow keys on your keyboard to move the overlay 1px at a time.
    • To move the overlay 10px at a time, hold the shift key and tap the arrow keys.
  • To edit the size of your overlay, in the preview screen, click and drag the corner of the image overlay.
Add a text overlay to your video

To add a text overlay to your video:

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the + add icon. Alternatively, click Add in the timeline editor.
  • In the left panel, select Text overlay. A timeline clip for the text will automatically appear in the timeline editor.
  • In the video preview screen, click the text field and enter your text.
  • To move your overlay, in the preview screen, click and drag the text overlay to the desired position. When moving your overlay, guide lines will automatically appear in the preview.
    • You can also use the arrow keys on your keyboard to move the overlay 1px at a time.
    • To move the overlay 10px at a time, hold the shift key and tap the arrow keys.
  • To edit the size of your overlay, in the preview screen, click and drag the corner of the text overlay.
  • To configure the design for your text, such as the font or background for your text, click the text overlay in the timeline editor, then click the edit pencil icon.
Add an image to the intro or outro of your video

You can also add a static image as an intro or outro to your video. For example, you may want to add a title card to give context, or your company logo at the end of your video.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the + add icon. Alternatively, click Add in the timeline editor.
  • In the left panel, select Text overlay.
  • In the right panel, upload or select an image for your intro or outro. The image will be added as a full-screen slide at the start of the video.
  • To move the slide to the end of your video, click on the image in the video timeline and select the edit pencil icon. Then, select Move to end.
  • To add a background to your image, click on the image in the video timeline and select the edit pencil icon. Then, select the Background checkbox and set your in the picker.
  • To remove a slide, click the image on the timeline and select the delete icondelete icon.

Combine multiple video clips using the video timeline

Combine multiple video clips into a single video to build a complete video from multiple source files. You can append video clips to the end of your video, or split an existing video track and insert a new one between.

Branding and captions will be applied across all segments automatically, and you can adjust the volume and crop of each individual video segment.

  • To append a video clip to your existing video:
    • In the bottom left, click Add.
    • In the left panel, select Video.
    • In the right panel, select an existing video clip. You can also upload a new video or record a video directly in HubSpot. The selected video will automatically appear in your video timeline.
  • To insert a video clip into a video:
    • In your video timeline, click on a point where you’d like to insert the new video.
    • On the top left of the timeline, click Split. This will split your video into two clips at the selected point.
    • In the bottom left, click Add. Then, select Video.
    • In the right panel, select an existing video clip.
    • In the video timeline, click and drag your new video clip to the split point.
    • To rearrange your video clips, click and drag the clip to the desired position in the video timeline.
  • To delete a specific clip from your video timeline, click on the clip and select the delete delete icon. The clip will be immediately removed from the video timeline.
  • To edit the crop of a specific clip, click on the clip. Any edits will only apply to the selected clip. At the top of the right panel, select from the following options:
    • Fit: fit the clip display to the selected aspect ratio, while ensuring that the entire clip still appears.
    • Fill: use the cropped clip to fill the entire display. This can result in certain areas in the clip being cropped if the aspect ratios are not aligned.
    • Crop: crop the video clip display to a specific size or ratio. After cropping your video, you can click and drag it to the desired position on your video display.
    • Reset: reset your crop and any positioning changes to the original video appearance.

Adjust video clip settings

Use the video editor to adjust clip settings after combining your clips. Add transitions between clips, control the volume for more balanced audio, or change the playback speed to cut pauses or highlight key moments.

Add transitions between clips
  • In the video editor, click the clip where you want to add a transition.
  • In the pop-up box, click the edit icon. Then, click Add transition.
  • In the dialog box, select a transition type.
  • At the bottom, use the slider to determine the length of transition between clips.
Adjust video clip volume
  • In the video editor, click the clip you want to adjust.
  • In the pop-up box, click the edit icon.
  • Use the slider to adjust the clip volume between 0 and 100. You can apply different volume levels to different clips.
Adjust video clip playback speed
  • In the video editor, click the clip you want to adjust.
  • In the pop-up box, click the edit icon.
  • Select a speed from the Speed dropdown menu, between 0.25x and 4x.
    • Different speed values can be applied to different clips.
    • The track duration updates automatically to reflect the new speed.

Crop and edit your video clip display

  • In the right panel, click Crop to begin editing the video.
  • To edit the aspect ratio for your video, click the first dropdown menu and select from Portrait (9:16), Landscape (16:9), or Square (1:1).
  • After editing the aspect ratio of your video, if your clip canvas has extra space above or on the sides, you can also choose from the following:
    • Fit to canvas: adjust the video to fit within the selected aspect ratio. To set the background , click the Background dropdown menu. Then, select a . This will fill in the background where your clip canvas has extra space above or on the sides.
    • Fill canvas: expand the clip to fill the entirety of the cropped area. When selecting this option, you can drag and drop the clip within the clip previewer to decide what part of the video should be retained.

Add video clip captions

You can add captions to your video clip based on the transcript. Design your caption and set your caption’s position.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • From the video library, hover over the video. Then, click the edit edit icon. You’ll be automatically redirected to the video editor.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click the captions & translations icon.
  • In the left panel, toggle the captions switch on.
  • Select your caption style. You can choose from six default styles. Alternatively, click + Add new custom caption style to create a custom caption.
  • In the Font size section, enter or edit the font size for your caption.
  • In the Position section, select the vertical height for your caption. By default, all captions are centered in the video.
Use karaoke-style captions

Add active word highlighting to a custom caption style to visually emphasize each spoken word as it’s spoken. You can choose a fill color and background color for the highlighted word, scale it for emphasis, and set how unspoken words appear. Preview your settings directly in the editor before exporting your video.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the captions & translations icon.
  • In the left panel, click + Add custom style.
  • In the pop-up box, toggle the Karaoke captions switch on.
  • In the Active word font color section, click the color picker and select a color, or enter a hexadecimal value in the field. Then, enter a percentage in the opacity field, or use the arrows to adjust.
  • In the Active word background color section, click the color picker and select a color, or enter a hexadecimal value in the field. Then, enter a percentage in the opacity field, or use the arrows to adjust.
  • In the Active word size section, use the slider to select a size between 1x and 2x.
  • To set visibility for unspoken words, click the Future word visibility dropdown menu and select one of the following:
    • Normal: unspoken words appear at full opacity.
    • Dimmed: unspoken words appear at reduced opacity.
    • Hidden: unspoken words are not visible until spoken.
  • At the bottom, click Save.
    • To edit your karaoke captions, hover over the style in the Custom styles section and click the edit style icon.
    • To remove your karaoke captions, hover over the style in the Custom styles section and click the delete style icon.

Add AI-translated video clip captions

Add AI-translated captions directly onto the video clip based on the video transcript. When exporting the video, separate videos will be created for each additional translation.

  • You can navigate to your captions from your Captions and translations settings or AI settings:
    • In the left sidebar menu, click the closedCaptionsIcon captions & translations icon. At the top, click the Translations tab.
    • Alternatively, in the left sidebar menu, click the artificialIntelligence AI icon. Then, select Multi-language.
  • In the left panel, click to toggle the switch on.
  • Click + Add language.
  • In the dialog box, click the Translate to dropdown menu and select the checkboxes next to the languages that you’d like to translate.
  • At the bottom, click Translate. The languages will automatically appear in the left panel after translation.
  • To preview what the translated caption will look like on your video, click Preview next to the language.
  • To delete a translated caption, click the delete delete icon.

Remove background noise using AI

Use AI voice isolation to remove background noise from your video’s audio.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the artificialIntelligence AI icon.
  • Toggle the Voice isolation switch on. Then, preview the edited audio in your video editor timeline.
  • To restore your original audio, toggle the Voice isolation switch off.

Remove AI-detected filler words

Use AI to identify and remove filler words from your video’s audio and transcript. This includes:

  • Filler words such as um, uh, and ah.
  • Words that are contextually considered as filler, such as like.

To remove AI-detected filler words:

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the artificialIntelligence AI icon.
  • Toggle the Remove filler words switch on. Once the analysis is complete, Removed [number] filler words will appear under the Remove filler words section.
    • To review the edited audio, check the video editor timeline.
    • In the transcript, removed filler words will appear greyed out with a strikethrough.
  • To restore specific words, you can click the word in your transcript. Then, select Restore. Learn more about editing your video using the video transcript.
  • To restore your original audio, toggle the Remove filler words switch off.

Use AI-powered smart framing

Use smart framing to keep people centered when cropping a horizontal video to a vertical aspect ratio. As people move, the crop adjusts to keep them in view without manual keyframing. When more than one person is detected, smart framing displays them in a grid layout.

To turn on smart framing in your video:

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the artificialIntelligence AI icon.
  • Toggle the Smart framing switch on. Smart framing will process the video and automatically adjust the crop to keep people in view
  • To turn off smart framing, toggle the Smart framing switch off.

Please note: longer videos may require additional processing time before smart framing is applied. A loading icon appears while the video is processing. Once processing is complete, the Smart framing switch turns on.

Add branding to your video clip

Add a brand or watermark to your video. A preview of the brand image will appear on the video in the right panel.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the brandingbrandingbranding icon.
  • In the left panel, click to toggle the switch on.
  • In the Image section, add a brand image to your video. You can select an image from the files tool, upload a new image, or import your company logo from your brand kit.
  • In the Size section, select the size for your brand image. You can select from small, medium, or large.
  • In the Position section, select the location where you’d like your brand image to appear in the video.
  • In the Opacity section, use the slider to determine the opacity of your brand image.

Create and apply templates to your video clip

Save your caption, branding, and video aspect ratio to use as templates whenever editing a new video.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click the partial templates icon.

  • Click + Create New.

  • In the dialog box, enter a name for your template.

  • Select the checkboxes next to the settings that you’d like to include in your template.

  • After setting up your template, at the bottom, click Create. The template will automatically appear in the panel with the details for each setting.

  • To use a template, hover over the template and click Apply.

    • The design selections will be applied to the current clip.
    • You can apply multiple templates into a clip.

Undo or redo changes

Undo and redo actions in your video editor. This applies to all actions including edits to the video transcript.

  • To undo an edit, click the undo undo icon in the top right. Changes will be undone one at a time.
  • To redo an edit, click the redo redo icon in the top right. Changes will be redone one at a time.

Export your video clip

After setting up your video, to export a clip:

  • After editing your clip, in the top right, click Export. After exporting your file, you’ll be taken back to your Video Details with the Variations tab open.
  • When your export is complete, you’ll receive an email notification.

Please note: after exporting your clip, a new video will be saved to the files tool by default.

File upload error: ‘There was an error uploading your file’

This message displays when your file upload has failed. Before uploading a file, review the file tool’s supported file types and sizes. If your file meets these requirements, but your uploads are still encountering the error, review the possible reasons below.

Permissions required Super Admin or Files permissions are required to upload files to the files tool.

  • Upload size and ISP upload speed: the size of the file can impact the time it takes to complete the process, especially if your Internet Service Provider (ISP) offers limited upload speeds. Larger files and slower ISP upload speeds will take longer to upload and can result in this error. To resolve this, try reducing your file size, or uploading the file on a different network.
  • Uploading on a mobile network: if you upload your files using a mobile network, your internet performance can be variable. Mobile networks can experience changes in speed and reliability, and certain mobile plans may slow down upload speeds after you use a certain amount of data. It is recommended to try uploading the file while connected to wifi or wired network.
  • Using a VPN: if you’re using a Virtual Private Network (VPN), your data is likely being encrypted and sent through a server in another location. The additional steps in sending the data can reduce the upload speed and cause your upload to time out, resulting in this error. To resolve this, try turning off your VPN and uploading your file again.
  • Using a company firewall: company networks often use firewalls to stop unauthorized data transfers and keep the network safe. These firewalls may block specific file types or limit the size of files you can upload. If your upload fails, check with your IT department to review if the file type and size are allowed by your company’s firewall.
  • Company Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies: company DLP policies may block uploads to cloud storage for security and data leakage purposes. To resolve this, you can reach out to HubSpot support to retrieve HubSpot’s upload bucket. Then, work with your IT department to allowlist the upload bucket to permit PUT requests.

Generate clips from videos using AI

Using HubSpot’s AI, automatically generate clip suggestions from longer videos in the content remix tool. For example, if you have a long product demo or webinar recording, HubSpot’s AI can identify and create shorter clips optimized for different channels or aspect ratios to post to your social media or use during presentations. After generating clips, you can save and edit them directly in the video editor.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Remix. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Remix directly.
  • In the top right, click Start remixing.
  • In the editor, click Add content.
  • In the left panel, select Video. Click Upload a file to upload a new video or click Browse file manager and select an existing video from the files tool.
  • At the bottom, click Add content.
  • Click the + plus icon.
  • In the left panel, click the checkbox next to the video option.
  • At the bottom, click Next.
  • Add custom instructions, select an aspect ratio, and enter the number of clips that should be created. Then, click Generate.
  • Click the Video clips output for a preview of the generated clips.
  • To save a clip, click Save and edit in app. You’ll be directed to the clip editor where you can further refine the clip.

To continue editing your clip, learn more about editing your video files.

Generate images using AI

Generate images using AI for blog posts, website and landing pages, emails, and social posts. When generating images, you can use existing image files as a reference and enter prompts to generate complex, detailed images.

After generating an image, you can continue editing with Adobe Express, save the image to the files tool, or add it directly to your content.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to use brand identity when generating and managing images.

  • To generate images, you must turn on the Give users access to generative AI tools and features setting. Learn more about managing your AI settings.
  • Before using your organization’s branding when generating images, you must set up your brand identity.

Generate images for your content

You can generate images using AI for blog posts, website and landing pages, emails, and social posts:

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to the asset that you want to add an image to.
  • Add an image to your content.
  • In the right panel, click Generate with AI.
  • In the dialog box, set up your image:
    • In the text field, enter your prompt for the image.
    • To use a reference image when generating a new image, click the + add icon.
      • To use a new image, click Upload an image.
      • To use an existing image from the files tool, click Browse images and select an existing image.
    • To use your company’s branding, click Brand identity. In the dialog box, click the Brand Identity switch to toggle it on.
    • To manage your image quality, click Image quality and select your quality level.
  • After setting up your image details, click the breezeSendIcon send icon in the bottom right.
  • To further edit your generated image, enter a new prompt in the text field. Then, click the breezeSendIcon send icon. For example, you may want to include more background or change the style of the image.

Manage your generated image

After generating your image, you can take the following actions on your generated image:

  • To use an image, click Insert.
  • To provide feedback about a generated image:
    • If the image was what you expected, click the thumbsUpIcon thumbs up icon.
    • If the image wasn’t what you expected, click the thumbsDownIcon thumbs down icon.
  • To review the image in full, click the enlarge expand icon. To crop your image, you can click the cropIcon crop icon.
  • If you’d like to use your image later, you can click the saveEditableViewIcon save icon to save your image to the files tool.
  • To edit the image directly, click the edit AdAedit icon. Learn more about editing AI generated images in HubSpot.

Edit your generated image

To edit the image directly in HubSpot:

  • Under the image, click the edit AdAedit icon.
  • To crop your image, at the bottom, click the cropIcon crop icon. You can crop your image to a custom size, or use an existing template.
  • To add a text overlay to your generated image, click the textIcontext icon.
  • To add a image overlay to your generated image, click the insertImageIcon image icon. You can use an existing image from the files tool or upload a new image.
  • To edit the image with Adobe Express, click the Adobe Express icon. Learn more about editing images with Adobe Express in HubSpot.
  • After editing your image, click Save. The edited image will be saved as a new file.

Manage individual file details

After uploading your file, learn how to edit and configure file details such as the file’s name, URL, and visibility settings. If you’re working on video files, you can turn on the file’s advanced features to configure additional details such as adding subtitles. Learn more about managing video files. If you no longer require a file, learn how to delete and restore your files. To restrict access to your files, learn how to partition files and folders.

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for files are required to manage file details.

Manage your file details

To review and update your file details:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • From the files tool, click the name of the file.
  • To edit your file name, at the top of the right panel, click the edit pencil icon. Then, enter a new name.
  • In the right panel, you can also configure the following options:

    • File URL visibility: change the visibility and accessibility of your file. Learn more about managing your File URL visibility.

    • File URL by domain: to update your file’s URL domain, click the dropdown menu and select one of your connected subdomains.

      • By default, files are hosted on HubSpot’s content delivery network system domain, with f.hubspotusercontent appearing in the domain of the file URL.
      • You can update your settings to host all files on one of your connected subdomains.

    • File expiration date: set a date and time for the file to expire.

      • To remove a file’s expiration date, select the date picker and click Cancel. If no expiration date has been set, the file will be retained indefinitely.
      • When the file has expired, it will automatically be sent to files trash.

    • Accessibility: add alt text to your image or video file. This text will apply as an alt text on image files and a title attribute on video files.

    • File Usage: review a list of HubSpot content and templates using images or video files hosted in the file manager.

    • File history: review a log of changes made to the file such as edits to the file visibility, previous file deletions, and more.

    • General: review general file details such as when the file was created and last updated, file size, file type, and internal file ID. If you’ve turned on your AI file data setting, this will also include AI-generated descriptions and keywords.

Replace, clone and edit, or download your file

At the bottom of the file details panel, you can replace, clone and edit, or download your file:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • From the files tool, click the name of the file.
  • To replace a file with an updated version:
    • At the bottom, click Replace.
    • Browse your computer hard drive and select a new file. After replacing your file:
      • The old file may be cached for up to two hours after it’s replaced, so you may not see the file update immediately.
      • To check if the file has been successfully replaced, try loading your file URL in a private browsing window such as in private mode in Safari or in an incognito window in Chrome.

Please note: video files cannot be replaced.

  • To clone and edit an image file:
    • At the bottom, click Clone and edit.
      • If you’re editing a Canva image, you can click Clone and edit and select Edit in Canva to create and edit a new Canva design.
      • To update your image design with Adobe Express, you can click Clone and edit > Edit with Adobe Express. Learn more about updating existing images with Adobe Express.
    • You cannot clone and edit Shutterstock image files.
    • Make edits to the clone of your file.
    • Click Save.
  • To download a file, at the bottom, click More and select Download. You cannot download Shutterstock image files.
  • To remix a file, at the bottom, click More and select Remix into other content. Learn more about repurposing content using AI with content remix.

Edit your file’s visibility settings

Editing the visibility option of a file will adjust whether the URL is public and if it’s indexed by search engines. You can edit the file visibility settings for individual files or in bulk. You can select from the following visibility options:

  • Public: the file URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL web address. Search engines will be able to index the file URL.
  • Public - noindex: the file URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL web address. Search engines are instructed not to index the file URL.
  • Private: the file URL will be private and require a URL to access. Search engines will not be able to index the file URL. After setting the file visibility to Private, choose from the following File URL options.
    • Internal share link: the file URL will only be accessible to other users logged into the same HubSpot account, this will link directly to the file itself.
    • Link to file preview: the file URL will only be accessible to other users logged into the same HubSpot account, this will link to a preview page for the file.
    • Temporary 24hr public share link: the temporary file URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL, and will expire after 24 hours. If you would like to temporarily share the file again, you can create another share link.

Please note: by default, file visibility is set to Public. If a file was previously indexed by a search engine, setting a file to Public - noindex will not remove it from search results. Instead, the file will not be re-indexed during the next crawl, which may take some time. To remove a previously indexed file, you can use external tools such as Google search console to request to remove these links.

Edit the visibility of a single file

To edit the visibility of a single file:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • From the files tool, click the name of the file.
  • In the right panel, under File URL visibility, click the dropdown menu and select a visibility option.
Edit the visibility of files in bulk

To edit the visibility of multiple files at the same time:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the files that you want to edit. Then, click Change file visibility at the top of the table.
  • In the right panel, click the radio button next to the visibility option you want to switch to. Then, click Save.

Review your file history

From the File details panel, you can display a log of historical changes made to the file such as changes to the file visibility, previous file deletions, and more. For existing files, the file history will only display changes from 1st August 2022 onwards.

To review your file’s history:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.

  • Locate and click the name of the file.

  • In the right panel, click File History. Then, click View full file history.

  • In the right panel, you can filter your file’s history with the following:

    • Performed by: filter by the user who made the changes to the file.
    • Activity: filter by the change activity type made to the file, such as a file delete, rename, and more.
    • Made on: filter by the date that the file was changed.

Manage the URL of files uploaded to the files tool

All files in the files tool will have a unique file URL. You can use HubSpot Content Delivery Network (CDN) domain for hosting, or customize a file’s URL to be hosted on any of your connected domains.

If you want the URL of your file to be removed from search engine results, or hidden from anyone outside your team, you can customize the visibility settings of your file. By default, all files attached to CRM records are private and hidden from search results.

To replace a file with an updated version while using the same file URL, learn more about replacing your HubSpot files.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Files permissions are required to edit and manage a file’s URL.

When using the files tool, please note the following:

  • Files uploaded to the files tool are hosted on a public CDN file URL by default. HubSpot does not support the management of sensitive information. For more information, please see our Terms of Service.
  • When visitors to your website load files on one of your pages, HubSpot may rewrite the domain of the associated file URLs to match the domain of the current page. Learn more about domain rewriting in HubSpot’s developer documentation.
  • If you’re experiencing loading images on HubSpot pages, please add these domains to your network or office’s firewall allowlist and try again:
    • [HubID].fs1.hubspotusercontent-na1.net
    • [HubID].fs2.hubspotusercontent-na1.net
    • [HubID].fs1.hubspotusercontent-eu1.net
    • [HubID].fs2.hubspotusercontent-eu1.net

Change the default URL for your files

After connecting a domain to HubSpot, you can change the default file URL that appears in the File URL by domain dropdown menu.

To change the URL of your files:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Content > Pages.
  • At the top, click the SEO & Crawlers tab.
  • In the Default File Manager Hosting Domain section, click the dropdown menu and select a domain.
    • Any connected domain can be used as the default hosting domain.
    • If your domain is not appearing, please check your account’s connected domains.
  • In the bottom left, click Save to update your settings.

Share your files with different domains

If you’ve connected a domain to HubSpot, you can change the File URL by domain dropdown menu. This will allow you to share your files with different domains.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • Locate the file and click the file name.
  • In the right pane, click the File URL dropdown menu and select the URL you want to use. The different URL options are based on the domains you have connected to HubSpot:
    • When you upload a file to the files tool with public visibility, HubSpot automatically creates multiple working URLs for the file at each of your connected subdomains, as well as the default [HubID].hubspotusercontent-[Region].net domain.
    • If you change the File URL of one of your files from one subdomain to another, the file will remain accessible at the previous URL. You do not need to add a redirect for the file.
  • Click Copy URL to use or share this URL.

Customize the visibility of your file URL

By default, files uploaded to the files tool are hosted on a public file URL and indexed by search engines. This means anyone with a direct link to the file URL can view this file on their web browser. It also means the file URLs are indexed by search engines and may appear in search results.

Please note: you cannot customize the visibility of the following file types:

  • Video URL with advanced features turned on.
  • Files collected from visitors in file upload fields in forms. By default, the File URL visibility will be set to Private.

You can customize the visibility of your file URL in the File details panel:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • Locate the file and click the file name.
  • In the right panel, check the File URL visibility on the web setting. To customize this setting, click the dropdown menu and select from the following:
    • Public: the file URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the file URL. Search engines will be able to index the file URL.
    • Public - noindex: the file URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the file URL. Search engines are instructed not to index the file URL.
    • Private: the file URL will be private and require a URL to access. Search engines will not be able to index the file URL. After setting the file visibility to Private, choose from the following File URL options.
      • Internal share link: the file URL will only be accessible to other users logged into the same HubSpot account, this will link directly to the file itself.
      • Link to file preview: the file URL will only be accessible to other users logged into the same HubSpot account, this will link to a preview page for the file.
      • Temporary 24hr public share link: the temporary file URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL, and will expire after 24 hours. If you would like to temporarily share the file again, you can create another share link.

Manage video files

After uploading a video, you can manage keywords, chapters, captions, thumbnail, and more. Review the video’s performance, additional video file details, and any variations created from the clip editor.

You can also turn on advanced features for your video files, such as tracking video performance, adding the video to your HubSpot content, and using subtitles.

After uploading and managing your video file, learn how to edit your video files and add videos to your HubSpot content. You can also share and embed videos using the video file URL, on external website or emails, or through social posts.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Navigate to your video details

After editing your video clip, you’ll be directed to the video details page for that clip. Alternatively, to navigate to your video details from the files tool or the video tool.

To navigate to your video details from the files tool:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • From the files tool, search for and select the name of the video file.
  • In the right panel, review your video details.

If you have a Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, to navigate to your video details from the videos tool:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • Search for and select the name of the video file. You’ll be directed to the video details page.

Set your video’s title, keywords, SEO description, chapters, and thumbnail

From the Optimization tab, set up your video details:

  • Video title: enter a title for your video, to be used in web pages, the sitemap XML, and when sharing the video.

  • Keywords: add keywords to fill in hashtags and metadata when sharing your video.

    • To manually add a keyword, click Add keyword. In the dialog box, enter your keyword and click Save.
    • If you have a Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, to automatically generate keywords using AI, click the artificialIntelligence AI icon. AI generated keywords will automatically appear in the keywords section.

  • SEO description: enter a SEO description for use in web pages, sitemap XML, and when sharing. To automatically generate an SEO description based on the video content, click the artificialIntelligence AI icon.

  • Chapters (Content Hub Professional or Enterprise only): click to toggle the Chapters switch on to add chapters and allow viewers to jump to different parts of the video.

    • When using chapters, please note the following:
      • Chapters will only appear in the player on supported platforms.
      • You can create up to 20 chapters per video.
    • To manage your chapters:
      • To preview the chapter, click the time code next to each chapter.
      • To edit the chapter name, hover over the chapter and click Edit. Then, enter your new chapter name and click Save.
      • To delete a chapter, hover over the chapter and click Delete.
      • To add a new chapter, enter a timestamp to mark when the chapter begins. Then, enter your chapter name and click Save. The chapter will end at the start time of the next sequential chapter.

  • Thumbnail: select or edit the thumbnail for your video. You can select from the following options:

    • Pick a moment from video: use a capture from specific point in your video as the video thumbnail. In the dialog box, scrub through your video for the moment that you’d like to use as the video thumbnail. Then, click Set as thumbnail.

    • Upload from library: use an image from your files tool as the video thumbnail.

    • Crop and resize: crop and resize the existing video thumbnail.

    • Edit with Adobe express: edit the existing video thumbnail with Adobe Express. For example, you may want to add additional clip art elements or a title to your thumbnail image. Learn more about editing images with Adobe Express in HubSpot.

Review your video’s performance reports

From the Performance tab, review the following performance reports for your video:

  • Video performance by social post (Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise only): the count of video views, interactions, and comments by social network. The video views metric does not apply to videos on X.

  • Video metrics: the Total plays and Unique viewers for the video.

    • Plays: each video play is tracked as soon as playback begins.
    • Unique viewers: each unique viewer is counted according to the HubSpot tracking code. If a visitor deletes their cookies, they will be considered a new visitor and will be assigned a new cookie. Learn more about tracking visitors in HubSpot.

  • Views over time: the count of total plays per day.

  • Video retention: the retention metrics for your video, including the Avg. view duration, Avg % duration, and Qualified views metrics.

    • Avg. view duration: the average amount of time a video is viewed for, in minutes.
    • Avg % duration: the average completion percentage of a video.
    • Qualified views: the count of qualified views where at least 75% of the video was watched.

  • Video performance by page: the video’s performance by web page.

  • Engagement by Contact: the video’s engagement by tracked contacts.

Add and manage your video captions

In the Captions tab, upload custom captions or use AI to generate captions. You can also add AI-translated captions directly on video clips from the video editor.

  • To manually upload a caption:

    • Click Upload file.
    • In the right panel, click the Language dropdown menu and select a language for your captions. Then, click Select file.

  • If you have a Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, to add an AI-generated caption, click Start with AI.

  • If you have a Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, you can also translate your generated captions using AI. Learn more about the available languages for translation.

    • In the top right, click AI Translate.
    • In the right panel, click the Translate to dropdown menu and select the checkboxes for the languages that you’d like to translate.
    • At the bottom, click Translate.

  • To manually upload another caption, in the top right, click Upload captions.

Manage uploaded or AI-generated captions

After adding your caption, you can review, edit, and delete your caption directly from the video details page.

You can also turn on and turn off each caption to control which language captions appear in your video player. For example, you may want to hide AI-generated subtitles entirely while still using your own uploaded caption files.

  • To turn a caption on or off, click to toggle the switch to the right of the caption. This will determine whether the caption appears to viewers on the video or not.

  • To review a caption, hover over the caption and click View.

  • To replace an AI-generated caption, hover over a caption. Then, click Actions and select Upload own captions.

  • To set a different caption as the primary language, hover over a caption. Then, click Actions and select Set as primary language.

  • To remove a caption, hover over a caption. Then, click Actions and select Delete. You can only delete captions that have been turned off. If the caption has not been turned off, this option will not appear.

  • To edit a caption directly from your video details, hover over a caption, then click Edit. In the right panel, continue editing your transcript:

    • To edit specific words in the transcript, click the word that you’d like to edit and select Edit word. In the pop-up box, enter your new word and click Save.
    • To delete a word, click the word that you’d like to remove and select Delete.
    • To find and replace all instances of a specific word in the transcript:
      • In the top right, search for the word that you’d like to find and replace.
      • Click the find and replace toggle to expand the section.
      • In the Replace field, enter the word that you’d like to replace with.
      • Click Replace all. Every instance of the word will be replaced in your transcript.
    • After updating your transcript, at the bottom, click Save.

Review your video file details and manage your video’s advanced features setting

From the Details tab, review your file details such as:

  • Advanced features: choose whether to turn advanced features for the video on or off. Learn more about using advanced features in HubSpot videos.

  • Created: the date the video was created.

  • Updated: the most recent date the video was edited.

  • Duration: the length of the video.

  • File Size: the size of the video file.

  • Dimensions: the visual dimensions of the video in pixels.

  • File type: the file type, such as mp4, mov, and more.

  • File usages: any other HubSpot content where the file is used.

  • File URL visibility: change the visibility and accessibility of your file. You can choose from the following visibility options. Learn more about managing your file URL visibility.

    • Public: the video will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL web address. Search engines will be able to index the video URL.
    • Public - noindex: the video will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL web address. Search engines are instructed not to index the file URL.
    • Private: the file URL will be private and require a URL to access. Search engines will not be able to index the file URL. Users must be logged into their HubSpot account to access the video. This is best for internal content.
    • Anyone with the link: the video will be accessible to anyone with the unique URL. No login us required and search engines are instructed not to index the file URL. This is recommended for one-to-one sales emails and direct customer sharing. The video URL will be protected by an unguessable token.

  • File URL by domain: to update your file’s URL domain, click the dropdown menu and select one of your connected subdomains.

    • By default, files are hosted on HubSpot’s content delivery network system domain, with f.hubspotusercontent appearing in the domain of the file URL.
    • You can update your settings to host all files on one of your connected subdomains.

  • File expiration date: set a date and time for the file to expire.

    • To remove a file’s expiration date, select the date picker and click Cancel. If no expiration date has been set, the file will be retained indefinitely.
    • When the file has expired, it will automatically be sent to files trash.

  • Marketing campaign: associate your file with a campaign. Learn more about using campaigns in HubSpot.

Review variations of your video clip

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to access and use the Clips tab.

In the Clips tab, review the different edited variations of the original video.

  • If your clip is longer than 5 minutes, AI will automatically generate and suggest three clips as well as titles for each clip. Each suggested clip will be shorter than 90 seconds.
    • To preview the clip, hover over the clip to autoplay. To turn on audio when previewing the clip, click the audio icon.
    • To open the suggested clip in the editor, hover over the clip and click Edit. Learn more about using the clip editor.
    • To save all suggested clips, click Save all as drafts. The new clips will appear in the Clips tab when reviewing your video file.
  • To continue editing a variation clip of the video, hover over the clip and click Edit. You’ll be redirected to the clip editor.
  • To delete a variation clip of the video, hover over the clip and click the delete delete icon.

Manage your files

After uploading files to the files tool in HubSpot, you can locate specific files by searching and filtering within the file manager. You can also organize your files with folders and export files. Learn more about exporting data from HubSpot.

You can also manage files in HubSpot using the Files API. If you want to restrict access to a specific file or folder, learn how to partition your files and folders. To manage your individual files, learn how to manage your individual file details.

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for files are required to manage files. Super Admin or Delete permissions for files are required to delete files or folders.

Review, search, and filter your files

In both list and grid view, to find specific files, you can search by the file’s name, description, or keywords. You can also filter your files by file type. Learn more about managing your file’s description and keywords.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • To toggle between list or grid view, click the listView list icon or the grid board icon in the top right.
  • In the top search bar, enter the name, description, or keywords for the file you want to locate. Learn more about using AI to automatically analyze and tag your files with descriptions and keywords.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to a specific folder or subfolder in the files tool. To expand a folder or subfolder, click the right right carat icon next to the folder. Any subfolders will appear in the sidebar menu.
  • To sort your files:
    • In the list view, to sort your file by name, file size, format, or last update date, click the column header.
    • In the grid view, click the dropdown menu in the top right, and select your sorting criteria. You can sort files based on file name, file size, last update date, and file format.
  • At the top, you can filter your files by the following:
    • File format: filter your files by file extension type. Categories include Images, Documents, Audio, All videos, Videos with advanced features, and Videos without advanced features.
      • In addition to extension types such as mp3, mov, pdf, jpg, and more, you can also filter by Videos with advanced features and Videos without advanced features.
      • Extension types are grouped by Images, Documents, Audio, and Videos.
    • Used in: filter your files by the content the file is used in. For example, you can filter files by those used in website pages, CTAs, case studies, and more.
    • Uploaded date: filter your files by the date uploaded, click the Uploaded date dropdown menu and set your Date range.
    • Uploaded by: filter your files by the specific user who uploaded the file.
    • Updated by: filter your files by the user that last updated the file. This includes edits such as renaming a file, editing alt text or metadata, deleting a file, moving a file, and more.
    • File status: filter your files by status. You can filter between from active or archived files.
  • To search by a file’s extension type:
    • In the top search bar, enter the file extension (e.g., jpg, pdf, mp3) in the top search bar.
    • You can also include the file’s name in your search, separated by a space. For example, entering dog png in the search bar would result in all png files that have titles that include the text dog.

Select files in bulk

In the files tool, you may need to select multiple files to take bulk actions such as moving files to a folder, deleting files, changing the files’ visibility, or exporting these files. In both list or grid view in the file manager, you can select multiple files by using checkboxes, using marquee select, or holding a key on your keyboard.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • To select multiple files manually, hover over the file and select the checkboxes next to the flies that you’d like to select.
  • To use a marquee select, you can click and drag a selection box to select multiple files. After selecting these files, the checkbox on the files will be automatically selected.
  • Depending on your device, you can also select multiple files by holding the shift key, command key, or ctrl key while selecting the files.

After selecting your files, you can take action on your files. You can also drag the selected files to a specific folder.

Manage files with folders

You can move files between folders to stay organized in the file manager. In both list and grid view, you can move individual files or multiple files in bulk.

Please note: when a file is moved to a new folder in the file manager, it will remain accessible at the old path. You do not need to add a redirect from the old URL to the new URL. If you upload a new file with the same name and path as the file you moved, HubSpot will serve the new file instead.

Create a new folder

To create a new folder in the file manager:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • From the files dashboard, in the top right, click Create folder.
  • In the dialog box, enter a name for your folder, then click Save.
  • After creating your folder, you can browse through your files or use the search bar at the top to search by file name.
  • To rename your folder, in the top right, click Actions and select Rename.
  • To move your folder to another location, in the top right, click Actions and select Move.
  • To delete a folder and the files within, in the top right, click Actions and select Delete.
Move files to folders in list view

To organize your files with folders:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • In the table, select the checkboxes next to the files you’d like to move.
  • At the bottom left, click Move.
  • After adding your files to a folder, you can restrict access to individual files or the overall folder.
Move files to folders in grid view

To organize your files with folders:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • To switch to a grid view, click the grid board icon in the top right.
  • To move an individual file to a folder:
    • Hover over a file and click Actions. Then, select Move. In the dialog box, select the folder you want to move the file to and click Move.
    • Alternatively, click and drag the file to the folder that you’d like to move it to.
  • To move multiple files to a folder:

    • Hover over and select the checkboxes next to the files and folders that you’d like to move. At the bottom, click Move. In the dialog box, select the folder you want to move the file to and click Move.

    • Alternatively, click and drag a selection box to select multiple files. Then, click and drag these files to the folder that you’d like to move it to.

Export your files

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to export files.

Export your files in list view

To export your files in a .zip folder:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • In the table, select the checkboxes next to the files and folders that you’d like to export. You can navigate between pages when selecting your files.
  • At the bottom, click Export (ZIP).
  • In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select the users that you’d like to receive a download link.
  • Click Export. Once the export is processed, you’ll receive a download link through email and in the notification center.
Export your files in grid view

To export your files in a .zip folder:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • To switch to a grid view, click the grid board icon in the top right.
  • In the table, hover over and select the checkboxes next to the files and folders that you’d like to export. Alternatively, click and drag a selection box to select multiple files.
  • At the bottom, click Export (ZIP).
  • In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select the users that you’d like to receive a download link.
  • Click Export. Once the export is processed, you’ll receive a download link through email and in the notification center.

Provide a direct download link to a file hosted on the files tool

If you want to share a file directly with your team or anyone else, you can retrieve a direct link and send this link to the file for download.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or View permissions for files are required to retrieve a file’s direct download link.

When sharing your file with a direct download link, please note the following:

  • Most browsers will open links to PDF files in a new browser tab or window, instead of downloading the file to the visitor’s computer. Whether the file opens in the browser or downloads automatically depends on the visitor’s web browser and its settings.
  • There isn’t a way to force the file to download without using server-side script, which is not supported in the files tool. You may consider packaging your file in a .zip file, which prompts an automatic download on most browsers.
  • To share your file in an email or on your website, the file’s visibility should be set to Public or Public - noindex. Learn more about setting your file’s visibility settings.

Retrieve your direct download link

To retrieve your direct download link to share your file:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • Locate the file you want to share and click the file name.
  • In the right panel, click Access and URLs.
  • In the right panel, click the File URL dropdown menu and select the URL you want to use.
    • The different URL options are based on the domains you have connected to HubSpot.
    • Based on your connected domains, you can also set a different default URL for your download links.
  • Under the File URL by domain section, click Copy URL to copy the link to your clipboard. By default, the file URL will follow a format with fxx.hubspotusercontentxx.net.
  • Depending on your subscription, you can also use a connected domain for the file URL:
    • Click the File URL by domain dropdown menu and select a domain.
    • Click Copy URL.

Share or embed your HubSpot-hosted videos

After uploading your videos to HubSpot’s video tool, you can share those videos using a URL. You can also embed HubSpot-hosted videos to your externally-hosted website (e.g., WordPress) or externally-hosted emails (e.g., Gmail). Then, track views, plays, and engagement events across all platforms directly within HubSpot.

You can also share your videos in a social post. If you’d like to keep a copy of the video as a backup or to manually share, you can download the video file.

Understand limitations and requirements

  • To embed a HubSpot-hosted video on an external page or email, the Advanced features must be turned on for that video. This will count toward the video limit for advanced features.
  • When embedding videos on externally-hosted pages:

    • To track your video data, you must install the HubSpot tracking code on your externally hosted website.

    • When embedding your video, by default, the video embed script will include JSON-LD injection for SEO benefits, using a <script> tag.

Copy and share your video URL

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • Hover over the video that you’d like to share, then click the shareIcon Share icon.
  • To manage advanced features for your video, click to toggle the Advanced features switch on or off. Learn more about advanced features in videos.
  • If the advanced features setting has been turned off, you can configure the visibility of your video URL. Click the Video visibility dropdown menu and select from the following:
    • Public: the video URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL web address. Search engines will be able to index the video URL.
    • Public - noindex: the video URL will be publicly accessible to anyone who has or guesses the URL web address. Search engines are instructed not to index the video URL.
    • Private: the video URL will be private and require a URL to access. Search engines will not be able to index the video URL.
  • To use a custom domain when sharing your video:
    • Click to expand the Advanced link settings section.
    • Click the Custom domain dropdown menu and select a domain.
  • After configuring your video share URL. click Copy.

Copy and use your embed code on external sites

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to embed videos on external sites.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​

  • Hover over the video that you’d like to embed, then click the shareIcon Share icon.

  • In the dialog box, click Embed. If advanced features have not been turned on for the video, the option will be greyed out.

  • Set up your share format:

    • Size: select whether the embedded video should be responsive or have a fixed video size. By default, the option will be set to Responsive, which will automatically adjust the video size based on page width.
    • Loop: automatically restart the video and play it continuously in a loop.
    • Mute by default: mute the video by default. Visitors will need to click to turn on audio.
    • Autoplay: automatically play the video when the page loads.
    • Visible controls: display a control bar to the visitor. By default, this option is turned on.
    • Play button color: use the color picker to set a color for the video’s play button.
    • Include SEO metadata: toggle this option to include video metadata onto the page for search engines to index the video.By default, this option is turned on.

  • After configuring the video’s settings, in the bottom left, click Copy embed code. The video embed code will automatically be copied to your device’s clipboard.

  • Navigate to your external website’s content management system (CMS).

  • Paste the video embed code into the HTML of your non-HubSpot page, wherever you want the video to appear. Additional recommendations are available for the following:

    • WordPress: it’s recommended to use a custom HTML block to add your HubSpot video embed code to WordPress pages and blog posts. Learn more about adding embeds to WordPress content.
    • Shopify: it’s recommended to insert your video’s embed code by either selecting the Add video rich text option or modifying the page’s HTML directly via the inline code editor. If you require a more complex use case, you can add your embed HTML to a Custom Liquid template as part of your Shopify theme. Learn more about using templates in Shopify.

  • Preview your video on the webpage to check what it looks like when live. The video should display with a responsive layout that automatically adjusts to page width. If the video is not displaying correctly, check that your external CMS has not altered the code that you copied.

  • When you’re finished, publish your page.

Copy and use your embed code on externally-hosted emails

Subscription required A Content Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to embed videos on external-hosted emails.

Generally, video isn’t supported on most email clients. Videos added to your emails will appear as a thumbnail image with a video player button. The thumbnail image will link to a page where your email recipient can view your video.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​

  • Hover over the video that you’d like to embed, then click the shareIcon Share icon.

  • In the dialog box, click Embed. If advanced features have not been turned on for the video, the option will be greyed out.

  • At the top, click the Email tab.

  • Configure your video settings:

    • Size: enter a size for your video preview image.
    • Domain: select a domain for your linked video’s URL. Learn more about connecting domains to your HubSpot account.

  • After configuring the video’s settings, in the bottom left, click Copy embed code. The video embed code will automatically be copied to your device’s clipboard.

  • Navigate to your external email host.

  • Paste the video embed code into the HTML of your email, wherever you want the video to appear. This can vary based on your email provider.

Share your video with a social post

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to create and publish social posts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • Hover over the video that you’d like to share, then click the shareIcon Share icon.
  • To share your video with a social post, at the bottom, click Social. You’ll automatically be directed to the social post editor.
  • Continue setting up your social post to share your video.

Download your video files

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • Hover over the video that you’d like to share, then click the shareIcon Share icon.
  • To share your video with a social post, at the bottom, click Download. the video file will automatically start download.

Supported file types and sizes

When uploading files to HubSpot, there are specific file types and size restrictions for each tool.

Please note: HubSpot does not support the management of sensitive information. For more information, please see our Terms of Service.

Files tool

Permissions required Super Admin or Files permissions are required to upload files to the files tool.

You can upload most file types to the files tool. When uploading your files, do note the following:

  • There is currently no total storage limit or restriction on the total number of files in the files tool. The upload size limits below apply to each file, not to cumulative account storage.
  • The file size limits for the files tool are:
    • Files up to 20 MB for accounts with only access to HubSpot’s free tools.
    • Files up to 2 GB for accounts with paid subscriptions. If a file is 1 GB or more, you may experience issues when uploading the file.
  • Generally, it isn’t recommended to host or render HTML or Javascript files in the file manager, as there may be issues when rendering the code. Instead, HTML or Javascript files should be uploaded for storage or sharing. To create a custom HTML page, learn how to build a custom template.
    • If a HTML or JavaScript file is uploaded to the file manager, then loaded using a default HubSpot domain, it will use Content Type: text/plain.
    • If a plain-text file, such as llms.txt, llm.txt, or ai.txt, is required at the root of your domain, the file must be hosted externally. Uploaded files are assigned generated URLs (e.g., /hubfs/ or hosted-files paths) and can’t be placed at the root level.
    • Web browsers will not render the code and if a user goes directly to the file, it will display the HTML code in plain text. To avoid this, you can set these files to use one of your connected domains instead of a HubSpot default domain.
  • When uploading images to the files tool, the following file formats are supported:
    • jpg
    • jpeg
    • png
    • tif
    • tiff
    • ico
    • bmp
    • webp
  • If you’re using HubSpot’s free tools, you cannot upload executable files. The following file types will be blocked:
    • sh
    • bat
    • com
    • elf
    • bin
    • exe
    • jar
    • rpm
    • deb
