Trim and edit video clips using the video timeline

In the video editor, you can trim and edit your video clip directly from the video timeline. Use the timeline to make precise edits to your clip, including reordering, splitting, trimming, and removing sections.

If your video file size is less than 200MB, an audio waveform will appear in the timeline to help you navigate your content.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.

  • From the video library, hover over the video. Then, click the edit edit icon. You’ll be automatically redirected to the video editor.

  • To zoom in or out of the timeline, in the bottom right, use the magnifying slider.

  • To review your video timeline in detail, hover over specific points in the timeline. The timestamp for that point will appear.

  • To hide or display the timeline, in the bottom right, click the down icon hide timeline icon or up icon show timeline icon. You’ll still be able to preview and scrub through your video using the minimized timeline bar.

  • To reorder your clips, click and drag the clip to the desired position in the timeline.

    • When moving your clips, alignment guides will automatically appear.
    • The transcript will also automatically reflect your new video order.

  • To split clip, hover over specific point and click Split. You can split video clips, image overlays, text overlays, and audio clips. After splitting your content, to add new content between existing sections, hover over the split point and click the + add icon.

  • To trim your clips, at the beginning or end of your video, click and drag the video edges to trim to the desired amount.

  • In the timeline, you can crop out specific sections of the video. For example, if you’d like to remove any mistakes, or create jumpcuts in your video.

    • Click and drag an area in the timeline to highlight the section that you’d like to remove. The corresponding section will be highlighted in the transcript.
    • Click Trim to remove the section. The cropped sections will automatically reflect with a strikethrough in the transcript. The trimmed section will also appear in the timeline with a dashed line.
    • To restore your trimmed area in the timeline, you can hover over the dashed line. Then, click Restore.

  • In the timeline, you can choose to retain only a specific section of the video clip for editing. For example, if you wanted to create a new clip from an existing video.

    • Click and drag an area in the timeline to highlight the section that you’d like to keep. The corresponding section will be highlighted in the transcript.
    • Click Keep only this to retain only the selected section. This will remove all other sections except for the area selected.

  • To delete a track from your timeline, click the track. Then, select the delete icon delete icon. Alternatively, you can also use the backspace or delete key in your keyboard.

    • You can delete video clips, image overlays, text overlays, and audio clips.
    • The deleted sections will automatically reflect with a strikethrough in the transcript.
    • You cannot delete the primary video clip track.

To continue editing your video, learn more about editing your video files.

Trim and edit video clips using the video transcript

Using the video transcript in the video editor, you can trim and restore sections, remove pauses, edit or replace spoken words, and generate new clips from specific parts of your primary video. Changes you make in the transcript are automatically reflected in your clip on the composition timeline.

Before you get started

Before editing your video clip, review how the transcript is structured and what to expect based on your track type.

  • In the transcript, each section reflects a video or image section, with timestamps that match the order of the composition timeline. For example, if a video is split in half, the transcript reflects two sections.
  • If you reorder tracks on the timeline, the updated order is automatically reflected in the transcript.
  • Sections not included in the clip are greyed out and displayed with a strikethrough. For example, sections that have been trimmed.
  • For slide tracks or videos without a transcript, a scrubber block displays a thumbnail, track name, and seek slider. You can use the seek slider to navigate the content or identify and delete the track using the ellipses three horizontal dots icon to delete the track.

Trim and edit a video clip using the video transcript

In the video editor, use the transcript to make edits to your video clip:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • From the video library, hover over the video. Then, click the edit edit icon. You’ll be automatically redirected to the video editor.
  • In the left panel, review a transcript of the video used.
  • You can control the size of the transcript editor:
    • To hide or display the transcript editor entirely, in the top left, click the < hide transcript or > show transcript icon.
    • To manage the size of the transcript editor, hover over the divider, then click and drag the divider to determine its size.
  • To review the transcript for just the remixed clip or the full script, in the top right, click More. Then, click to toggle the Show trimmed parts switch on or off.
  • To view sections without spoken audio in the transcript, in the top right, click More. Then, click to toggle the Show pauses switch on or off.
    • Each dot represents 0.5 seconds without spoken audio.
    • You can highlight the dots and then click Trim to remove sections without spoken audio from the clip.
  • To add a section back to the video, highlight a section that has been greyed out and and click Restore.
  • To remove a section from the video, highlight a section and click Trim. For specifically trimmed content at the start or end of an existing section:
    • To display trimmed content, click the upCarat icon.
    • To hide trimmed content, click the downCarat icon.
  • To edit specific sections or words in the transcript:
    • Click the section that you’d like to edit and select Edit.
    • In the pop-up box, enter your new content.
    • Click Save.
  • To find and replace all instances of a specific word in the transcript:
    • In the top right, search for the word that you’d like to find and replace. Matching words will be highlighted inline across all sections.
    • Click the find and replace toggle to expand the section.
    • In the Replace field, enter the word that you’d like to replace with.
    • Click Replace all. Every instance of the word will be replaced in your transcript.
  • To create an entirely new clip, highlight a section and select Keep only this. This’ll create a new clip based on the highlighted section.
    • Any previously added or removed sections or pauses will be disregarded.
    • To review the clip, in the top right, click Clip.
  • When editing your video from the transcript, you can only add assets such as images or overlays between existing sections. To add an asset from the video transcript, hover over the divider between sections and click the + add icon.

To continue editing your video, learn more about editing your video files.

Upload and manage files in the HubSpot mobile app

Upload files directly to your HubSpot file manager from your mobile device using HubSpot’s mobile app. Once uploaded, your images, fonts, audio files, PDFs, and other files will be hosted on HubSpot’s content delivery network servers. You can also attach files to content when logging activities or composing one-to-one emails in your HubSpot mobile app.

Please note: Files uploaded to the files tool are hosted on a public CDN file URL by default. HubSpot does not support the management of sensitive information. For more information, please see our Terms of Service.

Before you get started

Before uploading your files, please note the following:

  • Before uploading a file, review the file tool’s supported file types and sizes.
  • By default, files uploaded to the files tool are hosted on a public file URL. If you don’t want your files to be visible to search engines, learn how to customize the visibility of your file URL.
  • It is not possible to track views from the files tool. When a visitor accesses a file, whether as a download or a URL, it will not count toward any page view metrics.

Upload files

To upload a file:

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.

  • At the top, tap the menu icon.

  • In the Marketing section, tap Files.

  • At the top right, tap the + Add icon.

  • Tap Upload files.

  • At the bottom, select the source for your file:

    • To select a photo from your device’s stored photos, tap Choose photo.
    • To select a video from your device’s stored photos, tap Choose video.
    • To capture a photo or video directly from your device to the files tool, tap Take photo or video.
    • To select a file from your device, tap Choose file. You can upload the following file types:

  • To cancel a file upload, in the top left, click Cancel. You cannot cancel a completed upload. If you’ve incorrectly uploaded a file, you can delete the file from the file manager.

  • To upload another file, in the top right, click the + add icon.

  • After the file has been successfully uploaded, it will appear in the Done section. In the top left, click Done to return to the file manager.

Manage files

To manage your files from the HubSpot mobile app:

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.

  • At the top, tap the menu icon.

  • In the Marketing section, tap Files.

  • To filter your files, in the top left, tap All file types, then select Images, Videos, Documents, Images, or Videos.

  • To sort your files, in the top left, tap Sorted by, then select Most recent, Name, File size, or File type.

  • To search for a specific file, at the top, enter your search term in the search bar.

  • To review a file’s details, tap the verticalMenumore icon next to the file.

    • To preview the file, click Preview.
    • To share the file through other applications on your device such as Slack or Telegram, click Share.
    • To change the file visibility, click Change file visibility. Select Public, Public - no index, or Private.
    • To delete the file, click Move to trash. Learn more about deleting and restoring your deleted files.

Create folders

You can create folders to organize your files in the app or upload files directly to these folders.

To create a folder from the HubSpot mobile app:

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.

  • At the top, tap the menu icon.

  • In the Marketing section, tap Files.

  • In the bottom right, tap + Add.

  • Tap Create folder.

  • In the dialog box, enter your folder name, then tap Create.

  • To add a file to the folder, tap the folder name, then in the top right, tap Add.

  • Continue uploading your files. By default, when uploading files, the file visibility will be set to Public. This can be later updated directly within the mobile app.

After creating your folder and uploading your files, the folder and files will appear in the files tool on both the mobile app and on desktop.

Upload and manage videos

In the video tool, you can upload videos, then search for and filter your videos. You can also export files directly from your Descript account into HubSpot or record videos directly from your account.

After uploading your videos, you can further edit your videos or review and update your video file details. You can also upload and manage video files and any advanced features directly from the files tool.

Upload videos

When uploading videos, please take note of the following file size and type limits. While the size limit is 2GB, if a video is 1 GB or more, you may experience issues when uploading. It is also recommended to upload your videos in mp4 or mov format.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • In the top right, click Add videos. Then, select Upload, Record video, Descript, HeyGen, or Google Drive. Any videos uploaded will also automatically appear in the files tool.

Sort and filter your videos

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​

  • In the top search bar, enter the name of the video you want to locate.

  • To filter your videos:

    • In the top right, click Filters.
    • In the right panel, set up your filters.
    • After setting up your filters, at the bottom, click Show x videos.

  • To clear all filters, in the top right, click Clear all.

  • To sort your videos, in the top right, click the dropdown menu and select a sorting option. You can sort your videos by name, duration, file format, and last update date.

  • To take bulk action on your video, hover over and select the checkboxes on the videos that you’d like to take action on. The count of videos will appear in the bottom left.

    • To delete your videos, at the bottom, click Move to trash. In the dialog box, select Move files to trash.
    • To export your videos, at the bottom, click Export (ZIP). In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select the email address to export the videos to. Then, select Export.

  • To preview your video, hover over the video. The video will begin to auto-play.

    • To pause your video, click the pause icon.
    • To unmute your video, press the audio icon. Video previews are muted by default.

  • To review your video details, hover over the video and click the icon. Then, select View details.

  • To review your video details, hover over the video and click the three vertical dots icon. Then, select View details.

  • To edit your video , hover over the video and click the three vertical dots icon. Then, select Edit. Learn more about editing your videos.

  • To delete your video, hover over the video and click the three vertical dots icon. Then, select Move to trash. You can restore video files within 30 days of deletion. Learn more about archiving, deleting, and restoring files.

Upload files to use in your HubSpot content

Upload files to the files tool for use in your HubSpot content. Once uploaded, your images, fonts, audio files, PDFs, and other files will be hosted on HubSpot’s content delivery network servers. You can also upload files using the Hubspot mobile app.

In this article, learn how to upload files from your device or Google Drive, then use those files in HubSpot content. After adding files to your HubSpot content, you can review where the files are used in the file’s details. After uploading your files, you can organize, edit, and delete the files, or insert them into your content. You can also share files directly by providing a download link to a file.

Please note: by default, files uploaded to the files tool are hosted on a public CDN file URL. HubSpot does not support the management of sensitive information. For more information, please see our Terms of Service.

Before you get started

Permissions required Super Admin or Edit permissions for files are required to upload files to your HubSpot account.

Before uploading your files, please note the following:

  • Before uploading a file, review the file tool’s supported file types and sizes.
  • By default, files uploaded to the files tool are hosted on a public file URL. If you don’t want your files to be visible to search engines, learn how to customize the visibility of your file URL.
  • You can only upload up to 100 files at a time through the files tool. If you want to upload more files to your HubSpot account, you can use the external auth API. Learn more about using the file upload API in HubSpot’s developer documentation.
  • It is not possible to track views from the files tool. When a visitor accesses a file, whether as a download or a URL, it will not count toward any page view metrics.

Upload files from your computer

To upload a file:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • In the top right, click Upload files.
  • Browse your computer’s hard drive for files to upload. Select your files and click Open.
  • Alternatively, you can also drag and drop files in the open file manager window. You can drag and drop the files directly to a specific folder or the folder you’re in.

Upload files from your Google Drive

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.

  • In the top right, click Import from Google Drive.

  • In the dialog box, click the dropdown menu and select the Google account that you’d like to use. Alternatively, to add a new account:

    • Click the dropdown menu and select Add an account.
    • In the dialog box, click Approve and connect Google Drive.
    • In the pop-up box, select the account that you’d like to connect, then click continue.
    • Then, review the displayed permissions. HubSpot requires all of these permissions in order to retrieve files from your Google Drive. After reviewing the permissions, click Allow. The added account will appear in the dropdown options.

  • Click Open Google Drive Picker.

  • Select the files that you’d like to add and click Select in the bottom left. The files will be automatically added to the file manager with a File URL Visibility of Public.

Use uploaded files in HubSpot content

After you upload your files, you can use them as images, videos, or file download links in your HubSpot content. Learn more about inserting files into your content:

  • Insert an image in a rich text module
  • Add videos to your HubSpot content
  • Insert or edit a link in a rich text module

When using HubSpot Video, the file size may be reduced after upload. Video files are compressed to reduce the bandwidth required when playing. To view the size of an uploaded video in HubSpot:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • Click the name of a file.
  • In the right panel, click General. The File size will be displayed in this section.
  • To add videos to your HubSpot content, ensure that the Advanced features switch is toggled on.

Locate where files are used in HubSpot

You can review a list of HubSpot content and templates using images or video files hosted in the file manager. When reviewing your files, please note the following:

  • Only the locations of video and image files are indexed and displayed. The locations of other types of files, such as PDFs, are not indexed.
  • Only published content or templates will be listed in the File details panel.
    • If your HubSpot-hosted content or template is not published, it will not appear in this list.
    • For example, if an image file is used in an email, the email must be first sent.
  • External pages will not be included in this list.
  • Images injected via JavaScript will not be included in this list. For example, in certain custom accordion or gallery modules.

To review your file:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.
  • Locate the file you want to review and click the file name.
  • In the right panel, click File usage to view a list of HubSpot content and templates using this file.
  • Click the content type to expand a list of content using the file.
  • Click on a specific email, page, or blog post to open it in the content editor. Or, click on a template to open it in the design manager.

Use stock images in your HubSpot content with the Shutterstock integration

Use the Shutterstock integration to access 60,000 stock images royalty-free. These stock images can be used in your HubSpot content and social posts.

Save stock images to the files tool

To add stock images to your files tool:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Files. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Files directly.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Stock Images.

  • Use the search bar in the center of the screen to search for images.

  • In the search results, click the image that you’d like to use.

  • In the bottom right, click Save to your files.

  • To change which folder the image is saved to:

    • In the bottom, click Change folder and select the new folder. Then, click Save.
    • Then, click Save to your files.

Please note:

  • Only photos in the Stock Images section of the file manager are included in the integration. Any images outside of that on Shutterstock.com, or other places, may have a fee associated that is not covered by this integration.
  • Photos from the Stock Images section of the file manager cannot be exported.

Use stock images in your content

If you’ve saved a stock image to your file tool, you can select the image from the file picker when creating content. Alternatively, you can search for and add stock images directly from your content editor or social composer.

  • In the HubSpot content editor, start by adding an image to your social post, ad, page, or email:

    • When creating a page, blog post, or email using the classic email editor, click the image icon insertImage at the top of the editor.
    • When creating an email using the drag and drop editor, click and drag an Image element from the Content tab in the left pane into the email editor. Then click Select image.
    • When creating a social post, click the image icon insertImage at the bottom of the post composer.
    • When creating a Facebook lead ad or LinkedIn Lead Gen ad, click Select Image/Video in the Ad tab of the ad editor.

  • At the top, click the search bar and enter a search term. Then, press the Enter key.

  • At the top, click the Stock images tab.

  • Click an image to display the image details. Then, click Preview in full screen.

  • In the bottom left, click Save to your files. The image will be automatically inserted to your content or social editor. It will also be saved to your files tool.

Use TikTok audio when editing your video files

Add TikTok trending audio when editing your video files. On TikTok, usings popular sounds can increase your visibility and engagement. When users interact with a specific sound, TikTok’s algorithm surfaces content using that audio in more users’ feeds.

From HubSpot’s video editor, browse and add popular trending audio directly to your videos. Learn more about editing videos in HubSpot.

Please note: trending TikTok audio clips can only be used for videos shared directly to TikTok. If you try to add videos with TikTok audio to other content, such as blog or website pages, the audio track will not play.

To create a new clip from an existing video file:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Video. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Video directly.​
  • From the video library, hover over the video. Then, click the edit edit icon. You’ll be automatically redirected to the video editor.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click the + add icon.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the Audio section. Then, click Tiktok trending audio.
    • If this is your first time using this feature, click Connect now.
    • In the dialog box, follow the prompts to connect your TikTok account.
  • To search for a specific trending audio, at the top, enter a search term in the search bar. If the audio you’re searching for isn’t in the TikTok trending audio list, it will not appear.
  • To filter the audio options, click the dropdown menus to filter by Location, Genre, and Date.
  • To preview an audio, hover over the song name and click the playerPlayIcon play icon.
  • To use an audio, click the + add icon. The audio file will automatically appear in your video editor timeline.

Marketing: Forms

Add data privacy and consent information to a HubSpot form

To help visitors understand what they’re opting into when submitting a form, you can add notice and consent information. This also allows you to capture a visitor’s consent to the processing of their personal information as well as their consent to receive communication from your HubSpot account.

Permissions required Edit forms permissions are required to create or edit a form.

Before you get started

Please note the following:

  • While HubSpot provides these features, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific situation.
  • By default, there will be an option in your forms and pop-up forms called Data privacy options. This will display even if data privacy settings are not turned on in your HubSpot account.
  • If you turn on data privacy settings, all data privacy checkboxes on new forms will become mandatory.
  • When a contact fills out a form with notice and consent information:
    • The Legal basis for processing contact’s data property will be set to Freely given consent from contact.
    • The communication consent will appear in the subscriptions section of the contact record.
  • If you’d like to edit the default notice and consent text for both forms and pop-up forms, you can do so in the Privacy and consent settings. The default text set for your notice and consent options will apply to all subscription types. If you change the default text:
    • The new default text will be added to any new form or pop-up form you create.
    • Existing forms will not be automatically updated with this new default text. To update an existing form, delete the current Data privacy options field from the form and re-add it to include the updated wording.
  • The option to collect consent via form is only available for marketing emails, not SMS messages.

Add notice and consent to a form

To add the notice and consent option to your form:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.

  • Hover over the form name and click Edit, or create a new form.

  • In the top left, click the + add icon.

  • In the left panel, click Other.

  • Click and drag the Data Privacy field type onto the form preview on the right to include it on your form.

  • In the left panel, under Data privacy options, configure your consent and subscription settings, map each consent option to the correct marketing email subscription type, and choose whether to include a privacy policy statement.

  • To add additional subscription type checkboxes to allow visitors to consent to communication from multiple subscription types on a single form:

    • Under What consents do you want to collect?, click Add another subscription.
    • Select or clear the subscription types for each communication you want to offer on this form. When a contact selects a communication, they will be subscribed to it.

  • In the top right, click Review and update to publish your form updates.

Notice and consent options

When building your form, you can select from the following notice and consent options below:

  • Implicit processing consent and individual checkboxes for communications
  • Separate consents (Individual checkboxes per consent)
  • Legitimate interest
Implicit processing consent and individual checkboxes for communications
  • With this option, you can collect consent to communicate through an affirmative opt-in using a checkbox that specifies the communication/subscription type.
  • You can add more than one checkbox to allow visitors to consent to communication for more than one subscription type.
  • With this option, consent to process personal data is collected implicitly when the contact clicks the submit button.
  • If a contact submitting the form doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, the form submission will still be processed. However, the contact won’t be subscribed to any communications.
  • It is not possible to pre-select the consent to communicate checkbox. However, if you turn on data privacy settings, all data privacy checkboxes on new forms will become mandatory.
  • If the contact previously subscribed in the past and subsequently doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, this is not equivalent to the contact withdrawing their consent.
Separate consents (Individual checkboxes per consent)
  • With this option, you can collect consent to communicate through an affirmative opt-in using a checkbox that specifies the communication/subscription type.
  • You can add more than one checkbox to allow visitors to consent to communication for more than one subscription type.
  • With this option, consent to process personal data is collected explicitly:
    • The contact needs to select the consent to process data checkbox in order to give their consent. You cannot process a visitor’s data and accept the form submission if they have not given explicit consent.
    • Without selecting this checkbox, visitors will not be able to submit your form. If you want to offer visitors access to your content without processing their data, add the consent to process footer with a hyperlink to your content.
  • If a contact submitting the form doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, the form submission is still processed, and the contact won’t be subscribed to any communications.
  • It is not possible to pre-select the consent to communicate checkbox. However, if you turn on data privacy settings, all data privacy checkboxes on new forms will become mandatory.
  • If the contact has already subscribed in the past and subsequently doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, this is not equivalent to the contact withdrawing their consent.
Legitimate interest
  • If your legal basis for processing is legitimate interest, your form will show a notice informing visitors that you need their information to contact them about your products and services. They can unsubscribe from these communications at any time.
  • With this option, the contact is not required to give their consent to you, and will just see a notice.

Add data privacy and consent information to your HubSpot form (legacy)

To help visitors understand what they’re opting into when submitting a form, you can add notice and consent information. This also allows you to capture a visitor’s consent to the processing of their personal information as well as their consent to receive communication from your HubSpot account.

Please note: this article is for forms built with the legacy forms editor only. It’s recommended to use the updated form editor to create and manage new forms. Learn more about adding data privacy and consent information in the updated form editor.

Permissions required Edit forms permissions are required to create or edit a form.

Before you get started

Please note the following:

  • While HubSpot provides these features, your legal team is the best resource to give you compliance advice for your specific situation.
  • By default, there will be an option in your forms called Data privacy options. This will display even if data privacy settings aren’t turned on in your HubSpot account.
  • When a contact fills out a form with notice and consent information:
    • The Legal basis for processing contact’s data property will be set to Freely given consent from contact.
    • The communication consent will appear in the subscription section of the contact record.
  • If you’d like to edit the default notice and consent text for forms, you can do so in the Privacy and consent settings. The default text set for your notice and consent options will apply to all subscription types. If you change the default text:
    • The new default text will be added to any new form you create.
    • Existing forms will not be automatically updated with this new default text. To update an existing form, delete the current Data privacy options field from the form, and re-add it to include the updated wording.

Add your notice and consent options

You can add and configure notice and consent options in each of your forms.

Add notice and consent to a legacy form

To add the notice and consent option to your legacy form:

  • In the left panel, click to expand Other form elements.
  • Under Data privacy options, click the dropdown menu and select your notice and consent option.
  • If you’d like to make any changes to the notice and consent text for this form, in the form preview on the right, hover over the Data privacy options field and click the edit pencil icon.
  • In the top right, click Update to publish your form updates.
Additional notice and consent options

You can add additional subscription type checkboxes to allow visitors to consent to communication from multiple subscription types on a single form.

To add additional notice and consent options in legacy forms:

Please note: you can only add additional notice and consent options to legacy forms if you have selected Consent checkbox for communications; form submit as consent to process or Consent checkboxes for communications and processing option.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • Hover over the form name and click Edit.
  • In a legacy form, hover over the data privacy and consent option and click the edit pencil icon to edit your data privacy and consent options.
  • In the Data privacy consent section, click Add another checkbox.
  • In the Consent to communicate checkbox section, click the Subscription type dropdown menu and select a subscription type.
  • In the Checkbox Label section, you can make any edits as needed.
  • In the upper right, click Publish.
Style your notice and consent options (legacy)

If you want to style the notice and consent text without impacting the rest of the form styling, you can use the CSS selector listed below as a starting point:

.legal-consent-container .hs-richtext

Depending on the consent options your team has chosen, the selector may need to be modified

Notice and consent options

When building your form, you can select from the following notice and consent options below:

  • Implicit processing consent and individual checkboxes for communications
  • Separate consents (Individual checkboxes for each consent)
  • Legitimate interest

Consent checkbox for communications; form submit as consent to process

  • With this option, you can collect consent to communicate through an affirmative opt-in using a checkbox that specifies the communication/subscription type.
  • You can add more than one checkbox to allow visitors to consent to communication for more than one subscription type.
  • With this option, consent to process personal data is collected implicitly when the contact clicks the submit button.
  • If a contact submitting the form doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, the form submission will still be processed. However, the contact won’t be subscribed to any communications.
  • It is not possible to pre-select the consent to communicate checkbox, but if you’re using a legacy form, you can make it required.
  • If the contact previously subscribed in the past and subsequently doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, this is not equivalent to the contact withdrawing their consent.
Consent checkboxes for communications and processing
  • With this option, you can collect consent to communicate through an affirmative opt-in using a checkbox that specifies the communication/subscription type.
  • You can add more than one checkbox to allow visitors to consent to communication for more than one subscription type.
  • With this option, consent to process personal data is collected explicitly.:
    • The contact needs to select the consent to process data checkbox in order to give their consent. You cannot process a visitor’s data and accept the form submission if they haven’t given explicit consent for you to do so.
    • Without selecting this checkbox, visitors will not be able to submit your form. If you still want to offer the visitor access to your content without processing their data, you can do so by adding the consent to process footer with a hyperlink to your content.
  • If a contact submitting the form doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, the form submission is still processed, and the contact won’t be subscribed to any communications.
  • It is not possible to pre-select the consent to communicate checkbox, but if you’re using a legacy form, you can make it required.
  • If the contact has already subscribed in the past and subsequently doesn’t select the consent to communicate checkbox, this is not equivalent to the contact withdrawing their consent
Legitimate interest
  • If your legal basis for processing is legitimate interest, your form will show a notice informing visitors that you need their information to contact them about your products and services. They can unsubscribe from these communications at any time.
  • With this option, the contact is not required to give their consent to you, and will just see a notice.

Allow form submissions without email addresses to create contacts

By default, form submissions require a populated email address field to create contacts. However, you can turn on the Allow submissions without email addresses to create contacts setting to allow visitors to submit HubSpot forms without an email address and still be added to your CRM. This is an account-wide setting that affects all HubSpot forms.

A form submission without an email address may still be associated with an existing contact if the visitor is identified by tracking cookie. Learn more about how visitors are tracked in HubSpot.

Permissions required Edit forms permissions are required to edit form submission settings.

Before you get started

  • If you’re using a non-HubSpot form, this setting does not apply. A populated email address field is still needed to collect submissions. Learn more about using non-HubSpot forms.
  • Contacts are created only from future submissions after you turn on this setting. Past submissions without an email address won’t create contacts.
  • If you’re using a custom email field and have this setting turned on, form submissions will create contacts. However, when the default HubSpot Email property remains empty, contacts cannot receive marketing emails, which require a primary email address.
  • Since a form submission without an email address is deduplicated through tracking cookies, if two visitors with the same cookie fill out a form with no email address (e.g., if they were using the same device), both submissions may be associated with the same contact. However, if the Automatically create new contacts from unknown email addresses is turned on, each submission will create a new contact.

Allow form submissions without email addresses to create contacts

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Forms.
  • Click the Submissions Settings tab.
  • Toggle the Allow submissions without email addresses to create contacts switch on.
  • Click Save.

With this setting turned on, form submissions without an email address are deduplicated based on their cookies. If the visitor cannot be identified through a known cookie, a new contact may be created.

Analyze form performance with form submission reports

Form submission reports show how your forms are performing by tracking submission data and trends across your forms. Use these preconfigured reports to monitor submission activity, compare performance, and identify which forms generate the most conversions. For example, use these reports to compare submission volume by web page or track submissions for new versus existing contacts.

To create custom reports, learn how to report on forms using the custom report builder.

Permissions required

  • View forms permissions are required to access form submission data.
  • Reports access is required to view, create, or edit dashboards and reports.

Before you get started

To generate report insights with Breeze Assistant, HubSpot’s AI conversational assistant, turn on the Give users access to Breeze Assistant setting.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Review form submission reports

Form submission reports show how your forms are performing by tracking form submission data and trends for the selected date range.

To access form submission reports:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • At the top, click the Analyze tab.

Use the following reports to monitor form performance, compare results across forms, and identify areas for optimization.

Report

Description

Form overview

Review overall form performance with count of form submission metadata, conversion rate, and count of form views.

Form submission counts

Track submissions received for each form to identify which forms generate the most conversions.

Form submissions over time

Track submissions across forms over time to identify trends and changes in performance. Use this data to identify peak submission periods and monitor how your lead generation efforts are performing.

Form submissions over time broken down by form name

Track submissions for individual forms. Click form names to display or hide forms displayed in the report.

Form submissions by pages

Track submissions by page title to identify which web pages are most effective at converting visitors.

Form submissions over time broken down by page

Track submissions over time by web page. Monitor trends or performance changes to identify high-performing pages and help you optimize underperforming pages.

Form submissions by contact lifecycle stage

Track submissions by contact lifecycle stages to monitor which forms are being completed by contacts at different stages of the customer journey. Use this data to understand engagement patterns and optimize your form strategy for different audience segments.

Form submissions by new vs existing contacts

Track submissions by visitor type to monitor submissions from new contacts versus existing contacts for each form. Use this data to understand which forms are capturing new leads versus engaging your existing contacts.

Form submission totals

View top-performing forms based on the number of submissions in the last 30 days. Track the form views and conversion rates for each form.

Please note: if a single contact submits the same form multiple times, the submission count may be higher than the number of unique contacts who submitted the form.

Filter or edit a report

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • At the top, click the Analyze tab.
  • To filter the report data, at the top, select from the following quick filters:
    • Date range: filter based on the date that the form was submitted.
    • Form name: filter based on specific form names.
    • Contact lifecycle stage: filter based on the different stages of the contact’s lifecycle.
    • Marketing campaign: filter based on the campaign the form is associated with.
  • To apply a custom filter, at the top, click Advanced filters.
    • Click + Add filter.
    • Search for or select your property.
    • In the dropdown menu, select the filter criteria.
    • At the bottom, click Apply filter.
  • To edit an individual report, hover over the report and click the filter View and filter icon. Learn how to use the report viewer.
  • To generate report insights with Breeze Assistant, hover over a report and click the breezeSingleStar AI icon. Learn how to discover insights on reports.

Save a report

Save individual form submission reports to your report library or another dashboard.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • At the top, click the Analyze tab.
  • Hover over the report and click the filter View and filter icon.
  • At the bottom of the report viewer, click Save report.
  • In the right panel, configure the following report details:
    • Enter a report name.
    • Enter a description of the report.
    • Under Add this report to a dashboard, select the radio button to confirm whether you’d like to add the report to a dashboard:
      • Don’t add to dashboard: your report won’t be added to a dashboard. Instead, it’ll be saved in your report library so you can use it later.
      • Add to existing dashboard: you can select an existing dashboard to add the report to. When you select this option, you can select the dashboard from the dropdown menu.
      • Add to new dashboard: you can create a new custom dashboard and add the form report to the new dashboard. When you select this option, you’ll be prompted to enter a dashboard name in the following step.
    • In the bottom right, click Next or Save & add if you’re adding the report to an existing dashboard.
    • If you aren’t adding the report to a dashboard, or you’re creating a new dashboard, under Who can access this report, select the radio button to set the report access.
      • Reports that are added to existing dashboards will be controlled by the dashboard’s access settings.
  • In the bottom right, click Save or Save & add if you’re adding the report to a dashboard.

Create a custom dashboard using form reports

Create custom dashboards using the preconfigured form submission reports.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.

  • At the top, click the Analyze tab.

  • In the top right, click Actions and select Save dashboard.

  • In the right panel, under Reports included in this dashboard, all available form reports are selected by default. Clear the checkboxes next to reports that you don’t want to include in the new dashboard.

  • At the bottom right, click Next.

  • Enter a dashboard name.

  • Under Who can access this dashboard?, select the radio button to specify the users or teams that can access the new dashboard.

  • At the bottom, click Create dashboard. Learn how to manage your dashboard.

Associate forms with Salesforce campaigns

If you have the HubSpot-Salesforce integration enabled, you can associate a form with an active Salesforce campaign.

Before you get started

Before associating your form with a Salesforce campaign, do note the following:

  • The campaign status will be set to Responded and cannot be edited. If you want to edit the campaign status going forward, consider using a workflow to associate your contacts with your Salesforce campaign.
  • The contact’s association with the Salesforce campaign cannot be removed.
  • Forms submitted using a share link cannot be associated with a Salesforce campaign.
  • If you’re embedding a form on an external page:
    • If you’re using the legacy form editor, you can add contacts to a Salesforce campaign directly from the form editor. This option is not available in the updated form editor.
    • If you’re using the updated form editor, it’s recommended to use a workflow to associate your contacts with your Salesforce campaign.

Associate a form on a HubSpot page with a Salesforce campaign

Permissions required

  • Edit forms permissions are required to create or edit a form.
  • Edit and Publish page permissions are required to edit and publish pages.

After adding a form module to your HubSpot page, you can associate the form with a Salesforce campaign.

  • Navigate to your content:
    • Website Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Website Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Website Pages directly.
    • Landing Pages: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Content > Landing Pages. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Content > Landing Pages directly.
  • Click the name of your page.
  • In the content editor, click the form module.
  • In the left panel, scroll down and click the Salesforce campaign dropdown menu and select the Salesforce campaign to associate the form with.
  • In the upper right, click Publish or Update to take your changes live.

Associate a legacy form embedded on an external page with a Salesforce campaign

Permissions required Edit forms permissions are required to create or edit a form.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • Hover over the form name and click Edit.
  • In the upper right, click Share.
  • In the dialog box, under Embed code, click the Add contacts to a Salesforce campaign dropdown menu and select the Salesforce campaign to associate the form with.
  • Click Copy.
  • Paste the embed code in the HTML of your external page.

Please note: these changes will not automatically update existing forms embedded on your external pages. You must replace the embed code for each existing form with the new embed code that contains the selected Salesforce campaign.

Auto-populate form fields with a query string

Automatically populate form fields by adding query strings to the page URL before sending the form to your contacts. Form fields, including hidden fields, will automatically populate based on the query string added. For example, you can create custom UTM properties and use UTM parameters to auto-populate a hidden form field.

Before you get started

  • Query strings cannot auto-populate dependent form fields.
  • Dependent form fields cannot be triggered based on multiple values within a query string.

Create static query strings with pre-defined values

To create a URL with a static query string, you’ll need to copy the internal property name of any fields you want to auto-populate, then add them to the end of your page URL.

Copy the property’s internal name
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Properties.
  • Click the name of a property to pre-populate values.
  • Copy the Internal name of the property. Learn more about internal property names.
  • Repeat this for any other properties you want to auto-populate values for in your form.
Create the URL with static query strings

After copying the internal property names, you can set up the page URL that you’ll send to your contacts:

  • In your browser, navigate to the page your form is on. Then, copy the URL.
  • Add a question mark (?) to the end of the page URL. If the page URL already has query parameters, add an ampersand (&) instead.
  • Add the internal name of the property, followed by an equal sign and the value to auto-populate in the field. Take note of the rules for adding values, depending on the field type of the property:
    • Single checkbox: query strings must contain either a true or false value, not yes or no.
    • Date picker: query strings must contain a date value in a YYYY-MM-DD format.
    • Multiple checkboxes: query string values must match the property’s value options exactly, with a semi-colon separating multiple values.
    • Radio select/Dropdown select: query string values must match the property’s value options exactly.
    • For all field types: when creating query strings, these rules apply to all field types.
      • Spaces in a property value must be separated with %20.
      • Multiple different properties must be separated with an ampersand (&).
Example URL with a static query string

After creating the URL with static query strings, you can use it as a link in your content such as emails and pages. A contact who clicks the link will see the form on the page auto-populated with the pre-defined values in the query string. Here’s an example and breakdown of a URL with properly formatted static query strings:

`[domain.com](http://www.domain.com/marketing-offer?firstname=John&lastname=Smith&email=jsmith@email.com&favorite_season=Winter%20Season&favorite_fast_food=Burger;Taco&number_property=7&will_you_come_to_the_party=Maybe&do_you_like_parties=true&date_of_party=2018-10-24) `

  • Beginning of query string and single-line text field: ?firstname=John
  • Single-line text field: &lastname=Smith
  • Single-line text field: &email=jsmith@email.com
  • Dropdown select field: &favorite_season=Winter%20Season
  • Multiple checkboxes field: &favorite_fast_food=Burger;Tacos
  • Number field: &favorite_number=7
  • Radio select field: &will_you_come_to_the_party=Maybe
  • Single checkbox field: &do_you_like_parties=true
  • Date picker field: &date_of_party=2018-10-2

Create dynamic query strings with personalization tokens

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to create dynamic query strings.

Use personalization tokens to create dynamic query strings that auto-populate form fields based on known contact properties.

Please note:

  • Dynamic query strings with personalization tokens will only function correctly when the URL is directed to a HubSpot-hosted page with a HubSpot form.
  • This functionality will not work if the URL is directed to a HubSpot standalone form page.
  • The URL with the dynamic query strings must also be placed in your HubSpot content or an external page with your HubSpot tracking code.
Retrieve the personalization token

Retrieve the personalization tokens needed to create your query strings.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click Create email or click the name of a draft email.
  • In the rich text toolbar, click Personalize.
  • Set up your personalization tokens:
    • In the dialog box, select a personalization token to auto-populate in your form.
    • Select the Use this property’s global default value checkbox when inserting your personalization token.
    • Continue adding additional personalization tokens as needed.
  • In the rich text toolbar, click More and select the codef source code icon to view the HTML of your email.
  • In the source code, you’ll see the raw code for each personalization token added to the email body. Each token will be enclosed with double brackets {{ }}. Highlight a token (e.g., {{ contact.firstname }}), then right-click and select Copy.
  • Repeat this for any personalization tokens you want to pre-populate in your form.
  • At the bottom of the dialog box, click Cancel and close to exit the source code.
Create the URL with dynamic query strings

Use the personalization tokens to create a URL with dynamic query strings. This URL can be used as a link in your HubSpot content such as emails and pages, or on an external page with your HubSpot tracking code. A contact that clicks the link will see the form on the page auto-populated with their information if they have known values for the fields in the query string.

To create a URL with dynamic query strings:

  • In your browser, navigate to the page your form is on. Then, copy the URL.
  • Using the page URL and personalization tokens, format your dynamic query string:
    • Add a question mark (?) to the end of the page URL. If the page URL already has query parameters, add an ampersand (&) instead.
    • Add the internal name of the property, followed by an equal sign and the personalization token. Ensure all spaces are removed from the token (e.g., {{contact.firstname}} ).
    • Separate multiple properties with an ampersand (&).

The following is an example of a URL with properly formatted dynamic query strings:

[domain.com](http://www.domain.com/marketing-offer?firstname={{contact.firstname}}&lastname={{contact.lastname}}&email={{contact.email}})

Next steps

Learn how to pass contact property values with hidden form fields.

Automate form submission actions

Use form automations to trigger actions that occur after a visitor submits a form. For example, after a contact submits a demo request form, you can send a confirmation email or add the contact to a segment.

Form automations help you respond to leads immediately and standardize follow-up processes directly in the form editor. For more advanced automation, learn more about creating workflows.

Permissions required The following permissions are required:

  • Edit forms permissions are required to create and edit forms.
  • Edit workflows permissions are required to create and edit simple workflows in the form editor.

Before you get started

Before you begin using automations with forms, take note of simple workflow behavior and subscription limits.

Understand simple workflow behavior

Set up a simple workflow directly from the form editor to automate follow-up actions, such as sending an email or creating a task. When creating a simple workflow:

  • By default, the simple workflow’s enrollment trigger will be set to the form submission. This enrollment trigger cannot be changed.
  • Contacts are enrolled in the simple workflow each time the form is submitted, even if they have been enrolled before.
  • If you have a Marketing Hub subscription that includes marketing contacts, your contacts must be set as marketing contacts to receive emails sent from workflows. Learn more about setting contacts as marketing.

After a contact submits a form, the actions you’ve configured will be triggered. For example, you can set up a workflow to automatically send an internal email notification to a team member.

Understand simple workflow limits

The number of simple workflows you can create, the number of actions, and the type of actions you can add depends on your subscription. Learn more about form automation subscription limits in the HubSpot Product & Services Catalog.

  • If you’re using HubSpot’s free tools, you can create one Send an email after form submission simple workflow for each form. There’s a limit of one action for each simple workflow.
  • If you have a Starter, Professional, or Enterprise account that doesn’t include Marketing Hub, you can create one simple workflow for each form. There’s a limit of three actions for each simple workflow.
  • In a Marketing Hub Starter account, you can add up to 10 actions in a simple workflow and create one simple workflow for each form.
  • In a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise account, you can add as many actions as you need to your simple workflow and add multiple simple workflows for each form. If you have Workflows View permissions, you can also view simple workflows on the workflows index page. You can filter these simple workflows on the workflows index page by applying the Created in filter and selecting Forms.

If you need to create more workflows or add more actions and have a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, build custom workflows in the workflows tool.

Choose your simple workflow actions

The following actions are available in simple workflows:

  • Communications: send a marketing email, internal email notification or an internal marketing email.
  • CRM: create a new record, task or assign the enrolled contact within a selected team or between specified users. This action is only compatible with activated, paid users.
  • Marketing: add to or remove from an ads audience or static list.
  • Data ops: send a webhook to an external application. For example, webhooks can send a HubSpot company’s information (formatted in JSON) to an external CRM. Learn more about triggering webhooks.

If you have a Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription, you can access more actions by building a workflow using the workflows tool. Learn more about the workflow actions available.

Create a simple workflow in the form editor

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.

  • Hover over the name of an existing form, and click Edit. Or, create a new form.

  • In the form editor, click the workflows automation icon in the left panel. If you’re editing a legacy form, navigate to the Automation tab.

  • Create a workflow to send an email after a form submission or create a custom workflow and select what actions are taken after a form submission.

    • To automatically trigger a follow-up email after each form submission, under Send an email after form submission, click Create this workflow.
    • To create your own workflow from a blank template, under Create your own simple workflow, click Create new workflow. In the right slide-in panel, under Trigger the action(s) when, select the option A contact submitted a form.

  • To add other workflow actions, click the + plus icon.

    • To edit an action, click the workflow action, then make changes in the left panel.

    • To delete workflow actions, on the workflow action, click the delete delete icon. Select This action to delete only the selected action, or select This action and all after it to delete the selected action and all following actions.

    • To leave a note on a workflow action for you or your team’s reference, hover over the action and click the comments comments icon. Learn how to add comments to workflow actions.

  • To edit the workflow’s name, at the workflow header, click the edit edit icon.

  • To delete a workflow, click Actions at the top. Then, select Delete workflow.

  • To turn on a workflow, next to the workflow name, toggle the switch on. Then, click Got it. After publishing your simple workflow, any changes made to the workflow will automatically apply to currently enrolled contacts.

Add another simple workflow

To add another simple workflow to your form:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • Click the name of an existing form, and click Edit. If you don’t have an existing form, learn how to create a new form.
  • In the form editor, click the workflows automation icon in the left panel. If you’re editing a legacy form, navigate to the Automation tab.
  • In the top right, click + Add a new simple workflow.
  • In the right panel, under Trigger the action(s) when, select the A contact submitted a form option.
  • Click Create, then set up your workflow.

You can also use simple workflows with Facebook, Google or LinkedIn ad campaigns. Learn more about using automation with HubSpot’s ads tool.

Turn on form automation notifications

Subscription required An Enterprise subscription is required to turn on form automation notifications.

After you turn on a simple workflow in the form editor, notify users when form automation needs review or when the enrollment rate changes.

  • In the form editor, click thesettis automati workflows automation icon.

  • In the top right of the simple workflow, click Actions and select Edit notifications.

  • In the right panel, toggle the Get notified when this automation has issues switch on to receive notifications if there are any errors that need attention.

  • To receive notifications when the enrollment rate fluctuates, toggle the Get notified if the enrollment rate changes switch on. Then, choose from the following options:

    • Use AI: toggle this switch on to automatically detect any changes to the rate of enrollment based on data from the last 30 days.
    • Use a manual range: toggle this switch on to manually set a fixed rate threshold that will trigger notifications when exceeded.

  • In the Notification recipients section, click the Users and Teams dropdown menus and select the recipients to send the notifications to. Only users who have turned on HubSpot notifications for at least one channel will be able to receive these notifications.

Block form submissions from specific email domains or free email providers

Block form submissions from email addresses that use free email providers or specific email domains. For example, blocking free providers like Gmail or Yahoo limits submissions to business contacts, while blocking specific domains reduces spam and unwanted submissions.

When a visitor enters a blocked email domain, they’ll be prompted to enter a different email address before submitting the form. Configure blocked email domains on individual forms, or use an account-level setting to apply them across all your forms.

Permissions required Edit forms permissions are required to create and edit forms.

Block email domains using account-level settings

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Forms.
  • Click the Submissions Settings tab.
  • To block specific domains:
    • In the Email domains to block field, enter the domains you want to block, separated by commas (e.g., domainexample.com, domaintest.com).
    • At the bottom left, click Save.
  • To block free email providers:
    • Toggle the Block free email domains switch on.
    • At the bottom left, click Save.

Once saved, any blocked domains or free email providers will apply across all your HubSpot forms.

Block email domains on individual forms

Block email domains in the updated form editor
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • Create a new form or hover over an existing form and click Edit.
  • In the left sidebar, click the settings settings icon.
  • In the left panel, click the Submission settings tab.
  • To block specific domains:
    • Enter domains in the Email domains to block field.
    • Enter only the root domain without the www prefix or @ symbol. For example, enter gmail.com, not www.gmail.com or @gmail.com.
  • To block submissions from HubSpot’s default list of free domains, toggle the Block free email providers switch on.
  • In the top right, click Review and update.
Block email domains in the legacy form editor
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • Hover over a form and click Edit.
  • In the form editor, hover over the Email field and click the edit edit icon.
  • To block specific domains:
    • In the Email domains to block field, enter the domains you want to block, separated by commas (e.g., domainexample.com, domaintest.com).
    • Enter only the root domain without the www prefix or @ symbol. For example, enter gmail.com, not www.gmail.com or @gmail.com.
  • To block HubSpot’s default list of free domains, select the Block free email providers checkbox.
  • In the top right, click Update or Publish.

Contacts from non-HubSpot forms not syncing to Mailchimp

If contacts submitted through non-HubSpot forms aren’t syncing to Mailchimp, the issue is typically caused by required merge tags in the corresponding Mailchimp audience.

Generally, HubSpot doesn’t send a value for merge tags, but will always sync email addresses to Mailchimp since the email address for a contact is always known. If your forms include a first and last name field, HubSpot should also capture this information and send it to Mailchimp.

Review sync errors in HubSpot

Permissions required App Marketplace access is required to view email sync settings.

To identify and troubleshoot the most recent error in your email sync settings:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Integrations > Email Service Provider.
  • Review the most recent error reported by Mailchimp.

Common merge tag errors include:

  • FNAME must be provided - Please enter a value
  • LNAME must be provided - Please enter a value
  • MMERGE2 must be provided - Please enter a value
  • MMERGE(x) must be provided - Please enter a value

Resolve merge tag errors in Mailchimp

After confirming the error, to resolve the error in Mailchimp:

  • Log in to Mailchimp and locate the audience connected to your non-HubSpot form.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Settings > Audience fields and |MERGE| tags.
  • Identify the field that corresponds to the error shown in HubSpot.
    • The value in the Put this tag in your content column matches the merge tag in the error.
  • Clear the Required? checkbox for the corresponding field to allow HubSpot to sync information to this audience.
  • In the bottom left, click Save Changes.

Convert non-HubSpot forms into HubSpot forms

When a submission to an external form is collected in HubSpot, a non-HubSpot form is created on the forms index page. If you want to use a HubSpot form instead of your external form, you can convert your external non-HubSpot form into a HubSpot form with the same fields.

After converting, you can then embed the HubSpot form to replace the existing non-HubSpot form on your external page.

Permissions required Edit forms permissions are required to convert non-HubSpot forms into HubSpot forms.

To convert a non-HubSpot form into a HubSpot form:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • In the upper left, click the Form type dropdown menu and select Non-HubSpot form.
  • Hover over the non-HubSpot form you want to convert and click Actions, then select Copy to HubSpot.
  • In the dialog box, click Copy to HubSpot to create a HubSpot form with the same form fields.
  • Once the HubSpot form is ready, you’ll be redirected to the form editor where you can customize your form fields.
  • In the top right, click Review and update.
  • Click Update to publish your form updates.
  • Embed the newly copied form on your website to replace the existing non-HubSpot form. The embedded HubSpot form will collect new submissions.

Once converted, a new HubSpot form will be created in your account, while the original non-HubSpot form and its historic submissions will remain. The HubSpot form can be identified by the word Converted in the title of your original form.

Create and customize forms

Use HubSpot forms to collect information from visitors and create or update records in your CRM. Capture leads, gather customer information, and trigger follow-up actions such as sending emails or adding contacts to segments.

For example, add a form to a landing page to collect email addresses for a newsletter. Then send an automated follow-up email after the visitor submits the form.

Learn more about building custom solutions using the Forms API.

Learn more about this feature by joining a small group coaching session

Permissions required Edit forms permissions are required to create and edit forms.

Create a form

Create a form to collect information from visitors and capture their information in the CRM.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Forms. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Forms directly.
  • To associate a form with a specific brand, click your profile picture, navigate to Brand, then select the Brand you want to associate the form with. Learn more about associating assets with brands.
  • In the top right, click Create form.
  • Select the Form Editor, then click Next.
  • Navigate to a pre-made template and click Use template. To build your own form, use the Start from blank template.

Add fields to a form

Form fields collect information from visitors and store it in specific CRM properties. The property a field is connected to determines which object the data is stored on (e.g., contact or company). For example, if you connect a field to the default company property, Company name, a company record may be created or updated and associated with the contact.

  • In the top left of the form editor, click the + add icon.
  • In the Fields panel, click and drag the field type onto the form.
  • In the Edit field panel, connect the field to an existing or new property:
    • Existing property: search for and select an existing property to connect the field to.
    • New property: click Create new property. In the right panel, set up your property. Then, click Create property.

Once created, the new property is automatically connected to the selected form field. In the property settings, the option to Show in forms and chatflows is selected by default. Learn how to manage your properties.
