Overview of email authentication

To ensure your marketing emails sent via HubSpot comply with the authentication standards and sending policies enforced by major email inbox providers (e.g., Gmail and Yahoo Mail), it’s recommended to connect your email sending domain to HubSpot. The domain connection process involves setting up four separate DNS record types in your DNS provider’s settings: MX, DKIM, SPF, and DMARC.

This article provides an overview of what these records are and how their associated authentication protocols work. Learn more about connecting an email sending domain.

Please note: your HubSpot account manager or members of HubSpot Support can help you understand best practices and how to use HubSpot tools to set up authentication, but they cannot make these decisions for you, nor can they manage your DNS settings. You will need to work with your IT team or your email administrator to fully set up email authentication. You can also contact a third-party DMARC consulting or reporting service for additional assistance.

Understand the impact of authenticated emails

Unauthenticated emails and email variable domains

All marketing emails and transactional emails sent via HubSpot that do not use a connected email sending domain are subject to a variable domain managed by HubSpot. This enables the automatic detection and removal of your unauthenticated domain without canceling the send. This process may negatively affect how your recipients engage with your emails.

For example, if you attempt to send an email from an unauthenticated domain, such as user@yourcompany.com, then HubSpot will modify the email address to use a HubSpot managed domain (e.g., hs-domain.com), so the resulting sending address will appear as: user=yourcompany.com@hs-domain.com.

Learn more about checking your automated emails to see if they require an authenticated From address.

Impact on your HubSpot account

While DKIM, SPF, and DMARC are not strictly required to send emails via HubSpot, you cannot send emails with your domain in the From address (e.g. user@company.com) until you connect that domain to HubSpot by setting up DKIM. This will also increase email deliverability for that domain.

Domains not connected as an email sending domain in your account will be modified to a HubSpot-hosted system domain.

Impact on email performance

Most inbox service providers prefer emails authenticated by DKIM. Emails sent without DKIM authentication are more likely to bounce, quarantine, or be categorized as spam. Quarantined emails will appear as delivered in HubSpot, but will not be visible to most recipients, so it’s highly recommended that you set up DKIM to improve deliverability.

Please note: some inbox providers, such as Google and Yahoo, will be requiring DMARC, DKIM, and SPF to be fully set up on any domain sending bulk emails to their users. If you don’t meet these requirements, emails from your domain will be bounced. These bounces will be categorized as a DMARC or Policy bounce.

Guide to DKIM

DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) is a method of email authentication aimed to prevent email spoofing, which is a technique used by malicious actors to send emails with forged sender addresses.

To set up DKIM in HubSpot, you’ll be guided to set up DKIM using two CNAME records in your DNS provider. Once you configure your DKIM records in your DNS provider using a public key that HubSpot provides you with, a receiving mail server (e.g. Gmail) will be able to verify the signature of your sent email that’s associated with your domain.

Learn how to add these records by following the instructions in this article.

Once you’ve added these DNS records and they’ve been verified by HubSpot and your DNS provider, the DKIM signature will be included in the headers of your sent emails, which correlates to the associated CNAME entries you configured.

Guide to SPF

SPF (Sender Policy Framework) is an email authentication standard used to verify that the sending email server is authorized to send email on behalf of a specific domain.

SPF is traditionally required for the envelope return path domain, which is the address that bounces will be sent to. HubSpot already has this configured for marketing emails sent through its shared servers. All dedicated IP customers are required to configure SPF on their envelope return path domain as part of their initial IP setup.

It’s also highly recommended that you add HubSpot’s SPF record to your From Address domain. This will be set up as a TXT record in your DNS provider, using the value provided in your HubSpot domain settings. This record will provide a regularly updated list of IP addresses that HubSpot will use to send marketing emails from your From Address domain.

You can follow this guide to add HubSpot to your SPF record.

Once you’ve added the SPF record and the verification process is complete, when an email server processes one of your sent emails, they can validate that HubSpot is on your domain’s allowlist of valid senders.

Guide to DMARC

DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting and Conformance) is an email authentication protocol that further safeguards email domain owners from email spoofing and other unauthorized use of their domain.

By configuring a DMARC record, inbox providers can confirm how to process any emails sent from your domain that do not pass SPF and DKIM checks. A DMARC also provides a reporting mechanism for domain owners to learn how often recipient servers around the world are receiving emails sent from their domain, and what percentage is properly authenticated.

Learn more about the available policy values and a couple example policies in the sections below. When you’re ready to set up your DMARC record, check out the instructions in this article.

Policy values

A DMARC policy can be defined by adding a TXT record in your DNS provider settings, with a value that can include the following semicolon-separated properties:

  • v: the DMARC version.
  • p: the policy type that dictates how to process emails that do not pass. The policy can be set to one of the following types:
    • none: used to collect feedback and gain visibility into email streams without impacting existing flows.
    • quarantine: filter emails that do not pass authentication into the recipient’s quarantine.
    • reject: bounce emails that do not pass authentication.
  • sp: used to apply a policy to a subdomain of the DMARC record.
  • pct: the percentage of total unique sends that failed authentication to apply this policy to. For example, if your DMARC record included p=reject; pct=25, and 100 emails failed authentication, only 25 of them will be bounced, while the other 75 will be delivered to their recipients.
    • Defining this property can help slowly ramp up your authentication policy to ensure it’s working as expected.
    • Note that this parameter is sometimes ignored by certain inbox service providers.
  • ruf & rua: two optional parameters that specify an email address to send DMARC reporting data to. These must be provided in URI mailto format (e.g., mailto:reporting@example.com). The reporting data that’s sent differs based on the parameter:
    • rua: an aggregate report of all your domain traffic.
    • ruf: failure reporting data that includes redacted copies of individual messages that failed authentication.
  • adkim & aspf: specifies the alignment mode for DKIM and SPF. These should both be set to r (i.e., a relaxed alignment). A relaxed alignment should be the default setting for DMARC for DNS services.

Once you’ve added and verified the DMARC record in your DNS provider, all receiving email servers can authenticate incoming emails from your domain and handle any failures according to the policy you specified.

Example policies

You can customize your DMARC policy to fit your business needs. Here are a few examples:

Neutral policy

v=DMARC1; p=none;

This is an example of a neutral DMARC policy with no additional parameters. A neutral policy is useful for senders who’re just starting to get familiar with DMARC. This is the bare minimum for DMARC to function.

Strict policy with aggregate reporting

v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:reporting@example.com;

The example above defines a strict DMARC policy to bounce any emails that fail authentication, and provides an email address to send aggregate reporting data to.

Quarantine policy with failure reporting

v=DMARC1; p=quarantine; pct=25; ruf=mailto:reporting@example.com;

This example defines a policy that will quarantine 25% of emails that fail authentication, while the other 75% of emails that fail authentication will be permitted for delivery. The policy also provides a reporting address where an individual notification email can be sent for each email that fails authentication.

Defining a value for the pct property can allow you to test a random sample of messages that failed DMARC to allow you to check that legitimate emails are still being delivered properly.

Please note: HubSpot Support cannot help with DMARC record setup. The DMARC policy you set up is unique to your business needs and your DNS provider. You should consult your IT administrator or whoever manages your DNS settings for help setting up DMARC. You can also consult third-party DMARC consulting or reporting services for additional assistance.

Guide to MX

MX (Mail Exchanger) records are DNS entries that specify which mail servers are authorized to receive email for a domain. While MX records are primarily associated with incoming email, they can also affect email sending.

A null MX record, configured as MX 0 ., tells receiving mail servers that your domain doesn’t accept incoming email. Some inbox providers reject emails sent from domains with a null MX record. When this occurs, emails can bounce with a permanent failure, which can impact your sending reputation.

If you’re using a custom sending domain or subdomain to send marketing emails through HubSpot, review your domain’s MX record using a DNS lookup tool, such as MXToolbox.

  • It’s recommended to remove a null MX record (MX 0 .) from your domain.
  • If the domain is used only for sending and you don’t want to receive incoming email, leave the MX record unset instead of publishing a null MX record. The absence of an MX record doesn’t carry the same email rejection risk as a null MX record.

Overview of email deliverability

Whether you’re sending marketing emails for the first time or migrating from another email service provider (ESP), you should follow a number of prerequisite steps to protect your sending reputation and get the most out of your marketing email efforts.

This guide will help you configure your email sending settings, provide best practices for migrating your existing contacts and ensuring they’re engaged with your emails, and recommend how to analyze your email sending performance.

Set up allowlisting and configure your DNS records

If your business has implemented security settings that prevent emails from unknown IPs from being delivered, you should coordinate with your IT team to discuss whether HubSpot’s IPs and email addresses need to be added to your company’s allowlist. You can also work with your IT team to connect your email sending domain and add HubSpot to your SPF record.

  • Set up allowlisting
  • Manage your email authentication (Starter, Professional, or Enterprise)

Migrate your contacts from another CRM or ESP

If you are migrating contacts from an existing CRM or ESP, it’s important to identify the contacts that have proper consent to receive marketing emails. If the contacts have met all consent and permission requirements for receiving your emails, they’re more likely to engage with your content and less likely to unsubscribe and negatively impact your sending reputation. You should also ensure that contacts who needed to allowlist sending IPs from your previous ESP also allowlist the HubSpot IPs associated with your account.

  • Understand sending marketing emails
  • Understand opt-in consent for email
  • Import opted out contacts
  • Understand why contacts didn’t receive marketing emails

Acquire and manage new subscribers

Using forms on your website to drive conversions is one of the best ways to gain new subscribers. You can ensure that your subscribers are legitimate and highly engaged by using CAPTCHA on your forms and setting up double opt-in for your new contacts.

  • Create and edit forms
  • Prevent spam form submissions
  • Set up double opt-in for emails

Drive engagement with emails

One of the best ways to ensure a positive engagement rate and maintain a healthy sending reputation is to tailor the content and delivery of your emails to each recipient. By personalizing your emails to individual recipients, sending at the right time, and making sure you don’t overwhelm them with emails, your contacts are more likely to open and convert on your content.

  • Use personalization tokens
  • Schedule emails based on your recipients’ time zones (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)
  • Run A/B tests for marketing emails (Marketing Hub Professional and Enterprise)
  • Set up an email frequency safeguard (Marketing Hub Enterprise)

Review and action post-send email data

As you continue to send marketing emails to your contacts, you can analyze your emails’ performance and engagement data. You can use this data to gain insight into bounce reasons, identify which emails have been more successful, and discover recommendations for improvement. If email open rates fall below critical thresholds for an extended period of time, your brand’s emails may be going to spam and you should consider implementing a reputation repair plan.

  • Monitor your email sending reputation with the email health tool
  • Analyze marketing email sending performance
  • Email bounce types
  • Improve your email sending reputation with a repair plan

Review your contacts

You should regularly review the contacts you’re emailing as your subscriber base grows. Emailing unengaged contacts is a common reason for reputation and inbox placement issues. To be proactive, you should build a plan for addressing unengaged contacts that you and your team can commit to and revisit often.

  • Understand graymail and avoid sending email to unengaged contacts
  • Exclude specific segments or contacts from receiving a marketing email

Personalize automated emails with nurture agent

With Breeze, HubSpot’s AI, you can use nurture agent to drive marketing email engagement by tailoring marketing email text to individual recipients. Nurture agent uses CRM data and web research to rewrite subject lines, preview text, CTA text, and the email body for a percentage of contacts who receive the email.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential considerations of using it.

HubSpot Credits required Nurture agent consumes HubSpot Credits each time it personalizes an email for a contact. Learn more about how many HubSpot Credits nurture agent uses in the Product & Services Catalog.

Understand requirements
  • In order to use this feature, the following AI settings must be turned on:
    • Give users access to generative AI tools and features.
    • CRM data.
  • It’s recommended to set up your brand voice so the tone of generated content is consistent with how your brand communicates. Once brand voice is set up, nurture agent will use it if brand voice is turned on for marketing emails.
Understand limitations and considerations
  • Nurture agent can only be used for published automated emails that are not transactional.
  • Personalization tokens and smart content will continue to work as expected for emails that use nurture agent. The agent may rewrite portions of smart content in the same way it rewrites other email text.
  • Once the nurture agent credit limit is reached, the original version of marketing emails will be sent instead of the personalized version until the next month.
Manage credit usage

Nurture agent uses HubSpot Credits each time it personalizes an automated email for a contact. This includes personalizing the subject line, preview text, email body, and CTA text. Credits are only expended when the agent is turned on and emails that are sent, not when previews are generated. Learn more about how many HubSpot Credits nurture agent uses in the Product & Services Catalog.

For example, if you send a re-engagement email to 100 contacts and use nurture agent to personalize the email for each contact, credits will be consumed for 100 personalized emails. If you set nurture agent to personalize emails for 50% of those contacts, credits will be consumed for 50 personalized emails instead.

To reduce the number of credits used by nurture agent:

  • Limit the number of credits used by your account across all features.
  • Set a credit limit specifically for nurture agent that limits the number of personalized emails it can generate in a month.
  • For individual emails, reduce the percentage of recipients who are receiving a personalized version.
  • For individual emails, turn off nurture agent entirely.

Use nurture agent

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing emails are required to view or edit nurture agent for an automated email. Publish permissions for marketing emails are required to turn nurture agent on or off.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of a published automated email.

  • At the top of the performance page, click Personalize with Nurture Agent.

  • In the Personalization inputs section, set the data sources the agent will use to generate the personalized email:

    • Click an object type dropdown menu and select a property to use that property as a data source. For example, if you click the Contact dropdown menu and select Persona, the data in the Persona property will be considered when generating the personalized email.
    • To include an additional object type, click Add object type, then select an object. You can then select properties for that object.
    • To add additional data, click the Add activity dropdown menu, then select additional activity types.
    • When you’ve finished customizing data sources, click Save and regenerate preview.

  • Three sample contacts will be selected for the preview. If the email has been added to a workflow, the three most recently enrolled contacts in that workflow will be selected. To select additional contacts:

    • Click the Preview as dropdown menu and select Add contacts.
    • In the dialog box, select the checkbox next to each contact you want to preview. You can preview up to 10 contacts at a time.

  • In the right column, click the version of the personalized email you want to view:

    • Original: general version of the email without personalization.
    • Personalized: version of the email personalized for the selected contact. The text highlighted in green has been generated by nurture agent. Hover over highlighted text to see more information on why the agent made this change.
    • Compare: version of the email directly comparing the original and personalized versions of the email. Content removed from the original version will be highlighted in red, while content added to the personalized version will be highlighted in green. Hover over highlighted text to see more information on why the agent made this change.

  • To prevent a module of the email from being personalized, hover over the module and click Lock text.

  • When you’re finished generating previews, click Review & turn on in the top right.

  • Click and drag the slider to reflect the percentage of recipients you want to receive a personalized version of this email. The default is 50% of recipients.

  • In the dialog box, click Turn on Nurture Agent.

Analyze personalized email results

Once you’ve sent an automated email using nurture agent, you can view results specific to contacts who received the personalized email.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of the automated email.

  • On the performance page, review the Nurture Agent performance report to compare key performance metrics for the original and personalized versions of the email.

  • To view the recipients who received the personalized version:

    • At the top of the performance page, click the Version dropdown menu and select Personalized with Nurture Agent.

    • Click the Recipients tab.

    • To view the version of the email a specific contact received, click the name of the contact, then view the email on their contact record.

View a personalized email

Once an email has been sent using personalization from nurture agent, you can view the version of the email sent to a specific contact for up to 30 days after the email is sent.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of the sent email.
  • Click the Recipients tab.
  • All contacts who have been sent a personalized version of the email will have Personalized as their value for the Version column. In the Date column for a contact sent the personalized version, click Expand.
  • Click View sent email to view the personalized email this contact was sent.

Turn off nurture agent

If you want workflows to go back to sending the original version of an automated email, you can turn off nurture agent for that email.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of the published automated email.
  • At the top of the performance page, click Manage next to nurture agent banner.
  • At the top right of the agent editor, click Turn off.
  • In the dialog box, click Turn off.

Personalize email subject lines

You can tailor the subject lines of marketing emails to your recipients by using personalization tokens and emojis. This can increase open and click rates by drawing attention to your emails in recipients’ inboxes.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails.

Add personalization tokens to email subject lines

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of an email draft, or click Create email.

  • In the email editor, click the inbox content module at the top of the page.

  • In the Subject line field, click Personalize.

  • In the dialog box, click the Type dropdown menu and select a token type.

  • Click the Property dropdown menu and select a property.

  • Enter a fallback value that will display if there isn’t a value for this property, then click Insert.

Add emojis to email subject lines

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of an email draft, or click Create email.

  • In the email editor, click the inbox content module at the top of the page.

  • In the Subject line field, click the emoji underundemoji icon, then click an emoji.

Personalize links in marketing emails

In the marketing email editor, you can add links to image and button modules that pull data from personalization tokens. You can use personalized links to send contacts to specific pages personalized to what you know about them.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails.

Personalize image modules in marketing emails

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of a drafted email, or click Create email in the top right.
  • In the email editor, drag the image module from the sidebar editor into the body of the email.
  • In the left sidebar editor, click Upload to add a new image or Browse images to add images from the files tool.
  • In the Link field, click Personalize.
  • In the pop-up box, click the Type dropdown menu and select a token type, such as contact or office location.
  • Click the Token dropdown menu and select a token.
  • If no global default value exists for the token, you can enter a fallback value. This will be the link used for any contacts without a value for the selected token. If left blank, the image module won’t contain a link.
  • Click Insert.
  • Finish editing your email.

Personalize button modules in marketing emails

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of a drafted email, or click Create email in the top right.

  • In the email editor, drag the button module from the sidebar editor into the body of the email.

  • In the Link URL field, click Personalize.

  • In the pop-up box, click the Type dropdown menu and select a token type, such as contact or office location.

  • Click the Token dropdown menu and select a token.

  • If no global default value exists for the token, you can enter a fallback value. This will be the link used for any contacts without a value for the selected token. If left blank, the button module won’t contain a link.

  • Click Insert.

  • In the Button text field, enter the text that will appear on the button.

  • Finish editing your email.

Preview marketing emails for specific email clients

As you design your marketing email, you can preview how it looks on different email clients across device types. This ensures you can address unexpected issues and create a consistent experience for all recipients.

To test how the email would appear in your own inbox, you can send a test email.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails.

Understand limitations and considerations

For each 30-day rolling period, you can generate inbox previews based on the following limits:

  • Marketing Hub Professional accounts can create up to 500 tests.
  • Marketing Hub Enterprise accounts can create up to 1500 tests.
  • Each time an email client is tested, it counts toward the limit.

Generate previews for email clients and devices

Before sending your email, you can preview what it will look like across different versions of email clients.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of a drafted email.

  • In the top of the email editor, click the Preview & test dropdown menu and select Preview in an email client.

  • By default, previews will be generated for the most popular email client versions. To view a larger version of a preview, click Expand under its name.

  • To preview more email client versions:

    • Click the Choose preview type dropdown menu in the top left and select the checkbox next to each version you want to preview. To remove a version, clear the checkbox next to its name.
    • In the top right, click Preview to generate previews for all selected versions.

  • To preview the email as a specific contact across email client versions, click the Preview as dropdown menu and select a contact. Then click Preview in the top right.

  • To access a previous set of previews, click the dropdown menu in the top left next to Display options and select a preview.

  • By default, many clients will initially turn off images when the email first loads. To see how your email appears without images, click the Display options dropdown menu in the top left, then toggle Image blocking on.

Redirect contacts to an unsubscribe survey

When a contact unsubscribes from all marketing emails via the subscription preferences page, you can redirect them to a short survey. By learning why contacts unsubscribe, you can improve customer retention by creating more relevant content.

Permissions required Subscription Type settings permissions are required to turn on unsubscribe feedback surveys.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • By default, the Unsubscribe feedback survey setting is turned on for the following types of accounts:
    • Accounts created after August 21, 2025.
    • Accounts with a Starter subscription or using HubSpot’s free tools.
  • The survey will only appear when contacts unsubscribe from all marketing emails. A contact managing which subscription types they receive will not trigger the survey.
  • The appearance of your subscription pages may vary depending on whether you have applied custom CSS to your templates.
  • If the language of the marketing email that the contact is using to unsubscribe exactly matches the language of the email’s subscription type, that language will be used for the unsubscribe survey. Otherwise, the language set as the user default for your account will be used.

Redirect contacts to an unsubscribe survey

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Email.
  • At the top, click the Subscriptions tab.
  • To preview the survey before turning it on, click Preview in the Unsubscribe feedback survey section.
  • Toggle the Unsubscribe feedback survey switch on.
  • In the bottom left, click Save.

Once this setting is turned on, any time a contact unsubscribes from all email communications, they’ll be redirected to a confirmation page containing a survey asking why they unsubscribed.

Contacts can choose from the following unsubscribe reasons:

  • I’m no longer interested.
  • I didn’t sign up for your mailing list.
  • I receive too many emails.
  • Your emails are not relevant to me.
  • Other. Contacts who select Other will be able to enter more details about why they unsubscribed.

Their response will be logged to the activity timeline on their contact record.

Report on unsubscribed contacts

Permissions required View permissions for marketing email are required to analyze marketing email performance. Create/own permissions for reports are required to create custom reports.

To view a breakdown of unsubscribe reason data, view the Unsubscribe reason report on the Performance tab of a sent marketing email. Learn more about analyzing marketing emails.

If you have a Professional or Enterprise subscription, you can also create a custom report using the custom report builder to access marketing email activities metrics, such as Gave reason for unsubscribe, alongside other email performance data.

Create an example report

View the number of unsubscribes and unsubscribe reasons per month with the following configuration:

  • Data sources: Contacts (primary), Marketing email activities
  • Chart type: column
  • X-axis: timestamp - Monthly
  • Y-axis: Gave reason for unsubscribe
  • Break down by: Reason

You can also customize your report filters. For example, filter the data by Brand (Business unit) or Subscription type. Learn more about the custom report builder.

Resolve an email sending probation

If you’re using HubSpot’s free tools, when any of your key email deliverability metrics drop below a certain threshold, you will be put on an email sending probation to safeguard your sending reputation.

Understand email sending probation

The deliverability thresholds that will trigger an email sending probation (for example, a high hard bounce rate) depend on the sending volume associated with the industry of your business. The email health dashboard provides a snapshot of your current email health based on your industry, as well as recommendations to ensure you maintain a healthy sending reputation.

If your account is put on probation, you’ll be prompted to review your contacts to confirm that you’re only sending to recipients who meet the following criteria:

  • Granted explicit consent to receive marketing emails from your business.
  • Have engaged with the contents of your marketing emails in the past.

Once you’ve completed the contact review process, your account will no longer be under probation and you can resume sending marketing emails.

Failure to address issues with your contacts will eventually result in a full email sending suspension. Email sending suspensions in free accounts cannot be lifted and will prevent you from sending additional marketing emails from HubSpot.

Resolve an email sending probation

If your HubSpot account is affected by an email sending probation, a banner will appear at the top of the marketing email tool.

Permissions required View permissions for marketing email are required to access marketing emails.

To review your contacts and resolve the probation:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • In the email sending probation banner, click Review contacts.
  • In the right panel, click Next.
  • Review the information on explicit consent, then click Next.
  • Review the information on how to avoid emailing contacts who haven’t provided consent, then click Next.
  • In a separate tab, delete any of your marketing contacts who haven’t consented to receive marketing emails. It’s recommended to also remove any contacts without a valid email address.
  • Once you’ve removed these contacts, select the I’ve reviewed my marketing contacts checkbox, then click Next.
  • Click Done.

After removing these contacts, your hard bounce rate should begin to improve. It’s recommended to regularly review your email health dashboard to ensure a healthy sending reputation.

Resolve email sending suspensions

When sending a marketing email, one-to-one email, or email from a HubSpot-hosted inbox, email sending may be suspended. When a suspension occurs, you will no longer be able to the type of email that triggered the suspension until the suspension is lifted.

Email suspensions only apply to sending emails. An email sending suspension will not prevent you from performing other activities in HubSpot.

Permissions required View permissions for marketing email are required to access marketing emails.

Understand marketing email suspensions

For marketing emails, email sending is suspended when HubSpot’s deliverability protection system detects a high bounce rate on your email recipients, or fraudulent account activity is detected. All marketing emails, including automated emails in workflows, will not be sent while marketing email is suspended.

Before a suspension occurs, you may see a warning on the Health tab in your email tool about a problem detected by the deliverability protection system. This warning contains more details about the problem, and recommendations to improve future emails.

Please note: you can reach out to marketing email experts for advice on improving your emails on the Email Deliverability topic board on the HubSpot Community.

Understand types of marketing email suspensions

There are two types of email suspensions:

  • The deliverability protection system detects excessive hard bounces, unsubscribes, spam reports, blocklisting, or abuse complaints. Your account may be suspended from repeated stopped sends, direct complaints received by HubSpot’s Abuse Prevention team or if you exceed the following limits in a specific month:
    • Hard bounce rate of 5%.
    • Spam report rate of .1%, i.e. one per every 1000 emails sent.
    • Unsubscribe rate of 3%.
  • The system detects fraudulent activity on your account, such as spam traps. Learn how to respond to this type of suspension.
Resolve marketing email sending suspensions

Please note: email suspensions in accounts using HubSpot’s free tools cannot be lifted. Once an email suspension has occurred, that account can no longer send emails.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the Health tab.
  • On the right side of the page, under How to Fix, click Start.
  • In the right panel, select the I understand I can only submit this information once checkbox, then click Next.
  • Select an option for whether you have contacts you haven’t emailed in over 12 months, then click Next. You can also click open this segment to review your email marketing contacts.
  • Select the checkbox next to each source that applies to your contacts, then click Submit.
  • Click Continue to next step.
  • Review the selected sources that you require verifiable permission, then click Next.
  • Click Next.
  • Click your segment of email marketing contacts to open a new tab, then opt out, quarantine, or delete the associated contacts. Once this is finished, return to the suspension appeal panel and select the I’ve opted out, quarantined, or deleted at least x email marketing contacts checkbox.

Please note: HubSpot will automatically suppress any contact that has already hard bounced, unsubscribed, or marked an email as spam. Removing these contacts alone is not sufficient to restore email access.

  • Click Continue to next step.
  • Select the I reviewed and managed contacts who haven’t given permission to get marketing emails checkbox, then click Next.
  • Confirm that you opted out, quarantined, or deleted the associated contacts for each contact source you originally selected, then click Next.
  • Select the checkbox next to each method you used to manage the contacts who you did not have permission to email.
  • Enter any additional context or information on how you resolved the issues with these contacts.
  • When you’re ready to submit your appeal, click Submit.

HubSpot’s Deliverability Team will review your appeal and contact you with their decision or a request for more information.

Resolve email sending suspended from HubSpot-hosted inboxes

Your ability to send emails from the CRM or from the conversations inbox may be suspended if HubSpot detects poor sending behavior from your HubSpot-hosted inbox. This includes any email sent from the email address that you set up to forward emails to the conversations inbox, such as support@hubspot.hs-inbox.com, or your fallback email address.

When email sending is suspended, a warning banner will appear when trying to send one-to-one emails or the conversations inbox. You will not be able to send emails from this inbox in HubSpot until the suspension is lifted.

You can appeal the suspension to resume email sending:

  • In the banner, click complete this form.
  • Fill out the appeal form.

HubSpot’s Deliverability Team will then review the appeal and make a decision regarding your email sending capabilities.

Resolve additional account reviews

Some accounts may require additional review to determine if marketing email access can be unlocked. Click the link in the banner to submit more information about your contacts and the email you want to send. HubSpot’s Deliverability Team will review the submission and respond within two business days.

The primary point of contact on your account will receive an email notification about the next steps based on your form submission. The banner information on your account will also update to reflect the decision.

Restore deleted emails

When a marketing email has been deleted within the past 90 days, it can be restored or permanently deleted from the Deleted view. This view will also display when the email was deleted and which user deleted it.

Permissions required Users with View permissions for marketing emails can access the Deleted view. Super Admin or Account Access permissions are required to restore or permanently delete emails.

Understand limitations & considerations

  • Restored emails will have their performance data added back to your account.
  • Automated emails need to be manually added back to workflows once restored.
  • Emails that were scheduled when deleted need to be manually scheduled again.
  • Emails cannot be restored if:
    • It has been longer than 90 days since they were deleted.
    • The email has been permanently deleted from the Deleted view.

Restore deleted emails

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • To the right of the existing views, click Add view.

  • If not visible, click therightExpand column icon in the HubSpot provided section.

  • Click Deleted.

  • The Deleted view will display the following information:

    • Email name: email’s internal name.
    • Deleted date: date the email was deleted.
    • Deleted by: user who deleted the email.
    • Created date: date the email was originally created.

  • To restore an email, hover over the email and click Restore. In the dialog box, click Restore.

  • To permanently delete an email, hover over the email and click Permanently delete. In the dialog box, enter delete, then click Delete.

Resubscribe contacts to your marketing emails

Contacts who unsubscribed from some or all of the marketing emails sent from your HubSpot account will need to take action to resubscribe to your emails or update their email preferences.

The sections below outline how a contact can resubscribe on their own, but you can also update the subscription statuses for contacts individually or in bulk.

The steps in this article are intended for contacts who have opted out of receiving marketing emails. Learn more about fixing issues with email addresses that have bounced.

Understand limitations & considerations

  • Opt-out status is tied to a contact’s email address, not the contact record. If a contact’s email address is changed, their previous opt-out status will not apply unless they choose to opt out again using the new address.
  • Contacts who have opted out of marketing emails can still receive one-to-one emails and transactional emails.
  • Contacts who have unsubscribed from your communications must also resubscribe to receive emails again; they can’t be manually opted into those subscriptions by a HubSpot user.

Please note: you can manually resubscribe a contact who opted out of receiving marketing emails on their contact record, as long as you provide a legal basis and explanation for consent to communicate. This option should only be used if the contact was manually opted out in HubSpot.

Resubscribe using a previously sent marketing email

Contacts can resubscribe using a previously sent email with these steps:

  • Navigate to their email inbox.
  • Locate and open a marketing email that you’ve previously sent them from your HubSpot account.
  • In the email footer, click the Manage preferences link to resubscribe or update their email preferences.

Resubscribe using a HubSpot form

If a contact can’t locate a previously sent marketing email sent from your HubSpot account, they can resubscribe using a form that’s associated with a subscription type. The contact will then be resubscribed to that subscription type. Learn more about associating a form with a subscription type.

Resubscribe using a resubscription email

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Professional or Enterprise subscription is required to send resubscription emails.

Permissions required Website settings permissions are required to edit resubscription emails.

For forms that aren’t associated with a subscription type, you can also set up a resubscription email to send to contacts who request one while filling out a form. Contacts can then click a link in that email to resubscribe.

To turn on resubscription email for forms in your account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Email.
  • Click the Subscriptions tab.
  • In the Resubscription and sending options section, toggle the Resubscription email switch on.
  • To edit resubscription email content, click Edit email.

Learn more about resubscription email settings and limitations. To manage the subscriptions that a contact can opt into within the form, learn more about customizing form notice and consent options.

Review and archive subscription types

You can review your actively used subscription types on the email settings page to check for outdated or redundant subscriptions that can be safely archived. This helps keep your subscription preferences page confined to only relevant subscription types.

Review subscription types

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Email.
  • Click the Subscription Types tab.
  • Hover over a subscription type, then click the Actions dropdown menu and select Edit.
  • In the right panel, click the Used in tab.
  • Click to expand each section to see the assets of that type using this subscription type. Asset types include forms, automated emails, and workflows.

Archive subscription types

If you are no longer using a subscription type, you can archive it to remove it from your subscription preferences page.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Email.
  • Click the Subscription Types tab.
  • Hover over a subscription type, then click the Actions dropdown menu and select Archive.
  • In the dialog box, review any assets using the subscription type, then click Archive subscription type.

Review and decrease the size of marketing emails

In some providers, such as Gmail, email content above a certain size threshold will be clipped - hidden behind a “View entire message” link. This can hide certain email elements like images or CTAs, interfere with open tracking, and decrease the likelihood recipients will read the entire email.

In the email editor, you can monitor your email’s estimated size to verify it’s under Gmail’s clipping threshold of 102 KB. Estimated size is calculated using the size of the email’s HTML markup and will include links, formatting, and images.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails.

Review a marketing email’s size

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of a drafted marketing email.

  • In the email editor, the email’s approximate size will appear in the bottom right.

  • An email’s estimated size does not include content in personalization tokens. To review an email’s size for a specific recipient:

    • In the top right, click the Preview and test dropdown menu and select Preview as contact.
    • On the preview page, click the Preview as contact dropdown menu and select a contact. The Estimated size will appear at the top of the page.

Reduce a marketing email’s size

If your marketing email is over 102 KB in size, it’s recommended to review the following recommendations for reducing its size:

  • Reduce the number of tracked links: each tracked link in an email can add hundreds of characters to the email’s length due to the size of tracking parameters. Evaluate the links you’re tracking to see if any aren’t necessary.
  • Condense the content: review the content of the email to see if any text or assets can be removed or potentially include in a later email.
  • Use unique subject lines: if you send multiple emails to a recipient with the same subject line, Google will combine them into a single thread. Use unique subject lines to ensure your emails load individually.
  • Remove redundant formatting: remove unused columns and sections from the email, as well as any unused formatting pasted from an external editor like Google Docs.
  • Turn off hiding body text from preview text: in the email’s sending information, clear the Hide body text from preview text checkbox.

Run a re-engagement email marketing campaign

Securing verified consent is important to maintaining a good sender reputation for email marketing. A re-engagement campaign is an effective way to confirm the opt-in status of contacts who previously provided your brand with verifiable consent to be sent marketing emails.

To deliver to the most engaged contacts, it’s recommended to use double opt-in and run re-engagement campaigns every quarter.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails. Edit permissions for segments are required to create segments.

Please note: you should only use a re-engagement campaign to reconfirm opt-in status for your contacts. You should not use a re-engagement campaign to gain opt-in for contacts who haven’t yet provided it directly to your brand. HubSpot requires a verifiable opt-in record for any contact included in a marketing email send.

Understand re-engagement campaigns

A re-engagement campaign is a one-time email campaign that requests any contacts who haven’t already used some form of double opt-in to confirm that they would still like to receive emails.

Only the contacts who confirm their subscription status are then kept in your account. Those who don’t confirm will then be opted out of your marketing emails in HubSpot. The result is a highly engaged segment of contacts who have proven that they want to continue receiving marketing emails from your company.

You can see some examples of re-engagement campaigns on the HubSpot Community.=

Prepare for the re-engagement campaign

Before you begin your re-engagement campaign, it’s recommended to do the following:

  • Add notification and consent information to forms: add notification and consent information to forms so customers who fill them out know what communications they’re opting into receiving.
  • Set up a form for resubscription: you can create a form associated with a subscription type that customers can use to opt into a specific subscription type. Learn more about resubscription forms.
  • Set up subscription types: set up subscription types so customers can opt into receiving only the types of emails they want to receive.

Create a segment of inactive contacts

Create an active segment of contacts who have not engaged with your emails recently.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • In the upper right, click Create segment.
  • In the top right, click Next.
  • At the top of the segment editor, click the edit edit icon and enter a name for your segment.
  • Add the following property-based filters:
    • Last marketing email open date | is unknown
    • Marketing emails delivered | is greater than | 11
  • In the top right, click Next.
  • In the right panel, click Save and process segment.

Create a re-engagement email

Create a new email to send to your segment. This email will include a link to encourage your recipients to confirm their subscription.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • In the upper right, click Create email.
  • In the right panel, select Regular.
  • Select a template.
  • In the email editor, add a link to the email that recipients can click to stay opted in. It’s recommended to direct the link to a simple thank you page where you can confirm the recipient’s opted in status.
  • Click the Send to section at the top of the page.
  • In the sidebar editor, click the Send to dropdown menu and select the segment you created of unengaged contacts.
  • Edit and send the email.

Create an opt out segment

Once you’ve waited a week for your contacts to receive the email and click the link if they want to resubscribe, you can make a segment of contacts who were sent the email, but didn’t click the link.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • In the upper right, click Create segment.
  • In the top right, click Next.
  • At the top of the segment editor, click the edit edit icon and enter a name for your segment.
  • Add the following events-based filter:
    • Marketing emails | [Your re-engagement email] | Email was sent to contact but they didn’t click on a link.
  • In the top right, click Next.
  • In the right panel, click Save and process segment.

Opt out unconfirmed contacts

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • Hover over the segment of contacts to opt out, then click the More dropdown menu and select Export.
  • In the dialog box, select the checkbox next to any additional properties you want to include, then click Next.
  • Click the File format dropdown menu and select CSV.
  • Click Export.
  • Import these contacts as opted out.

Moving forward, these contacts won’t receive marketing emails unless they resubscribe.

Run A/B tests on marketing email subject lines

An A/B test measures engagement for different versions of the same email with a sample of your recipients. The best performing version is then sent to the rest of the recipients.

While creating a marketing email, you can use Breeze, HubSpot’s AI, to create an A/B test for the email’s subject line.

This article covers creating an A/B test for marketing email subject lines during the email creation process. Learn more about creating A/B tests for marketing email content.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential considerations of using it.

Understand requirements
  • To generate A/B tested subject lines, you will need to turn on Give users access to generative AI tools and features in your AI settings.
  • At least one segment must be selected in the Send to dropdown menu to perform an A/B test.
Understand limitations and considerations
  • Marketing emails can use either a generated A/B tested subject line or a customizable A/B test. If you want to run a customizable A/B test, remove the subject line A/B test first.
  • For best results, send the email to at least 1000 recipients.

Add an A/B tested subject line to an email

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of a marketing email, or click Create email in the top right.

  • In the email editor, click the inbox content module at the top of the editor.

  • In the sidebar editor, enter a subject line in the Subject line field.

  • Under your subject line, an alternative will be generated based on subject lines from other emails you’ve sent with high open rates.

  • To use this generated option for A/B testing, click A/B test subject line.

  • To proceed without A/B testing the subject line, click Dismiss.

  • To edit settings for the A/B test before sending:

    • In the sidebar editor, click Manage A/B test.

    • In the dialog box, select whether you’ll send the email to a percentage of your contacts, then the winner to the rest, or send both versions equally to all contacts.

    • If you selected Send winner automatically, you can click to expand Adjust settings to set how the winner is determined, how long the test takes, and the test sample size.

    • Click Save.

  • To cancel the A/B test before sending the email:

    • In the sidebar editor, click Manage A/B test.
    • In the dialog box, click Remove test.

  • Finalize and send the email.

Analyze A/B test performance

After your email is sent, wait enough time to gather results. You can analyze the performance of your email variations in the email details:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of your A/B email. The results of the A/B test will be summarized on the Performance page. The winning email version and metric will be highlighted in green.
  • In the upper left, click the Email version dropdown menu to analyze the email results for your email overall, or for either of the variations.

Save marketing emails as templates

If you want to use the layout of a regular marketing email created in the drag and drop editor multiple times, you can save it as a template. You can also create a template from scratch, rather than using an existing email.

Templates work well for recurring content types such as newsletters, although they aren’t supported for blog and RSS emails.

This article covers saving marketing emails as templates. Learn more about creating and sending sales emails using templates.

Permissions required Super Admin or Design tools permissions are required to manage marketing email templates.

Save a marketing email as a template

  • In the email editor, click the File menu and select Save email as template.
  • In the dialog box, enter a template name, then click Save.

Create a new marketing email template

Manage saved marketing email templates

Schedule emails based on your recipients’ time zones

You can schedule a marketing email to send at a specific time in your recipients’ time zones. This lets you reach all recipients at an optimal point in their daily schedule.

The email will be sent in batches based on the values in the manually set Time Zone property. If no values exist in that property, the IP Timezone property will be used. IP Timezone is set automatically from location data received through the HubSpot tracking code.

Any contact without values for either property will receive the email in your account time zone. Contacts imported from segments and those who have never visited your website will likely not have IP Timezone data.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • Emails scheduled according to recipient time zone will be sent whenever the specified time next occurs in that time zone. If that time has already passed on the day when the email is scheduled, it will be sent the following day.
  • You can’t schedule emails based on recipients’ time zones in A/B tested emails.
  • If you selected a segment for an email scheduled according to recipient time zone, any contacts added to that segment after the email is scheduled will not be sent the email.
  • The send to more feature is not available for emails sent using recipient time zones. Instead, it’s recommended to clone these emails to send them to additional recipients.

Schedule an email based on recipients’ time zones

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of a drafted email.
  • In the email editor, click the timschedule icon in the left sidebar.
  • In the When will you send the email section, select Schedule for later.
  • Click the Date date picker and select a date.
  • Select the Time dropdown menu and select a time.
  • In the What time zone do you want to use? section, select Recipient’s time zone (varied).
  • To see a breakdown of your recipients’ time zones:

    • Below Recipient’s time zone (varied), click [#]% of your recipients.

    • In the right panel, you can review the number of recipients who will be sent the email in each time zone.

  • In the top right, click Review and schedule.
  • Review the email’s information, then click Schedule.

Analyze email performance

On an email’s performance page, you can analyze your email’s performance in all time zones or a specific time zone. The email will remain in processing until all time zone batches have been sent.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of your sent email.
  • To see data for a specific time zone, click the Time zone dropdown menu in the top left and select a time zone.
  • To see the email’s performance across all time zones or monitor sending progress, click the Time zones tab.

Send a marketing email from a contact’s owner

Sending marketing emails from someone the recipient knows at your company can increase email engagement. You can use personalization tokens to set an email’s from name, address, and signature as belonging to a contact’s owner.

If you want to send your emails from someone other than the contact owner, you can use these same steps using custom contact properties.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • All test emails are sent from noreply@hubspot.com, to protect your email deliverability rates. When you send the email to your contacts, it will be sent with the From name and From address you’ve specified.
  • When sending a test email, the signature will only appear if you choose to receive the email as a specific contact.
  • Each contact owner can customize their own signature. You cannot edit another user’s signature.

Set from name and address

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of an existing email draft, or click Create email in the upper right.

  • In the email editor, click the inbox content module at the top of the page.

  • Click the From name dropdown menu and select owner.fullname in the Personalization token section.

  • Click the From address dropdown menu and select owner.email in the Personalization token section.

Add the contact owner’s signature

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of a drafted email.
  • In the email editor, place your cursor where you want to insert the signature token.
  • In the upper right section of the rich text toolbar, click Personalize.
  • In the dialog box, click the Token dropdown menu, then select Contact owner > Signature.
  • If the contact who receives the email does not have an assigned owner, the signature will come from the fallback user. If you don’t have a fallback user set, enter an email signature in the Fallback value field.
  • Click Insert.

Send a test marketing email

To test how a marketing email will appear in recipients’ inboxes before you send it, you can send a test email from the email editor. This allows you to correct any issues that may not be apparent in the editor before sending the email.

This article covers how to send a test email on desktop in the email editor. Learn more about sending a test email using the HubSpot mobile app.

Subscription required Edit permissions for marketing emails are required to send test emails.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of a drafted email.
  • In the email editor, click the Preview & test dropdown menu at the top of the page and select Send test email.
  • In the right panel, click the Send test to dropdown menu and select a recipient.
  • To send the test email to a new recipient, click the Send test to dropdown menu, then enter the recipient’s email address. Only verified email addresses can receive test emails.
  • To receive the test email as a specific contact, click the Preview as contact dropdown menu and select a contact.
  • To receive a test email of the plain text version of the email, click to expand the Advanced section and select the Send plain text version checkbox.
  • Click Send.

The recipient you selected will receive the test email in their inbox. The test email will have a from address of noreply@hubspot.com and from name of Marketing Email Preview Send.

When you send the actual email, the from address and name will appear as you set them in the email editor.

Send automated emails in workflows

You can use workflows to send automated emails to contacts. For example, you could set up a workflow to send a welcome email to contacts who fill out a form. If you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription, you can also create custom tokens to use data from your workflows in your automated emails.

Permissions required Edit permissions for marketing email are required to edit marketing emails. Publish permissions for workflows are required to send automated emails in workflows.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • If you add personalization tokens that aren’t contact or company tokens into an automated email, the email can only be used in workflows corresponding to the token type. For example, automated emails with deal personalization tokens can only be used in deal-based workflows. Contact and company personalization tokens can be used in any workflow type.
  • If you edit your automated email after it’s been published, any changes to unengaged contacts settings will not be applied.
  • Automated emails will only be sent to contacts who are eligible to receive marketing emails. For example, non-marketing contacts or contacts who have unsubscribed from all emails will not be sent automated emails from workflows.
  • In workflows that set contacts as marketing, then send them a marketing email, it’s recommended to add a short delay between the two actions. This ensures the system has time to process the status change. Contacts should only be sent marketing emails if you’ve received explicit consent to email them.

Create automated emails

You can create automated emails from the workflow editor or the marketing email tool. To create an automated email from the workflow editor:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.

  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.

  • In the workflow editor, click the add add icon to add a workflow action.

  • In the left panel, click to expand the Communications section, then select Send email.

  • Click the Automated email dropdown menu and select Create new email.

  • On the template selection screen, hover over a template and click Choose template.

  • In the email editor, edit and set up your email.

  • In the top right, click Review and publish.

  • In the right panel, review and resolve any issues with the email, then click Publish.

Once your automated email has been published, you can use the Send email action.

Review automated email authentication

To ensure that your emails are delivered to recipients, it’s recommended to send automated emails using an email sending domain. Any emails not sent using an email sending domain will be sent from a domain managed by HubSpot.

To view a list of automated emails not being sent from email sending domains:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • In the top right, click the Email tools dropdown menu and select Check automated email sending domain status.
  • To connect the domain used in a from address, click Connect domain and connect the email sending domain.
  • To change the from address used in the email:

    • Click Change address.

    • In the email editor, click the inbox content module at the top of the page.

    • In the left sidebar editor, click the From address dropdown menu and select an email address that uses a connected email sending domain.

    • In the top right, click Review and publish.

    • In the right panel, review and resolve any issues with the email, then click Publish.

Send blog subscription emails for external blogs using RSS feeds

For blogs hosted outside of HubSpot, you can use an RSS feed to send subscribers emails about your new blog posts. The email can pull in key information about each post from the RSS feed, including the post name, publication date, and summary.

Understand limitations & considerations

  • RSS emails will always be sent based on the timezone you’ve configured in your HubSpot account, and will not be sent based on the recipient’s timezone.
  • Each send will only include new posts since the prior send of the email, even if that’s fewer than the maximum number of posts you’ve selected.
  • Featured images will not be automatically added to the email. To include images, it’s recommended to add them to the <description> tag of your RSS feed.

Create a subscription type

Your contacts manage subscriptions to all your email subscription types separately. This way, if they decide to unsubscribe from one subscription type, they won’t have to unsubscribe from them all. To create a subscription type for your blog subscription emails:

Next, create a custom contact property for your external blog. This will be used in your subscription form to manage which contacts receive your blog subscription emails. Click the Field type dropdown menu and select Single checkbox. Then, click Create.

Create a subscription form for your external website

Permissions required Edit permissions for forms are required to edit forms.

Create an active segment of blog subscribers

  • Click Create segment.

      • Click Add filter.

      • Scroll or type to search for the custom property you created, then select the property to filter by.
      • Click the top dropdown menu then select is equal of all of. Then click the bottom dropdown menu and select Yes.
    • Add another filter to ensure that the segment only includes contacts set as marketing:
      • In the left panel, under AND, click Add filter.

      • Scroll or type to search for Marketing contact status then select it.
      • Click the top dropdown menu then select is equal to all of, then click the bottom dropdown menu and select Marketing contact.
  • Save the segment as active.

If you already have an existing segment of contacts subscribed to your blog emails, you can import the segment from a spreadsheet. It’s recommended to include:

  • A column for Email with your contacts’ email addresses.
  • A column that matches your subscription status property. Enter Yes as the value for all rows in this column.

Please note: only images hosted in HubSpot’s files tool can use a custom max width.

  • At the top of the page, click the inbox content module.

Review RSS email performance

Send emails to contacts who previously bounced

A bounced email is one that cannot be delivered to the recipient’s email server. This is typically due to issues with the email address (such as typos or an unknown user) or the recipient server.

When an email sent to a contact bounces, HubSpot may prevent you from sending future emails to that contact. This helps protect your sender reputation.

Not all bounces are permanent. Depending on the nature of the bounce, you can try to resend email to a bounced email address, audit your bounced email addresses, or unbounce an email address.

Understand how bounces work in HubSpot

HubSpot automatically avoids sending emails to contacts that have bounced previously for a permanent reason to protect your sender reputation. These contacts will appear in the Not Sent section of an email’s recipients.

Contacts whose email addresses have bounced remain in your CRM, but cannot receive marketing emails until the bounce has been removed. Because bounces are associated with email addresses and not the contact record, a contact whose email address is updated will no longer be treated as a bounced contact.

Unless a contact’s email address has globally bounced in other HubSpot accounts, HubSpot will not automatically drop emails sent to an invalid email address that hasn’t previously bounced in your account.

View bounced contacts

You can create filters or segments that identify contacts who have hard bounced when sent marketing emails from your HubSpot account.

View all contacts who bounced on a specific marketing email

Permissions required View permissions for marketing email are required to view marketing email bounce data.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • Click the name of a sent marketing email.
  • On the email performance page, click the Recipients tab.
  • In the left column, click Bounced.
  • To view the reason a contact bounced, click Expand in the Date column.
  • To create a segment of all contacts from an email who bounced:
    • Click the Actions dropdown menu in the top right and select Create a new segment.
    • In the dialog box, enter a name for the segment, then click Create segment.
View all contacts who have hard bounced on any marketing email

Permissions required Edit permissions for segments are required to create segments.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Segments. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Segments directly.
  • In the top right, click Create segment.
  • In the top right, click Next.
  • In the segment editor, click the edit edit icon and enter a name for your segment.
  • In the left column, click Add filter.
  • In the second column, click Contact properties, then click Email hard bounce reason.
  • Click the top dropdown menu and select is known.
  • In the top right, click Next.
  • In the right panel, review your segment details, then click Save and process segment.

Remove a contact’s hard bounce

If you know that an email address is valid, you can unbounce the contact to restore marketing email eligibility.

Permissions required Super Admin or Marketing email permissions are required to unbounce a contact.

Understand requirements to unbounce a contact

Because sending marketing emails to an invalid email address can harm sender reputation, ensure the following before unbouncing a contact:

  • You are sending marketing emails using a connected email sending domain (not available in accounts using HubSpot’s free tools).
  • You have received an email from the bounced email address confirming that the email address is valid and they want to receive marketing emails from you.
  • Any issues with the recipient’s email server causing the email to bounce have been resolved. Learn more about resolving issues with delivered emails.

If any of the following are true, you will need to contact HubSpot Support about unbouncing this contact:

  • You’ve unbounced more than 1,000 contacts or more than 2% of the total contacts in your account this month.
  • The contact has been unbounced previously.
  • The contact is a global bounce.

Before contacting HubSpot Support, it’s recommended to take a screenshot of an email you received from the bounced address showing the sender, recipient, and send time. Unbounces performed by HubSpot Support can take a few minutes to take effect.

Unbounce contacts

Contacts who have hard bounced once will have a “Contact has bounced” alert on their contact record where you can unbounce them.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • Click the name of the contact.

  • In the top left, click Unbounce above the contact’s name.

  • In the dialog box, select the I confirm that this email address is correct checkbox.

  • Click Unbounce this contact.

Once you’ve unbounced a contact, they will be eligible to receive future marketing emails, as long as they are set as a marketing contact and aren’t unsubscribed.

Any emails that were dropped while the contact was marked as bounced will need to be cloned and resent for the unbounced contacts to receive them.

Remove a HubSpot user’s hard bounce

If HubSpot users experience issues that cause their email addresses to bounce in HubSpot, Super Admins can unbounce those users’ emails once the issues are fixed. This process only applies to email addresses that belong to HubSpot users in your account.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • Hover over a user who has had emails bounce and click the Actions dropdown menu, then select Unbounce email.
  • In the dialog box, confirm that you want to unbounce this user’s email.

After a few minutes, the user should be able to receive emails from HubSpot again. Any marketing emails that were dropped while the user was marked as bounced will need to be cloned and resent.

Send marketing emails to more contacts

After you’ve sent a marketing email, you can send the email to additional contacts and segments at a later time. This can be useful to gauge an email’s effectiveness on a small group of contacts before sending it to all relevant recipients.

Permissions required Publish permissions for marketing emails are required to send marketing emails.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • You cannot send the following types of marketing email to additional contacts and segments:
    • Automated emails
    • Emails using A/B testing
    • Emails sent using the recipients’ time zones
    • Emails canceled before they finished sending
  • Recipients of the original email will never be sent the email again using this feature. If you need to send these recipients the email again, it’s recommended to clone the email and send the clone.
  • Any contacts or segments excluded from the original email will need to be manually excluded on each subsequent send.
  • You can only send the same email to more contacts a maximum of 100 times per email.

Send marketing emails to more contacts

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.

  • Click the name of a sent marketing email.

  • In the top right, click the Actions dropdown menu and select Send to more.

  • In the right panel, click the Send to dropdown menu and select the checkbox next to each segment or contact you want to receive the email. Recipients of the original email send will be automatically skipped.
