  • If needed, click the tool to edit or remove how the property is used.

Score history and performance

Once you’ve created and turned on scores, you can view more details and charts about a record’s score history using cards on records. You can also analyze reports that show how scores are performing and how records are being categorized into your score thresholds.

Use lead scores in HubSpot tools

Once you’ve turned on scores, you can use the score properties in other tools to identify, segment, and report on your leads. For example, you could:

  • Create a saved view or segment of all contacts with a High score according to your score thresholds.
  • Create a workflow to automatically assign an owner to unworked contacts with a score over 50.
  • Create a workflow to send a notification to the record owner when a deal’s score goes above 75.
  • Create a custom report to compare lead scores of contacts by the channel they first interacted with your business. To use lead scores in reports, use the scored object as a data source (e.g., contacts if reporting on contact lead scores) and include the score properties as fields.

Additional resources

For instructions on how to build scores, refer to these articles:

  • Manually build lead scores
  • Build contact lead scores with AI (Marketing Hub Enterprise only)

For a video walkthrough, watch the Lead Scoring lesson on the HubSpot Academy.

Reset a contact engagement lead score

If a contact has been disqualified, you may want to reset their value for an engagement lead score. Use a workflow to automatically reset an engagement score (or engagement portion of a combined score) to zero based on certain triggers.

Once the workflow is turned on, the engagement score is reset when contacts are enrolled. If you’ve selected a combined score, only the engagement portion is reset. When a score is reset, scoring resumes based on events after the most recent reset time. Events before the most recent reset timestamp are ignored.

Permissions required Workflows permissions are required to create workflows.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Create a contact-based workflow.
  • Click Set up triggers, then select the enrollment triggers that’ll decide when a contact’s engagement score is reset. For example, any contact with an internal email address or with an associated deal moved to a closed lost stage.
  • Click the + plus icon to add an action.
  • In the left panel, click CRM, then select Reset marketing lead engagement score.
  • Select the score you want to reset, then click Save.
  • Finish creating your workflow and turn it on.

Please note: the following behavior applies when resetting an engagement score:

  • The reset action only works if a score is turned on. If the score is turned off, contact engagement scores will not be reset.
  • Points granted to a score based on segment membership criteria are not included in a reset.

Test records in lead and health scores

For lead scores and heath scores, to verify a score is working as expected, you can test individual records or access a preview of the expected score distribution. You can test records or view score distributions when creating a new score or for existing scores.

You can test and preview record scores with the following options:

  • Test a record: checks what the score would be for a specific record. Use this option if you want to test one record at a time and see how points are added or subtracted for individual rules.
  • Preview distribution: shows insights into scores for a range of records. Use this option if you want to test multiple records at once and see an overview of total scores rather than points for individual rules.

Permissions required View permissions for Lead Scoring are required to test lead scores. View permissions for Manage Customer Success Settings are required to test health scores.

Test a record in a score

When you test an individual record, you can see the test record’s total score as well as points for each rule.

  • Navigate to your scores:
    • Lead scores: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
    • Health scores: In your HubSpot account, navigate to Workspaces > Customer Success. In the top right, click the settings gear icon. At the top of the page, click the Health scores tab.
  • Choose the score for which to test a record:
    • To test a record in an existing score, click the name of the score. To test in the published version, click Actions, then select See live score. To test while editing the score, click Edit score.
    • To test a record while building a new score, create a lead score or health score.
  • In the top right, click Test a [contact/company/deal].
  • Click the Search dropdown menu to search for and select the record to test.
  • At the top, the total score and number of criteria matched is displayed.
  • To view how the score was calculated based on specific rules, scroll down to view your criteria:
    • If the record meets the criteria of a rule, there will be a green checkmark and the number of points added or subtracted. Learn more about filter criteria.
    • If the record does not meet the criteria of a rule, there will be a red X with 0 points.
  • To test another record, click the dropdown menu and select another record to test.
  • To stop testing, click Stop testing or click the X on the right of the testing banner.

Preview score distribution for multiple records in a score

You can view insights into how scores would be distributed across a range of records.

  • Navigate to your scores:
    • Lead scores: In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
    • Health scores: In your HubSpot account, navigate to Workspaces > Customer Success. In the top right, click the settings gear icon. At the top of the page, click the Health scores tab.
  • Navigate to the score for which you view the score distribution:

    • To preview the score distribution in an existing score, click the name of the score. To preview in the published version, click Actions, then select See live score. To preview while editing the score, click Edit score.

    • To preview the score distribution while building a new score, create a lead score or health score.

  • In the top right, click Preview distribution.
  • In the right panel, view insights into how a sample of records would be scored. The preview includes the average score, totals in each score range, and a distribution graph with more range data. For combined scores, you can view distribution previews for the total combined score, fit criteria alone, and engagement criteria alone.

Please note: in accounts containing a high number of records, the distribution preview is based on a representative sample (i.e. 20% of eligible contacts) rather than all records.

Troubleshoot score tests with unexpected results

If you’ve tested a score for one or multiple records and are getting unexpected results, review the following troubleshooting steps:

  • Review guidance about how scores are calculated. Certain scoring logic is different for engagement and fit criteria. You may need to adjust how your rules are configured to carry out the goal of your score.
    • Filter criteria behavior
    • Scoring individually vs. scoring together
  • Check the property history of records to verify if properties related to fit criteria or engagement have expected values. If not, edit the property value or verify which actions update certain activity-based properties. Review the contact properties article, company properties article, and deal properties article for more information about automatic property updates.

Use AI insights to score records based on high-impact events

In the lead scoring tool, use AI-powered insights to set scoring criteria based on your account’s event conversion data. The insights show events with conversion rates and confidence levels so you can create effective scoring rules based on your highest-impact events.

For example, companies often move to the Customer stage after an associated contact visits the Sales Demo page. Create a rule that adds points when a company’s associated contacts visit that page. This signals to the sales team that the company is likely to become a customer and is a lead worth engaging.

Permissions required Edit permissions for Lead Scoring are required to create lead scores and set up lead score criteria.

Before you get started

Key terms

The following are terms used when reviewing the high-impact event rule recommendations:

  • AI Rules: rule recommendations for events that most often lead to a goal stage conversion. Rules are based on the last 90 days of activity, showing events up to 14 days prior to goal stage conversion.
  • Goal stage: the lifecycle stages and deal stages toward which you want to track conversions. For example, Lead tracks which companies moved to Lead following an event occurrence.
  • Conversion rate: the percentage of contacts or companies that performed the event and then converted to the selected goal stage.
  • Confidence level: how reliable the signal is, based on an event’s conversion rate and sample size.
Tracked events

The following events are tracked to create rule suggestions:

  • Form submission
  • Page visited
  • Opened email
  • Workflow enrolled
  • Clicked link in email
  • Updated email subscription status
  • CTA click
  • Marketing Event Attended
  • Marketing Event Registered
  • Bounced email
  • Media Played
  • Email Delivered

Set lead scoring criteria for high-impact events

To set up scoring criteria for high-impact web pages:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
  • Create a new engagement or combined score, or edit an existing engagement or combined score.
  • For a new score, click Discover AI rules. If you’re editing an existing score, click Discover rules in the top right. In the right panel, review and filter high-impact events.
  • Select whether insights rank activity for contacts or companies.
  • All goal stages are shown by default. To filter by specific stages, select the Goal stages. This filters insights by the lifecycle or pipeline stage you want to optimize conversions toward. For example, select Lead to track which companies moved to Lead following event conversions.
  • All events are shown by default. To view a specific type of event (e.g., Opened email), click Criteria types, then select the event.
  • To filter the view to only show specific confidence levels, select High, Medium, or Low above the table.
  • Events are automatically sorted from High to Low confidence, and within each level, are ranked by number converted. To change the sort, click a column header to sort by that property.
  • To search for a specific event, use the search bar. For example, search the URL of a page or the name of a marketing email.
  • Each rule includes a points recommendation based on the signal’s confidence, sample size, and your existing scoring scale. For example, add 10 points to the score for an event with a High confidence level. To edit the suggested points, enter a new value in the Suggested points field. This will update the points for all other rules based on that event.
  • To add recommended rules, select the checkboxes of the rules, then click Add to score. Each selected rule is scored individually when added.
  • The rules will automatically be added to your scoring criteria. To customize a rule, click the rule and edit the filters and options.
  • Finish setting up or editing the score, then click Review and turn on for a new score, or Review and update for an existing score.

Learn more about the lead scoring tool and how to set up scores based on other events or property values.

View insights for lead score rules

Review rule insights to understand how each rule in a lead score impacts the score as a whole. For example, you can check how many records had points added to their score from a specific rule. If the rule changes the score for only a few contacts, you may decide to adjust the rule’s criteria to target other attributes or lower the points it adds so the rule has less weight.

Rules insights are shown for each rule in a score. To review scoring predictions and insights for an entire score, you can:

  • Preview score distributions
  • View lead score performance reports

Permissions required View permissions for Lead Scoring are required to view rule insights.

If you’re a Super Admin, you can opt your account into the Rule Insights for Building Scores beta.

To view insights for lead score rules:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
  • Create a new score, or view or edit an existing score.
  • Navigate to the rule for which to review insights. If the rule is collapsed, click the Rule Insights button. If the rule is expanded, click to expand the Rule Insights section.
  • Review the following insights for the rule. For large databases, the insights are based on a representative sample of records.
    • Reach and impact summary: how the rule ranks in reach and contribution to the score compared to other rules.
    • [Records] reached by rule: the percentage and number of records with scores impacted by the rule.
    • Average points per [record]: the average number of points added to or subtracted from records based on the rule. To include records unreached by the rule, select the Include [records] not reached checkbox.
    • Distribution of points: a visual representation of how points are spread across each scored record.
  • Edit the rule as needed. For example, if the impact of the rule is too high, lower the number of points it adds. Insights update in real time when you make changes.
  • For engagement rules, if conversion data is available for that event, click View x similar to [event]. This opens the AI rules panel where you can explore similar high-impact rules.

Learn more about the lead scoring tool.

View lead score history and performance

To understand how your lead scores are being used, review record lead score history and analyze the performance of your scores.

To view lead score history for records, add score properties as index page columns or add the Lead score card to the right sidebar. To understand the performance and distribution of scores, view lead score reports.

Permissions required View permissions for Lead Scoring are required to view lead score history and performance reports.

View lead score history for individual records

To access an overview of a record’s current and past scores, you can:

  • Add score properties as columns on index page views.
  • Add the Lead Score card to the right sidebar of your records.
View score history in index page views

To add score histories to your index pages:

  • Navigate to a view.
  • Click Edit columns.
  • Search for and select the checkboxes of the score properties you want to include as columns, then click Apply. Learn more about customizing columns.
  • Once added, navigate to the column and click the score value.
  • In the right panel, the Score trend graph shows score trends by month, and the Score history chart shows events that caused the score to change. To view score trends and history for a specific timeframe, click the Last x days dropdown menu, and select the timeframe.
View score history on records

The Lead score card will appear once added to a record view. The card will show details about a record’s current and past scores.

  • Navigate to your records.
  • Click the name of a record.
  • Navigate to the Lead Score card in the right panel or in the middle column depending on your record view. On the card, you can view the record’s value for each score you’ve created for the object.
  • To edit a score, click the score’s name.
  • To view more details about the score values, click See score history. In the right panel, the Score trend graph shows score trends by month, and the Score history chart shows events that caused the score to change. To view score trends and history for a specific timeframe, click the Last x days dropdown menu, and select the timeframe.

Learn more about using cards on records.

View lead score performance reports

To view lead score Performance reports:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
  • Hover over the score to analyze, then click View performance.
  • Analyze reports for the following:
    • Scored record overview
    • Score distribution
    • Scores over time
Review scored records
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
  • Hover over the score to analyze, then click View performance.
  • In the Overview table, review the following data about scored records:
    • Contacts/Companies/Deals: total number of contacts, companies, or deals in your account.
    • Contacts/Companies/Deals scored: total number of contacts, companies, or deals scored. Learn more about excluding records from scoring.
    • Average score: average score of the contacts, companies , or deals that were scored.
    • Min score: minimum score of all the contacts, companies, or deals that were scored.
    • Max score: maximum score of all the contacts, companies, or deals that were scored.
Analyze score distribution
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
  • Hover over the score to analyze, then click View performance.
  • In the Score distribution chart, review scores for contacts/companies/deals grouped by the score thresholds. For engagement and fit scores, records are grouped into three labels: Low, Medium, and High. For combined scores, records are grouped into six labels based on varying levels of fit vs. engagement.
  • To view and use the records within a threshold label:

    • Click a threshold label. For example, click High to view high fit or high engagement records or click A3 to view high-fit, low-engagement records.

    • In the pop-up box, view a list of all records within that threshold.

    • Use the filter dropdown menu to update which threshold levels are included. For example, view records with Medium and Low scores, or view all high-fit scores across engagement score ranges (A1, A2, and A3).

    • To view more details about a record, click the name of the record.

    • To use the records in another HubSpot tool, click Use in, then select the tool:

      • Segments: create a segment of the records. The segment’s filters are automatically set to [Score name] threshold is [threshold label]. Save the segment as active to automatically add and remove records that meet the criteria moving forward, or static to only include the records at that moment in time.
      • Workflows: enroll the records in a new workflow. The workflow’s enrollment trigger is automatically set to [Score name] threshold is [threshold label].
      • Views: access the records in an index page view. Save the view to revisit the records at a later time.
Analyze score trends over time
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Lead Scoring directly.
  • Hover over the score to analyze, then click View performance.
  • In the Score over time report, review trends for the score over time. View the trend lines to analyze the following values over time:
    • Average score: the typical score for records.
    • Max score: the highest-scoring record.
    • Min score: the lowest-scoring record.
  • By default, the reports shows trends based on the monthly average, maximum, and minimum scores from the past 365 days.
    • To view a specific date range, click In the last 365 days, then select a date range. You can select a rolling date range (e.g., This week) or a specific number of days (e.g., Last 7 days).
    • To change how often the average, minimum, and maximum are shown, click the Frequency dropdown, then select Daily, Quarterly, Weekly, or Yearly.

Marketing: SMS

Analyze SMS performance

Once you’ve started sending SMS messages, you can analyze engagement metrics like message clicks, as well as any errors that have occurred. This can help you ensure delivery of future messages.

Permissions required View permissions for SMS are required to view SMS performance.

Analyze individual message performance

You can analyze the overall performance of an individual SMS message, as well as verify the delivery status of that message for individual recipients.

Analyze performance
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.
  • At the top of the table, filter your SMS messages:
    • To filter by associated campaign, click the Campaigns dropdown menu and select a campaign.
    • To filter for SMS messages sent a specific way, click the Sending method dropdown menu and select Automated, Regular, or Time Zone. Automated messages are those sent by workflow.
    • To create simple filters, click More, then select an SMS property. Then click the property’s dropdown menu and select a value.
    • To create a more complex filter, click Advanced filters. In the right panel, set up your filter criteria. At the top of the page, add filters:
  • Click the name of a sent message.

On the Performance tab, you can review the following performance data:

  • Delivery rate: what percentage of the SMS messages sent were delivered to recipients. Messages can be sent, but not delivered for a number of reasons, including SMS service provider issues and invalid recipient contact numbers.

  • Click rate: what percentage of the delivered SMS messages resulted in clicks.

  • Delivery and engagement funnel: customer journey report of the funnel for these SMS messages, comparing the number of messages sent, delivered, and clicked.

  • Time series comparison chart: comparison of two metrics over time, such as total clicks and unique clicks. Use the dropdown menus at the top of the chart to select the metrics being compared, appearance of the chart, and measurement frequency.

  • Sending failed report: number of contacts who couldn’t be sent this SMS message. Reasons include invalid number, network failure, and recipient opted out.

  • Delivery failed report: number of contacts who weren’t delivered this SMS message. Reasons include recipient unavailable, and phone number does not exist.

Analyze recipients

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.

  • At the top of the table, filter your SMS messages:

    • To filter by associated campaign, click the Campaigns dropdown menu and select a campaign.
    • To filter for SMS messages sent a specific way, click the Sending method dropdown menu and select Automated, Regular, or Time Zone. Automated messages are those sent by workflow.
    • To create simple filters, click More, then select an SMS property. Then click the property’s dropdown menu and select a value.
    • To create a more complex filter, click Advanced filters. In the right panel, set up your filter criteria. At the top of the page, add filters:

  • Click the name of a sent message.

  • Click the Recipients tab.

  • Click a category to view all contacts who’ve met the requirements for that category. The following categories are available:

    • Sent
    • Not sent
    • Not delivered
    • Total delivered
    • Total clicks

Please note: contacts may be present in multiple categories if they meet multiple sets of requirements. For example, if a message was sent, but not delivered to a specific contact, they would be in both the Sent and Not delivered categories.

  • Click the right expand icon next to a contact’s name to view all events for that contact. For Not sent and Not delivered events, a reason will be given if available.

Analyze overall message performance

You can view the performance of all your SMS messages over time on the Analyze tab.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.

  • Click the Analyze tab.

  • At the top of the table, filter your SMS data:

    • To set a rolling date range, click the first date picker and select a range, such as Last 30 days or This year.

    • To set a specific date range, click the first date picker and select a start date, then click the second date picker and select an end date.

    • To filter by associated campaign, click the Campaign dropdown menu and select a campaign.

    • To filter for SMS messages sent a specific way, click the SMS Type dropdown menu and select Automated, Regular, or Time Zone. Automated messages are those sent by workflow.

  • To change the filters used in a specific report, click the filter filter icon in the top right of the report.

  • To use Breeze Assistant to generate insights, click the breezeSingleStar Breeze Assistant icon in the top right of the report. Learn more about working with Breeze Assistant.

  • To save a specific SMS performance report:

    • In the top right of the report, click theverticalMenumenu icon and select Save report.
    • In the right panel, enter a name and description for the report.
    • Select whether you will add the report to a new or existing dashboard, or save it without adding it to a dashboard, then click Next.
    • Select an access option for this report, then click Save.

  • To refresh a report’s data, click theverticalMenumenu icon in the top right of the report and select Refresh.

  • To export the data used to create a report:

    • In the top right of the report, click theverticalMenumenu icon and select Export unsummarized data.
    • In the dialog box, enter a name for the export.
    • Click the File format dropdown menu and select CSV, XLS, or XLSX.
    • Click Export.
    • When the export is finished processing, click the notification notification icon in the top navigation bar, then click the export notification to download the export.

On the Analyze tab, you can review the following data over the specified date range:

  • Overview: overview of the total SMS messages sent, delivered, clicked, and not delivered, as well as the number of contacts who opted out.
  • Delivery and engagement funnel: customer journey report of the funnel for all SMS messages, comparing the number of messages sent, delivered, and clicked.
  • Failures: overview of the number of SMS messages not sent or with failed sends.
  • Time series comparison chart: comparison of two metrics over time, such as total clicks and unique clicks. Use the dropdown menus at the top of the chart to select the metrics being compared, appearance of the chart, and measurement frequency.
  • Opt outs over time: number of contacts that opted out of SMS communication over time.

Please note: opt outs cannot be attributed to a specific SMS message, so adding filters such as Campaigns will display no opt out data.

  • Sending failed report: number of contacts who couldn’t be sent SMS messages for specific reasons over time. Reasons include invalid number, network failure, and recipient opted out.
  • Delivery failed report: number of contacts who weren’t delivered SMS messages for specific reasons over time. Reasons include recipient unavailable, and phone number does not exist.

Create and send SMS messages in HubSpot

You can send SMS messages to your contacts to engage more directly with customers who opt into communication with your business. The number of SMS messages you can send monthly depends on the number of message segments available to your account.

Once you’ve started sending SMS messages, learn more about analyzing their performance.

Permissions required Edit permissions for SMS are required to create SMS messages.

Understand requirements

  • You must have registered an SMS number in HubSpot and received approval to use it for marketing communications. Learn more about setting up SMS messaging.
  • You must have purchased the Marketing SMS Add-On or the Marketing SMS Short Code Add-On.
  • In order to receive SMS messages, contacts must:
    • Be set as marketing contacts.
    • Have provided explicit consent to receive SMS messages.
    • Be opted into the subscription type of the SMS message.
    • Have a US-based phone number that starts with +1 and contains 11 digits. For example, +1-800-555-5555 would be a valid number. Learn more about reformatting contact numbers.
    • Have their phone number stored in the Mobile phone number or Phone number property. If phone numbers opted into receiving messages are present in both properties, the mobile phone number will be used.

Create SMS messages

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.
  • In the top right, click Create message.
  • In the right panel, enter a name for the message in the SMS name field.
  • Fill in any required or optional custom properties, then click Create message.
  • In the editor, enter the content of your message in the Body text section.
    • To generate SMS content based on a prompt, click the breezeSingleStar AI icon, then enter a prompt and click the breezeSend send icon.
    • To personalize your message content, click Personalize.
    • To add a link, emoji, or special character, click the icon in the rich text toolbar.
    • By default, SMS messages will include the standard opt-out text, “Text STOP to opt out.” To customize this text, clear the Include default opt-out text field, then enter custom opt-out text in the content of the message. Including opt-out text is required to send SMS message through HubSpot.
  • In the right column, preview how your message will appear to your recipients:

    • To preview the message for a specific contact, click the View default preview message dropdown menu and select a contact.

    • To preview the message in different font sizes, click thetexttext icon, then click and drag the slider to change the text size.

    • To preview the message in dark mode, click Turn on dark screen mode.

    • Above the preview, review the message’s character count and message segments.

  • To change the language of the default opt-out text:
    • Click the Settings tab.
    • Click the Language dropdown menu and select a language. Learn more about HubSpot’s supported languages.
  • To associate the message with a campaign:
    • Click the Settings tab.
    • Click the Marketing campaign dropdown menu and select a campaign. Learn more about associating assets with campaigns.

Send a test message

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.
  • Click the name of a drafted message.
  • In the top right of the editor, click Send test message.
  • In the right panel, click the Choose one or more recipients dropdown menu and select a phone number.
  • To add a phone number not associated with a HubSpot user:
    • Click the Choose one or more recipients dropdown menu.
    • Enter the phone number manually, including the country code, then click Create option [###]
  • Repeat for each additional phone number.
  • To receive the version of the message a specific contact would be sent, click the Receive SMS as a specific contact dropdown menu and select a contact.
  • Click Send test message.

Send SMS messages

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.

  • Click the name of a drafted message.

  • In the editor, click the Sending tab.

  • In the right column, click the Send to dropdown menu and select each segment or contact you want to add as recipients. Skip this step if sending this message through a workflow.

  • Click the Don’t send to dropdown menu and select each segment or contact you want to exclude from the recipients. Skip this step if sending this message through a workflow.

  • In the Estimated recipients section, review how many selected contacts will be sent the message and why the other contacts won’t be sent the message.

  • In the left column, click the How will you send this message? dropdown menu and select a sending option:

    • Send now: message will send immediately
    • Scheduled for later: message will send at a time you select.
    • As part of a workflow: message will be published and can be sent from a workflow.

  • If you’re schedule the message to send later:

    • Click the Date field and select a date.
    • Click the Time dropdown menu and select a time.
    • In the Time zone section, select an option:
      • Your account time zone: send time will be calculated using the time zone set in your account’s settings. All recipients will be sent the message at the same time.
      • Your time zone: send time will be calculated using your user’s time zone. All recipients will be sent the message at the same time.
      • Contact time zone: send time will be calculated using the recipients’ time zones.
        • Recipients will be sent the email on a staggered basis over 24 hours.
        • Click Check contacts’ time zones to see more information about the time zones of your recipients.
        • Contacts without time zones will sent the email as if they were in your account’s time zone.

  • By default, SMS messages are not sent from HubSpot from 8PM to 8AM in a contact’s time zone. To remove this restriction, toggle the Quiet hours switch off. This is not recommended, as it can result in violations of SMS sending laws. Learn more about quiet hours.

  • In the top right, click Review and send or Review and schedule.

  • Review the estimated message segments and minimum send time, as well as any errors or warnings.

  • Click Send message or Schedule message.

Cancel scheduled SMS messages

If you’ve scheduled an SMS message to send at a later date, you can prevent the message from sending by canceling it first.

Please note: archiving a scheduled message will not cancel the send. You must cancel the send from the performance page or delete the message.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.

  • Click the name of a scheduled SMS message.

  • On the SMS performance page, click Cancel send under the message preview.

  • In the dialog box, click Cancel scheduled SMS.

The message will revert to draft mode and will not be sent.

Export SMS messages

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.
  • In the top right of the table, click the Actions dropdown menu and select Export SMS messages.
  • In the dialog box, enter a name for the export in the Name field.
  • Click the Format dropdown menu and select a format for the exported file. You can select CSV, XLS, or XLSX.
  • In the Choose what you’d like to export section, select an option:
    • SMS dashboard data in current view: only export data from the SMS messages included in the current saved view.
    • All available SMS dashboard data: export all SMS data.
  • Click Export.

The exported file will be sent to your user’s email address and added to your notifications.

Filter SMS messages that use AI content

If you used Breeze Assistant to help you draft your SMS messages, you can filter which messages were generated or co-created with AI on the SMS home page.

Permissions required View permissions for SMS are required to view SMS messages.

Understand AI filters

When drafting an SMS message, you can use Breeze Assistant to generate content for your message.

There are two filters available to help you review which messages were created using Breeze Assistant:

  • Generated by AI: content in your message was fully generated by AI without any further edits made by a user in your account.
  • Co-created by AI: content in your message was initially generated by AI but was later edited by a user in your account. This filter includes:
    • Messages cloned from a message where content was generated with AI.
    • Messages where content was generated, then later deleted.

Add filters to the SMS index page

You can add columns for messages created with the help of AI to the SMS index page.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.
  • In the top right, click the Actions dropdown menu and select Edit columns.
  • In the dialog box, select the Co-created with AI and Generated by AI checkboxes.
  • In the Selected Columns section, click and drag each property into its final position.
  • Click Apply.

Filter for messages that use AI content

You can filter existing messages to see what kinds of AI content they contain, either by looking at the default AI view or creating a custom filter that identifies messages that were partially generated or co-created with AI.

Add the default AI view
  • At the top of the page, click Add View.
  • In the dialog box, click AI in the HubSpot Provided section.
Create a custom AI filter
  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Email. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Email directly.
  • At the top of the page, click the Advanced filters.
  • In the right panel, click Add filter.
  • In the pop-up box, click AI-generated or co-created.
  • In the right panel, click True in the AI-generated or co-created filter.
  • Add any additional filters.

Improve SMS performance

You can send SMS messages to your contacts to engage more directly with customers who opt into communication with your business. To improve delivery and click rates, it’s recommended to set up branded links and verify that phone numbers are formatted correctly.

Permissions required Edit permissions for SMS are required to use SMS tools.

Manage branded links

To increase recipient trust and improve deliverability, it’s recommended to use links that contain your company’s domain.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to SMS.
  • Click the Tools tab.
  • In the Branded links section, click Add branded link under a connected SMS number.
  • In the right panel, click the Select domain dropdown menu and select the connected domain that best matches the brand sending the SMS messages. Learn more about connecting domains to HubSpot.
  • Click Save.

SMS links will always include the UTM parameters listed below:

  • utm_source=hs_sms
  • utm_medium=sms
  • utm_campaign=[Name of your campaign]
  • utm_content=[ID of your campaign]

Reformat phone numbers

Only phone numbers that use the required format of +1 (000) 000 0000 can receive SMS messages in HubSpot To reformat phone numbers without a country code in a specific contact segment:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar, navigate to SMS.
  • Click the Tools tab.
  • In the Phone number formatting section, click Select contacts.
  • Click the Choose a segment to be reformatted dropdown menu and select a contact segment. Only contacts in this segment with a number in the Phone number or Mobile phone number property that lacks a country code will have the +1 country code added. If both phone numbers are eligible, both will be edited.
  • If you have already received explicit consent to reach out to these contacts via SMS and wish to subscribe them:
    • Select the Yes, subscribe eligible contacts checkbox. This will opt all contacts who have not already opted out into the SMS subscription type.
    • Click the Subscription type dropdown menu and select each SMS subscription type you are opting contacts into.
    • Click the Legal basis dropdown menu and select the justification for storing this contact’s data. Learn more about legal basis.
    • In the Describe how this contact gave consent field, enter a description of how you obtained this contact’s consent to store their data and communicate with them.
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
  • Click Send [your user’s email address] a CSV of proposed changes, then review the CSV when it’s delivered. Make sure that the correct contacts are being edited and that you have obtained explicit consent for every contact you’re subscribing.
  • Select the I’ve reviewed the proposed changes and I’m happy to proceed with reformatting checkbox.
  • In the bottom right, click Proceed with reformatting.

Manage SMS subscription consent

After you set up your SMS number in HubSpot, you must get explicit consent from contacts to communicate with them using SMS.

Contacts can grant explicit consent via specific keywords in an SMS thread. You can also manually opt your contacts to receive SMS messages if they’ve given express and verifiable consent, or set their SMS subscription consent with a workflow.

Permissions required Which contact records you are able to edit depends on your CRM objects permissions for contacts.

Please note: SMS subscription status is tied to a contact’s phone number. If a contact is deleted, any contact with the same phone number created in the future will retain the same subscription status.

Disclaimer: this page is neither an exhaustive summary of consent requirements nor legal advice for your organization to use in complying with it. Instead, it provides background information to help you better understand SMS consent options and how it can apply to your organization. This information is not the same as legal advice, where an attorney applies the law to your specific circumstances, so you should consult an attorney if you’d like advice on your interpretation of this information or its accuracy.

Understand subscription keywords

Contacts can opt in to receive SMS messages from your business by sending one of the following keywords to your registered SMS number:

  • START
  • UNSTOP
  • SUBSCRIBE

If a contact wants to unsubscribe from messages, they can send one of the following keywords to your registered SMS number to opt out:

  • STOP
  • STOPALL
  • UNSUBSCRIBE
  • CANCEL
  • END
  • QUIT

After a contact sends a message with one of the opt-in or opt-out keywords above, their subscription status for the SMS channel will be updated automatically.

Please note: in accounts with the Marketing SMS Short Code Add-On, an opt-in confirmation message is automatically sent when a contact opts in. This message will count toward your account’s message segment limits.

Manage opt-in status for individual contacts

If you have received a contact’s explicit and verifiable consent to receive SMS communications from your business, you can opt them into receiving SMS messages from their contact record.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of the contact.
  • In the left column, click View subscriptions in the Communication subscriptions section. Any SMS subscriptions will have SMS listed in the Channel column.
  • To subscribe the contact to receive SMS messages:
    • Hover over the subscription and click Subscribe.
    • In the dialog box, click the Legal basis for communicating with contact dropdown menu and select a legal basis. Learn more about legal basis.
    • In the Explanation for communication consent field, enter a description of why you’re legally allowed to communicate with this contact.
    • Click Save.
  • To unsubscribe the contact from receiving SMS messages, hover over the subscription and click Resubscribe.

Bulk edit contact opt-in status

You can edit the SMS subscription status for multiple contacts at once, as long as you’ve received their explicit and verifiable consent to receive SMS communications.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.

  • Select the checkboxes next to the contacts whose subscriptions you want to update.

  • At the top of the table, click the More dropdown menu and select Edit communication subscriptions.

  • To subscribe these contacts to receive SMS messages:

    • In the right panel, select SMS.

    • Click Next.

    • Under What subscription status are you updating?, select Subscribe.

    • Click the Communication subscription types dropdown menu and select the checkbox next to your SMS subscription type.

    • Click the Legal basis for communicating with contact dropdown menu and select a legal basis. Learn more about legal basis.

    • In the Explanation for communication consent field, enter a description of why you’re legally allowed to communicate with this contact.

    • Click Finish.

  • To unsubscribe these contacts from receiving SMS messages:

    • In the right panel, select SMS.

    • Click Next.

    • Under What subscription status are you updating?, select Unsubscribe.

    • Click the Communication subscription types dropdown menu and select the checkbox next to your SMS subscription type.

    • Click Finish.

Send automated SMS messages using workflows

You can reach out to opted in contacts with marketing or transactional information by sending SMS messages via workflows. You can also set up a workflow to subscribe a contact to SMS messages when they take an action to opt in.

Before you get started

Before you begin working with this feature, make sure to fully understand what steps should be taken ahead of time, as well as the limitations of the feature and potential considerations of using it.

Understand requirements
  • You must have registered your business to send SMS messages before sending them from workflows.
  • Contacts must be opted in and set as marketing contacts to receive automated SMS messages.
  • Phone numbers must be formatted correctly, including the use of a country code, to receive automated SMS messages. Learn more about using workflows to format phone numbers.
Understand limitations and considerations
  • Workflows that send SMS messages will send the messages to the number in the contact’s Mobile Phone Number property. If this property is empty, the messages will be sent to the number in the Phone Number property instead.

Create an automated SMS message

Permissions required Edit permissions for SMS are required to create SMS messages.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.
  • In the top right, click Create message.
  • In the right panel, enter a name for the message in the SMS name field.
  • Enter values for any required properties, then click Create message.
  • In the message editor, edit and configure the SMS message.
  • If you are enrolled in the beta for multi-object personalization tokens in SMS, you can add personalization tokens for any object type as long as they match the type of workflow where the message will be sent. For example, use deal-based tokens if using the message in a deal-based workflow.
  • Click the Sending tab.
  • In the Sending method section on the left, click the How will you send the message? dropdown menu and select As part of a workflow.
  • By default, quiet hours are turned on for all SMS messages, including those sent in workflows. Learn more about SMS quiet hours.
  • In the top right, click Review and publish.
  • In the right panel, review your SMS message details, then click Publish message.

Add an SMS message to a workflow

Once you’ve published your SMS message, you can create a workflow to send SMS messages.

Permissions required Edit permissions for workflows are required to add SMS messages to workflows.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, set enrollment criteria.
  • Click the add plus icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the Communications section and select Send SMS message.
  • Click the Contact dropdown menu and select Enrolled contact to send an SMS message to the contact enrolled in the workflow. To send messages to related contacts, click the Contact dropdown menu, then select More data. Learn more about using data variables in workflows.
  • Click the Choose a published SMS message dropdown menu and select an SMS message that’s been published for automation.
  • At the top of the left panel, click Save.
  • Set up and turn on your workflow.

Use a workflow to set a contact’s SMS subscription status

You can use the workflows tool to set a contact’s SMS subscription status and provide legal basis for communicating with the contact. This option is only available for workflows that enroll contacts. Learn more about managing consent to contact subscribers with SMS.

Permissions required Edit permissions for workflows are required to set SMS subscription status in workflows.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, set enrollment criteria.
  • Click the add plus icon to add a workflow action.
  • In the left panel, click to expand the CRM section and select Manage communication subscriptions.
  • Click the Contact dropdown menu and select Enrolled contact to manage subscriptions for the contact enrolled in the workflow. To send messages to related contacts, click the Contact dropdown menu, then select More data. Learn more about using data variables in workflows.
  • Click the Messaging Channel dropdown menu and select SMS.
  • Click the Subscription status dropdown menu and select Subscribe.
  • Click the Communications subscription type dropdown menu and select the type of SMS communication the contact has agreed to receive.
  • Click the Legal basis for communicating with contact dropdown menu and select a legal basis option. Learn more about legal basis.
  • In the Explanation for communication consent field, enter a description of how you obtained the contact’s consent to communicate with them. This should support the legal basis option you’ve selected.
  • At the top of the left panel, click Save.
  • Set up and turn on your workflow.

Send SMS messages in the conversations inbox

If you purchased the Marketing SMS Add-On and set up messaging in HubSpot, you can connect your SMS number to a single channel in the conversations inbox.

Once connected, you can review, organize, and reply to incoming SMS messages within the conversations inbox. You can also use SMS channel data in conversations-based workflows and in the reporting tool.

Permissions required Access to the conversations inbox depends on the inbox access settings in your account.

Connect SMS as a channel in your inbox

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to SMS.
  • In the Marketing section, click Manage next to a registered phone number.
  • In the right panel, click Connect in the Reply management section.
  • Click the Choose an existing inbox dropdown menu and select an inbox, or click Go to inbox settings to create a new inbox.
  • Click Save.

Your SMS number will now appear as a connected channel in your connected inbox settings.

Create an SMS view in the conversations inbox

Once you’ve connected your SMS number, incoming SMS messages will appear in the list of conversations associated with any of the status filters in the left sidebar (such as All open and All closed).

You can also create a custom view to filter for messages that come from your connected SMS channels.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Inbox. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Inbox directly.
  • In the bottom left, click the Actions dropdown menu and select Create a view.
  • In the right panel, enter a name for the view, then click Next.
  • Click Add filter.
  • In the pop-up box, click Source.
  • In the Source filter, click the second dropdown menu, then select the SMS checkbox.
  • In the bottom right, click Create view.

The new view will appear below the other default inbox filters and views.

Reply to incoming SMS messages

When a contact receives an SMS message you’ve sent or scheduled or sent with a workflow, they can reply to the message. Any replies they’ve sent will appear as a new conversation in your inbox.

Users can then review the contact’s information and reply, as long as the contact meets the requirements to be contacted via SMS.

Click on an SMS conversation to view the conversation history and use the reply editor to compose a response.

Please note: incoming and outgoing inbox messages count against your monthly SMS segment usage. MMS messages are counted as 5 message segments.

Review SMS activities on the contact record

Permissions required Which contact records you can view depends on your CRM objects permissions for contacts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to CRM > Contacts. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to CRM > Contacts directly.
  • Click the name of a contact.
  • On the contact record, click the Activities tab.
  • Click the Activity dropdown menu and select the SMS checkbox. To narrow down the activities that appear, select and clear the Select all checkbox, then select the SMS checkbox again.

Set up SMS messaging for marketing communications

You can use SMS messages to send time-sensitive marketing communications to customers. For example, you could send SMS messages about upcoming events or offers only available for a limited time.

To send marketing SMS messages in HubSpot, you need to register your business and receive approval. After submitting your registration in HubSpot, it may take six to eight business days for 10DLC numbers and 8 to 12 weeks for Short Code registrations.

Please note: HubSpot works with a third-party SMS service provider, Twilio, to provide SMS messaging services to customers who purchase either of the SMS add-ons. Please review the information listed below carefully:

  • You must comply with applicable laws, regulations, Twilio’s policies, including, but not limited, to the Twilio Acceptable Use Policy and the Twilio Messaging Policy, Twilio’s Forbidden Message Categories for US and Canada, and industry standards, including, but not limited to, telecommunications providers’ policies and US carrier requirements. Please carefully review Twilio’s Forbidden Message Categories for US and Canada to make sure you can use HubSpot’s SMS tool. Please review US carrier penalties for non-compliant messaging here. To date, T-Mobile is the first U.S. telecommunications provider to announce non-compliance fees for violations of T-Mobile’s Code of Conduct. Twilio will update these guidelines accordingly if/when additional U.S. telecommunications providers announce non-compliance fees.
  • Twilio uses A2P, a system that allows authorized businesses to send Application-to-Person (A2P) type messaging via standard 10-digit long code (10DLC) phone numbers, as well as via short code numbers for high volume senders. Carriers in the US consider all Twilio traffic to be A2P. Learn more about A2P and the required information for registration in Twilio’s documentation.
  • A Twilio account is not required to use SMS messaging in HubSpot.

Permissions required Super Admin or SMS setup permissions are required to set up SMS messaging in your HubSpot account.

Understand limitations & considerations

  • You can only send SMS messages from US-based numbers.
  • Each HubSpot account can only generate a single number for marketing SMS communications. If you have the Transactional SMS Add-On, you can generate an additional number for transactional SMS communications.
  • SMS messaging in HubSpot is not currently supported for sole proprietors.
  • Certain types of messages and business categories are not allowed on SMS platforms in the United States and Canada. Review the forbidden message categories in the documentation of Hubspot’s SMS provider, Twilio, to verify they don’t apply to your business or message content.
  • Super Admins can review SMS account limits.

Understand differences between short and long code SMS

The Marketing SMS Add-On grants access to a long code (10DLC) number and is designed for basic SMS marketing. Purchasing this add-on provides a ten digit phone number after a six to eight business day waiting period. This add-on works best for customer service, two-way communication, and smaller campaigns where a local presence is helpful.

The number of messages you can send on a long code number depends on a trust score determined by a third party based on their independent reputation checks of your brand. Learn more about trust scores in Twilio’s documentation.

The Marketing SMS Short Code Add-On grants access to a short code SMS number and is designed for high volume SMS marketing. Purchasing this add-on provides a five or six digit phone number after an eight to twelve week waiting period. This add-on works best for large marketing campaigns, promotions, and time sensitive alerts.

Get a long code SMS number

For long code SMS numbers, you will need to provide information about your business and the type of marketing SMS messages you plan to send, then wait to be approved. Once you’ve been approved, you can get the number you’ll use to send SMS messages.

Please note: this process only applies to long code SMS numbers. To begin the registration process for short code SMS numbers, contact your HubSpot Customer Success Manager.

Register your business

Provide details about your business, including where it is registered, the business type, and your business number.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Calling & SMS > SMS Setup.
  • Click Start registration next to Marketing SMS long code in the Marketing section.
  • In the right panel, click Provide registration details from the Step: 1 Provide required registration details section.
  • For businesses registered in the United States:
    • Click the Country of registration dropdown menu and select United States.
    • In the Legal business name field, enter the business name exactly as it appears on your CP575 form.
    • In the EIN field, enter the EIN exactly as it appears on your CP575 form.
  • For businesses registered in Canada:
    • Click the Country of registration dropdown menu and select Canada.
    • In the Legal business name field, enter your legal business name exactly as it appears on your official company registration record.
    • In the Business number (BN) field, enter your business number. If your number is longer than nine digits, only enter the first nine.
  • For businesses registered outside of the United States or Canada:
    • Click the Country of registration dropdown menu and select Rest of world.
    • In the Legal business name field, enter your legal business name exactly as it appears on your official company registration record.
    • Click the Business registration type dropdown menu and select an option. If your registration type isn’t listed, select Other, then enter your registration type in the Other business registration type field.
    • In the Business number (BN) field, enter the business number recommended for your registration type.
  • Click the Business type dropdown menu and select a business type, such as Corporation or Non-Profit.
  • Click the Business industry dropdown menu and select the industry that most closely aligns with your business.
  • In the Website field, enter the URL of your business’s website.
  • Click the Regions of operations dropdown menu and click each region where your business operates.
  • In the Company type section, select a status:
    • Public: your company is listed on a stock exchange or over-the-counter market. If you select this option, you must also select the stock exchange where your business is traded and enter its stock ticker symbol.
    • Private: your company is not listed on a stock exchange or over-the-counter market.
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
  • In the Business address fields, enter the address of your business.
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
  • In the Point of contact fields, enter the contact information for the person who will be contacted about your registration. The email address you enter must use the format name@company.com.
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
Provide SMS details

Once you’ve provided your business information, you must provide details about how you will be using SMS messages, including all opt-in methods, your privacy policy and terms of service, and the type of messages you’ll send.

Failure to include sufficient information in these fields or providing information that doesn’t apply to the same sender and SMS use case may result in a failure of your registration.

  • In the SMS details fields, enter two sample messages in the Write two sample SMS messages you’ll send section, with the kind of marketing content you’ll be sending in SMS messages. These should match your brand and not include any other type of content, like support conversations or account updates. Your example messages should contain the following:
    • Your business name.
    • Information on how users can opt out, including a keyword like STOP.
    • A public link to a privacy policy that includes a statement of non-sharing for mobile numbers, message frequency, and a Message and data rates may apply disclosure.
    • If you’re using personalization, brackets around personalized content. For example: “Hey [first name]”.
  • Select an option for whether you are a financial institution that uses direct, first-party lending. This is a forbidden business category.
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
  • In the Opt-in details section, select the checkbox next to each way recipients will provide opt-in consent:
    • By texting START to our designated SMS number: recipients text START to your designated SMS number from the number where they consent to receive SMS messages.
      • Click choose a file, then upload an image of how you will inform recipients to text START to your SMS number.
    • By entering their phone number and giving consent via a website form: recipients fill out a form to opt into receiving SMS messages.
      • This form must include the following:
        • Separate checkbox to collect Marketing SMS consent. This consent must be optional and explicit, rather than tied to other services or message types. This checkbox should not be pre-checked, should not appear checked in any screenshots, and should be not be required to submit the form. It’s recommended to place this checkbox near the field for entering a phone number.
        • No mention of types of messages other than marketing.
        • Legal business name.
        • Types of marketing messages recipients will receive, such as event reminders or product showcases.
        • Message rates.
        • Frequency of messages.
        • How to opt-out of receiving messages.
        • Live, publicly accessible links to a privacy policy and SMS terms of service. These links should point directly to the relevant policies.
      • For public forms, select Public form, then enter a link to the form.
      • For private forms, select Private or restricted access form, then click Choose a file and upload a screenshot of the form.
      • For drafted online forms, select Form screenshot. Enter the URL where the form will be hosted, then click Choose a file and upload a screenshot of the form.
      • For paper forms, select Paper form, then click Choose a file and upload an image of the form.
  • In the bottom right, click Next.
  • In the Privacy policy section, enter the live, publicly accessible URL of your SMS privacy policy. It must meet the following requirements:
    • The privacy policy should state that the business does not share SMS consent data with third-parties third parties/affiliates/non-affiliates.
    • If the privacy does mention sharing SMS consent data, the following disclaimer should be included: “All the above categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties, excluding aggregators and providers of the Text Message services.”
  • In the Terms of service section, enter the live, publicly accessible URL of your SMS terms of service. Your terms of service include the following information:
    • Legal business name.
    • Types of messages recipients will be sent.
    • How to opt out. For example: “Reply STOP to opt out.”
    • Message rates. For example: “Message and data rates may apply.”
    • Frequency of messages. This can be a specific number of messages or a disclaimer that “Message frequency varies.”
    • Carrier disclaimer. For example: “Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.”
    • Link to your privacy policy.
  • In the bottom right, click Done.

After you’ve submitted your SMS details, the approval process by mobile carriers may take a few weeks.

Get an SMS number

Once your registration has been approved, you can generate an SMS number.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to SMS.
  • Click Get number.
  • In the right panel, click the Area code/prefix dropdown menu and select an area code.
  • Click Generate number. A preview of your new number will appear.
  • Click Next.

Understand message segments for SMS

SMS messages longer than 160 characters will be split into 153 character message segments for sending. When you purchase any of the SMS Add-Ons, you will have access to a certain amount of message segments per month. To increase your message segment limit, you can purchase the SMS Limit Increase.

Understand limitations and considerations

  • Test sends count toward message segment limits.
  • If you have the Marketing SMS Short Code Add-On, the required subscription confirmation message counts toward message segment limits.
  • Unused message segments will not be added to the subsequent month’s available message segments.
  • Additional message segments will be added monthly based on your account’s renewal date, not the date you purchased a limit increase.

Understand message segments

SMS messages that contain more than 160 characters will be split into 153 character message segments for transmission, then reassembled by the recipient’s device. A message with multiple message segments will still appear as a single message to the recipient.

You should consider the following when composing SMS messages:

  • Characters outside the standard SMS character set, such as emoji, cause messages to be encoded using a different system. The character limit for segmenting these messages is 70 characters instead of 160, and they are split into 67 character segments.
  • Opt-in text such as START and SUBSCRIBE does count toward a message’s character count.
  • Links count for 36 characters.
  • Personalization tokens will cause variation in the amount of characters in a message depending on the recipient.

Estimate message segments

You can view an estimate of how many message segments an SMS message will require within the message editor:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > SMS. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > SMS directly.

  • Click the name of a drafted SMS message.

  • In the right column, you will see the Character count and Estimated message segments above a preview of the message.

  • To recalculate character count and message segments for a specific contact, click the View default preview message dropdown message and select a contact.

If a message uses personalization tokens, the default preview will use the number of characters in the token’s default value, or 15 characters if no default value is provided.

Understand SMS quiet hours

If you’re sending SMS messages through HubSpot, any SMS messages sent during quiet hours will automatically be deferred until quiet hours are complete.

Quiet hours are the period from 8PM to 8AM in a contact’s local time zone when SMS laws in some places require they not be contacted. This restriction applies to both individual SMS messages and SMS messages sent through workflows.

Please note: your legal counsel is the best resource to give you advice about your company’s legal obligations. This page is provided for information purposes only and is not included as part of the HubSpot Customer Terms of Service. It is not intended to provide legal advice, and HubSpot encourages customers to consult with their own legal counsel to understand the legal obligations applicable to their business. The information here is subject to change

Review quiet hour settings

You can review whether your contacts will be affected by quiet hour sending restrictions in the SMS message editor.

Permissions required Edit permissions for SMS are required to edit SMS messages.

  • In your HubSpot account, navigate to Marketing > SMS.
  • Click the name of a drafted SMS message.
  • Click the Sending tab.
  • In the Sending method section, an alert will appear if you’ve scheduled your message during a time that falls within the quiet hours of any of your recipients.

Please note: if timezone information is not available for a recipient, their quiet hours will be set to the default for recipients in the United States, which is 8:00 PM US/Eastern to 8:00 AM US/Pacific.

  • To turn off quiet hours restrictions, toggle the Quiet hours switch off. This is not recommended, as it can result in violations of SMS sending laws.

Use custom SMS keywords in workflows

When communicating with customers using SMS, you can provide them with custom keywords to trigger specific actions in HubSpot. For example, after instructing interested customers to text WEBINAR, you could set up a workflow to add those contacts to a segment of webinar participants.

Create SMS keywords

Permissions required Edit permissions for SMS are required to use SMS tools.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to SMS.
  • Click the Tools tab.
  • In the Inbound keywords section, click Add keywords.
  • In the dialog box, enter a keyword.
  • Click Add keyword.
  • To delete a keyword, click the delete delete icon next to that keyword.

Use SMS keywords in a workflow

Once you’ve set up your SMS keywords, you can create a workflow to take specific actions when contacts send SMS messages containing those keywords. By using branches, you can set separate actions for each keyword in a single workflow.

Permissions required Edit permissions for workflows are required to edit workflows.

Please note: inbound keywords from phone numbers associated with multiple contacts will not trigger this type of workflow.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Automation > Workflows. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Automation > Workflows directly.
  • Click the name of an existing workflow, or create a new workflow.
  • In the workflow editor, click the Trigger box.
  • Select SMS replied. The trigger should display as “SMS replied has been completed any number of times anytime.”
  • Set whether you want contacts to be able to re-enroll in the workflow, then click Save.
  • In the workflow editor, click the plus icon under the enrollment triggers.
  • In the left panel, click Branch.
  • Select One property or action output.
  • Click the Property or value to branch on field, then select Inbound SMS keyword.
  • Select the Create a separate branch for each value in this property checkbox, then click Next.
  • Make any changes to the branches for your workflow, then click Save.
  • For each branch, click the plus icon, then add an action.
  • When you’re finished editing your workflow, click Review and turn on in the top right.

Marketing: Social

Analyze social media performance

Analyze your social media performance and engagement with social analytics. Monitor social reports and dashboards built for tracking your social media reach, audience growth, engagement, lead generation, and publishing trends. For example, you can monitor which publishing times or media types result in higher engagement, across your connected social accounts.

This article provides information about the new analytics view. If you’re using the classic analytics view, learn more about analyzing social reports with classic analytics.

Permissions required

  • Social permissions are required to access social analytics.
  • Dashboard, reports, and analytics Create/Own and Edit permissions are required to edit reports and dashboards.

Before you get started

  • The new analytics view does not include historical data earlier than July 1, 2025. If you connected your social accounts before this date, you can view earlier data in the classic analytics view.
  • The new analytics view does not include the option to compare date ranges in social reports. To compare two time periods, such as this year and last year, switch to the classic analytics view.

Switch between new and classic analytics

To switch between social analytics views:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • Click the Analyze tab.
  • In the upper right, use the selector to switch between New analytics and Classic analytics.
New analytics

The new analytics view includes preconfigured reports for reach, engagement, lead generation, website traffic, and audience insights. Filter reports by social account, network, or date range, or customize reports using the report builder.

Classic analytics

The classic analytics view includes the previous social analytics experience, including the option to compare social performance across date ranges. Learn more about analyzing social reports with classic analytics.

Review social analytics

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • Click the Analyze tab.
  • In the upper left, click the dropdown menu to select a dashboard.

Dashboard

Use it to:

Optimize your content

Compare social engagement by media type, timing, and content type to guide future strategy.

Leads from social

Track how social media contributes to your pipeline by showing where leads and deals originate. Reports highlight conversions, attribution, and post performance.

Drive engagement

Review how audiences interact with your content across social platforms. Reports measure likes, comments, shares, and video engagement.

Grow your brand reach

Monitor your brand’s visibility and reputation over time. Reports show follower growth, impressions, reach, and sentiment trends.

Performance Overview

Monitor your brand’s visibility and reputation over time. Reports show follower growth, impressions, reach, and sentiment trends.

Filter social analytics

Filter social analytics data by social account, date range, or other criteria.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • Click the Analyze tab.
  • At the top of the dashboard, set your filters:
    • Accounts: select the social accounts to include in your analytics.
    • Date range: select the time period to analyze.
      • If the selected date range is Last 30 days, social posts published more than 30 days ago will not factor into the reports, even if the posts are still receiving clicks and interactions.
    • Advanced filters: apply additional filters to refine the data displayed in your reports.
  • To remove all applied filters, click Clear all.

Learn more about applying dashboard filters.

Add a custom dashboard

Add a custom dashboard to review additional reports alongside the default social analytics dashboards.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • Click the Analyze tab.
  • In the upper left, click the dropdown menu to select Add and manage dashboards.
  • On the Manage dashboards page, click Add dashboard.
  • In the right panel, click the Select a dashboard dropdown menu and select a dashboard.
  • In the Who can view this dashboard on the analyze tab field, select Everyone or Specific teams.
  • At the bottom, click Add dashboard.

Learn more about customizing the analyze tab.

Overview of social reports and key metrics

Review the reports available in each default social analytics dashboard. Report data is based on the selected date range, which is set to the last 60 days by default.

Optimize your content
  • Which content types bring the most traffic?: displays the sum of HubSpot tracked link clicks each week, by social post media type.
    • Tracked link clicks for Instagram and TikTok may be low because links in captions display as plain text and aren’t hyperlinked by these networks.
  • What content type drives the most engagement?: tracks the social media engagement for each post media type.
  • Best times to post for engagement: reports on the historical average of social media engagement across hourly publishing times.
Leads from social
  • Which social platforms are sending us the most website traffic: displays which social media platforms are most effective at driving traffic to your website.
  • New contacts from social: tracks the total number of new contacts generated as a result of social media activities.
  • How many deals were influenced by social: shows the number of closed deals where a social media interaction was a touchpoint in the customer journey.
Grow your brand reach

  • Where are we getting the most visibility?: shows the total number of times your content was displayed to visitors across your social channels during the last 60 days.
