Images

The following image requirements apply to Instagram feed posts, reels, and stories.

  • File types: PNG, JPG, or JPEG.
  • Resolution: 320 - 1440 pixels wide. If your images are outside of this range, Instagram may automatically resize the images when published.
  • Maximum file size: 8 MB.

Learn more about Instagram image requirements in Facebook’s developer documentation.

Videos

The following video requirements apply to Instagram feed posts, reels, and stories.

  • File types: MP4 or MOV.
  • Maximum width: 1920 pixels.
  • Frame rates: 23 fps - 60 fps.
  • Maximum audio channels: two channels (stereo).

LinkedIn

Image requirements for LinkedIn media posts

It’s recommended to use images larger than 552 (width) x 276 (height) pixels. Once images are uploaded, they cannot be resized.

  • File types: PNG, JPG, JPEG, or GIF.
  • Maximum file size: 10 MB.
  • Recommended aspect ratio: 3:1 to 2:3 (width/height). If the ratio is larger, the image will be centered and cropped.
  • Images per post: up to nine images.

Learn more about LinkedIn image recommendations in LinkedIn’s Help Center.

Video requirements for LinkedIn media posts
  • Minimum file size: 75 KB.
  • Maximum file size: 5 GB.
  • Video duration: 3 seconds to 30 minutes.
  • Aspect ratio: 1:2.4 - 2.4:1.
  • Videos per post: one video only.

Learn more about LinkedIn video requirements in LinkedIn’s Help Center.

TikTok

Image requirements for TikTok
  • File types: JPG, JPEG, or WebP.
  • Resolution: images must be exactly 1080×1920 or 1920×1080 pixels.
  • Maximum file size: 20 MB per image.
  • Images per post: up to 35 images.
Video requirements for TikTok
  • File types: MP4, MOV, or WebM.
  • Video duration: three seconds to 10 minutes. The maximum video duration may vary based on your TikTok account type.
  • Frame rate: 23 to 60 fps.
  • Minimum file width and height: 360 pixels.
  • Maximum file size: 1 G.
  • Videos per post: one video only.

X

Image requirements for X

Your image will be automatically scaled when a user expands a post, or when displayed in your gallery.

  • File types: PNG, JPG, JPEG, or GIF.
  • Maximum image size: 5 MB.
  • Maximum file width and height: 8192 pixels.
  • Maximum GIF size: up to 5 MB on mobile devices and up to 15 MB on desktop.

Learn more about X image requirements in X’s Help Center.

Video requirements for X
  • Minimum resolution: 32 x 32 pixels.
  • Aspect ratios: 1:2.39 - 2.39:1 range (inclusive).
  • Maximum frame rate: 60 fps.
  • Maximum file size: 512 MB.

Learn more about X image requirements in X’s Help Center.

Instagram account not connecting to HubSpot

To connect an Instagram account to HubSpot, the account must be a professional Instagram account linked to a Facebook page that you manage. If you’re unable to connect the Instagram account to HubSpot, it’s usually due to a disconnected Facebook Page, an Instagram account type, or missing user access.

This article covers common reasons an Instagram account won’t connect and how to resolve each issue.

Confirm the Instagram account type

Only professional Instagram accounts can be connected to HubSpot. This includes both Business and Creator accounts.

  • On your mobile device, open the Instagram app.
  • Navigate to your profile, then tap the menu icon.
  • Tap Account type and tools.
  • In the Account type section, confirm that your account is set to Professional.

If you have a personal account, learn how to set up a professional Instagram account.

Check the Facebook page connection

A professional Instagram account must be linked to a Facebook Page before it can be connected to HubSpot.

  • On your mobile device, open the Instagram app.
  • Navigate to your profile, then tap Edit profile.
  • Under Profile information, confirm that your Facebook page is listed.

If your Facebook page isn’t connected:

  • Learn how to connect your professional Instagram account to a Facebook page.
  • Revisit your Facebook page’s Instagram settings and ensure that the correct Instagram account is connected.

Manage user access

  • Navigate to your Meta Business Settings.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click Settings.

  • In the left panel menu, click Business assets.

  • In your list of assets, click the name of your Instagram account.

  • In the right pane, click People.

  • Locate or search for the user that you want to edit access for, and click Manage.

  • In the dialog box, under the Full control (business tools and Facebook) section, turn on the Everything toggle. Or, if the user doesn’t have full control, under the Partial access (business tools only) section, turn on all toggles.

Verify HubSpot integration permissions

You’ll also need to verify HubSpot’s app permissions on the linked Facebook page. If you’re unable to connect your Facebook page, learn how to troubleshoot connecting your Facebook page to HubSpot.

  • Navigate to the business integration settings for your Facebook user.
  • In the upper right, click your profile picture. Then, click Settings & privacy > Settings.
  • In the left sidebar, under Your activity, click Security and Login. Then, click Business Integrations.
  • In the Active tab, next to the HubSpot integration, click View and edit.
  • Confirm that all app permission switches are toggled on. If you authorized specific pages when you first connected your account to the HubSpot social tool, ensure that each page is listed beneath each app permission. This ensures all necessary permissions are given to HubSpot to publish to Instagram.

Reset the Instagram account and Facebook page connection

If you’re still unable to connect to your Instagram account, you can disconnect then reconnect the link between your Instagram account and Facebook page. Then, try connecting your Instagram account to HubSpot again.

  • To disconnect the link between your Instagram account and Facebook page:

    • On your desktop, log in to the Facebook account that is connected to HubSpot.

    • In the upper right, click your profile picture. Then, click Settings & privacy > Settings.

    • In the left panel menu, under Permissions, click Linked accounts.

    • In your list of Linked accounts, click Instagram.

    • In the upper right, click Disconnect Account.

  • To reconnect the link between your Instagram account and Facebook page, follow the steps to link your Instagram professional account to your Facebook page.
  • Once the accounts have been linked, verify the connection in the your Instagram account’s Sharing to Other Apps settings then follow the steps to connect your Facebook and Instagram accounts to HubSpot.
  • If your Instagram professional account still isn’t showing up when you try to connect it, contact HubSpot Support.

Install and use the HubSpot Social Chrome extension

The HubSpot Social Chrome extension allows you to schedule or publish content through HubSpot directly from the page you’d like to share. When using the extension, you can publish through HubSpot without having to navigate to the HubSpot social tool.

Permissions required All accessible accounts or Their connected accounts social permissions are required to install and publish social posts with the Chrome extension.

Please note: the HubSpot Social Chrome extension will only work properly when your Chrome cookie settings are set to Allow all cookies or Block third party cookies in Incognito. Learn more about how to change your Chrome cookie settings in Google Chrome’s Help Center.

Install the HubSpot Social Chrome extension

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.

  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.

  • Click the Publishing tab.

  • In the Publish from your browser section, click Install the Chrome Extension.

  • In the Chrome Web Store, click Add to chrome. Then, in the dialog box, click Add extension. You’ll be redirected to a confirmation page for the extension, and the HubSpot Social Chrome extension should appear in your browser toolbar as an orange sprocket icon sprocket.

Necessary disclosure: The HubSpot Social Chrome extension only accesses information about the current page, after its toolbar button is clicked, using the permissions granted by the Google Chrome’s activeTab permission.

Select the HubSpot account to use with the extension

If you’re a user in multiple HubSpot accounts, you can select the account to use with the HubSpot Social Chrome extension:

  • Click the sprocket HubSpot social icon in your browser toolbar.
  • In the right panel, click the dropdown menu to select a HubSpot account.

Share content with the HubSpot Social Chrome extension

  • On the page you want to share, click the HubSpot social icon sprocket in your browser toolbar.
  • In the right panel, select the social network to publish your social post.
    • The social post will automatically populate the title and URL of the website page you’re on, and a post preview will be generated from the URL metadata.
    • The post preview will include an image, title, meta description, and link. This may vary depending on the page shared.
  • Set up your post details:
    • Select accounts: select the accounts to publish the social post to.
    • When to Publish: select a specific date and time to publish the social post, or click Publish now to publish the post immediately.
    • Schedule another: after setting up your social post, publish another post or publish to another social account by clicking the corresponding social icon. This will automatically duplicate your existing post content into the new post.
    • Add to a marketing campaign: select a campaign to associate the social post with.
  • Once your post is ready to publish, in the upper right, click Schedule or Publish. Learn more about managing your social posts.

Limit access to social post publishing

Limit which users can publish social posts by setting their social permissions to Draft only. With these permissions, users can create and save social posts as a draft, without the option to publish. Once social posts are drafted, you can review, approve, and schedule the social posts to be published.

Understand Draft only social permissions

Before setting a user’s social permissions to Draft only, note the following:

  • Draft-only users can set a publish date and time for draft social posts. However, they will only be able to save the post as a draft and will not have access to review and publish it.
  • Draft-only users can bulk upload social posts, but will not be able to schedule the social posts for publishing.
  • Draft-only users can delete draft social posts, but will not be able to delete scheduled or published social posts.
  • Draft-only users will not be able to add social posts to campaigns, or edit campaigns already on social posts.
  • Draft-only users are read-only in X feeds and social inbox activity. They can view activity, but cannot respond or react.
  • Draft-only users will not be able to connect social accounts or disconnect existing social accounts. They can set default social accounts to post from.
  • Draft-only users will not be able to edit blog auto-publish settings.
  • Draft-only users can only edit their own social activity email notification preferences in the Email Notifications tab in social settings.

Set social permissions to Draft only

Permissions required Add and edit users permissions are required to customize user permissions.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Users & Teams.
  • Hover over the name of a user and click Edit permissions.
  • Under Choose permissions, click Marketing.
  • Navigate to the Social section.
  • Click the dropdown menu next to the permission and select Draft only.

Approve draft social posts

Permissions required All accessible accounts or Their connected accounts Social permissions are required to approve and publish social posts.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • In the left sidebar menu, click Drafts.
  • To review a draft, click the draft social post.
  • You can approve drafts individually or in bulk with the following steps:

    • To approve an individual draft, hover over the social post and click Actions. Then select Approve draft.

    • To approve drafts in bulk, select the checkboxes next to the draft social posts that you want to approve. At the top of the table, click Approve Drafts.

  • Once you’ve approved a draft, you’ll be directed to the social composer, where you can review or edit the social post content.
  • To publish your social post, in the top right, click Review & Schedule.
  • In the right panel, review your social posts’ details. At the bottom, click Schedule or Publish.

Link shortening in social posts

When you publish social posts through HubSpot, URLs within your social post will be automatically shortened to save space, track clicks, and create simple links for your audience.

By default, shortened links use the hubs.ly, hub.li, or hub.lu domain. If you want to shorten links using a branded short domain on Bitly, learn how to connect your Bitly account to HubSpot.

Understand how links are shortened in social posts

  • By default, all links shared within social posts are shortened to a 23-character hubs.ly, hub.li, or hub.lu tracking link. Shortened links cannot be previewed in the social tool and will only display once the post is published.
  • Tracking parameters are automatically added to URLs (utm_content, utm_medium, and utm_source) to track traffic metrics back to the original post. Custom tracking URLs are not supported in social posts published through HubSpot.
  • While some social networks track multiple interactions with a post as a click, HubSpot only tracks direct clicks to the shortened URL as a click.
  • The character limit for X posts includes URLs, so if you’re including a link, your effective character limit will be reduced by 23 characters.
    • The character count within the social publishing tool will automatically adjust for the shortened link once a URL is added, but the link itself will not appear shortened until your post is published.
    • Images also count as links for this purpose, so including an image in your post will also use 23 characters.
  • If you downgrade or cancel your HubSpot account, all shortened links in your existing social posts will continue to work.
  • Automatic link shortening cannot be turned off.

LinkedIn page not connecting to HubSpot

If you can’t connect your LinkedIn page to HubSpot, there may be issues with permissions or account access. This article covers why a LinkedIn page won’t connect and how to troubleshoot the issue.

Review your LinkedIn page admin permissions

If you don’t see your page when connecting your LinkedIn account to HubSpot, it usually means you do not have the necessary permissions:

  • Ensure that you have Super Admin access for the LinkedIn Company pages you’re connecting to HubSpot.
  • Only users with administrator role permissions on LinkedIn can connect, users with content admin role permissions will not be able to do so.

To ensure you can connect your page to HubSpot, confirm that your LinkedIn account has the necessary LinkedIn page admin permissions:

  • Log in to your LinkedIn account.

  • In the upper right, click your profile image and in the Manage section, select your page.

  • In the left sidebar menu, click Settings.

  • In the right panel, click Manage admins.

  • On the Page admins tab, locate your LinkedIn user and confirm that you’re listed as a Super admin. If you’re not listed as a LinkedIn Super admin, you’ll need to request admin access to the LinkedIn page.

  • Once the admin permissions have been granted, navigate back to your HubSpot account and reconnect your LinkedIn account.

Reset your HubSpot social tool connection

If you have the necessary LinkedIn page permissions, but still don’t see your page, a connection issue may have occurred when adding your LinkedIn account to HubSpot. To resolve the issue, follow the steps to reset your connection.

  • Open a new incognito or private window in your browser.
  • Log in to your HubSpot account.
  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • On the Accounts tab, hover over your LinkedIn account and click Disconnect.
  • Log in to your LinkedIn account to reset the HubSpot social tool connection:
    • Ensure that you have Super Admin access for the LinkedIn Company pages you’re connecting to HubSpot.
    • In the upper right, click your profile image and select Settings & Privacy.
  • In the left sidebar, click Data privacy.
  • Scroll down to the Other applications section. Then, click Permitted services.
  • In the HubSpot or HubSpot Social v2 section, click Remove.
  • Navigate back to your HubSpot account and reconnect your LinkedIn account.

Manage social account settings

Manage your connected social accounts in HubSpot to control how your team publishes and tracks your social content. In your account’s social settings, you can:

  • Set up auto-publishing to automatically post new blog articles to your social channels.
  • Manage which users and teams have access to each social account.
  • Set default accounts to post from when creating new social posts.
  • Configure email notifications to receive social activity and reporting summaries.
  • Assign social accounts to specific brands.

Set up blog auto-publishing

Permissions required

  • All accessible accounts social permissions are required to configure blog auto-publishing for any connected social account.
  • Their connected accounts social permissions are required to configure only the social accounts the user connected.

If your blog is hosted on HubSpot, you can set up blog auto-publishing to publish a new post on your social accounts whenever you publish a new blog post.

These posts include the blog post title, meta description, link, and featured image. Each post will be published 15 minutes after your blog post is published. Learn more about blog auto-publishing in HubSpot.

Please note: blog auto-publishing is not available for Instagram accounts because links are not allowed on Instagram posts.

To set up blog auto-publishing:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • On the Accounts tab, navigate to the account you want to auto-publish to.
  • In the Blog auto-Publish column, click Choose blog or Manage blogs. This option is only available in social accounts where Accounts access is set to Everyone.
  • In the dialog box, click the Auto-publish new content for dropdown menu and select one or more blogs.
  • Click Submit.

Edit user access to a social account

Permissions required

  • All accessible accounts social permissions are required to edit user access for any connected social account.
  • Their connected accounts social permissions are required to edit only the social accounts the user connected.

Explicitly giving a user or team access to a social account will limit access for all others. Users or teams without access can’t view or manage posts from that account in the social tool. Learn more about limiting access to your HubSpot assets.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • Hover over your social account and in the Account Access column, click Edit.
  • In the right panel, select from the following options:
    • Private to me: limit access to your user account only. The account won’t be included in the social summary email notification.
    • Available to everyone: all users in the account will have access.
    • Select users and teams who can edit: only specified users in the account will have access. The account won’t be included in the social summary email notification. Only users in a Marketing Hub Enterprise account can limit access by users and teams.
      • If you’re selecting specific users or teams, in the search bar, search for and select the checkbox to the left of the user or team.
      • To remove access from an account, clear the checkbox next to the user or team’s name, or click the X in the Who has access section.
  • At the bottom, click Save.

Understand user permissions for social publishing

The level of access a user has to publish to a social account depends on their social publishing permissions and whether the user has account access.

The user’s social permissions

The user has account access

The user does not have account access

Draft only (Marketing Hub Enterprise only)

The user can create drafts. Learn more about Draft only social publishing permissions.

The user cannot create drafts or view the social account’s name in the social settings.

Their accounts only

The behavior will differ depending on whether the user connected the social account:

  • If the user connected the social account, they will have full access to the social account, such as publishing to or disconnecting the account.
  • If the user did not connect the account, they cannot post to the account. They can only view the social account’s name and its reporting and publishing data.

The behavior will differ depending on whether the user connected the social account:

  • If the user connected the social account, they will have full access to the social account, such as publishing to or disconnecting the account.
  • If the user did not connect the social account, they cannot view or access the account.

All accessible accounts

The user will have full access to the social account.

The behavior will differ depending on whether the user connected the social account:

  • If the user connected the account, they will have full access to the social account.
  • If the user did not connect the social account, they cannot view or access the account.

Super Admin

The user will have full access to the social account.

Select default social accounts to post from

Permissions required All accessible accounts or Their connected accounts social permissions are required to set default social accounts for publishing.

To select specific social accounts by default when creating new social posts:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • In the Default column, click to toggle the Default switch on. Any changes will be saved automatically.

Please note:

  • If you have a Marketing Hub Enterprise account, you can only select up to 60 default accounts to post from.
  • You can only set one default X account.

Configure which social posts to include in your reporting data

Permissions required

  • All accessible accounts social permissions are required to configure which social posts to include in reporting data for any connected social account.
  • Their connected accounts social permissions are required to configure only the social accounts the user connected.

When you connect your social account, the posts and interaction data included in social reports depend on the network of the account you connected:

  • Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and YouTube: posts published either from HubSpot or from the external social network will be available for reporting.
  • X: When you connect your account, you can choose whether you want to report on posts published from all sources, or posts published from HubSpot only. If you want to change your post visibility settings for X, you’ll need to disconnect your social account, then reconnect it with the desired setting.
Review post visibility for social accounts

To view which social posts HubSpot reports on for your connected social accounts:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • On the Accounts tab, review the Post Visibility column:
    • All posts: social posts from all sources are visible in social reports.
    • HubSpot: social posts published from HubSpot only are available for social reports.

Configure social activity summary and social report notifications

Permissions required Social permissions are required to access and edit social activity and report notifications.

Configure social notifications to stay updated on engagement across your connected social accounts and receive scheduled performance summaries. These notifications help you monitor interactions (e.g., comments, mentions, or new X followers) and review overall performance directly from your inbox.

Social activity summary and social report notifications are configured for each user.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • Click the Notifications tab.
  • In the Social activity summary section, select the frequency of social activity summaries. These emails don’t include data from externally published posts.
  • In the Social Reports section, select the Yes, send me a monthly email with my social reports checkbox to receive monthly report summaries. This includes data for posts published from HubSpot and externally published posts.

Please note:

  • Instagram and YouTube interactions and activities are not included in any social email notifications.
  • Only data for social accounts set to Available to everyone will be included. If access to a social account has been restricted to specific users or teams, the social account will not be included in any social email notifications.
  • Only new X followers will be included in this email notification. New followers from other networks such as Facebook, Instagram, or LinkedIn will not be included.

Configure account expiration notifications

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to configure account expiration notifications.

Configure account expiration notifications to manage which users receive alerts when a connected social account is nearing expiration. This helps ensure the proper users are notified and can reconnect the account to maintain uninterrupted publishing.

Account expiration notifications are set at the HubSpot account level, meaning the selected users will receive expiration alerts for all connected social accounts in your HubSpot account.

To configure account expiration notifications:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • Click the Notifications tab.
  • In the Account expiration notifications section, select the users who should get notified when a connected social account is nearing expiration.
  • Click Save.

If the selected users are no longer active in your account, all Super Admins will receive the expiration notifications.

Assign social accounts with brands

Subscription required A Marketing Hub Enterprise subscription and the Brands Add-on are required to assign social accounts with a brand.

Permissions required Social permissions are required to assign social accounts with a brand.

Connected social accounts can only be associated with one brand at a time. Learn more about associating your assets with brands.

To assign a social account with a specific brand:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • Hover over the social account and in the Brand column, click Edit.
  • In the right panel, select the brand to associate with that social account.
  • At the bottom, click Save. The social account will be moved to that selected brand.
  • You can also navigate to a specific brand and then connect a social account to be assigned under that brand. Learn more about how to navigate between brands.
    • When switching between brands in the social account settings, only social accounts associated with the brand will appear in your social settings.
    • When switching between brands in the social tool, only data and assets (e.g., posts, replies) associated with the social accounts assigned to the selected brand will appear in the social tool.

Set default social follow links for marketing emails

Permissions required All accessible accounts or Their connected accounts social permissions are required to set default social follow links.

Social follow links let visitors access your social media profiles directly from your marketing emails using the social follow module. You can set one default follow link for each social network.

Manage social posts in the social calendar

Use the social calendar to review drafted, scheduled, and published social posts, identify gaps in your publishing schedule, and manage posts across your connected social accounts. The calendar displays social posts published through HubSpot or externally.

You can also review the social calendar in the HubSpot mobile app.

Permissions required Social permissions are required to manage and review social posts.

Filter social posts in the calendar

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • On the Calendar tab, filter social posts using any of the following filters:
    • Accounts: the social account associated with the post.
    • Campaigns: the campaign associated with the social post.
    • Users: the user who created the social post.
    • Post types: the post type, such as link posts, image posts, or video posts.
    • Publishing status: the publishing status, such as Published, Scheduled, and Draft.

Review and edit social posts in the calendar

  • To view a social post’s details, click the post in the calendar. The dialog box displays the post content, publishing date, and associated campaign.

    • To edit the post, click Edit post or Edit draft. You’ll be directed to the social composer where you can continue editing your post.
    • To clone the post, click Clone. The cloned post will appear in the social composer.
    • To delete a post, click Delete. Then, in the dialog box, click Delete post.

Learn more about managing social posts in the HubSpot mobile app.

Associate drafted and scheduled social posts with campaigns from the social composer. You can also associate externally published posts or multiple social posts with campaigns from the social List view. Learn more about associating assets and content with campaigns.

Delete drafted or scheduled social posts

To delete multiple drafted or scheduled social posts in bulk:

Delete published social posts

Before deleting published social posts, review the following limitations:

  • Only posts published through HubSpot can be deleted from the social tool. Externally published posts cannot be deleted through HubSpot and must be deleted directly from their respective platforms.
  • Deleting a post externally will not delete it in HubSpot. If a post is deleted from the social platform, the post and associated data will still be displayed in HubSpot.

    • If you try to view the post on the social platform from HubSpot, an error will occur.

    • To remove the post from HubSpot, you must also delete it from the social tool.

  • LinkedIn, X, and Facebook posts can be deleted through HubSpot after they are published. Facebook stories and Instagram posts cannot be deleted through HubSpot once published. They must be deleted directly from their respective platforms.

To delete a published social post:

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.

  • In the dialog box, click Delete post.

Monitor social sentiment

Monitor social sentiment in your social inbox to gain insight into how your audience perceives your social media content. By understanding your social sentiment, you can better tailor your social media strategy and boost engagement. This AI-powered feature analyzes social comments and mentions to assign a positive or negative sentiment category. These categories help you track positive trends or address negative feedback in your social interactions. Social media threads with ten or more interactions assigned with a sentiment category will display a net sentiment score. This score can help you understand the overall sentiment across the thread.

Permissions required Social permissions are required to access social posts.

Before you get started

Before you begin, be aware of the following requirements and limitations for using the social sentiment feature.

Requirements

To monitor your social sentiment, you must turn on Customer conversation data in your AI settings. Learn how to manage your AI settings.

Please note: you can manage AI feature access in your AI settings and configure what data is shared. Review HubSpot’s AI Trust FAQs and AI Model Cards for detailed information on AI security controls, data use, and compliance.

How social sentiment is calculated

Social sentiment categories are assigned to comments and mentions with more than 40 characters that contain favorable (Positive) or unfavorable (Negative) content. Interactions with fewer than 40 characters, or with insufficient information, remain Untagged.

A net sentiment score (highly positive, positive, neutral, negative, or highly negative) is calculated for threads with ten or more tagged comments.

  • Comments from the original poster’s social profile are not included in this calculation.
  • The score is calculated daily at 9:00 AM UTC.
Limitations and considerations
  • Social sentiment is available for social posts published after July 1, 2025.
  • Sentiment categories are applied to comments and mentions only, not to other interactions like messages or reposts.
  • Supported languages include English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, and Japanese.

Review social sentiment

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.

  • At the top, click the Inbox tab.

  • You’ll be redirected to All activity in your social inbox. The social sentiment category will be displayed in the upper right of the social interaction. This may be displayed as either Positive or Negative.

  • To filter social interactions based on the sentiment category, click the Sentiment dropdown menu at the top.

  • To review social sentiment in a social thread, click the comment.

    • Comments with more than 40 characters will display a sentiment category in the upper right of the interaction.
    • Threads with ten or more interactions assigned with a sentiment category will display a net sentiment score. This score is automatically calculated to display the thread’s aggregated sentiment. The score includes the following overall values: highly positive, positive, neutral, negative, or highly negative.

Monitor your social posts in the HubSpot mobile app

Publish YouTube videos from HubSpot

Use HubSpot’s social composer to publish YouTube videos directly from your HubSpot account.

To publish from the HubSpot mobile app, learn how to publish YouTube videos from the HubSpot mobile app.

Permissions required Social permissions are required to create and publish social posts. Users with Draft only permissions can save posts as drafts, but cannot publish.

Before you get started

  • Connect your YouTube account to HubSpot.

Necessary disclosure: this feature uses YouTube’s API Services. By connecting your YouTube account to HubSpot, you agree to comply with YouTube’s Terms of Service

Publish a YouTube video from HubSpot

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.

  • In the upper right, click Create post or Create, then select Create from scratch.

  • In the social composer, click the Select accounts dropdown menu in the top left. Then, select the checkboxes next to the YouTube accounts you want to post to.

    • To select all connected YouTube accounts, click the YouTube checkbox.

  • In the upper left, click the socialBlockYoutubeplay YouTube icon.

  • In the Draft content section, configure the details for your YouTube video:

    • Title: the title for your YouTube video.
      • You can use a maximum of 100 characters.
      • The title cannot include invalid characters.
    • Description: the description for your YouTube video. You can include keywords in your description to help users find your video when searching on YouTube.
      • When publishing through HubSpot, your channel must have YouTube’s advanced features for any links in the video description to be clickable.
    • Upload video: click the Select media dropdown menu and select Select video.
      • When selecting an existing video from the files tool, the video must have visibility set Public or Public - noindex. If the video’s visibility has been set to Private, you will not be able to select the video.
      • The video must meet YouTube’s video and audio formatting specifications.
      • The video will be automatically posted as a YouTube short if it’s three minutes or less and has a square or vertical aspect ratio. Learn more about YouTube shorts.
    • Audience: select Yes, it’s made for kids or No, it’s not made for kids to set whether your video is suitable for children.

  • Click to expand the Schedule post section, then select your publishing option:

    • Publish now: publish the video immediately.
    • Schedule for later: select a specific date and time to publish the video. Or click to expand Your saved times and select a time from your social publishing schedule.

  • Click to expand the Add to campaign section:

    • Click the Select a campaign dropdown menu and select a campaign.

  • Click to expand the More options section and configure your video details:

    • Playlist: select an existing YouTube playlist to add this video to. Learn more about creating and managing YouTube playlists.
    • Tags: add tags to your YouTube video to allow users to find your video more easily. Each tag should be separated by a comma. Learn more about YouTube tags.
    • Language: select the primary language for your YouTube video.
    • License: select the license type for your video. By default, Standard YouTube License will be selected.
    • Allow embedding: allow other users to embed your YouTube videos on their websites.
    • Publish to subscriptions feed and notify subscribers: notify your YouTube subscribers when you’ve published this video.
    • Category: select a category to allow users to find your video more easily. For example, you may want to categorize an instructional video as Educational.
    • Visibility: set a visibility option for your YouTube video. You can set a video as Private, Unlisted, or Public. Learn more about YouTube’s visibility options.
    • YouTube first comment: add a first comment to your post.

  • After setting up your YouTube video, in the top right, click Review & Schedule or Review & Publish. Alternatively, continue editing posts for other social networks.

Publish YouTube videos from the HubSpot mobile app

While on the go, capture, upload, and publish videos to YouTube from the HubSpot mobile app. If you’re using a computer or laptop, learn how to upload and publish YouTube videos on desktop.

Permissions required Social permissions are required to create and publish social posts. Users with Draft only permissions can save posts as drafts, but cannot publish.

Before you get started

Before you use this feature, review the requirements and video specifications for publishing to YouTube.

Requirements
  • Connect your YouTube account to HubSpot.
  • Verify your YouTube account. Non-verified accounts cannot publish from the HubSpot mobile app.
YouTube video specifications
  • The video must meet YouTube’s video and audio formatting specifications.
  • To publish a YouTube short, the video must be three minutes or less and have a square or vertical aspect ratio. Regular videos should be less than 15 minutes. Learn more about YouTube’s network specifications.

Publish a YouTube video from the HubSpot mobile app

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.

  • In the top right, tap the add add icon. Then, tap Social post.

  • Tap the checkboxes next to YouTube accounts that you’d like to post to. Then, tap Done.

  • Enter your social post content. The following fields are required:

    • Video title: the title for your YouTube video.
      • You can use a maximum of 100 characters.
      • The title cannot include invalid characters such as ‘<’.
    • What would you like to say to your network: add a description for your post. The description has a 5,000 character limit. You can also include keywords to help users find your video when searching on YouTube.

  • To add a video, under Add media, select from the following:

    • Upload a video from your mobile device: tap From Device and then tap Choose video or Choose file.
    • Record a new video: tap From Device and then tap Take video.
    • Select a video from HubSpot files: tap HubSpot Files and then tap Choose video from HubSpot Files.
      • When selecting an existing video from the files tool, the video must have visibility set Public or Public - noindex. If the video’s visibility has been set to Private, you will not be able to select the video.

  • To remove the video, tap the uploaded video. Then, tap Remove.

  • To preview your thumbnail image, tap the uploaded video. Then, tap Preview.

  • To customize the thumbnail image, tap the uploaded video and select from the following:

    • Set thumbnail from video frame: under Change Thumbnail, click and drag on the video timeline to select the video frame. Then, tap Update to [timestamp] to save that frame as the thumbnail.
    • Set thumbnail from HubSpot files: under HubSpot Files, enter the image search term in the search bar. Then, tap on the image that you’d like to use as the thumbnail.

  • Set your YouTube post details:

    • Publish time: choose to publish your video immediately or schedule to publish your video at a specific date and time.

    • Campaign: choose to associate your video with a new or an existing campaign.

    • Audience: select Yes, it’s made for kids or No, it’s not made for kids to determine whether or not your video is suitable for children. This field is required.

    • Language: select the primary language for your YouTube video.

    • Category: select a category to help users find your video more easily. For example, categorize an instructional video as Education.

    • Visibility: select a visibility option for your YouTube video. You can set a video as Public, Private, or Unlisted. Learn more about YouTube’s visibility options.

    • Tags: enter tags to your YouTube video to allow users to find your video more easily. Learn more about YouTube tags.

    • License: select the license type for your video. By default, Standard YouTube License will be selected.

    • Allow embedding: allow other users to embed your YouTube videos on their websites.

    • Publish to subscriptions: publish the YouTube post to your subscriptions feed and notify your YouTube subscribers when you’ve published.

  • To save your post as a draft, at the bottom, tap Save draft.

  • To schedule or publish your YouTube post, at the bottom, tap Review.

  • Review your YouTube post details. Then, at the bottom, tap Publish now or Schedule post.

Reauthorize or disconnect social accounts from HubSpot

If your social account is disconnected from HubSpot, you’ll need to reauthorize the connection. Social networks may disconnect your account for privacy and security reasons. This can happen if your social media account is deleted, not used for a long time, or is compromised.

At any time, you can also manually disconnect or remove a social account from HubSpot. Social networks will also ask you to reauthorize your connected accounts for privacy and security reasons at the following intervals:

  • Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, and TikTok: every 90 days.
  • LinkedIn: one year after you first connect your account.
  • X: after 90 days of inactivity.

Before you get started

Before reauthorizing or disconnecting your social account, review how this action affects your data and scheduled activity.

  • When a social media account is disconnected:
    • All scheduled posts will be canceled.
    • Previously published posts will no longer display on the Published tab.
  • If you reconnect a social media account within a certain time frame, your social data will still be available in the social tool. This includes the following:
    • Social posts published through HubSpot up to when the social media account was disconnected.
    • Externally published posts for the last 60 days before the social media account was reconnected. Social posts that were published directly on the social network between the date of the disconnect and 60 days before reconnecting will not be included.
    • Previously scheduled posts will also be published at the scheduled time after re-connecting a disconnected account.
    • To retain your social data, your social accounts must be reconnected by the following:
      • Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, TikTok, and X accounts: you’ll need to reconnect your account within one year.
      • LinkedIn and YouTube accounts: you’ll need to reconnect your account within 60 days.
    • If a disconnected social account is not reconnected within the above time frames, your post history, previously scheduled posts, and draft posts may no longer be accessible in HubSpot.

Reconnect a social media account

Permissions required All accessible accounts Social permissions and account access are required to reconnect a social account.

It is recommended for the user who originally connected the social account to go through the reauthorization process. If you run into any issues when reconnecting, try disconnecting and reconnecting the account.

To reconnect your social account:

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • Hover over the account you want to reconnect, click Reconnect, then follow the prompts to reauthorize the account.

When you reconnect a social account, your existing account access (e.g., Only me) will stay the same.

If your account has been disconnected for more than 90 days, it will not display in the social settings. To reconnect these accounts:

  • In the upper right, click Connect accounts. In the dialog box, the disconnected accounts will display as selected but grayed out.
  • Click Continue. The reconnected account will display in your social settings.
Reconnection notifications

If you need to reauthorize your account, whether you receive a notification depends on the following:

  • If your account is disconnected for security reasons or inactivity, you will not receive a notification.
  • If a social network is prompting you to reauthorize your account, you’ll receive a notification one week before the account needs to be reauthorized.

To manage users that receive these notifications, learn how to configure account expiration notifications.

Please note: if you’ve received a reauthorization notification, but the Reconnect option is not displayed, this still means that your account may be disconnected soon. It is still recommended to disconnect and reconnect your social media account before it expires.

Disconnect a social media account

Permissions required Super Admin permissions are required to disconnect a social account. Or, the user who originally connected the social account can disconnect it.

  • In your HubSpot account, click the settings icon in the top navigation bar.
  • In the left sidebar menu, navigate to Marketing > Social.
  • Hover over the account you want to disconnect and in the Status column, click Disconnect.
  • In the dialog box, click Disconnect account.

Report on social posts using the custom report builder

Use the custom report builder to configure reports for specific social media metrics and performance data. Compare key metrics, such as engagements, impressions, reactions, or clicks, across your connected social accounts or marketing campaigns. This can help you analyze social data and trends to inform your social media strategy.

Before you get started

Before you begin creating custom reports, review the requirements and available data sources.

Requirements

Permissions required

  • Dashboard, reports, and analytics Create/Own and Edit permissions are required to create custom reports.

  • Social permissions are required to access social post data.

  • Your social account must be connected to HubSpot.

Limitations and considerations
  • When you create a custom report with social data sources:
    • Historical data is available starting from July 1, 2025, or the date your social account was connected, whichever is later.
    • Available social data is based on your user access to the social account. Learn more about managing user access to your connected social accounts.
  • Custom social reports show new data based on the report’s date range. For example, the Impressions by channel report using a date range set to this week will display the total number of new impressions made during this calendar week. It does not display cumulative impressions.

Social data sources

Social data sources

Social activities

Social interactions detected and social channels

Social posts

Social posts, social channels, and social post metrics

Social channels

Social channels and social channel metrics

Social profiles

Social profiles

Please note: the Social Channel property is being deprecated. It’s recommended to use the Channel property when reporting on your social media channels.

Create custom reports for social posts

  • In the upper right, click Next.
  • In the left panel, use the search bar, click the Browse dropdown menu, or click the filter filter icon to filter fields based on the report data source, field types, or property groups.
  • To view property details, hover over the property and click the [icon] three vertical dots icon, then select View property info.
  • Click and drag properties from the left sidebar into the Configure tab. Or click Actions, then select Add to X.
  • After adding your properties, continue setting up your custom report.

Review example reports

Below are sample report configurations you can use to analyze your social posts, activities, and channels. Learn more about the social metrics available in the custom report builder.

Engagement rate by social account

To compare your social media engagement rate across different social accounts, broken down by social network, you can create your custom report with the following configuration:

Impressions by media type

To compare the number of social media impressions by the social post content type (e.g., photo, video, or text), you can create your custom report with the following configuration:

  • X-axis: timestamp (weekly)
  • Y-axis: Impressions (Sum)

Review and manage your social posts in the HubSpot mobile app

After creating and publishing your social posts, use HubSpot’s mobile app to review your published, scheduled, and drafted social posts. On the mobile app, you can also use the social calendar to review your publishing schedule.

Permissions required Social permissions are required to manage and review social posts.

Manage and review your social posts

When reviewing your social posts, you can delete scheduled or drafted social posts. However, it is not possible to delete published social posts from the HubSpot mobile app. Published social posts must be deleted on a desktop or directly from their respective platforms.

To manage and review your social posts:

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • In the top left, tap the menu icon.
  • In the Marketing section, tap Social Publish.
  • At the top of the page, tap Published, Scheduled, or Draft.
  • To filter the posts by social account:
    • In the top left, tap All Accounts.
    • In the Select Accounts dialog box, select the checkboxes next to the social accounts to filter by.
    • In the top right, click Done. Only posts from the selected accounts will display.
  • To filter posts by campaign:
    • In the top left, tap All campaigns.
    • In the Select Campaign dialog box, tap the name of the campaign to filter by. Only posts from the selected campaign will display.
    • To remove any campaign filters:
      • In the top left, tap the name of the campaign.
      • In the Select Campaign dialog box, tap Clear.
  • To edit a social post:
    • Tap on the post that you want to edit.
    • In the top right, tap the menu icon.
    • Tap Edit.
  • To delete a scheduled or drafted social post:
    • Tap on the Scheduled or Draft tab.
    • Tap on the post that you want to delete.
    • In the top right, tap the menu icon.
    • Tap Delete.
Clone a social post

If you have an Android device, you can clone a social post:

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.
  • In the top left, tap the menu icon.
  • In the Marketing section, tap Social Publish.
  • Tap a social post.
  • In the top right, tap the menu icon.
  • Tap Clone.

Use the social calendar

Use the social calendar to review and manage your social publishing schedule. All scheduled and published posts will appear on the social calendar, including externally published posts. If you’re using a computer or laptop, learn how to use the social calendar on desktop.

To use the social calendar in the HubSpot mobile app:

  • Open the HubSpot app on your device.

  • In the top left, tap the menu icon.

  • In the Marketing section, tap Social post.

  • In the top right, click the calendar icon.

  • To review the social posts for another date, at the top, tap the date. Dates with scheduled or published social posts will be tagged.

  • To review additional details about each social post for each day, tap the social post name.

Please note: draft posts will not be included in the social calendar.

Review and reply to Instagram direct messages

Receive direct messages from Instagram and respond directly from HubSpot’s social tool. Managing direct messages in the social reply tool helps you track social activity and communicate with your audience, without switching platforms. For example, when a follower sends you a direct message through Instagram, you can reply to the message, assign the Instagram profile to a CRM contact, and manage the interaction alongside your other social activity.

This feature is available for Instagram messages only.

Permissions required

  • All accessible accounts social permissions are required to reply to social interactions for any connected social account.
  • Their connected accounts social permissions are required to reply to social interactions only for the social accounts the user connected.

Before you get started

Before you begin managing direct messages, review the following requirements, limitations, and considerations.

Requirements
  • Connect your Instagram account to HubSpot. If you’re setting up direct messages in HubSpot for the first time, you must disconnect and reconnect those accounts to authorize this feature.
  • To receive Instagram direct messages in HubSpot, the Allow access to messages option in your Instagram settings must be turned on.
Limitations & considerations

  • When connecting or reconnecting your Instagram account to HubSpot, only direct messages from the last 7 days will be retrieved.

  • When reviewing your Instagram direct messages in HubSpot, the 200 most recent messages for each thread will appear. The full thread can be viewed directly on Instagram.

  • In the social tool, only incoming direct messages and messages with replies are displayed. If you send an outgoing direct message, it won’t be available in the social tool until the recipient replies.

  • Instagram direct messages are available through HubSpot’s social tool on the web, but not in the HubSpot mobile app.

Reply to direct messages

Reply to Instagram direct messages from HubSpot to keep customer conversations in one place. Engage with your audience using automatically generated reply recommendations and attach media files to your reply.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • At the top, click the Inbox tab.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under All activity, click Direct messages.
  • Click a direct message.
  • In the right panel, enter your response or insert a reply recommendation.
  • Click Reply.
Send file attachments

Attach images, videos, audio files, or PDFs when replying to Instagram direct messages. A single reply can contain text or an attachment, but not both. To send both content types, split them into two separate messages.

  • To send file attachments in your reply, click the attach attach file icon.
  • In the right panel, search for and select a file or click Upload to add a file from your device.
  • Click Reply.

The following media types are supported for Instagram direct messages:

Organize direct messages

Filter messages and update their status to help your team prioritize conversations.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.
  • At the top, click the Inbox tab.
  • In the left sidebar menu, under All activity, click Direct messages.
Filter direct messages

At the top of the Inbox tab, apply the following filters:

  • Accounts: connected Instagram accounts.
  • Statuses: the message status (e.g., Read, Unread, Replied to, Saved, and Archived).
  • Date range: the date the last message was sent.
Update direct message status

To change the status of a direct message, click Actions and select a status:

  • Save: mark the message as saved and move it to the saved folder.
  • Archive: archive the message and move it to the archived folder.
  • Move to spam: mark suspicious messages as spam and move it to the spam folder.
  • Mark as unread: mark the message as unread.

Assign a CRM contact

Assign Instagram profiles with CRM contacts to associate direct messages to your contacts. This can help you track conversation history and maintain context for future interactions.

  • In your HubSpot account, click More, then navigate to Marketing > Social. If More doesn’t appear in your account, navigate to Marketing > Social directly.

  • At the top, click the Inbox tab.

  • In the left sidebar menu, under All activity, click Direct messages.

  • In the left panel, click a direct message.

  • In the right panel, click Actions and select Assign CRM contact.

  • In the dialog box, enter the contact’s name into the search bar to locate and select an existing contact. Click Create new to create a new contact.

  • Click Assign to contact or Create new contact.

Learn more about associating contacts with social interactions.

Troubleshoot direct messages

If Instagram direct messages aren’t displaying in HubSpot, confirm that Allow access to messages is turned on in your Instagram account.

To check this setting:

  • Open the Instagram app on your device.
  • Navigate to your profile.
  • In the top right, tap the menu icon.
  • Tap Messages and story replies > Message requests.
  • Toggle the Allow access to messages switch on.

Use the social inbox to review and manage social interactions across your connected social accounts. You can filter interactions by account, type, status, sentiment, and date range, then take action such as replying or assigning a contact to a social interaction.

Permissions required

  • All accessible accounts social permissions are required to reply to social interactions for any connected social account.
  • Their connected accounts social permissions are required to reply to social interactions only for the social accounts the user connected.
